articles.title: Por qué tu móvil muestra ‘5G’ y el de otros ‘5G+’
articles.text:
Algunos usuarios de iPhone notan, desde hace poco más de un mes, un cambio en la parte superior de la pantalla de su teléfono: junto a las barras de cobertura móvil aparece el ícono ‘5G+’ en lugar del habitual ‘5G’. El fenómeno no es aislado. Cada vez más usuarios reportan la misma novedad, que coincide con la actualización a iOS 27.
La explicación tiene que ver con una distinción técnica que existía desde hace años, pero que hasta ahora los teléfonos no mostraban: la diferencia entre la red 5G convencional y el 5G “real” o Stand Alone.
Hasta la llegada de este nuevo distintivo, todos los usuarios veían el mismo ícono de ‘5G’ en sus pantallas, sin posibilidad de saber si estaban conectados a una red 5G NSA, con arquitectura apoyada parcialmente en infraestructura 4G, o a una red 5G SA, diseñada de punta a punta para la nueva tecnología.
Ahora bien, el cambio no implica que antes no existiera esa cobertura superior, sino que el teléfono carecía de un ícono específico para señalarla.
Qué significa el ícono 5G+ y por qué aparece ahora
El ‘5G+’ es el nombre comercial que operadores como Orange y Movistar adoptaron, allá por 2023, para identificar la red 5G SA (Stand Alone) frente al 5G NSA que desplegaron inicialmente las compañías. La arquitectura Stand Alone implica que tanto la red de acceso radio como el núcleo central están construidos específicamente para 5G, sin depender de la infraestructura 4G previa.
Que el ícono aparezca recién ahora no significa que el usuario no contara antes con esa red SA. Simplemente, los teléfonos no diferenciaban visualmente entre ambas arquitecturas y mostraban siempre el mismo símbolo de ‘5G’.
Con la actualización reciente de los sistemas operativos, los dispositivos ya pueden detectar cuándo la conexión corresponde específicamente a una red 5G de extremo a extremo y mostrarlo al usuario.
Esta distinción responde a una pregunta que muchos usuarios se hacen al ver el nuevo ícono: el 5G+ identifica una conexión a la red 5G SA o “real”, construida íntegramente con tecnología 5G tanto en el acceso radio como en el núcleo de red, a diferencia del 5G convencional, que puede apoyarse parcialmente en infraestructura 4G.
Qué operadores ofrecen 5G+ en la actualidad
Algunos operadores muestran este distintivo a sus clientes: Movistar, O2 y Orange. Movistar fue de los primeros en activar su 5G+, y poco después Telefónica extendió esa misma red de mejor calidad a su marca O2. Orange, por su parte, comenzó a mostrar el ícono más recientemente, mientras que Movistar y O2 ya lo exhiben desde hace algunas semanas.
Para ver el símbolo en la pantalla, el primer requisito es contar con una línea móvil de alguna de estas tres compañías. No basta con tener cobertura 5G: es necesario que el operador específico ofrezca la variante SA en la zona donde se encuentra el usuario.
Qué teléfonos y sistemas operativos muestran el nuevo ícono
El segundo requisito tiene que ver con el propio dispositivo. No todos los terminales están homologados para mostrar el 5G+, y entre los que sí lo están, resulta necesario contar con una versión de software actualizada que habilite el ícono.
En el caso del iPhone, el distintivo apareció a partir de la actualización a iOS 27, desplegada en septiembre. En el ecosistema Android, la novedad llega de forma más progresiva: ya se puede ver en algunos modelos recientes de Samsung compatibles con One UI 9.0, además de ciertos dispositivos de Xiaomi, Motorola, OPPO, OnePlus y Google Pixel. El resto de los modelos irá incorporando la función de manera paulatina.
Qué ventajas ofrece la red 5G SA frente al 5G convencional
La diferencia entre ambas arquitecturas no es solo cosmética. Al estar diseñada íntegramente para tecnología 5G, la red SA habilita funcionalidades como el network slicing, que permite segmentar la red según las necesidades de cada servicio, y mejora la experiencia general del usuario.
Entre los beneficios concretos de esta arquitectura se cuentan tiempos de respuesta más bajos para aplicaciones en tiempo real, una gestión más eficiente del tráfico de datos y un mejor comportamiento de la red en entornos con gran concentración de usuarios.
También ofrece mayor capacidad para soportar millones de dispositivos conectados de forma simultánea, una condición cada vez más relevante a medida que crece el número de aparatos conectados a internet.

articles.title: Meta launches Muse AI agent for Apple Watch and Android Wear OS — so now you can talk to your fluffy life assistant anywhere
articles.text:
Meta launches Muse AI agent for Apple Watch and Android Wear OS — so now you can talk to your fluffy life assistant anywhere
Ever wanted to talk to an AI agent through your wrist? Now you can!
- Meta has announced Muse compatibility with Apple Watch and Wear OS
- Muse will now be able to help out with tasks through your smartwatch
- Your custom Muse agent will now show up on your wrist to answer questions and keep you on schedule
Meta has released Muse AI compatibility for Apple Watch and Android Wear OS allowing you to talk to your personal AI agent anywhere you go directly through your smartwatch.
As long as you can get past giving Muse total access to your personal life, you’ll find its ability to weigh in on your life really quite helpful, helping to keep you on task, on time, and in line with your life goals.
And now that you can interact with Muse’s AI persona Jolly through voice calls, text messages, or dictation on your smartwatch, you can cut out the crucial seconds it takes to pull your phone out of your pocket or log in to your laptop.
More ways to interact with Muse
Muse hit the AI agent market in September and surpassed 10 million US app store downloads within the first 40 days. The AI agent can help manage every facet of your life, from bills and your mortgage, to business meetings, client calls, and deadlines.
But it’s more than just a mundane task manager, Meta says Muse is also able to organize your social life and help achieve your life goals — and if you so desire, it can make purchases on your behalf.
In order to put a more likeable face on AI, Meta allows users to customize the look of their assistant who will pop up on your phone or watch screen whenever you need help.
Muse is quickly becoming a central focus of Meta’s consumer strategy, with the company teasing Muse Charm — essentially a Tamagotchi-sized device — that will allow you to see and communicate directly with your Muse from the palm of your hand.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
More recently, Meta announced that Muse would have access to Spaces, which gives users a way to create “custom experiences” with their Muse focused on particular tasks, topics, or goals.
If that wasn’t enough ways to communicate with your Muse, Meta also rolled out the ability to video call your AI assistant, with Jolly having the ability to convey “subtle expressions and gestures” to fit each conversation’s tone. Of course, Muse won’t be able to see you and will rely entirely on the tone of your voice and the topic of conversation to convey it’s ‘emotions’.
Of course, having this many ways to talk to your AI agent and giving it complete control over almost all of your data comes with a few downsides. Recent testing by Surfshark found that Meta’s Muse is the most data hungry consumer AI agent currently available, hoovering up double the types of data that its competitors do.
So if you’re on a phone plan with limited data, you might want to consider conducting your Muse conversations over Wi-Fi.

articles.title: Over 35,000 Grok-Built Apps Exposed Online, Some Leaking Confidential Data and Passwords
articles.text:
Of the 37,571 Grok-built apps that security company Claroc found online, 35,578 were open to anyone without a sign-in, the researchers said yesterday.
They included 24 apps built by staff at the social network X and at SpaceXSI, the company that makes the Grok AI assistant. Most of the open apps were games, landing pages, and calculators, but about 1 in 10 contained internal business or personal data.
The staff apps included a confidential onboarding plan for a new sales hire, a sales territory map of 594 accounts, and an X advertising proposal to a U.S. federal agency marked confidential. SpaceXSI, formerly known as xAI, has since taken down all 24 staff apps but not other users' apps, the researchers said.
Besides those staff apps, the open apps contained internal data from 30 other organizations the researchers could identify, across fields ranging from construction and energy to healthcare and defense. Of those, 26 have more than 1,000 employees, and 6 are Fortune 500 companies.
According to the researchers' estimate in their report, roughly 2% of the open apps contained material serious enough to rate as high or critical.
The exposed material included a hospital group's searchable list of more than 3,500 employees, an intensive care briefing on a single patient, a fire department's live shift board, and a contractor's timesheet whose code held every employee's password in plain text.
Grok can build a working app from a description typed into its chat, a feature its maker opened to every Grok plan on August 19. This chat builder shares the Grok Build name with a separate terminal coding tool, whose repository uploads were reported on July 14.
Each published app gets its own subdomain of grok.me, and its creator chooses who can open it, according to the company's launch announcement.
No app goes public until its creator clicks Publish. In the paid account the researchers used, the next step offered 3 access settings: "Anyone with the link", "Invited users" and "Only you". "Anyone with the link" was already selected.
The setting matters because an app's address does not stay secret, the researchers say. Opening an app makes the visitor's computer look up its subdomain in DNS. Passive DNS services record such lookups, and anyone with an account can search those records by pattern.
Grok suggests 4 random words as each app's name, and about half of the names the researchers found followed that pattern. Such names are hard to guess, but that does not protect an app whose name already sits in a searchable list.
ChatGPT's app builder also puts each app on its own subdomain. But when the researchers shared an app there, its access was set to "Only me" until they changed it. A ChatGPT app address found in DNS data would lead to an app that only its owner can open, they say.
The researchers found the Grok app names using common subdomain discovery methods and loaded each app's first page once, without signing in.
To see what protection Grok adds on its own, the researchers built 2 test apps with made-up data and published both with the access setting already selected, "Anyone with the link".
The first, a contact list, got a database but no sign-in. Without signing in, the researchers added a row from a private browser window, and the next visitor saw it.
The second, a customer list for a 4-person sales team, got sign-in buttons that Grok added on its own: "Continue with Google" and "Continue with X". But the code Grok wrote added each person who signed in to the team before checking whether they belonged, so the check always passed.
An uninvited Google account belonging to someone other than the owner got in, viewed every customer, edited one record, and deleted another.
The researchers ran these tests only on their own apps. They did not test whether any of the open apps they found would accept such changes.
The researchers reported their findings to SpaceXSI on Sunday through the address in its security.txt file, including 2 of the staff apps. They reported the other 22 on Monday.
By the time the researchers published yesterday, the company had not replied to their report, but it had answered a reporter's questions about the research.
As the researchers describe, the company said Grok apps stay private until their creator shares them. Publishing takes several steps, including choosing between "Only you" and "Anyone with the link," as well as a legal disclaimer. Employee accounts are set to "Only you" by default.
Even so, 24 apps built by staff at the company and at X were open to anyone, the researchers say.
With their report, the researchers had asked the company to make "Only you" the default and to add an option that limits an app to a company's own email domain.
The company's response did not state that it would contact the owners of other open apps, according to the researchers. They have started emailing the affected organizations themselves and had emailed 3 by the time they published. They withheld every app address and title from the report.
On October 18, the same researchers published Muse research showing that pages shared from Meta's Muse AI agent could be found through passive DNS. Meta disabled sharing, then announced a sharing fix on October 22 that gave shared items new addresses.
How to Check Your Organization's Grok Apps
Claroc, which sells tools to find and secure apps built with AI, recommends these checks:
- Find out which AI app builders your staff uses. Builders such as Grok, Lovable, Replit, v0, Bolt, Base44 and Google AI Studio can be used without IT setting them up or a company account.
- If you have access to passive DNS data, look up the builders' domains and open any results in a private browser window.
- Make sure any Grok app with internal data is set to "Invited users" or "Only you", and that a stranger gets an error page.
- Try to sign in with an account from outside your company. If it gets in, the app needs a list of who is allowed.
- Check the scripts each app loads for names, email addresses and passwords, and unpublish apps that have no owner.
In the researchers' tests, setting an app to "Only you" caused it to return a 401 error to a stranger for both the page and its data, and unpublishing took an app offline within seconds.

articles.title: Reddit teste une IA qui résume les avis de ses membres pour vous aider à choisir quoi acheter
articles.text:
Avant d’acheter une machine à expresso, vous tapez peut-être « reddit » à la suite de votre recherche Google, pour lire l’avis de vrais propriétaires. Avec Reddit Reviews, la plateforme confie ce tri à une IA, et rassemble sur une seule page ce que ses communautés racontent de chaque produit.
Reddit a lancé aux États-Unis les tests de Reddit Reviews, son nouveau service d’avis sur les produits. Sur chaque page, Reddit résume par IA les commentaires publiés dans les subreddits, les forums thématiques du site, et vous indique sur une jauge la part des conversations positives, mitigées ou négatives. Sur r/espresso, baristas et amateurs de café comparent leurs machines, et sur r/skincareaddiction, des membres racontent leur expérience avec les soins pour peaux sèches. Selon Reddit, la moitié des consommateurs américains affirment se rendre sur ses forums pour vérifier les conseils d’achat d’une IA, et c’est une IA de Reddit qui leur résume ces discussions.
Reddit résume les avis de ses communautés produit par produit
Pour trouver un avis, il vous suffit de chercher un produit ou une catégorie dans la barre de recherche de l’application, ou de toucher le nom d’un produit mis en évidence dans un commentaire. Pour une machine à expresso, Reddit regroupe les commentaires par thèmes, la facilité de prise en main pour un débutant ou la place que l’appareil occupe sur le plan de travail, avec les points forts et les points faibles signalés par les membres.
Des filtres par thème vous permettent ensuite de parcourir tous les commentaires sur le produit. En touchant l’un d’eux, vous ouvrez la discussion d’origine, où vous pouvez poser une question ou rejoindre la communauté. Sur chaque page d’avis, Reddit met aussi en avant les produits souvent comparés à celui que vous regardez, avec un lien vers sa catégorie complète. Dans cette catégorie, Reddit classe les produits selon les besoins exprimés dans les discussions, les petits prix ou les plus appréciés par exemple.
Reddit ajoute à beaucoup d’avis des images, des prix et des liens d’achat, quand les marques et les revendeurs les fournissent dans leurs catalogues. Si aucun avis n’existe encore pour le produit qui vous intéresse, c’est la recherche par IA de Reddit qui vous répond à partir des conversations des membres. Cet outil, Reddit Answers, est disponible en français.
- Une très grande communauté (à condition de comprendre l'anglais)
- Des tonnes de sujets abordés
Reddit ouvrira Reviews en dehors des États-Unis en 2027
Reddit déploie le service au cours des prochaines semaines aux États-Unis, sur iOS, Android et le Web. Au départ, Reddit propose des avis sur environ 10 000 produits souvent mentionnés sur le site, en électronique, santé et beauté, maison et jardin, mode et vêtements. Alfonso Maruccia, journaliste chez TechSpot, n’a trouvé ces avis générés par IA que sur le design actuel du site, et pas sur l’ancienne interface, old Reddit. Tout au long de 2027, Reddit prévoit d’ajouter des produits et de proposer le service dans d’autres pays.
Les marques ne peuvent pas payer pour apparaître dans ces avis. « Le contenu de Reddit Reviews est déterminé par les communautés Reddit, et non par un placement de produit payant », souligne Reddit, qui compte sur ses modérateurs bénévoles et sur les votes des membres pour écarter le spam.
Reddit lance ce service alors que Steve Huffman, son PDG, a signalé fin octobre une perte moyenne de plus d’un million de visites par semaine en provenance des moteurs de recherche. Il a annoncé dans la foulée une version de Reddit réservée aux membres connectés, testée d’ici à la fin de l’année dans certains pays en dehors des États-Unis, sans préciser lesquels. Comme l’explique Steve Huffman, « la grande majorité des accès non autorisés à Reddit (en gros, le scraping et le vol des données de Reddit) passe par nos expériences hors connexion ». Selon lui, les robots d’IA aspirent ses discussions sans rien rapporter à l’entreprise, alors qu’avec Reviews, c’est Reddit qui les résume, et vous lisez la synthèse sans quitter le site.

articles.title: Bungie Hopes To Grow Marathon With Free-To-Play Week Alongside New PvE Update
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 11th 2026
Bungie Hopes To Grow Marathon With Free-To-Play Week Alongside New PvE Update
It's been known for a while now that Bungie has been toying with the idea of a permanent PvE mode for Marathon, much like Embark has been for Arc Raiders, but it seems as though Bungie is playing things a little more by ear, with the game studio previously announcing that a permanent PvE mode would be coming to Marathon in December. In a recent Marathon developer update, Bungie spilled the beans on what the start of Season 2 will look like and announced that there will be a free week coinciding with the launch of the Symbiosis update. 
The Marathon Open Play Week, as it has been dubbed, will start on December 7 and run until December 15, and Bungie is seemingly hopeful that this will allow players to try the game and potentially turn into long-term Marathon players. December 8 marks the introduction of the new Expedition gameplay mode, which is a PvE-exclusive game mode that allows players to "form a team with your friends and explore Tau Ceti IV with a more collaborative mindset."In addition to the new Expedition mode, the Symbiosis update introduces a new speed-and-stealth-oriented Bishop shell, sweeping changes to the Perimeter map, and a new Crew Up even that will reward players with new cosmetics, including:
- Queen's Nest emblem
- Queen's Dominion Background
- Queen's Maw weapon sticker
- Cluster Bunch weapon charm
- Arata Vectus Destroyer skin
- Exterminator title
The Crew Up event will run until December 22, and it will be open to any players who have completed the tutorial, including those simply participating in the Open Play Week, although once the free week ends, free players will no longer be able to access the event unless they buy the game.
Bungie has more or less admitted that Marathon's launch was softer than Bungie and PlayStation had hoped it would be, and Bungie has been working hard to try to grow the player base and improve player retention, with testing for the much-requested PvE game mode beginning in July 2026 and getting extended, seemingly by popular demand.

articles.title: Cómo compartir internet desde un celular Android o iPhone
articles.text:
Compartir internet desde un celular puede ser útil cuando un amigo se quedó sin datos móviles y necesita resolver una situación prioritaria, como solicitar transporte a través de una aplicación, comunicarse con alguien o consultar una dirección.
La función convierte al teléfono en un punto de acceso Wi‑Fi para que otro celular, tableta o computadora se conecte mediante los datos móviles del equipo que comparte la conexión. Tanto Android como iPhone permiten hacerlo desde sus ajustes de red.
Antes de activar esta opción, conviene revisar el plan de telefonía: algunos operadores pueden limitar el uso del punto de acceso o cobrar un cargo adicional. Además, compartir datos puede aumentar el consumo de batería y agotar más rápido el paquete de internet móvil.
Cómo compartir internet desde un celular Android o iPhone
En Android, se debe deslizar el dedo desde la parte superior de la pantalla y buscar la opción “Hotspot de Wi‑Fi” o “Punto de acceso”.
Si no aparece entre los accesos rápidos, puede agregarse desde el botón de edición. Al mantener presionada la opción, es posible activar el hotspot, modificar el nombre de la red y establecer una contraseña.
La otra persona debe abrir la lista de redes Wi‑Fi de su dispositivo, seleccionar el nombre del teléfono que comparte internet e ingresar la clave. Android permite compartir la conexión por Bluetooth o mediante un cable USB.
Según la guía de Android, un hotspot Wi‑Fi puede conectar hasta 10 dispositivos al mismo tiempo, aunque el rendimiento dependerá de la señal y del plan de datos.
En iPhone, la opción se encuentra en Ajustes, dentro de “Datos celulares” y “Configurar punto de acceso personal”, o directamente en “Punto de acceso personal”, según la versión del sistema.
Desde allí se puede habilitar la función y cambiar la contraseña de Wi‑Fi. El otro dispositivo deberá buscar el nombre del iPhone entre las redes disponibles e ingresar esa clave para conectarse.
iPhone permite compartir la conexión mediante Bluetooth o cable USB. Para utilizar el punto de acceso, ambos dispositivos deben tener activados Wi‑Fi y Bluetooth y mantenerse cerca uno del otro.
Apple indica que el punto de acceso personal utiliza los datos celulares del iPhone, no una red Wi‑Fi a la que el teléfono esté conectado.
Consejos para compartir internet desde un celular Android o iPhone de forma segura
Es recomendable compartir internet solo con dispositivos de personas de confianza y cuya seguridad se conozca.
Conectar equipos desconocidos o que podrían tener programas maliciosos instalados implica un riesgo para la privacidad y puede provocar un consumo inesperado de datos.
La red debe tener una contraseña distinta de la que se utiliza en otras cuentas o servicios. Conviene evitar configurarla como una red abierta: Android permite quitar la contraseña, pero esa opción facilita que otras personas cercanas se conecten sin autorización.
Al terminar, se debe desactivar el punto de acceso para evitar que otros dispositivos vuelvan a conectarse automáticamente y para reducir el consumo de batería y datos móviles.
En Android, además, puede activarse una opción para que el hotspot se apague cuando no haya equipos conectados.
Google llevó Gemini Intelligence a los Pixel 10
Google lanzó una actualización para los Pixel que incorpora Gemini Intelligence en los Pixel 10, 10 Pro, 10 Pro XL y 10 Pro Fold.
El paquete de inteligencia artificial incluye Rambler, una herramienta que transforma dictados en textos ordenados y elimina muletillas, y Create My Widget, que permite crear widgets mediante instrucciones escritas.
La función puede utilizar información de Gmail, Calendar y el buscador; llegará también a los Pixel 11, pero no al Pixel 10a. La actualización amplía las acciones de Gemini en aplicaciones, como pedir comida, solicitar transporte o buscar restaurantes, y extiende esa capacidad al Reino Unido, India y Japón.
Además, los Pixel 10 reciben sugerencias proactivas y resúmenes de conversaciones en seis idiomas, incluido español.
Google anticipó nuevas herramientas para Android Auto, mientras que los Pixel desde el 6a suman 10 estilos adicionales de íconos personalizados. La disponibilidad de estas novedades dependerá del modelo, país, idioma y distribución gradual.

Officially, the Dyson Black Friday 2026 sale in Australia started on November 10, but there is a possibility that the prices might drop further between November 27 and November 30, which is the actual Cyber Weekend sale period.
Should I buy directly from Dyson during Black Friday?
You most certainly can buy directly from Dyson during Black Friday, especially since there are exclusive models of vacuums, purifiers and hair styling tools that you won't get anywhere else.
However, if you aren't too fussed about Dyson exclusives, you could likely find a slightly better price at an authorised retailer. The difference between what you'd get as a Dyson exclusive and what's available from authorised stockists is essentially a different colour scheme and less attachments that's included with a specific vacuum cleaner.
What is the best time to buy a Dyson?
When it comes to getting your hands on a Dyson product – whether it be for the home or your glorious tresses – the best time to pick them up is when there's a steep discount.
And the best discounts on pretty much anything is during Black Friday. Last year saw some topnotch offers directly from Dyson, with some bonuses thrown in, but don't ignore the discounts on eBay. Chances are you'll be able to save a little more with a coupon code – with the potential for even better discounts for Plus members – and still shop directly from Dyson's official eBay store.
Then there's Amazon. During major sales, Amazon has had some of the best prices on select Dyson products. And if the identical model is listed at The Good Guys, the retailer will price beat. So definitely shop around.
Dyson Black Friday 2026 deals: predictions
It's very tempting to say that you'll find offers on every single Dyson product in the brand's repertoire for Black Friday, but that would be wishful thinking.
However, considering the latest Dyson vacuum cleaners like the V10 Konical and the V16 Piston Animal are already seeing discounts, don't be surprised if you find them for cheaper.
Also keep an eye on the prices of the older models, starting with the V15 Detect and the Gen5Detect. They're surely going to see big discounts, while you could pick up an older V10 or V8 for cheap.
There was a time when it was pretty rare to see Dyson's haircare products get steep discounts, but we have been seeing upwards of AU$250 in savings on some of these coveted tools. As for the purifier fans, you'll be able to save hundreds even when shopping directly from Dyson.

articles.title: We Built An Agent That Broke All of Our Security Rules. Here's What We Learned.
articles.text:
We tell customers three things about securing AI agents: they need their own identities, access that fits the job they’re given, and traceability that’s separate from any human’s. That was true for us at Token as well. Then, we built an agent that broke all three by default.
This helped us think through how such agents should be defended. When a browser agent acts inside a user’s authenticated session, the application may see the user but not the agent, the delegation, or the task’s intended scope. By creating an agent that breaks all the security rules, Token learned how companies should be using identity to gain control, especially as agent use scales. Standards are coming, but there are steps security teams can take today.
The agent we would have flagged
The agent we created is named Rehearsal. Its job is to answer questions inside the Token platform by doing rather than telling. It autonomously opens pages in the browser tab, sets filters, and fills in forms.
From a security perspective, it’s a typical UI agent that runs in the user’s browser. That’s what makes it useful. But it also means the agent runs within the user’s session and has their reach.
Moreover, to the server behind the page, the agent’s clicks are inherently indistinguishable from the user’s, because nothing in a session cookie points to who the session driver is.
What controlling both sides made possible
Because Token owns both the agent and the app it runs, we can close each gap from the inside. For example, Token knows who’s driving the session because Rehearsal tells it who is.
We learned that there are multiple best practices that you can apply when you control the AI agent itself:
- While the agent moves, dim and lock the application and clearly indicate who has control.
- Record every move for each session, including those that were blocked.
- Reduce the agent’s reach below the user’s. For Rehearsal, we ensure the dashboards are read-only. It can’t save anything without the user’s approval, doesn’t fill in secret fields, and never sends a call that the platform has refused. It also understands the dashboard controls through the page’s accessibility labels.
This works for our own agent, but only because it relies on access that no outside agent has.
Who has to fix it for everyone else?
We could give Rehearsal an actor, a scope, and a page map because we're the ones who wrote it. A browser agent driving your CRM or your cloud console has none of that. The app can't tell that it’s there, and the agent can't tell which field holds a secret or which button deletes a record. The session itself carries the user's identity.
The way out is to give agents their own lanes, separate from human users'. The web has started building them, but it isn't necessarily focused on holistic approaches.
The browser can mark when its agent is driving and restrict itself accordingly. Chrome auto-browse, for example, already requires a person’s approval before high-stakes actions such as payments or mass emails, limits its agent to the sites the task requires, and tags the pages the agent visits in the user’s history. Microsoft lets admins turn agentic browsing on per site and pause it before passwords and card numbers are entered.
The app can publish its actions as tools. WebMCP, a draft that Google and Microsoft are writing in a W3C community group, lets a site expose actions that an agent can call directly and flag each one as read-only or consequential. That way, the agent doesn't need to guess what a button does.
The agent can sign its requests. Web Bot Auth, now an IETF working group draft, lets a site verify which agent sent a request.
What’s missing is a layer that connects them. Each lane knows something the others don’t, and none of them passes it on. The browser knows its agent is driving, but neither Chrome nor Edge describes how to tell the app on the other end. A WebMCP tool runs inside the user’s session, with the user’s rights, so it doesn’t, by itself, narrow what the agent can reach. Web Bot Auth names the agent, but the draft makes it plain that it doesn’t cover delegation, so it omits the person the agent works for.
The app ends up holding on to pieces of context rather than delivering something actionable.
Now consider that the agents are arriving faster than the standards. Agent-friendly isn’t enough on its own. Every lane built for agents should carry the agent’s identity, a verifiable link to the person it acts for, and a scope narrower than that person’s. Together, those three signals give an application the minimum context it needs to make an authorization decision. Otherwise, a faster lane is just a faster path to the misuse of privilege.
What security teams can do before standards catch up
Waiting for standardization is not an option. You need to start discovering agentic browsers and extensions as soon as possible, including the users whose sessions they borrow. And while you can’t tell who clicked, you can choose which clicks need a person by adding a step-up check such as a passkey prompt.
- Inventory browser agents, agentic extensions, and endpoint agents that can act through authenticated sessions and map them to users and owners.
- Trace every AI agent consumer, so you know which people (and other agents) are using each individual agent
- Review every identity that each individual agent has access to
- Identify potential attack paths that use agents to bypass access controls
- Require explicit approval or step-up authentication before sensitive or irreversible application actions.
- Ask critical SaaS vendors whether their audit records distinguish agent activity from human activity and whether they support task-scoped delegation.
Until browsers and applications can carry agent identity, human delegation, and task scope together, companies should treat every agent using a human session as delegated access that must be discovered, constrained, and audited.

articles.title: Tesla obtient un feu vert temporaire en Finlande pour son système de conduite assistée
articles.text:
Tesla vendra bientôt en Finlande son système Tesla Assisted Driving, le nouveau nom européen du FSD, aux propriétaires d’environ 6 500 voitures compatibles. Avec ce feu vert, onze pays de l’Union l’autorisent, mais ils ne réunissent qu’un peu plus de 15 % de la population européenne.
Traficom, l’agence finlandaise des transports et des communications, a reconnu l’homologation provisoire accordée en avril par la RDW, son homologue néerlandaise. Malgré son ancien nom, le FSD (Full Self-Driving) ne rend pas votre Tesla autonome. C'est toujours la voiture qui décide d'accélérer, freiner et tourner, mais c'est encore au conducteur de surveiller la route en permanence et de reprendre le volant à tout moment. Dans l’Union européenne, chaque pays décide de reconnaître ou non la décision néerlandaise sur ses routes. La France, deuxième pays le plus peuplé de l’UE, ne l’a toujours pas fait.
Tesla a bridé le dépassement de la vitesse autorisée
Traficom étudiait le dossier depuis juin et a choisi de ne pas attendre le vote européen pour deux raisons. Tesla a d’abord renommé son système et resserré ses réglages de vitesse, des réglages que la RDW a validés début novembre. Vous pouviez programmer votre Tesla pour dépasser jusqu’à 50 % la limite autorisée. L’écart maximal passe à 10 %, avec un retour à zéro à chaque démarrage. Tesla avait promis ce plafond à l’Allemagne en octobre, avec un changement de nom réclamé par Berlin. En échange, le gouvernement allemand a promis de défendre l’homologation dans toute l’Union. « Le changement de nom aide les utilisateurs et le marché à comprendre la vraie nature du système », précise Jukka Juhola, expert principal chez Traficom.
L’agence a aussi voulu laisser aux propriétaires le temps de prendre en main le système avant les plus grands froids. Si de la neige, de la neige fondue ou de la saleté recouvre les caméras, le système peut subir diverses limitations, prévient Traficom. L’agence conseille de garder les mains sur le volant devant une flaque de profondeur inconnue, une plaque de verglas ou un fort vent latéral. La responsabilité de la conduite vous revient tout entière. Comme l’explique Jukka Juhola, « c’est toujours le conducteur qui reçoit l’amende pour excès de vitesse ». Tesla Europe a annoncé sur X un déploiement prochain en Finlande.
La France n’a toujours pas reconnu l’homologation néerlandaise
Le plafond de 10 % répond au reproche de Philippe Tabarot. En juillet, le ministre des Transports avait refusé d’autoriser le FSD en France, parce que la voiture pouvait dépasser jusqu’à 50 % la limite de vitesse quand le trafic roulait plus vite. Il reprochait aussi à Tesla de ne pas garantir une vigilance suffisante du conducteur lors des changements de voie, aux intersections et dans les ronds-points. En septembre, après une visioconférence avec Elon Musk, il a autorisé des essais sur route avec deux voitures fournies par Tesla, sans dire ce que la France voterait à Bruxelles.
Les représentants des Vingt-Sept voteront au comité technique des véhicules à moteur (TCMV). Ce vote était attendu le 6 octobre, mais le comité n’a consacré qu’une discussion de 25 minutes au dossier et ne se réunira pas avant décembre. Pour l’emporter, Tesla a besoin d’au moins 15 États représentant 65 % de la population de l’Union. Les onze pays favorables comptent environ 70 millions d’habitants sur 450 millions, d’après les chiffres d’Eurostat. La France, l’Allemagne, l’Italie et l’Espagne réunissent à elles seules environ 58 % des Européens, selon Reuters. Si Berlin tient sa promesse, les pays favorables pèseront environ un tiers de la population, encore loin du seuil.
Traficom précise que sa décision n’engage pas le vote finlandais. L’agence annonce aussi d’autres modifications de Tesla avant le vote européen, pour aider le conducteur à garder son attention sur la route.

articles.title: EU Draft "Digital Fairness Act" Details New Restrictions on Loot Boxes and "Addictive Design"
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 11th 2026
EU Draft "Digital Fairness Act" Details New Restrictions on Loot Boxes and "Addictive Design"
When Stop Killing Games's Ross Scott previously spoke about the initiative, he mentioned that the upcoming Digital Fairness Act was considering addressing game licensing but ultimately passing up the opportunity. Now, the European Commission has officially published a draft of the Digital Fairness Act, allowing us to see what the proposed legislation is targets and how that might affect video games and their makers. The draft act aims to "tackle unfair commercial practices affecting consumers online, while simplifying and harmonizing parts of the existing legal framework," and it will affect everything from dark patterns and subscription services to loot boxes, in-game purchases, digital contracts, and even influencer marketing. 
What will be most pertinent to gamers and gaming companies is that gaming companies will be forced to be more transparent about in-game spending. This means they will need to show the real-world monetary value of virtual items purchased with in-game currency; loot boxes and other paid variable rewards systems will need to have rewards clearly shown as well as the probability of obtaining those rewards, and these systems will be unavailable for minors; and pay-to-win mechanics will be prohibited for minors under certain conditions. Platform designers, like social media companies, will also need to abide by new rules relating to what the Commission is calling "addictive design and attention-maximizing features."If the Digital Fairness Act passes, social media platforms will need to provide reasonable tools to disable:
- Autoplay and infinite scrolling features
- Notifications unrelated to the user's own activity or content
- Streaks, rewards, or penalties that pressure users into returning to the platform
- Automated features that "simulate interpersonal relationships" and effectively manipulate users into spending more time on the platform
The Digital Fairness Act also seeks to regulate influencer and social media marketing, calling for clearer disclosure of sponsored or commercial content or collaboration, banning promotions disguised as independent recommendations, restricting marketing to minors and their parents, and putting the onus on brands to enforce disclosure when it comes to commercial collaborations, instead of leaving it to the influencer alone. The full draft act is available here, and the EU has published a guide about the new act here.

articles.title: Con AO3 caído, lectores copian historias de fanfiction a Google Drive y varios autores protestan
articles.text:
Archive of Our Own (AO3) cumple dos semanas fuera de línea y sus lectores empezaron a compartir copias de las historias en carpetas de Google Drive. Varios autores rechazan esas copias porque no las autorizaron, según informó Wired.
AO3 dejó de funcionar el 29 de octubre. Primero avisó de un mantenimiento de al menos 12 horas, pero ese mismo día elevó la estimación a entre dos y cuatro semanas. El 30 de octubre, la organización que lo administra, Organization for Transformative Works (OTW), explicó que había detectado un incidente de seguridad.
El archivo aloja 18,8 millones de obras en 83.000 comunidades de seguidores, según The New York Times, y reúne a unos 12 millones de usuarios. Allí se publican relatos escritos por aficionados sobre personajes de Harry Potter, Crepúsculo o Heated Rivalry, entre muchos otros universos.
La OTW no tiene empleados: lo sostienen alrededor de 1.000 voluntarios, según contó a Today la cofundadora Rebecca Tushnet. Ella calificó la caída como la mayor desde que el sitio abrió al público, en noviembre de 2009.
Qué dijo la organización sobre el incidente
La OTW informó el 30 de octubre que ninguna obra, marcador ni kudos (reconocimiento de los lectores) se borró. Aclaró que no cree que se haya robado la base de usuarios, aunque no puede descartarlo. Esa base contiene nombres de usuario, correos, direcciones IP y contraseñas cifradas. AO3 no pide nombres reales.
La organización recomendó cambiar la contraseña en otros sitios donde se use la misma que en AO3. También advirtió sobre estafas que piden dinero para “traer de vuelta” el archivo y negó que existan espejos o aplicaciones oficiales para entrar a sus servidores.
El 6 de noviembre publicó su primera novedad: el trabajo para restablecer el sitio avanza bien y la estimación original sigue vigente. También dijo que busca que los borradores guardados no se pierdan. No dio la causa del ataque ni nombró a responsables.
Lectores y autores chocan por las copias
Mientras tanto, los lectores armaron bibliotecas de emergencia. AO3 permite descargar cada historia en formatos como PDF o ePub, y muchos conservaban copias propias. Según NBC News, los moderadores de la comunidad de AO3 en Reddit abrieron hilos para intercambiarlas, y algunos autores subieron capítulos nuevos a Tumblr.
Berklie Novak-Stolz, una lectora de Alabama con más de 300.000 seguidores en TikTok, creó una carpeta pública de Google Drive para reunir esas descargas. “Sería como si Netflix o HBO Max dejaran de funcionar entre dos y cuatro semanas”, comparó otro usuario, Brandon Frye, de Ohio, en declaraciones a Today.
Para otros, el problema es el permiso. Una autora que pidió ser identificada como Avery, que escribe sobre Heated Rivalry desde hace unos seis años, encontró sus relatos en los sitios espejo Squidgeworld y AO3.Life, donde nunca los había publicado. Pidió que los retiraran y lo logró, pero dijo que no sabe si halló todas las copias.
El presidente de Squidge.org, Walter Hopgood, dijo a Wired que su sitio elimina los textos publicados sin autorización de su autor. AO3.Life ya fue dado de baja. Avery teme además que alguien inserte malware (programas dañinos) en una carpeta compartida.
El 2 de noviembre, Riley, una autora con más de 90.000 seguidores en X e Instagram, compartió un documento con un catálogo de esas carpetas. Algunos autores lo consideraron una violación de la privacidad. La cofundadora Tushnet reconoció que hay autores que “solo quieren saber dónde están sus cosas”, algo que calificó de razonable.
La plataforma de escritura Ellipsus registró un aumento de más de 500% en registros desde la caída, según informó a Wired. La OTW mantiene su estimación original de entre dos y cuatro semanas desde el 29 de octubre y publicará novedades en su página de estado.

articles.title: 'Teams are moving to new models almost as fast as labs release them': Vercel data reveals AI models now have a half-life of just six weeks — with most most AI traffic running on models less than two months old
articles.text:
'Teams are moving to new models almost as fast as labs release them': Vercel data reveals AI models now have a half-life of just six weeks — with most most AI traffic running on models less than two months old
AI now has a half-life
- Vercel finds a typical AI model peaks within four weeks of its launch
- Anthropic is outperforming OpenAI in attracting new teams of users
- Users are keen to stay ahead of the curve, with no show of loyalty
The time spent with a new AI model is decreasing, with teams using paid AI services sticking with a new model for an average of four weeks. At that point, they switch to another new model, aiming to keep their AI code development or agents competitive.
Vercel’s AI Gateway Production Index report for November 2026 claims this trend indicates that AI models effectively have a half-life of around six weeks. At that point, attention and use of the model decreases as teams and developers proceed to switch to the latest shiny alternative.
Illustrating the trend, Vercel reports that Anthropic Claude Opus 5.5 was the top model by spend in its first full month, following its launch on September 22, 2026.
The AI half-life
While the concept of an AI model having a half-life may initially seem outlandish, it actually makes perfect sense.
Vercel’s analysis of token transactions via its gateway shows that teams adopt new models within days of them being launched. Assuming the use of a code editor or tool wrapper, pointing a development environment to a new model can be achieved relatively painlessly.
Vercel’s data breaks down the adoption rate into 00-14 days, 15-30 days, and 31-60 days, and highlights a trend towards increased early adoption from June 2026 onward. By September, almost 17% were using models that had been available for under two weeks.
But older models are retained to some degree, but these are typically relying on less usage and, consequently, token spend.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
So, with new models being released relatively regularly by competing AI platforms, and with easy model switching essentially baked into developers environments, they’re being used with an initial intensity that wanes when the next model launches. Hence Vercel’s determination that models “have a half-life of about six weeks.”
Video models
Vercel also determined that the top model by spend in its first full month in October was Anthropic Claude Opus 5.5, drawing just over 14% in spend.
Meanwhile, the most widely used paid models are dominated by Anthropic. Sonnet 5.5 (26%), Haiku 5.5 (22%), Haiku 4.5 (20%), and Opus 5.5 (18%) are the most widely-used, although there is duplication, with many team apparently relying on multiple models.
Significantly, image and video generation was also prominent, with more spend and adoption than in previous months. One in six AI development teams are now using a video model, up from 10% in previous months. This is where OpenAI had a rare chance to shine in Vercel's report, with its GPT-Image-2.5 Sunburst leading in image generation model spend during October.

Christian Cawley has extensive experience as a writer and editor in consumer electronics, IT and entertainment media. He has contributed to TechRadar since 2017 and has been published in Computer Weekly, Linux Format, ComputerActive, and other publications.
He currently heads up the team at smart home website Matter Alpha, and writes about retro gaming at Gaming Retro.

articles.title: eMudhra Revokes 8 More CAs It Previously Declared Unaffected by Key Compromise
articles.text:
The in-house Python script behind eMudhra's October key compromise has now cost the company 8 more of its intermediate certificate authorities (CAs), even though it did not weaken their keys.
Each intermediate CA has its own private key, which the company uses to sign the certificates it issues. The 8 intermediate CAs compromised in October had a different problem: a single line in the script cut each of their keys to one byte, the company said this week.
The script also retrieved the RSA keys of the 8 newly revoked CAs from the company's hardware security modules (HSMs). The company says it cannot show that the keys were handled as required by its own rules. It revoked the CAs late last week.
The company had called those CAs unaffected. "The RSA issuers went through a different path as per our assessment of the code and are therefore not impacted," it wrote on Mozilla's bug tracker on October 19.
Of the 8, 6 were for website (TLS) certificates and 2 for code signing. The company had put 4 of them into production in May. Its list names 195 certificates from them, 29 for its own domains.
Both problems began at a key ceremony on April 30, 2025, according to the full incident report the company posted to the same bug tracker this week. That day it generated 16 CA keys on Utimaco HSMs, including the 8 behind the October key compromise.
The keys were meant for Crypto4A HSMs at the company's US and EU sites. Moving keys between HSMs from different vendors is limited, the company says, so its PKI operations team wrote the Python script to wrap each key for transport and unwrap it again.
The round trip that day was a practice run of the transfer, and the source HSM's FIPS-approved mode was switched off for it as an approved exception.
After the round trip, the script read each private key out of the HSM into the ceremony computer's memory and rebuilt the key from that copy. For the 8 ECDSA keys, "a single line in that read‑back truncated the private value to its leading byte," the report says.
The rebuilt key carried a label almost identical to the original's, which allowed the weak copy to be sent for signing and certification.
The Hacker News worked out all 8 keys from their public certificates. The smallest, for EM OV TLS CA - G3C, is 4, and the largest is 237.
Nothing in the ceremony tested the key's strength or checked the certified key against the first generated key. The weak keys still produced valid signatures, and their certificates passed linting and 2 WebTrust audit cycles unnoticed.
The HSMs worked correctly throughout, according to the company, which puts the fault in its own script and process controls.
Invalid CRL signatures in June 2025 were an early sign of the same fault, according to the report. The company fixed them at the time by re-signing the lists with the keys that matched the certificates, which were the weak ones.
According to the report, the 8 RSA keys went through the same read-back step that the company's earlier response had ruled out. Early last week, the company said its earlier answers reflected only what its teams had gathered so far, including which script paths each set of keys took.
The script did not shorten those keys, and every signature still checks against the certified key. But their private parts, such as the private exponent and one of the primes, sat in the memory of a Python process on the ceremony computer.
As a result, the company "cannot positively demonstrate that this key material was in compliance with CPS §6.2.6," its own rule on moving keys into and out of an HSM. Logs and files from that computer cannot reliably show how the material was handled.
The company reached that view in early November, after discussions with browser root programs. The 8 RSA CAs were revoked late last week with the reason code cessationOfOperation, not the CA-compromise code used when the first 8 were revoked on October 18.
Participants in the bug thread have asked why the company chose that code rather than keyCompromise.
Of the 195 certificates in the company's certificate list, 130 came from EM DV TLS CA - G2C, 63 from EM OV TLS CA - G2C, and 2 from the code-signing CA, EM OV CS CA - G2C.
Besides the company's own domains, the certificates name several universities and colleges, a county, and other organizations. The newest was issued last week, days before the CAs were revoked. All their holders have been moved to new certificates, the company says.
The company says the wrap-and-unwrap process was used only this once, and that its other key ceremonies all created keys in place.
Participants in the bug thread also want the script published, and some have asked how private keys could leave its HSMs at all.
KPMG, which the company hired as an independent reviewer, is due to finish by December 4. The company's inventory of all its CA keys is due November 30.
The company knows of no case of misuse. Anyone holding one of the October keys could have impersonated any website, according to a disclosure site run by Dennis Jackson, who investigated the keys for Mozilla.
Browsers that enforce Certificate Transparency could not have been fooled. Whether anyone used the keys against software that skips that check is not known.
What emSign Certificate Holders Need to Check
eMudhra, which sells certificates under the emSign brand, is exiting the publicly trusted TLS business following its October 22 announcement.
Holders can find affected certificates in the company's list or by searching Certificate Transparency logs for the revoked G2C TLS issuers.
All issuance from the company's G1 hierarchy is due to stop before November 16, as the remaining customers, mainly a university federation in North America, move to another provider.
Microsoft will start removing the 10 remaining eMudhra roots, including emSign Root CA - G1, on November 16, according to an update to its security response post earlier this week. Certificates that chain to those roots will then lose default trust in Windows and Edge, and in some of its other products on their own timelines.
According to the Indian company's phase-out schedule, Chrome and Firefox will not trust G1 certificates issued after November 16, and Apple will end trust in all G1 certificates, including older ones, on November 30.
macOS 27.2.1, 26.7.3 and 15.8.3 stop bundled command-line tools such as curl and git from accepting the compromised TLS CA certificates, Apple said in a support note earlier this week. They also drop 5 roots, including emSign Root CA - G1, from /etc/ssl/cert.pem, so tools relying on that file may not verify some sites chaining to them.

articles.title: Nvidia préparerait le départ de Jensen Huang, son PDG historique
articles.text:
Dimanche, le conseil d’administration de Nvidia assurait avoir confiance en Jensen Huang. Trois jours plus tard, selon le Wall Street Journal, il se prépare à écarter le cofondateur qui dirige le géant des puces d’IA depuis 1993, après la révélation d’une liaison avec une dirigeante placée sous ses ordres.
Dans un message à ses salariés, Jensen Huang avait avoué dimanche son infidélité, sans nommer Alice Huang, une femme d’affaires que le renseignement américain soupçonne d’espionner pour Pékin. Le conseil d’administration avait aussitôt ouvert une enquête indépendante. Mercredi, le New York Times a rapporté une seconde relation, avec Kimberly Powell, vice-présidente chargée de la santé chez Nvidia, sur la foi de cinq anciens salariés. Peu après, le Wall Street Journal a révélé que les administrateurs se préparaient à pousser le patron de Nvidia vers la sortie. Les statuts de l’entreprise autorisent une majorité simple du conseil à le démettre « avec ou sans motif », et Jensen Huang ne détient qu’environ 3,6 % du capital.
Nvidia n’a désigné aucun successeur à Jensen Huang
D’après une source de Reuters, les administrateurs se sont réunis mercredi soir pour décider de son avenir. À 6 heures, heure de Paris, Nvidia n’avait rien annoncé. Selon Bloomberg, le conseil travaille avec un cabinet extérieur chargé de lui trouver des candidats, et il pourrait nommer un patron intérimaire.
Jensen Huang dirige Nvidia depuis sa création et il n’a jamais désigné de successeur. Une soixantaine de cadres lui rendent compte directement, et aucun d’eux ne fait figure de numéro deux. « Une éviction immédiate de Jensen Huang pourrait poser problème à Nvidia, puisque l’entreprise n’a pas de plan de succession », précise Gil Luria, analyste chez D.A. Davidson, interrogé par Reuters.
Selon l’agence, de nombreux analystes et investisseurs voient deux candidats probables, au moins pour une période transitoire. Ian Buck a créé CUDA, la plateforme logicielle avec laquelle les développeurs programment les puces de Nvidia, et il dirige l’activité consacrée aux clients des centres de données. Colette Kress, la directrice financière, commente chaque trimestre les résultats aux côtés de Jensen Huang. Un autre analyste cite aussi Rene Haas, patron du concepteur de puces Arm, qui a travaillé sept ans chez Nvidia.
Rappelons qu'en 2018, ce scnéario s'est déroulé chez Intel. Son patron, Brian Krzanich, avait démissionné après la découverte d’une relation avec une salariée, et faute de successeur prêt, le groupe avait confié l’intérim à son directeur financier, Bob Swan, pendant sept mois.
Les investisseurs chiffrent le départ de Jensen Huang
Le titre Nvidia a reculé jusqu’à 9 % dans les échanges après la clôture de Wall Street, mercredi. Si ce recul se confirme jeudi, Nvidia aura perdu environ 600 milliards de dollars de valeur boursière depuis l’annonce de l’enquête, selon les calculs de Reuters. Dan Ives, analyste chez Yorkville Ives, estime que l’entreprise vaudrait 25 à 30 % de moins sans son fondateur.
Comme l’explique Armina Rosenberg, gérante chez Minotaur Capital, qui détient des actions Nvidia, « le marché commence à intégrer un Nvidia sans son fondateur comme l’issue probable, et plus comme un risque improbable ».
Le sort de Jensen Huang concerne toute la filière de l’IA. Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Meta et OpenAI utilisent les puces de Nvidia, et son patron tranche en personne la plupart des grandes décisions de l’entreprise. Il plaide aussi depuis des années pour vendre ses puces en Chine, et l’affaire Alice Huang a relancé les questions sur l’origine de ces positions.
Si vous détenez des actions Nvidia, directement ou par un fonds indiciel, le prochain rendez-vous est le 17 novembre, date de publication des résultats trimestriels. Le lendemain, les présidents républicains de trois commissions de la Chambre des représentants veulent interroger le patron de Nvidia à huis clos sur ses échanges avec Megaspeed, la société singapourienne où travaillait Alice Huang. Nvidia n’a pas répondu aux questions de Reuters sur la réunion de son conseil.
Joint par le New York Times au sujet de Kimberly Powell, Jensen Huang a seulement répondu « Je ne pense pas que vous devriez vous adresser directement à moi ».

articles.title: Thieaudio Introduces the Clairvoyance MKII
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 11th 2026
Thieaudio Introduces the Clairvoyance MKII
The original Clairvoyance was a groundbreaking tribrid IEM that helped shape the industry and establish Thieaudio's presence in the global audiophile market. Beyond pioneering the tribrid configuration, it introduced a distinctive tuning signature that would go on to influence the industry. After six years of innovation and refinement, Thieaudio proudly presents its modern successor: the Clairvoyance MKII.
An All-New 2DD + 5BA + 2EST Tribrid Configuration
The Clairvoyance MKII features a completely modernized driver platform, combining the latest-generation IMPACT² dual 8 mm isobaric subwoofer system with five balanced armature drivers and dual Sonion electrostatic tweeters. The IMPACT² system delivers tight, impactful sub-bass, while four Knowles BA drivers maximize midrange resolution and preserve the natural timbre of vocals and instruments. A dedicated latest-generation Knowles mid-treble driver enhances vocal presence and imaging, while the dual Sonion EST ultra-tweeters extend the highest frequencies for an airy, lifelike presentation.A Modern Tonal Balance
Building on the original Clairvoyance signature, the MKII introduces a more contemporary tuning approach. Its carefully shaped 9dB sub-bass shelf delivers powerful kick drums and robust bass guitar notes. Across 200 Hz-1 kHz, a natural midrange with a precise ∆2dB slope adds warmth and depth while maintaining clarity and separation. A precisely positioned 3 kHz treble peak follows the natural acoustic transfer function of the human pinna. Smooth treble decay and extension up to 40 kHz bring added air and sparkle without compromising the overall tonal balance.
An IEM for Pure Musical Enjoyment
While the Monarch was developed as a highly technical studio monitor for engineers and musicians, the original Clairvoyance offered a more musical presentation for audiophiles. The Clairvoyance MKII continues this tradition. Its tuning is fun and engaging without overly coloring the sound, while its refined technical performance reveals the details and nuances within every track. It is designed to let listeners experience their music to its fullest potential.
Excellence in Engineering and Craftsmanship
Developed through over a year of research and refinement, the Clairvoyance MKII underwent countless tuning revisions and driver adjustments to achieve its final acoustic presentation. A comprehensive 4-way crossover, featuring 13 passive components and 4 sound tubes, ensures precise driver integration.
Its unibody 316 stainless steel shell is CNC-machined from solid blocks and hand-polished to a premium satin finish, offering a refined appearance and exceptional durability.
Two Distinct Faceplate Options
The Clairvoyance MKII is available with two faceplate designs. The Guilloché edition features intricate, diamond-like patterns precision-cut into mirror-polished stainless steel through a meticulous multi-step process. For a more understated aesthetic, the Studio edition features solid satin-finished stainless steel with beveled edges, delivering a clean and professional appearance.
Custom Modular Cable
The Clairvoyance MKII comes with a custom ultra-pure 6N OCC silver-and-copper mixed Litz cable. Featuring 0.78 mm 2-pin connectors and Thieaudio's modular plug system, it supports both 3.5 mm unbalanced and 4.4 mm balanced connections.
Thieaudio Clairvoyance MKII
Specs:
- Frequency Allocation: 2 Ultra-High | 1 High | 4 Mid | 2 Low
- Driver Configuration: 2EST + 5BA + 2DD
- Crossover: 4-Way, 4 Sound Bores
- Sensitivity: 102dB @ 1 kHz (±1dB)
- Impedance: 8 Ω @ 1 kHz (±1 Ω)
- Frequency Response: 20 Hz - 40 kHz
Cable Specs:
- Conductor Material: 6N Silver-Plated Single-Crystal copper + Alloy copper

- Cable Diameter: 2.8 mm
- Outer Jacket Material: PVC (Polyvinyl Chloride)
- Cable Construction: Coaxial Litz Wire Structure
- Wire Gauge: 20 AWG (American Wire Gauge)

articles.title: Muse de Meta llega a los smartwatches y permite gestionar tareas mediante servicios conectados
articles.text:
Meta amplía el alcance de su agente de inteligencia artificial y ya permite controlar Muse desde relojes inteligentes. La función, que hasta ahora estaba limitada a móviles y ordenadores, llega ahora al Apple Watch y a los dispositivos con Wear OS, según recoge TechCrunch.
Desde la muñeca, los usuarios pueden pedirle al asistente que haga una reserva, gestione una cita o compre un producto sin necesidad de sacar el teléfono del bolsillo.
El movimiento se produce apenas dos meses después de la presentación de Muse, un agente que se diferencia de herramientas como ChatGPT o Siri porque no se limita a responder preguntas. Su funcionamiento se basa en utilizar aplicaciones y servicios externos para completar tareas concretas, siempre que el usuario autorice las operaciones que lo requieran.
Cómo funciona Muse en el Apple Watch y los relojes con Wear OS
En el caso del Apple Watch, Muse llega a través de una actualización de la aplicación para iPhone, que incorpora además la posibilidad de añadir un acceso directo en la esfera del reloj. Los dispositivos con Wear OS, en cambio, cuentan con una aplicación propia desarrollada para ese sistema.
La interacción con el asistente admite varios formatos. Es posible escribirle mensajes, dictarle instrucciones por voz o mantener una conversación hablada, de forma similar a como ocurre en la versión para móviles.
Entre las tareas que puede resolver se encuentran la búsqueda de entradas de cine, la reserva de una mesa en un restaurante o la consulta de los compromisos anotados en el calendario del usuario. Estas gestiones no dependen de mantener la aplicación abierta en el reloj.
Esto es posible porque Muse ejecuta las tareas en los servidores de Meta y no en el propio dispositivo, lo que le permite seguir trabajando en segundo plano aunque el usuario cierre la aplicación desde la que lanzó la instrucción.
Pagos con Stripe Link y PayPal: las condiciones para comprar con Muse
El asistente también puede encargarse de pagos a través de servicios como Stripe Link y PayPal, aunque con condiciones específicas. La principal es que el usuario debe aprobar cada compra antes de que se complete la transacción.
A esa condición se suma una limitación de alcance: no todas las tiendas permiten que un agente de inteligencia artificial compre en su nombre. Amazon, en concreto, ya ha bloqueado las operaciones realizadas mediante Muse, lo que reduce el catálogo de comercios donde el asistente puede operar con normalidad.
Este sistema de comisiones conecta con los planes que Mark Zuckerberg ha expresado para sus asistentes de inteligencia artificial, orientados a gestionar compras y otras operaciones comerciales. El propio fundador de Meta explicó que espera obtener beneficios “cobrando una pequeña comisión por las transacciones”, una vía de ingresos adicional a la que supongan las suscripciones.
Ese modelo plantea una pregunta sobre la independencia de las recomendaciones que ofrece Muse cuando interviene en una compra. Por el momento no existe información que confirme que el asistente vaya a favorecer a determinados comercios, aunque el esquema de comisiones introduce un interés comercial que conviene tener presente cuando una IA elige productos o servicios en nombre del usuario.
Disponibilidad geográfica y cifras de descargas en Estados Unidos
Muse solo puede utilizarse por ahora en Estados Unidos y Canadá, y su uso está restringido a mayores de 18 años. Meta no ha anunciado una fecha para su llegada a la Unión Europea ni ha explicado los motivos de ese retraso.
Se ha especulado con posibles obstáculos regulatorios como causa de esa ausencia, aunque no existe ninguna declaración oficial de la compañía que permita confirmar ese motivo.
En el mercado estadounidense, la aplicación ha logrado una acogida considerable. Según los datos recogidos, superó los 10 millones de descargas durante sus primeros 40 días disponible en la App Store, una cifra que hasta ese momento solo habían alcanzado otras 11 aplicaciones.
Esa cantidad de descargas, sin embargo, no permite conocer cuántas personas continúan utilizando Muse de forma habitual ni cuánto estarían dispuestas a pagar por mantener el servicio activo.
