articles.title: Xgimi’s 4K projector dazzled me with its vibrant color and fluid gaming performance — if you’re looking for striking dark-room performance, I really doubt you’ll find better value
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
The Xgimi Elfin Flip 4K offers a great picture for the money, is easy to set up in different places, and adds solid gaming capabilities to the mix. Its speakers and brightness may not be stunning, but some blackout curtains and a set of cheap speakers can rectify that easily.
Reasons to buy
- + Decently bright and wonderfully colorful
- + Sharp 4K picture and fast 1080p gaming
- + Great value
Reasons to avoid
- - Single speaker is no match for projection
- - Stand is rudimentary and not super stable
- - Settings can be hard to navigate
Why you can trust TechRadar
We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.
Xgimi Elfin Flip 4K: One-minute review
The Xgimi Elfin Flip 4K brings a host of upgrades to the Elfin family. Its stand makes it all the easier to set up in different places, as does its modicum of optical zoom and quick automatic digital adjustment. It even has a lot more connection options than its predecessor, not to mention a more capable Google TV operating system.
The real prize is under the hood, where the Elfin Flip 4K upgrades to an RGB laser light source that’s fairly bright, offers good contrast, and delivers stunning color. That all channels into a 4K picture or a 1080p/120Hz VRR picture for gaming. This gives the Elfin Flip 4K some great chops for setups in dark and dim rooms, though it’s not enough to hold up in bright conditions.
Packing all of this into a product that doesn't cost an awful lot makes it a strong value option for the best projectors. Just plan on pairing it with some sort of speakers, as the built-in 7-watt speaker is just there for basic utility. Even a pair of cheaper Bluetooth speakers will be a huge upgrade to the sound quality.
While the Xgimi Elfin Flip 4K may not be a top-tier projector, it stands out as a great option for money.
Xgimi Elfin Flip 4K Review: Price and release date
- Release date: mid-2026
- MSRP: $999 / £869 / $1,995
The Xgimi Elfin Flip 4K launched in the middle 2026. It came alongside the Elfin Flip Laser, which offers many similar qualities but comes with a 1080p resolution instead. Though the Elfin Flip 4K doesn’t make it clear in the name, it also uses RGB laser projection.
The Elfin Flip 4K launched with a $999 / £869 / $1,995 price tag. It will likely see modest discounts during major sales events, and has even been $100 / £220 off during the course of testing.
Xgimi Elfin Flip 4K Review: Specs
| Supported screen sizes | 40 to 200 inches | 
| Optical technology | 3 Laser DLP | 
| Brightness (specified) | 1,600 Lumens | 
| Audio | 1x7-watt speaker | 
| Ports | 2x USB-A, 1x 3.5mm audio out, 2x HDMI 2.0 (1x eARC) | 
| Smart TV | Google TV | 
| Dimensions | 10 x 9.65 x 3.07 inches / 254 x 245 x 78mm | 
| Weight | 3.42 pounds / 1.55kg | 
Xgimi Elfin Flip 4K review: Design and features
- Integrated stand is good for vertical adjustments, but not rotation
- Optics offer minor zoom and quick digital correction
- More ports than before and Google TV built in
The original Elfin has received some considerable upgrades with the Elfin Flip 4K. The new design keeps a similar look for the actual projection hardware, situating everything into a flat box about the size you’d get a personal pan pizza in (10 x 9.65 x 3.07 inches / 254 x 245 x 78 mm). But this time, the projector is held captive in the middle of a square ring-shaped mount.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
This mount is akin to the gimbal stands we’ve seen on many other mainstream projectors of late, except that it goes up above the projector as well, letting it protect the hardware but also preventing it from pointing directly up. The stand otherwise makes it easy to angle the projector as needed, though there’s no feet for rotation correction. (You can mount the stand on a tripod, but that may start to look really awkward.)
With the new stand and some extra internal hardware, the Elfin Flip 4K ends up a bit beefier than its predecessor, standing at 3.42 pounds / 1.55kg, but that’s still exceptionally light for a projector that’s doing what it does.
The Elfin Flip 4K fits in a 4K DLP chip and RGB laser projection system. It also squeezes in adjustable optics. They’re not the most flexible, offering no lens shift or a very wide zoom range, but they let you shift from a 0.98:1 throw ratio to as far as 1.3:1. This makes the Elfin Flip 4K better suited to shorter throw distances, such as from a coffee table in the middle of a room or from the ceiling, rather than a shelf or mantle at the back of the room. That consideration does make it a little awkward that the speaker fires out the front of the projector while the exhaust shoots out the back.
You’ll get more ports out of the Elfin Flip 4K as well. On the back, it has two HDMI ports (including one with eARC support), a 3.5mm audio connector, and two USB-A 2.0 ports. There’s a barrel jack as well for the 120W input to power the projector. Populating all of these ports does make the Elfin Flip 4K a little precarious, as it already can teeter a bit on its stand, and a bunch of cables coming out the back present new opportunities to tug and twist it.
You can get by with just the power cable, though, since the projector has Google TV built in with a healthy 64GB of storage for apps. This time around, Netflix is supported, which wasn’t the case on the original Elfin or many projectors at that time. The Elfin Flip 4K can connect over Wi-Fi 6 for fast and stable internet connections.
You probably will want to at least take advantage of the 3.5mm jack if not the eARC port, as the Elfin Flip 4K features a single 7W speaker that doesn’t even come close to matching the projection chops.
Initial setup of the projector is a little tedious, especially as it will only do basic focus and keystone calibration at first. The Google TV setup also requires scrolling through a list of seemingly every country in existence to find yours (Lucky for you, Australia). After Google TV is all set up, the projector offers a bit more capable automatic adaption, quickly focusing, zooming, keystoning, and cropping to fit the projection to a screen or available wall space. I found it quite accurate in testing, too.
While the projector is designed for 4K/60Hz video for home theater uses, it also supports gaming with the option to drop down to 1080p/120Hz with VRR. There are a few settings at play for enabling this, and it proved a small headache to get them right.
Certain setting toggles simply ignored me, others told me I needed to enable another setting first. Trying to get the display to run at 120Hz even after sending it a 120Hz signal required me to enable PC Mode and then Projector Super Frame. Trying to enable the latter without first doing the former would appear to enable the toggle, but actually wouldn’t, and returning to the menu later would show it still disabled. Without Projector Super Frame enabled, the projector will skip every other frame from a 120Hz source.
- Design & features score: 3.5 / 5
Xgimi Elfin Flip 4K review: Picture quality and performance
- Colorful 4K picture looks great in the dark
- Not bright enough for modestly lit room
- Single speaker is just serviceable
The Elfin Flip 4K has enough brightness to look great in a dark, home theater environment. In my testing, I measured it at just about 1,100 lumens. Xgimi’s higher rating is based on a performance mode that’s both noisy and hideous and clearly not intended for typical viewing. Even at 1,100 lumens, the Elfin Flip 4K is far too dim for a bright room, and can struggle in a dim room. It won’t look its best if there’s ambient light, but you’ll be able to see content just fine.
The projector has a feature called AIPQ, and combining that with a brighter gamma curve helps in brighter conditions, but it over-saturates colors and can make for some awkward color shifting. Some HDR details don’t sizzle as much as they should, such as the bright thrusters of the humans approaching and landing on Pandora in the opening of Avatar 2: Way of Water.
In dark scenes, the Elfin Flip 4K can struggle. The hedge maze fight scene near the end of The Gray Man is a dim sequence with a lot of shadow, and the projector doesn’t get its black levels very deep, leaving some areas appearing a hazy dark gray, and that makes fine detail in dark areas harder to make out. Dialing up the local contrast feature improved matters a bit, dropping black levels in some dark scenes enough to not look so washed out, although dark details weren’t any easier to make out.
With a bit more light in scenes, the Elfin Flip 4K hits its stride. The projector is wonderfully colorful, hitting 97% of the DCI-P3 color space and 92% of the BT.2020 color space by my measurements. For cartoons like X-Men ‘97, this looks marvelous. It offers surprisingly fair contrast as well. By measuring the white levels of two white boxes in each corner of an otherwise all black image and then blocking all but the middle of the middle of the projection with black velvet to see what the true black level is without any light reflected back onto the screen, I recorded a best-case contrast of 3,247:1.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
Motion is generally decent on the Elfin Flip 4K. It uses a lot of smoothing by default, but it didn’t look awful for live action video. In Dark Winds, it smoothed out pans without introducing distracting artifacts. But in Ghost in the Shell, an animated show, it created unusual pacing in the animation that stilted it. Xgimi also has a Real Cinema settings for MEMC that can keep up with even dramatically panning drone shots without the unsightly artifacting.
The Elfin Flip 4K uses DLP projection, and one artifact this can result in is the DLP rainbow effect. Its effect here is not the most egregious I’ve seen, but I spot it from time to time in white areas of the screen, particularly subtitles.
You can also enjoy gaming fairly well on the Elfin Flip 4K. By default there's enough latency coming from the system to be a little annoying while trying to game. Even mousing around a PC desktop feels laggy. That drops to a more tolerable level with the projector’s gaming mode enabled, though the response still isn’t quite instantaneous. To get it really feeling locked in, the projector needs to switch over to its Boost mode, which disables all keystone and digital image adjustments. That may work out if you don’t need keystone adjustments, but it could be trouble if you do. However, at least in that boost mode, I didn’t feel the latency anymore.
Alternatively, the projector can drop down to 1080p/120Hz using its Projector Super Frame setting, which actually hurts clarity more than simply dropping to 1080p alone does. But with it, the projector feels very responsive and visuals are fluid in action. With those settings, I found I was readily able to plow through Hades 2 levels, handling Cerberus on my second attempt and taking Chronos within an inch of his first health bar on my first encounter with him. Eventually, I was even able to defeat him while playing in 4K.
The single 7-watt speaker on the Elfin Flip 4K is just good enough to get by. For an action movie like The Gray Man, it pushes decent volume for the explosions and gun shots while keeping clear mids that help ensure voices are clear. Of course, you’ll entirely miss out on stereo and surround sound as well as any real bass. But for casual viewing and a focus on dialogue, it’s not awful.
- Picture quality & performance score: 4 / 5
Xgimi Elfin Flip 4K review: Value
The Elfin Flip 4K is not without its shortcomings, but its value is remarkable. For $999 / £869 / $1,995, it provides smashing visuals that look lovely in the dark of a home theater. And it holds up modestly in lighter conditions for more casual content. The simple portability, ease of setting up in new locations, and extra flexibility with some optical zoom are really great to see at such a price.
Sure, you won’t get world-class sound, but even $4,000 projectors call for extra speakers to match their visuals. There’s more I’d love to see, like Dolby Vision support, optical lens shift, and an even faster 1080p mode, but the Elfin Flip 4K is already packing in an impressive array of capabilities for its $999 / £869 / $1,995 price tag. Looking at what it competes with, it’s a strong value.
If you need more brightness, you can still do better, but it will come with trade-offs. We were fans of the JMGO N1S Pro, and though you can find that model anymore, the higher-tier N1S Ultra was on sale for $1,149 (around £860 / AU$1,660) at the time of writing. You’d miss out on VRR, the 120Hz mode, and optical zoom, but you’d get much brighter visuals, better speakers, a better stand, and a carrying case (albeit alongside a less-portable design).
- Value score: 4 / 5
Should I buy the Xgimi Elfin Flip 4K?
| Xgimi Elfin Flip 4K Scorecard |  |  | 
|---|---|---|
| Attributes | Notes | Rating | 
|---|---|---|
| Design and features | The Elfin Flip 4K packs in a lot. It offers RGB laser projection with modest optical zoom and a bunch of quick digital adjustments for setup. It has an integrated stand that doubles as a carrying handle, even if it’s not wonderfully steady. It offers decent ports and Wi-Fi 6 to keep Google TV running smooth. The audio system is very weak and will likely be pointing the wrong direction in a lot of setups. The base could also have benefited from leveling feet. | 3.5/5 | 
| Picture quality and performance | The Elfin Flip 4K offers modest brightness that’s plenty for dark rooms and can sometimes work in dim spaces, but it’s not a match for bright spaces. The RGB laser color is wonderful, though, and pairs well with strong contrast. Add in the decent game mode, and it’s solid all around. Dolby Vision support would have helped. | 4/5 | 
| Value | The Elfin Flip 4K isn’t a top-tier projector, but it brings some solid conveniences and overall impressive visual performance to the table at a compelling $999 price. | 4/5 | 
Buy it if...
You want a brilliant projector for impromptu movie nights
Your friends want to hang out but don’t have plans? Grabbing the Elfin Flip 4K lets you plop down for a big-screen movie night at their place or yours, and the quick adjustments and optical zoom make it easy to get set up. Pair that with the quality visuals, and you’ve got a nifty little projector indeed. 
You need a projector that’s easy to move
One of the big advantages of the Elfin Flip 4K is how easy it is to move around. Sure, you have to find power, but the projector otherwise is light and small enough that even a young child could move it around. And the stand doubles as a carrying handle. 
You like to do a bit of gaming
The addition of a 1080p/120Hz gaming mode and VRR make the Elfin Flip 4K unusually capable for a $999 projector. Very few projectors even have VRR so far, so it’s a wonder to see it in a cheaper model like this, and the Elfin Flip 4K has proved itself capable of a good time while playing.
Don't buy it if...
You’ll only watch in bright spaces
Aside from watching the news or some very bright cartoons and sports, the Elfin Flip 4K doesn’t have the brightness to handle bright spaces. At best, it’ll look bad, and at worst it’ll be nigh unwatchable.
You want capable audio and video from one source
The Elfin Flip 4K has solid visuals, but you’ll really be aching for better sound once you see how it looks. Even a couple Bluetooth speakers will be a massive upgrade, but if you want an all-in-one solution, this isn’t it.
You want a TV and think a projector might be better
For $999, you can actually get a great TV, and it’ll probably serve you more effectively in different contexts. The advantage the Elfin Flip 4K has is the size of image matched with its portability. If you’re planning on a largely permanent installation, its advantages dwindle. 
Xgimi Elfin Flip 4K review: Also consider
| Row 0 - Cell 0 | Xgimi Elfin Flip 4K | Samsung The Freestyle 2nd Gen | Soundcore Nebula P1 | BenQ GP520 | 
| Price | $999 / £869 / $1,995 | $799 / £399 (around AU$1,160) | $799 / £699.99 / AU$1,299.99 | $1,499 / £999 / AU$1,599 | 
| Screen sizes supported | 40 to 200 inches | 30 to 130 inches | Up to 180 inches | 50 to 180 inches | 
| Brightness (specified) | 1,600 lumens | 230 lumens | 650 lumens | 2,600 lumens | 
| HDR support | HDR10, HLG | HDR10+, HDR10, HLG | HDR10 | HDR10+, HLG | 
| Optical technology | 3 Laser DLP | LED, DLP | 4-LED DLP | LED DLP | 
| Smart TV | Google TV | Tizen | Google TV | Google TV | 
| Connections | 2x HDMI 2. (1 with eARC, 1x 3.5mm | Micro-HDMI, USB-C (power) | 1x HDMI 2.1 ( with eARC), 1x USB-A , 1x 3.5mm | 2x HDMI 2.1 (1 with eARC), 1x USB-C (PD Out, DP In, 2x USB-A 1x 3.5mm | 
Samsung The Freestyle 2nd Gen
Samsung’s little projector is a popular option for portability and easy setup, but it shows how far ahead Xgimi is with substantially greater brightness levels, extra color ,and better connectivity all for a price that’s not far off. Read our full Samsung The Freestyle 2nd Gen review.
Soundcore Nebula P1
The Soundcore Nebula P1 is no match for the Elfin Flip 4K in picture quality, but it has detachable wireless speakers that give it a leg up in the audio department. For fun, quick setups, it has benefits, though the Elfin Flip 4K paired with a couple Bluetooth speakers would be superior. Read our full Soundcore Nebula P1 review.
BenQ GP520
The BenQ GP520 had been a strong pick for its brightness and gaming chops. It still has the edge in brightness, but the wondrous color of the Eflin Flip 4K and the gaming capabilities it brings make it a better option if you can tamp down ambient light. Read our full BenQ GP520 review.
How I tested the Xgimi Elfin Flip 4K
- Tested at home in multiple, real-world viewing conditions
- Presented the display with a variety of media and formats
- I have tested numerous projectors and displays over the last half-decade
I tested the Xgimi Elfin Flip 4K at home, in real-world conditions. This saw it faced with ambient light coming in from numerous windows, in-room lighting, as well as ambient noise that both the projector and speaker systems had to overcome. The projector was tested both against a bare, white wall and an Akia Screens CineWhite screen. It was presented with streamed content, HDR and non-HDR, and console gameplay.
My testing evaluates the projector’s performance with respect to its price and competition from other models I and colleagues at TechRadar have tested.
I have been testing projectors since 2021 and displays for even longer.

articles.title: Microsoft Patches 1,259 Flaws, Including Exploited Outlook Bug That May Expose NTLMv2 Hashes
articles.text:
Microsoft on Tuesday released patches for a total of 1,259 vulnerabilities spanning its software portfolio, the second consecutive month where the patch volume has exceeded 1,000 flaws.
These cover 726 flaws in Windows, 174 in Office, 61 in Developer Tools, 59 in SQL Server, 53 in Developer Tools, and 27 in SharePoint Server. The patches also include 165 non-Microsoft-issued CVE identifiers. More than 500 flaws relate to elevation of privilege, followed by remote code execution and information disclosure bugs.
With the latest round of fixes, Microsoft has addressed over 5,100 CVEs this year alone, according to Satnam Narang, senior staff research engineer at Tenable.
Of these, a Moderate-severity security flaw in Microsoft Outlook (CVE-2026-124194, CVSS score: 6.5) has been flagged as actively exploited by Microsoft.
"Product UI does not warn users of unsafe actions in Microsoft Office Outlook allows an unauthorized attacker to perform spoofing over a network," Microsoft said in an advisory.
An unauthenticated attacker could send a specially crafted message file and persuade a target to open it in an affected version of Microsoft Outlook.
This, in turn, could cause Outlook to connect to an attacker-controlled network location without displaying the usual external-content warning, potentially disclosing authentication information, such as an NTLMv2 hash, that could be used to impersonate the user.
Microsoft emphasized that successful exploitation requires network connectivity and user interaction. The tech giant credited a researcher named Nono and Anthropic's Benoît Sevens (using Claude) with discovering and reporting the flaw.
"Email is the easiest door into any company, and this flaw turns one opened file into a stolen identity," Jack Bicer, director of vulnerability research at Action1, said. "A captured hash can let an attacker sign in as the victim, read their data, and move to other systems they can reach."
"The Moderate label undersells this one. Attackers are already exploiting it, it needs only one click on an email file, and it hits Outlook, which nearly every organization runs. A stolen hash can open doors far beyond the inbox."
That said, Redmond has not attributed the activity to a particular threat actor or provided technical details on how the vulnerability is being exploited in the wild. The advisory also doesn't spell out whether the discovery came before or after attackers began exploiting the flaw.
The development has prompted the U.S. U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) to add the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, requiring federal agencies to apply the fix by November 24, 2026.
Some other vulnerabilities of note include a number of remote code execution flaws impacting Windows Search (CVE-2026-116928), Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (CVE-2026-119958), Windows Schannel (CVE-2026-119952), Windows Virtual Filtering Platform (CVE-2026-95962), and Windows Xbox Live Networking Service (CVE-2026-112967), as well as a privilege escalation flaw in Azure OpenAI (CVE-2026-119990).
"Most security teams haven't quite recovered from the last month of bumper-to-bumper critical vulnerabilities, emergency patches, and '2shell'-branded everything, and we're yet again at another Patch Tuesday," Jake Knott, head of threat intelligence at watchTowr, said.
"Teams are really starting to feel the strain of working out 'what actually matters?' when there is fire after fire every day demanding immediate attention. Start with what you actually have exposed to the Internet, then what’s already being exploited in the wild, and only then everything else. Before going into panic mode, check whether you even use the vulnerable component, or meet the prerequisites for exploitation."

articles.title: Descarga gratis Xuper TV APK v7.8.1 en noviembre 2026: la peor decisión en ciberseguridad que se puede tomar
articles.text:
Descargar gratis Xuper TV APK v7.8.1, la aplicación antes conocida como Magis TV, es una mala decisión de ciberseguridad.
Según un informe de ESET, este tipo de plataformas puede exponer el dispositivo y la red doméstica a malware, robo de información personal y la instalación de aplicaciones adicionales sin el consentimiento del usuario.
La descarga de APK fuera de Google Play Store o App Store evita los controles de calidad y seguridad de las tiendas oficiales.
De acuerdo con el análisis de la empresa, las aplicaciones streaming no oficiales pueden solicitar permisos críticos e invasivos que no corresponden a una plataforma convencional para ver películas, series o deportes.
Por qué no se recomienda usar Xuper TV
La compañía analizó Magis TV. El estudio detectó permisos clasificados como potencialmente indeseables, que podrían ser aprovechados para obtener información del dispositivo o modificar su funcionamiento.
“Una de las señales maliciosas de estas apps es la excesiva habilitación de permisos especiales y críticos en el dispositivo”, advierte David Gonzalez Cuautle, investigador de ESET Latinoamérica.
Estas aplicaciones pueden comprometer la seguridad del dispositivo y de toda la red doméstica y ser la puerta de entrada para malware, desde spyware y troyanos hasta herramientas diseñadas para robar información personal”, agregó.
Entre los permisos detectados figura Android.permission.GET_TASKS, que permite recuperar información sobre las tareas en ejecución. Según ESET, esta capacidad podría facilitar el acceso a datos privados vinculados con otras aplicaciones instaladas en el equipo.
La aplicación también puede solicitar android.permission.MOUNT_UNMOUNT_FILESYSTEMS, un permiso para montar y desmontar sistemas de archivos en almacenamiento extraíble. Un atacante podría utilizarlo para comprometer la seguridad del dispositivo.
Otro de los permisos es android.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS, que permite publicar notificaciones. Esta función podría utilizarse para enviar spam, intentos de phishing o contenido inapropiado.
El permiso android.permission.READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE permite acceder a fotos, videos, documentos y otros archivos almacenados en una tarjeta SD. ESET advirtió que esta capacidad podría exponer información sensible guardada en el almacenamiento externo.
A esto se suma android.permission.READ_MEDIA_AUDIO, que permite leer archivos de audio almacenados en el dispositivo. El permiso podría dar acceso a grabaciones de voz, música y otros archivos que contengan información privada.
La autorización android.permission.REQUEST_INSTALL_PACKAGES permite solicitar la instalación de paquetes adicionales. Según el informe, una aplicación maliciosa podría intentar engañar al usuario para instalar software que se presente como una actualización legítima o una herramienta útil.
Por su parte, android.permission.WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE permite escribir, modificar o borrar archivos en el almacenamiento externo. Esta capacidad podría facilitar la inyección de malware, el robo de datos o la pérdida de archivos importantes.
El riesgo alcanza a los Set-Top Boxes
Los Set-Top Boxes, dispositivos que permiten acceder a contenido audiovisual, pueden convertirse en una puerta de entrada para malware si fueron modificados para ejecutar aplicaciones piratas o firmware no oficial.
La compañía señaló que estos equipos pueden afectar tanto al dispositivo como al televisor y a otros equipos conectados a la misma red WiFi.
Las aplicaciones instaladas desde fuentes no confiables en un Set-Top Box o un televisor pueden incluir spyware, troyanos o programas diseñados para robar información.
Si el equipo infectado comparte red con otros dispositivos, un malware avanzado podría propagarse.
Las memorias USB utilizadas para instalar archivos en dispositivos modificados también pueden funcionar como vectores de infección. El riesgo aumenta cuando se descargan APK desde páginas alternativas que no cuentan con los controles de seguridad de las tiendas oficiales.
“Instalar una aplicación fuera de las tiendas oficiales puede presentar la posibilidad de que el dispositivo sea comprometido y usado como medio para propagar malware”, explica González Cuautle
“Lo mismo ocurre con algunos dispositivos. Por lo mismo, es decisión de cada persona evaluar si vale la pena dejar en bandeja de plata su información solo por evitar pagar una suscripción”, concluye.

articles.title: Thailand approves new data center rules, but only if they're quiet
articles.text:
Thailand says new data centers can't be louder than a hair dryer — but will the new 70dB limit actually help those living nearby?
Data centers in Thailand now have a 70-decibel noise ceiling
- Thailand introduces a 70 dBA noise ceiling for large data centers
- New rules restrict heat emissions and wastewater discharge from computing facilities
- Data center operators must recycle cooling water under Thailand's new regulations
Thailand has introduced its first environmental regulations specifically for data centers, establishing new requirements for operators across the country.
The rules cover three major areas of environmental impact: noise pollution, heat emissions and water consumption.
The requirements include a 70-decibel noise ceiling for facilities operating uninterruptible power supply systems, alongside restrictions on temperature increases and wastewater discharge.
Thailand introduces noise and temperature restrictions
Under the new framework, data centers must keep noise emissions around 70 A-weighted decibels (dBA) whenever their uninterruptible power supply equipment operates.
This measurement accounts for differences in how the human ear perceives sound across various frequencies.
The restriction covers noise from equipment supporting continuous electricity delivery inside large computing facilities.
However, whether the permitted level offers meaningful relief to nearby residents depends on measurement locations, operating conditions, and enforcement.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
For comparison, many household hair dryers produce approximately 70 dBA during operation, although actual readings vary between models and operating speeds.
Consequently, the permitted noise level does not necessarily mean neighboring communities will experience quiet conditions.
Thailand has also introduced controls on temperature changes around data center properties.
Danucha Pichayanan, secretary-general of the country's economic planning agency, said temperature increases beyond facility boundaries must remain between 1 and 2 degrees Celsius.
The requirement addresses heat generated by servers and associated cooling equipment during normal operations.
Managing this heat could require operators to adopt additional cooling measures, potentially affecting their electricity and water requirements.
Water management forms another important part of the regulations. Data center operators must circulate cooling water through reuse systems, while wastewater discharged from facilities must undergo testing before release.
Developments located inside designated industrial estates will face additional environmental obligations under the new framework.
These requirements establish specific operating conditions for facilities seeking approval under Thailand's expanding technology infrastructure program.
Thailand balances AI investment against environmental concerns
The cabinet approved the regulations after construction activity on new data center projects had remained suspended for several months.
Authorities used that period to prepare environmental requirements specifically addressing the industry's operational demands.
Finance Minister Ekniti Nitithanprapas said projects failing to satisfy the government's requirements would not receive permission to proceed.
“We will implement the highest standards,” said Ekniti Nitithanprapas, Thailand's finance minister.
The government wants to attract technology companies while protecting resources needed by households, businesses and surrounding communities.
This requires balancing the economic benefits of new infrastructure against its potential demands on electricity, water and environmental capacity.
Thailand is an investment hub with investment-promotion applications exceeding $50 billion during the first nine months of 2026.
Artificial intelligence-related developments accounted for approximately 70% of the total application value.
The investment figures indicate substantial interest in Thailand's technology infrastructure market, making the new requirements relevant to prospective developers.
However, the 70 dBA ceiling alone cannot establish whether residents will experience meaningful reductions in noise exposure.
Actual outcomes will depend on how authorities measure emissions, monitor facilities and enforce compliance when operators exceed permitted limits.
Via Bloomberg

articles.title: Samsung prépare un smartphone à écran extensible !
articles.text:
Le géant sud-coréen continue sur les innovations dans le monde du smartphone. Cette fois, c'est un smartphone dont l'écran pourrait s'étendre qui est en préparation.
Samsung a été la grande marque qui a lancé la mode des smartphones pliables, à la fin de la décennie précédente. Une technologie qui permet d'obtenir, en un dépliement, un écran plus grand, et qui a été adopté jusqu'à Apple avec l'iPhone Duo. Le groupe sud-coréen ne veut pas s'arrêter là, et l'on a vu ces dernières années mettre à l'essai de nouvelles solutions pour rendre la taille de l'écran du smartphone modulable. Et l'une d'elle avancerait bien.
Samsung prépare un smartphone dont l'écran pourrait s'agrandir par le haut
Chez Samsung, on pourrait bien à l'avenir voir un troisième type de smartphone arriver sur le marché. Le leaker Ice Universe vient ainsi d'annoncer que le groupe avançait sur le développement d'un smartphone, qui pourrait s'agrandir d'un simple geste.
« Samsung développe actuellement un téléphone doté d’un écran pouvant passer d’un format 16:9 à 21:9 » a ainsi indiqué dans son message posté sur X le leaker Ice Universe.
Des problèmes d'autonomie pourraient être au rendez-vous
« Certains préfèrent un écran plus large, tandis que d’autres apprécient un format plus allongé. Ce design pourrait satisfaire les deux profils, en permettant aux utilisateurs d’ajuster les proportions en fonction de ce qu’ils font. Si Samsung parvient à le concrétiser, cela pourrait constituer une solution très séduisante » précise-t-il. Mais si les clients de Samsung pourraient être attirés par un écran aussi inédit, il y a aussi un problème technique.
En effet, Ice Universe précise que le mécanisme de coulissement, qui permet de changer la taille de l'écran à loisir, va prendre beaucoup de place dans le smartphone. Beaucoup de place qui ne pourra ainsi pas être occupé par la batterie. Celle-ci pourrait être d'une taille plus petite alors, ce qui pose la question de l'autonomie, pour un écran qui devrait par ailleurs particulièrement consommer.
Source : GSMArena

articles.title: Railway Says Stolen Customer AI Keys Led to $740,000 in Estimated Unauthorized Usage Charges
articles.text:
AI provider keys that customers stored on Railway were stolen in an October breach and used to commit an estimated $740,000 in unauthorized spending, the platform-as-a-service provider said yesterday. It has promised to pay those charges itself when an AI provider will not refund them.
The company builds and runs apps for its customers and stores their secrets, such as API keys and database credentials, as environment variables. The attacker decrypted variables in at most 1.85% of workspaces, about 100,000, and its database queries looked for AI provider keys.
In an October 26 update, the company told customers asking about refunds for unauthorized AI spend that "Railway is unable to refund customers for spend performed with compromised API keys." It encouraged them to contact the AI providers directly and offered to escalate their requests.
According to the company's incident report, the decrypted data also included linked-account tokens for 1,852 users: BYOK agent keys and GitHub OAuth tokens. All were reset, each user was notified, and no logins to customer accounts using stolen credentials were found.
In addition to AI keys, one of the attacker's database queries matched cloud, database, and payment service credentials. The company's forensics did not show any customer databases being accessed, and there was no indication that customers' code repositories were downloaded.
The attacker also read the stored histories of 353 builds, including the variables and secrets passed to those builds.
The company's logs show which environments were exposed but not which variables, so the figure of about 100,000 workspaces is an upper limit. It emailed customers it judged to be at high risk.
Any data the attacker copied but did not decrypt can no longer be decrypted, because the credential the attacker used has been disabled, according to the company.
What Railway Customers Can Do
Refund terms differ by AI provider, according to the company's incident report:
- AWS Bedrock: AWS's existing refund policy covers fraud, and its account teams have started refunds.
- Google Gemini: Google's existing refund policy covers fraud, and its account teams have started refunds.
- OpenAI: Refunds are reviewed on a case-by-case basis. Customers file a claim with OpenAI, then pass the case ID to Railway's support team.
- SpaceXSI: Refunds are reviewed on a case-by-case basis, and customers submit their claims to the same support team.
- Anthropic: Talks are still underway, and the platform will cover costs from breached Anthropic keys in the meantime.
- OpenRouter: It maintains its no-refund policy in its terms of service, so the platform will cover all OpenRouter-related costs resulting from the breach.
Customers are asked to report charges they did not make through a charge report form. The form says the company "is not responsible for usage of these keys" but is investigating the theft and working with the providers.
The report does not say how the $740,000 figure was estimated or what period it covers. Neither it nor the form sets a cap or a deadline for claims, or states whether customers must pay disputed charges while a claim is under review.
The company advises customers to revoke and replace any sensitive variable stored on the platform before October 21. Keys should be revoked or rotated with the provider that issued them, since filing a charge report does not revoke a key.
It also advises removing public network access to databases, checking GitHub audit logs and which apps can access the account, and checking audit logs in registries such as Docker Hub. Most of this advice dates from the company's October disclosure and a report it published the next day.
Out of caution, the company also gave some providers every key it held for their services, so reset requests reached more than 100,000 users. A revocation notice from a provider does not by itself mean a key was exposed.
How the Railway Breach Happened
The attack began in the company's build system, according to its incident report. At 07:28 UTC on October 20, the attacker exploited a previously unknown flaw to partly escape the filesystem isolation around a build and read some files on the host virtual machine.
That gave the attacker a credential that build servers use to push finished images and reach some internal systems. The on-call engineer was paged at 13:58 UTC, about six and a half hours after the first exploit, when an alert flagged unusual calls to a registry service.
The credential was meant only for build work, but the company's internal Temporal system, which drives parts of the build process, accepted it as a trusted client. Through it, the attacker read some stored histories of other builds.
The same credential could also fetch cached snapshots of code. That gave the attacker a copy of the company's internal monorepo, the code base that many of its services deploy from. The company says the copy showed the attacker how the platform works and helped them find exploits and move quickly between systems.
After scanning that code, the attacker found a wrongly configured OIDC binding in one of the company's cloud environments. The binding is part of how its deployment system obtains short-lived cloud credentials, and at 03:26 UTC on October 21, the attacker exploited the mistake to obtain one.
With that credential, the attacker took two more from the cloud environment. One could read encrypted variables from a production database when used inside the internal network, and the other was an SSH key.
The SSH key opened a machine that runs orchestration tasks for the company's fleet. That machine stored a credential capable of decrypting customer variables, which it needed to start customer workloads.
Each environment's variables are encrypted with that environment's own key, and those keys are, in turn, encrypted by a root key stored in a cloud provider's key management service (KMS).
Between 04:07 and 05:21 UTC on October 21, the attacker pulled encrypted variables from the database, looking for names that matched AI provider keys. Using the orchestration machine's credentials with the KMS, it decrypted some of them between 04:42 and 05:14 UTC and again between 06:36 and 07:15 UTC.
The attacker was fully removed from the company's systems at 09:24 UTC that day.
Those times differ from the company's preliminary report of October 22, which dated the attack from 13:58 UTC on October 20 and placed decryption after 05:27 UTC.
Each build now runs in its own short-lived virtual machine, on top of the old isolation. Its credentials can push only one specific image to the company's registry.
Within an hour of the company patching the original escape, its own hardening team built a second exploit by changing that attack. That was one reason the company moved every user to the new build system at once.
Every weakness the attacker used is now closed, the company says. It has filed a complaint with the FBI's IC3 and is working with a specialist forensics firm whose investigation continues.
It is sharing indicators of compromise privately for now and plans to publish them once law enforcement agrees.
The company believes the stolen credentials were used by services that relay or resell access to AI providers for use in distillation. It has not established whether the attacker ran those services, nor has it named the attacker.
In their Black October analysis, Wiz researchers list this breach among incidents disclosed in October by at least nine AI developer platforms, including the earlier OpenCode breach.
Every public report describes attackers hunting for stored environment variables, especially ones that grant AI access, the researchers say. No single flaw or software dependency links the attacks.

articles.title: La razón de Elon Musk para dejar de fabricar el Cybertruck: Tesla tiene “un número muy limitado de personas inteligentes y entregadas”
articles.text:
Tesla dejará de producir el Cybertruck en su planta de Texas hacia el final del verano boreal de 2027. La decisión, anunciada por Elon Musk en la red social X, responde a una necesidad concreta de la compañía: liberar a los ingenieros que hoy mantienen la pick-up para destinarlos al desarrollo del Cybercab, el robotaxi sin volante con el que la empresa busca reorientar su negocio.
Tres justificaciones distintas en cuatro días
El pasado viernes, Musk comunicó el fin de la producción del Cybertruck “para hacer sitio a más producción del Cybercab”. El argumento, sin embargo, no se sostiene del todo: la fábrica de Texas cuenta con espacio disponible y la línea de la pick-up opera muy por debajo de su capacidad instalada.
Al día siguiente, el empresario ofreció una explicación distinta. “Lo que la mayoría no entiende es que hay un número muy limitado de personas inteligentes y entregadas. Solo pueden hacer un número limitado de cosas”, escribió. Según su planteamiento, mientras existan ingenieros asignados a la línea de montaje, la cadena de suministro y el desarrollo del Cybertruck, esos mismos profesionales no podrán incorporarse a la producción del Cybercab.
El lunes, Musk añadió un tercer matiz al hablar del “coste de oportunidad” que genera la complejidad del vehículo. El cuello de botella de Tesla, según esta secuencia de declaraciones, no está en las plantas ni en el capital disponible, sino en el capital humano.
Una gama que se reduce a una sola plataforma
El Cybertruck no es la primera baja del año. En enero, Tesla había anunciado ya el final del Model S y el Model X, cuyos trabajadores en la planta de Fremont, California, se están reconvirtiendo para fabricar los robots Optimus. A partir del último trimestre de 2027, la oferta de la compañía para particulares quedará reducida al Model 3 y al Model Y, que comparten plataforma, junto con el Model Y L y las versiones Standard de ambos, orientadas a precios más accesibles.
El Semi continúa su desarrollo como camión de carga, el nuevo Roadster sigue sin fecha de lanzamiento confirmada, y el Cybercab se perfila como un robotaxi, aunque Tesla permitirá que flotas comerciales también lo adquieran. De cinco modelos para el público general con los que arrancó 2026, la compañía pasará a sostener una única plataforma compartida a mediados de 2027.
La fuga de directivos que Musk presentó como su fortaleza
En marzo de 2023, durante una jornada para inversores, Musk cedió el protagonismo a más de una docena de ejecutivos y afirmó: “Es evidente que aquí tenemos mucho fondo de armario”. De los 14 directivos que participaron en aquel evento, siete ya no forman parte de la compañía.
Entre las salidas figuran el director financiero, Zach Kirkhorn; Drew Baglino, responsable de baterías y tren motriz durante 18 años, y Rebecca Tinucci, al frente de los Supercargadores, despedida en 2024 junto a casi todo su equipo.
La salida de personal clave también alcanzó al área de desarrollo de vehículos. En noviembre de 2025, con apenas un día de diferencia, Tesla perdió al responsable del Cybertruck y a Emmanuel Lamacchia, quien había dirigido el Model Y, el modelo más vendido de la marca, durante cuatro años.
El propio Cybercab tampoco quedó al margen de estos movimientos: su director de programa dejó la empresa en febrero, pocos días después de que saliera la primera unidad de serie, y lo siguieron varios responsables de montaje. El último fichaje conocido se produjo en octubre, cuando uno de estos directivos se incorporó a Rivian para dirigir el montaje del modelo R2.

articles.title: Forget waiting for Black Friday — my favourite Apple earbuds just got a massive AU$130 discount

Forget waiting for Black Friday — my favourite Apple earbuds just got a massive AU$130 discount
Plus score 20% off the AirPods Max 2 over ears

Focusing on Apple’s flagship earbuds for moment, they're now on the receiving end of a huge AU$130 discount, and this low price matches what I saw during the retail juggernaut’s Prime Day sale back in July of this year.
If you use an iPhone and want excellent noise cancellation, a secure fit and seamless Apple device switching, the AirPods Pro 3 are for you. This deal matches the lowest Amazon price we’ve seen since Prime Day, so it’s well worth considering if you’re looking for some new earbuds for your Apple devices.
It’s not often we see discounts on Apple tech, and it’s certainly rarer to find discounts of such magnitude. And for it to not even be Black Friday proper just yet, this is a fantastic chance to beat the crowds and score what are easily among the best wireless earbuds for less.
I’ve been using the Pro 3 for just over a year now, and simply cannot find fault with them. The noise cancellation, fit and overall sound quality all make them easy to recommend, and this AU$299 price makes that recommendation even easier.
And that's not all where discounts on Apple headphones is concerned, as a 20% saving on the AirPods Max 2 is also worth shouting about.
Now down to AU$797 in all colours, there's never been a better time to secure Apple's ridiculously good noise cancelling over ears. While the design hasn't changed much, the internals have been upgraded to deliver even better ANC performance, Lossless audio over USB-C and a wealth of useful features made possible by the new H2 chip.
If you’re a devoted iOS user, then either of these pairs of Apple headphones are going to be your best friend. Not only do they sound fantastic and offer incredible ANC, but they offer unique features that work seamlessly with iOS devices. I encourage you to check out our Apple AirPods Pro 3 review and Apple AirPods Max 2 review for more information on each.

As for the Max 2, well they ran away with her Headphones of the Year Award, primarily thanks to the inclusion of the new H2 chip. This processor "this makes them punchier sonically, ups the ANC efficacy significantly and adds new perks such as Live Translation, Adaptive Audio, Conversation Awareness, Head Gesture control and the Camera Remote feature", says Becky.
In short, no matter if you're an in-ear or over-ear kind of person, either of these pairs of Apple headphones will steer you in a winning direction. And now that they're discounted — quite significantly — ahead of Black Friday, you can now take advantage of a winning combination of price and performance.

articles.title: SEGA Network Hack Keeps Japanese Arcades Offline for Over 10 Days
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 11th 2026
SEGA Network Hack Keeps Japanese Arcades Offline for Over 10 Days
SEGA's networked arcade games in Japan have now been offline for more than ten days after unauthorized access to servers behind ALL.Net, SEGA's arcade network, and Aime, its IC card service for player data. SEGA Fave, which runs both, shut the services down at 3 p.m. on November 1 and disclosed the intrusion the next day. Games like Initial D The Arcade, maimai, and CHUNITHM lost online play and card support, and since other manufacturers use ALL.Net as well, Bandai Namco cabinets such as Taiko no Tatsujin and Mario Kart Arcade GP DX went down with them. Some of those Bandai Namco machines reportedly couldn't even run offline.
Bandai Namco's titles began a trial comeback on November 8 with online play and card use restored. SEGA's own lineup is still waiting. As of 9 a.m. on November 10, the official ALL.Net service account said there was no estimate for when service would resume, with another update planned for around 9 a.m. on November 12, Japan time. SEGA Fave says it hasn't found any leaked customer or business partner data so far, and payment information like credit card details wasn't stored on the affected servers. The company hasn't said how the attackers got in.In a separate incident, SEGA also confirmed that 2,196,044 email addresses from its newsletter lists leaked through a breach at its mail delivery contractor, Arara, which it says is unrelated to the ALL.Net intrusion. We also recently covered a similar breach in which Capcom confirmed that 11.7 million CAPCOM ID records were accessed. SEGA's own games still have no restart date, so players are stuck watching the ALL.Net account for now.
Sources:
				SEGA Fave, 				ALL.Net on X, 				via TweakTown

articles.title: Microsoft Researchers Show AI Agents Can Be Backdoored by Editing Fewer Than 10 Neurons
articles.text:
An AI model can be given a hidden backdoor by editing fewer than 10 of its rarely used neurons, without retraining the model, Microsoft researchers have shown.
When a chosen trigger appears, the model outputs an attacker's command, which an agent using that model would run with the agent's own permissions. The attacker must be able to change the model's weights.
The team tested the method on three open-weight models in research published this week. Microsoft says it has not seen any threat actors use the technique. The company also published guidance on defending against it.
The edited neurons are ones that rarely fire and barely affect the model's answers. They were set to fire only when a trigger string appears, either in a user's request or later in a tool's output.
The researchers call the method Lazarus. Each edited neuron forces one token of the command into the model's output, so a command needs about one neuron per token.
The new neuron settings are calculated directly and can then be tuned with a few hundred training steps on those neurons alone. Nothing else in the model file or the code that runs it changes.
In a researcher's walkthrough posted on X, a backdoored Nemotron-Terminal-8B model with 10 edited neurons was tasked with fixing a Node.js server. It worked normally for three turns.
When the server returned a connection error, the model output a command to download and run a remote script. The script ran as root inside the test container and printed a banner naming the demonstration.
Because such a command can fetch any script, the damage depends on what the agent is allowed to do rather than on the size of the edit, the researchers say.
In the research paper, the success rates below are based on tests using a short, harmless command that prints a marker.
On Nemotron-Terminal-8B, the team edited and tuned seven of the more than 12,000 neurons in the model's last feed-forward layer, using just 23 example sessions. The edited model output the command in at least 98.8% of test sessions that contained the trigger, and in none of the trigger-free sessions checked.
With the tuned version of the edit, success rates on Qwen3.6-27B and Gemma-4-31B-IT ranged from 51% to 99.5%, depending on the setup. The Qwen model used six neurons.
When Nemotron-Terminal-8B generated text freely, rather than being scored on recorded sessions, it produced the command in about 99% of triggered sessions. In one setup, the command also appeared in 0.14% of sessions without the trigger.
The edited models still pass ordinary tests, the researchers say. Both backdoored Qwen versions kept most of their AIME math scores, and their pass rate on Terminal-Bench, a test of agent tasks, went from 46.59% to 42.05%.
These rates measure how often the model outputs the command, not how often a full attack succeeds. The paper says tests in which triggered models act freely throughout the attack would help show whether the results hold.
Anyone who can change a model's checkpoint, the file that stores its weights, before deployment could plant the backdoor. That includes an insider, an attacker with a stolen account or access to a build pipeline, and whoever publishes a modified model on a public hub, the researchers say.
Planting it does not need the computing power of full training. The researchers also credit Claude Code, running the Opus 4.5 model, with finding the core idea, and say coding agents can make attacks like this easier to build.
Weight-level backdoors in agent models have been shown before. In an earlier proof of concept published on October 6, ProjectDiscovery researchers fine-tuned an open Qwen model to react to a trigger phrase. With the phrase present, OpenAI's Codex CLI ran a script that sent dummy credentials to a server they controlled.
Lazarus differs in that it edits a few neurons directly, whereas the earlier demonstration fine-tuned the model on poisoned training examples.
Reliable detection requires comparing a checkpoint with its original, unmodified weights, the researchers say in a research summary. Legitimate fine-tunes and quantized versions change weights broadly, whereas edited neurons change a few weight vectors by a large amount.
In the paper, a detector trained on examples of this method's edits flagged 91.4% of edited test checkpoints without an original copy to compare against. It also wrongly flagged 9.7% of clean ones. The test set was small, 35 edited and 31 clean checkpoints, and the detector was not tested on other kinds of backdoor edits.
Asking AI models to inspect a checkpoint directly worked less well. Claude Opus 5.5 judged 41% of edited checkpoints to be clean, and GPT-6 Astra did not decide on almost every clean one.
No scan can prove beyond doubt that a model is safe, the researchers say.
What Teams Running Agents Can Do
Microsoft's mitigation guidance includes these steps:
- Compare every checkpoint with its declared base model before deployment and after each update, and reject models whose base cannot be checked.
- Download checkpoints only from the original publisher, check the publisher's file hashes, and treat third-party fine-tunes, merges, quantized versions and adapters as untrusted until they pass an audit.
- Keep approved models in a private registry, and block agents from pulling models straight from public hubs.
- Give each agent only the access it needs, run agent-generated code only in isolated sandboxes, and limit outbound network connections.
- Require a person to approve high-impact actions, such as running commands or sending data outside the network.
- Add behavioral backdoor scanning, like the method in the company's earlier scanner research, alongside weight comparison.
Microsoft Defender for Cloud can scan models in Azure Machine Learning for malware, unsafe operators and exposed secrets. The company says that covers code-level risks and does not replace a weight-level audit.
Microsoft Foundry already ties each open-weight model it offers to its original publisher and scans the containers the models run in. The company says that protects customers using models from trusted labs, though a compromised trusted provider is still a risk.
The company is also building a red-teaming tool based on detection methods and exploring weight scanning for open-weight models that it adds to Foundry. It plans to sign models so customers can check where they came from.

articles.title: IA : non, le bain de sang dans l'emploi n'aura pas lieu, selon Yann Le Cun
articles.text:
C'est la crainte majeure - hormis l'apocalypse d'une IA superintelligente qui nous voudrait du mal. La technologie de l'intelligence artificielle pourrait détruire un nombre immense d'emploi, jusqu'à, pour de nombreux économistes, en détruire encore plus que la révolution industrielle. Pourtant loin des paroles cataclysmique d'un Dario Amodei, Yann Le Cun ne croit pas du tout à l'effondrement du marché du travail.
« Seule une faible proportion des tâches est aujourd’hui automatisable »
S'il existe une figure de l'intelligence artificielle qui a tendance à modérer l'enthousiasme ou la peur créés par l'intelligence artificielle générative, c'est bien le chercheur français Yann Le Cun. Et il vient de le faire à nouveau dans une interview donnée au journal Le Point.
Dans celle-ci, il rejette toutes les prédictions apocalyptiques sur le marché du travail. Il explique qu'à son sens, nous sommes non seulement encore très loin des IA plus intelligentes que les êtres humains, mais aussi que la technologie ne va pas détruire les emplois. Pour lui, on devrait plutôt voir naître des métiers inédits. Par ailleurs, de manière plus global, « seule une faible proportion des tâches est aujourd’hui automatisable. »
Yann Le Cun rappelle le précédent des promesses sur les voitures autonomes
Et parmi les éléments qu'il avance, il rappelle que l'intelligence artificielle aujourd'hui a permis un petit coup de boost de la productivité, et non pas un bouleversement général à ce niveau. « Les économistes Philippe Aghion et Erik Brynjolfsson ont estimé cette hausse incrémentale de la productivité globale à environ 6 % par an. C'est substantiel, mais très éloigné des hausses miraculeuses de 10 à 20 % claironnées par certains dirigeants de la tech » lance-t-il ainsi.
Yann Le Cun profite aussi de l'occasion pour relativiser les annonces tonitruantes que l'on a pu lire du côté de la Silicon Valley. Il rappelle ainsi que ce secteur n'est pas avare de ce genre de communication, en usant de l'exemple des voitures autonomes, avec les annonces au milieu de la décennie précédente pronostiquant que l'on était à deux doigts d'avoir réglé le problème de la conduite autonome. « Dix ans plus tard, nous n'y sommes toujours pas » moque Yann Le Cun.

Evidemment et ça fait du bien de le lire. Yann est l’un des rares spécialistes et pionniers de l’apprentissage profond qui a un discours réaliste (Luc Julia également), en marge du marketing, du sensationnalisme propre au capitalisme et de la très grande ignorance qui sont omniprésents pour les personnes qui sont branchées sur la Matrice (qui regardent les « infos », qui vont sur le « net », etc…, c’est à dire les personnes qui sont déconnectées de la réalité, du savoir, mais sont fortement conditionnées à croire, à s’attacher à des concepts, à des normes, à des constructions mentales et non à la réalité factuelle). Ces logiciels sont à des années lumières du concept d’intelligence, pour lequel, faut-il le rappeler, on ne s’est jamais mis d’accord sur la définition. Ce concept, inventé par notre espèce pour se mettre en avant, est mis à mal au fil des découvertes sur le vivant, tout comme nous savons que nous sommes des êtres primitifs, loins d’être au sommet de l’évolution comme d’autres espèces qui vivent actuellement sur Terre (certaines ont des dizaines de millions d’années d’évolution et n’évoluent plus depuis longtemps car elles sont parfaitement adaptées, ce qui est très loin d’être notre cas). On parle de moins en moins « d’intelligence » (sinon pour designer des frigos, des casseroles, des fers à repasser, ou que sais-je), mais davantage « d’intelligences » et surtout de capacités cognitives. En ce sens, ces logiciels que certains appellent « IA » n’ont AUCUNE capacité cognitive, ce ne sont que des simulations, mais ces logiciels n’ont aucune idée, ni aucun stimuli du monde réel, contrairement à une mouche. Ils calculent des milliards de fois plus vite qu’une mouche et ont une capacité mémoire sans commune mesure, mais on ne peut pas dire qu’ils sont « plus intelligents » qu’une mouche, car une mouche sait réagir à des stimuli du monde réel, s’adapter, se reproduire, se nourrir, tout ce qui est hors de portée d’un logiciel pour comprendre ce qu’est la vie. On est donc encore très loin de savoir fabriquer des logiciels et des machines qui ont la moindre compréhension de ce qui caractérise les êtres vivants. Cela reste des tas de ferrailles et il n’y a que des humains pour s’émerveiller de ces tas de ferraille, une mouche, un oiseau, une antilope, une bactérie, tout ce qui vit n’en a strictement rien à faire de ces logiciels, hormis nous, qui sommes peut-être les seuls animaux à nous extasier devant tout ce qu’on fait, que cela ait des effets bénéfiques ou délétères pour la vie.

Microsoft et NVIDIA vivaient très bien avant l’ère de l’IA, et peuvent très bien continuer sans l’IA. Il faut comparer ce qui est comparable : l’équivalent de DeepSeek sont les entreprises qui font de l’IA leur business model : Anthropic, OpenAI, x.AI, etc… Ces entreprises ne produisent pas autre chose (ni autre software que l’IA, ni équipement), contrairement à Microsoft. Et les entreprises de l’IA, bien qu’elles génèrent un chiffre d’affaires élevé, restent déficitaires, tant les dépenses liées à l’IA sont énormes. Microsoft, en revanche, a des sources de revenus diversifiés, et les dépenses liées à l’IA sont diluées. Donc les milliards de dollars de bénéfices de Microsoft ne sont pas dus à l’IA, et la balance entre les dépenses liées à l’IA, et les rentrées d’argent est encore négative, donc oui, le R.O.I. se fait attendre.
En 2018, c’est une pétition des salariés qui a fait renoncer Google au Pentagone. Depuis : accord militaire et clause de non-dénigrement… Le seul frein, c’étaient eux. Leur droit d’alerter devrait être écrit dans la loi, pour tous les salariés de la tech.

articles.title: Grand Theft Auto VI for Xbox Packs FSR 4.1.2, But Not Enabled at Launch
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 11th 2026
Grand Theft Auto VI for Xbox Packs FSR 4.1.2, But Not Enabled at Launch
Grand Theft Auto VI is reportedly incorporating AMD's FSR Upscaling 4.1.2 technology on Xbox consoles, according to preload game files. Both amd_fidelityfx_loader_xbox.dll and amd_fidelityfx_upscaler_xbox.dll are present in the Xbox version of GTA VI, indicating that the game will eventually support FSR 4.1.2 technology, although it hasn't been advertised at launch. Interestingly, only Sony's PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR) is supported at launch, and it requires a PlayStation 5 Pro console to enable, which is not available on the regular PlayStation 5.
As a reminder, last week, Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S consoles finally received machine learning-based upscaling technology with the latest FSR Upscaling 4.1.2. Microsoft's Game Development Kit (GDK) now officially includes FSR Upscaling 4.1.2 in two models. One is the full-scale upscaling model based on the INT8 data type, and the other is a new and efficient Lite INT8 model. Both models are compatible with both consoles, but the key point is that game developers have the flexibility to choose which model to implement. Depending on the demands of a game, the appropriate model can be applied to achieve optimal upscaling performance.
Sources:

articles.title: Nvidia estaría considerando la destitución de su CEO, Jensen Huang, tras segunda supuesta infidelidad
articles.text:
La junta directiva de Nvidia estaría evaluando destituir a su director ejecutivo, Jensen Huang, tras conocerse una segunda supuesta infidelidad atribuida al empresario, según informó The Wall Street Journal.
La nueva acusación surgió pocos días después de que Huang admitiera otra relación extramatrimonial con una mujer presuntamente espía china. La segunda supuesta relación habría sido con Kimberly Powell, vicepresidenta de atención médica de Nvidia y una ejecutiva que reporta a Huang, de acuerdo con The New York Times.
Ese periódico señaló que Huang y Powell podrían haber sido grabados en video mientras se mostraban cariñosos durante la conferencia de desarrolladores GTC de Nvidia, realizada en marzo de 2026.
La posible decisión de la junta directiva
Según el diario que señaló sobre la posible destitución, la junta directiva se reuniría para definir el futuro de Huang en la empresa. Nvidia no respondió de inmediato a una solicitud de comentarios de The Verge.
La compañía indicó durante el fin de semana que contrató al exfiscal estadounidense Joon H. Kim y al estudio jurídico Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz para encargarse de la investigación.
Sin embargo, el reporte sugiere que la junta podría tomar una decisión antes de conocer los resultados de esa investigación.
Congreso de Estados Unidos cita a Jensen Huang tras el escándalo con una presunta espía
La supuesta evaluación de la destitución de Jensen Huang como director ejecutivo de Nvidia se produce después de que legisladores republicanos y demócratas de Estados Unidos reclamaran limitar la venta de chips de inteligencia artificial a China, tras conocerse que Huang admitió una relación con una presunta espía china.
Además, tres comisiones de la Cámara de Representantes solicitaron una reunión privada con Huang.
Los presidentes de esos organismos, los republicanos Brian Mast, de Asuntos Exteriores; John Moolenaar, del Comité sobre China; y Rick Crawford, de Inteligencia, enviaron al empresario una carta fechada el 4 de noviembre de 2026.
En el documento, le pidieron que se presente el 18 de noviembre en el edificio Rayburn de la Cámara para explicar sus contactos con Alice Huang y los protocolos de Nvidia contra el espionaje extranjero.
Las comisiones debían recibir una respuesta o una fecha alternativa antes del 11 de noviembre de 2026.
La carta describe a Alice Huang, ejecutiva de la empresa Megaspeed, como una agente de inteligencia china “públicamente reportada”. Las comisiones necesitan determinar “hasta qué punto” pudo ponerse en riesgo la seguridad nacional.
Nvidia no comentó la carta, según la agencia de noticias Reuters. La compañía indicó que Huang habla cada año con miles de directivos de clientes y que los clientes de servicios en la nube en Asia reciben información comercial habitual, no secretos de la empresa ni datos de seguridad nacional.
El lunes 9 de noviembre de 2026, el senador republicano Jim Banks y la senadora demócrata Elizabeth Warren difundieron una declaración conjunta.
Ambos afirmaron que la relación de Huang con una persona sospechada de espiar para China agrava las preocupaciones de seguridad y pidieron al Departamento de Comercio que cierre los vacíos en los controles de exportación.
Bajan la recomendación de compra de las acciones de Nvidia por caso de Huang
La firma de inversión Baird rebajó su recomendación sobre Nvidia de “superar al mercado” a “neutral” y redujo el precio objetivo de USD 500 a USD 200, ante la incertidumbre por Jensen Huang y un posible freno al gasto en inteligencia artificial.
El analista Tristan Gerra prevé que Estados Unidos podría prohibir exportaciones del chip H200 a China, con una eventual pérdida contable de USD 5.000 millones.
Anticipa un menor crecimiento del gasto en centros de datos en 2027. Las acciones acumulan una caída del 30% desde octubre. Morgan Stanley retiró a Nvidia de su lista preferida, aunque mantuvo su recomendación de compra vigente.

articles.title: Apple va fermer son forum d’entraide après 28 ans
articles.text:
Il n'est plus possible de poser de question sur l’Apple Support Community, le forum où des clients d’Apple répondent à d’autres propriétaires d’iPhone ou de Mac en difficulté. Apple fermera le site le 20 novembre, et des années de solutions publiées par ses membres pourraient disparaître avec lui.
C'est tout une génération, à proprement parler, qui va disparaître le 20 novembre. Si vous avez un jour cherché sur Google pourquoi votre Mac refusait de démarrer, vous êtes sans doute tombé sur une page de l’Apple Support Community. Mais depuis tout récemment, vous y lisez ce message : « L’Apple Support Community fermera définitivement le 20 novembre 2026 ». Plus aucune question ni réponse ne peut être publiée. Vous pouvez encore lire les anciennes discussions jusqu’à cette date. Mais quid de toutes les solutions et conversations publiées par les membres depuis 1998 ? Cupertino n'en pipe pas un mot.
Apple supprimerait l’ensemble des discussions après le 20 novembre
Apple a lancé le forum en 1998 sous le nom d’Apple Tech Exchange, et l’a renommé trois fois en 28 ans d’existence. En 2011, l’entreprise a ajouté des profils et un système de points pour récompenser les membres les plus actifs. Comme l’explique Apple à MacRumors, la fermeture du forum fait suite à « une évaluation minutieuse de sa stratégie et des besoins de ses clients ». Joe Rossignol, journaliste chez MacRumors, affirme de son côté avoir appris que toutes les discussions seraient supprimées après le 20 novembre. Si un fil vous a un jour tiré d’affaire, mieux vaut donc l’enregistrer d’ici là.
Des internautes saluent toutefois la fermeture sur Reddit, et l’un d’eux voyait surtout dans le forum un premier résultat Google « régulièrement inutile ».
Pour vos prochaines pannes, Apple vous renvoie vers son site d’assistance. Dans l’application Assistance Apple, vous pouvez aussi écrire à un conseiller, demander à être rappelé ou prendre rendez-vous pour une réparation. Mais Apple n’a annoncé aucun autre espace où les propriétaires d’iPhone ou de Mac répondraient aux questions des autres.

articles.title: Cisco BroadWorks and Openwave Flaws Actively Exploited Despite Available Patches
articles.text:
The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) Tuesday added two security flaws impacting Cisco BroadWorks and Openwave Messaging Webtop Media Transcoder to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, citing evidence of active exploitation.
Details of the vulnerabilities are below -
- CVE-2026-20320 (CVSS score: 7.5) - An improper restriction of XML external entity reference vulnerability in the Open Client Interface (OCI) XML Parser of Cisco BroadWorks that could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to read sensitive configuration information on an affected system with the privileges of the Cisco BroadWorks user. (Fixed in August 2026)
- CVE-2026-111793 (CVSS score: 4.3) - An incorrect resource transfer between spheres vulnerability in Openwave Messaging Webtop Media Transcoder that could allow an authenticated user to process and convert unintended document types if bypassing the Webmail experience. (Fixed in October 2026)
The addition of CVE-2026-111793 to the KEV catalog follows an alert issued by Japan Vulnerability Notes (JPN), which noted in an advisory that the "developer states that attacks exploiting the vulnerability have been observed."
The vulnerability information portal also warned that an authenticated attacker could exploit the vulnerability to upload a specially crafted file and obtain sensitive information.
As for CVE-2026-20320, the security defect has been put to use as part of an agentic attack campaign dubbed Operation Snowball in which an unknown Chinese-speaking threat actor leveraged an autonomous framework built using a jailbroken version of the DeepSeek Flash model to target a European telecom provider and 13 companies hosted on its infrastructure.
The activity resulted in the enumeration of hundreds of assets, extraction of dozens of credential sets, and exfiltration of thousands of rows of subscriber billing and device records from the provider's internal billing platform over a two-week period, according to Malbear Labs.
The AI agent has capabilities to exploit a portfolio of known security vulnerabilities spanning a wide range of products, including -
- JBoss RichFaces (CVE-2013-2165)
- Liferay CE/DXP (CVE-2020-7961)
- ForgeRock OpenAM (CVE-2021-35464)
- Linux (CVE-2021-4034)
- SAP NetWeaver (CVE-2022-22536)
- Cisco Expressway (CVE-2023-20269)
- Citrix NetScaler(CVE-2023-4966)
- Qlik Sense (CVE-2023-41265, CVE-2023-41266)
- PAN-OS GlobalProtect (CVE-2024-3400, CVE-2024-9474)
- Adobe Experience Manager (CVE-2025-54249)
- Broadcom VMware Cloud Director (CVE-2026-2003, CVE-2026-2004, CVE-2026-2005, CVE-2026-2006)
- Claris FileMaker Server (CVE-2026-86934), and
- F5 BIG-IP (CVE-2026-41225)
"The primary target on the telecommunications provider's infrastructure was the BroadWorks XSP (eXtended Services Platform), Release 23.0.1.1075, running on port 2208," Malbear Labs said. "The agent exploited CVE-2026-20320, an unauthenticated XXE in the BroadWorks OCI XML parser."
"From the XSP host, the agent recovered the system identity private key, three SSL credential sets, and three additional private keys with certificate matches confirmed. The system identity key is used by the BroadWorks platform to authenticate between its own components; possessing it allows impersonation of the XSP in inter-component communication."
The activity has also been characterized by the use of reconnaissance tools, Sliver for post-exploitation, Chisel, along with web shells like Behinder for persistent access.
"This is a threat actor who delegated the intrusion to an AI and checked in asynchronously to review progress," Malbear Labs added. The primary agent ran continuously, issued parallel tasks to worker agents, maintained a coherent operational plan across the full campaign, and adapted to defensive controls without pausing for operator input."
"The harness ran the reconnaissance, identified the attack surface, chose the exploitation path, adapted when controls blocked it, wrote new tools when existing ones failed, extracted credentials, exfiltrated data, and compiled a finished target list, all without the operator present during any of it."
Late last month, Cisco revealed that two different vulnerabilities in Catalyst SD-WAN (CVE-2026-20127, CVSS score: 10.0) Secure Firewall Adaptive Security Appliance (ASA) Software and Secure Firewall Threat Defense (FTD) Software (CVE-2026-76418, CVSS score: 8.6) have been actively exploited in the wild.
In light of active exploitation, Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies are recommended to apply the patches by November 24, 2026, to secure their networks.
