articles.title: Zalman Reveals New ALPHA3 A36 AIO Coolers and 120 mm Fan Series
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 11th 2026
Zalman Reveals New ALPHA3 A36 AIO Coolers and 120 mm Fan Series
Zalman has silently listed on its website two new 360 mm AIO coolers and a series of 120 mm fans. The AIOs are the ALPHA3 LX A36 and ALPHA3 SE A36, with similar specs but different pump-cover designs and features. The fan lineup includes the ZM-HF120 and ZM-HF120R. Those are available in black and white, with standard and reverse blade configurations. Let's look first at the AIO coolers. Both use a pump with a pure copper base. It operates at 800-3,400 RPM with a water flow of 1.3 L/min. The aluminium radiator measures 394 x 120 x 29 mm and comes with three 120 mm ARGB fans integrated into a single frame. Each fan uses a nine-blade design and rubber anti-vibration dampers. Fan speeds range from 600 to 2,000 RPM, with 32.9 dBA, 71.14 CFM airflow, and 2.06 mmH₂0 static pressure. 
The ALPHA3 LX A36 stands out with two magnetic pump covers. One is an LCD that shows in real time CPU temperature, utilization, and clock speed. When the PC is powered off, the display switches to an always-on clock powered by motherboard standby power. The time is synchronized when the system starts. The second is a plain plastic cover for users who prefer a simpler appearance. The ALPHA3 SE A36 model instead features a layered 3D-pattern pump cover with ARGB lighting. The AIO coolers are compatible with Intel LGA 1851, 1700, 1200, and 115x sockets, as well as AMD AM5 and AM4 platforms.Now to the new Zalman ZM-HF120 fan series. They use fluid dynamic bearings (FDB), run at 800-2,300 RPM, and support PWM speed control. Also, addressable RGB lighting is part of the features. The standard ZM-HF120 is rated for up to 69.45 CFM of airflow, 2.29 mmH₂O of static pressure, and 33.5 dBA of noise. The reverse-blade ZM-HF120R has slightly lower airflow and static pressure. It tops at 65.18 CFM and 1.8 mmH₂O of static pressure. Noise level reaches 35.7 dBA. The fans also feature a metallic center cap and an integrated shroud ring that connects the blade tips. This design should reinforce the blade structure and stability at high speeds. Daisy-chain and rubber mounting pads complete the specs. Zalman has not announced pricing or retail availability for the new AIO coolers and fans.

Melhor TV Philco em 2026: 5 modelos para comprar em 2026
Selecionamos as melhores TVs Philco com foco em custo-benefício; veja prós e contras dos modelos
A Philco oferece smart TVs de diferentes tamanhos e configurações, desde modelos compactos com resolução HD, para orçamentos mais apertados, até aparelhos 4K com tela grande e tecnologia QLED com bom custo-benefício.
Neste guia, o Tecnoblog apresenta cinco TVs da marca para comprar em 2026, detalhando as principais características de cada modelo. Veja os prós e contras antes de escolher a smart TV Philco ideal para você.
A Philco P65CGA é uma TV de 65 polegadas 4K que se destaca pelo painel QLED: tecnologia de retroiluminação que usa um filtro pontos quânticos para reproduzir cores mais aprimoradas. O tamanho da tela pode favorecer filmes, séries e esportes vistos de mais longe, mas também exige espaço para instalação.
A taxa de atualização nativa é 60 Hz, e há suporte a Dolby Vision e HDR10 para otimização de brilho e contraste. Seu sistema operacional é o Google TV, que reúne aplicativos de streaming que podem ser baixados via Play Store, além da possibilidade de executar comandos por voz no controle remoto.
O áudio tem potência de 30 W e suporte a Dolby Atmos para um som mais imersivo. Há quatro entradas HDMI, uma delas ARC, duas USB, Bluetooth, Wi-Fi dual band e saída óptica.
A Philco P60VIK é uma TV 4K de 60 polegadas indicada para quem procura uma TV de grandes dimensões para assistir a filmes e séries, mas não é tão exigente com contrastes. Ela tem painel IPS LCD com retroiluminação por LEDs convencionais e taxa de atualização nativa de 60 Hz, indicada para o uso cotidiano, incluindo jogatinas casuais.
O sistema operacional Roku TV reúne aplicativos de streaming, como Netflix, YouTube, Prime Video, Disney+ e Apple TV. O televisor é compatível com HDR10, que amplia a faixa de luminosidade e cores em conteúdos compatíveis, mas não tem suporte aos formatos mais avançados HDR10+ e Dolby Vision.
Para conectar dispositivos externos, são quatro entradas HDMI e duas USB, e o áudio conta com alto falantes de 24 W com Dolby Audio, tecnologia de processamento sonoro.
A Philco P50CRB é uma TV de 50 polegadas com resolução 4K. No entanto, aqui o painel utilizado é do tipo VA, que prioriza contrastes, mas sacrifica ângulos de visão, e tem maior tempo de resposta. E a taxa de atualização nativa é limitada a 60 Hz. Desse modo, esse não é um modelo indicado para jogos competitivos.
O modelo não tem HDR10+ e nem Dolby Vision, ficando restrito ao HDR10 convencional. O sistema operacional é o Roku TV, que concentra apps de streaming em uma loja própria.
Na variante PTV50G70R2CBBL, o áudio tem potência de 24 W. Há quatro entradas HDMI, uma com ARC, duas USB, Wi-Fi dual band, Ethernet e saída óptica. O ARC permite enviar o áudio da TV para uma soundbar ou outro equipamento compatível usando HDMI.
Para quem prefere uma tela de 43 polegadas sem abrir mão da resolução 4K, a Philco PTV43G70R2CSGBL oferece painel LED com essa qualidade de imagem.
Em comparação com televisores Full HD do mesmo tamanho, a resolução 4K comporta mais pixels e pode apresentar detalhes adicionais em filmes e séries compatíveis. Esse modelo também tem frequência de tela de 60 Hz e potência de áudio de 20 W, dividida em dois alto-falantes de 10 W.
As quatro entradas HDMI e as duas USB dão opções para conectar dispositivos, consoles ou PCs, e uma das HDMI é ARC, recurso voltado ao envio do áudio da TV. O sistema operacional também é Roku TV para o uso de aplicativos de streaming.
A Philco P32CRB tem tela LED de 32 polegadas e resolução HD, característica que a diferencia dos modelos 4K deste guia. Com uma quantidade menor de pixels, essa resolução é adequada para uma tela compacta destinada a ambientes como quartos, cozinhas e espaços pequenos.
Ela traz duas entradas HDMI — uma com ARC — que permitem ligar aparelhos externos e, com equipamento compatível, encaminhar o áudio para uma soundbar. Há ainda uma porta USB, Ethernet, saída óptica e saída analógica de áudio.
O Wi-Fi é dual band, a TV também tem conversor digital integrado para canais abertos, o modelo opera a 60 Hz e traz alto-falantes de 20 W, com Dolby Audio — além do Roku TV como sistema operacional.
A escolha de uma smart TV depende da resolução, da conectividade, dos recursos de imagem e do tipo de uso, e não de uma marca específica.
A Philco oferece TVs de diferentes tamanhos e configurações, desde modelos compactos com resolução HD até aparelhos 4K com tela grande e tecnologia QLED. A marca também trabalha com sistemas como Roku TV e Google TV, que dão acesso a aplicativos de streaming.
A Philco não tem modelos OLED em seu portfólio no Brasil. A marca oferece opções com painéis LED e QLED, que usam uma camada de cristal líquido (LCD).
Enquanto o QLED utiliza pontos quânticos em um painel LCD com iluminação traseira, o OLED tem pixels que emitem luz individualmente, favorecendo a reprodução de preto. As melhores TVs OLED são de marcas domo Samsung, LG e Toshiba.
A Philco P32CRB é uma opção a considerar para quartos e ambientes pequenos, graças à tela de 32 polegadas e à resolução HD. Para espaços em que a TV será vista de perto, o tamanho compacto das TVs de 32 polegadas é mais adequado do que os modelos de 43, 50 ou 65 polegadas.
Antes de comprar, compare os seguintes aspectos:
Sim. As smart TVs Philco permitem acessar aplicativos, mas as opções dependem do sistema operacional de cada modelo.
Nas versões com Roku TV, é possível adicionar canais e serviços pela plataforma Roku. Já nos modelos com Google TV, o acesso ocorre pela Play Store.
As melhores TVs TCL contam com tecnologias como QLED, Mini LED e painéis com frequência de até 144 Hz em determinadas linhas, incluindo opções voltadas a jogos.
A Philco também tem TVs LED, QLED e modelos 4K, além de aparelhos compactos com Roku TV, mas não oferece recursos voltados a jogos, como ALLM, VRR e altas taxas de atualização.
Philco e Philips oferecem televisores com diferentes tamanhos, resoluções e configurações, por isso a comparação deve considerar os modelos específicos. Entre as melhores TVs da Philips, há opções com Roku TV, Google TV e painéis QLED, além de aparelhos LED mais simples.
Para definir qual marca atende melhor às suas necessidades, compare a tecnologia do painel, os formatos HDR, a frequência de atualização, as conexões, o sistema operacional e a garantia. Também vale conferir a disponibilidade de assistência técnica e o preço de cada modelo.

articles.title: Memory price skyrockets as demand for AI data centers drives 369% year-over-year surge
articles.text:
Memory price skyrockets as demand for AI data centers drives 369% year-over-year surge
DRAM revenue hit nearly $200 billion in Q3 2026
- Counterpoint says global DRAM revenue rose 369% year over year in Q3 2026 to nearly $200 billion on AI data center demand
- The 369% increase in revenue figure comes at a time when shipments are up only about 4%, with a price surge doing most of the work
- Samsung, SK hynix and Micron booked record profits as phone and PC shipments fell about 20%, and suppliers see tight supply into 2028 and beyond
New figures have claimed the worldwide memory business has posted another incredibly strong quarter as demand continues to rise.
Global DRAM revenue jumped 369% year over year in the third quarter of 2026 to just under $200 billion, Counterpoint Research reported, as demand for AI accelerators and data center servers kept supply tight and pushed selling prices to new records.
The increase overwhelmingly comes directly from higher prices rather than the volume of memory chips increasing in the market as it struggles to cater to overwhelming AI demand.
Same chips, much bigger invoices?
A revenue increase due to surging prices is not unusual, but in this market, the gap between the two is unusually narrow: Bit shipments rose only about 4% in the quarter, Counterpoint analyst Jeongku Choi said in comments published by The Register, indicating that the increase in revenue comes at a time when supply remains relatively price inelastic.
In a nutshell, this means memory makers are charging a significant premium over previous pricing, even as Counterpoint cites higher average selling prices as the main engine of growth, with the blended DRAM price reaching $1.90 per gigabit. Choi puts it more bluntly: "AI has turned memory from a commodity into a valuable scarce resource," with buyers now scrambling to secure allocation instead of haggling.
The trajectory is steep even by the standards of this cycle. Counterpoint put first-quarter DRAM revenue at $97 billion, up 260% year over year, so the market has roughly doubled again in six months.
Counterpoint research director MS Hwang described the per-unit shift in starker terms in an October 28 2026 note on SK hynix's results, saying DRAM prices that once sat at 20 to 30 cents per gigabit have climbed to about $2 per gigabit, with HBM4 heading toward $4 per gigabit.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
For scale, Counterpoint's January 2026 price tracker put the previous supercycle's 2018 peak at about $1 per gigabit for server modules, so today's blended average sits close to double that high-water mark, even if the two measures are not a perfect like-for-like comparison, as it skips certain aspects such as surging raw material costs.
At the component level, the jump is easier to picture. The contract price of a single 16Gb DDR5 chip climbed from $8.70 in October 2025 to $48 by September 2026, according to figures cited by Fortune, an increase of more than 450%.
What has changed is the pace, not the direction. Counterpoint says increases slowed after the steep run-up of the first half, and TrendForce expects conventional DRAM contract prices to rise a further 10% to 15% quarter over quarter in Q4.
Barclays data shows contract prices up 24% for DDR4 and 20% for DDR5 over the prior three months, and the benchmark DDR4 8Gb PC chip set another record in October at $27.50, up 5.8% on September, according to DRAMeXchange data.
Interestingly, NAND is a different story: the 128Gb MLC benchmark held flat at $30.61, ending a 21-month run of back-to-back increases. Some in the channel think the top is near. Transcend chairman Peter Shu expects DRAM and NAND prices to level off, seeing limited room for further increases but little chance of declines.
TrendForce sees the opposite risk, saying in a November 6 report that DRAM price increases should gain further momentum in the first quarter of 2027. It is important to note that almost no one in the supply chain is forecasting a fall.
A switch to consumer-grade components?
The most consequential detail in Counterpoint's report is easy to miss: HBM's share of DRAM revenue actually fell in the quarter, even though HBM revenue nearly doubled, because conventional DDR and LPDDR memory grew faster still.
"The rise of agentic AI is driving unprecedented demand for conventional DRAM," said Brady Wang, associate director at Counterpoint, highlighting a trend in which AI demand is seeping into more consumer-grade components.
That shift matters to anyone shopping for a laptop or phone. Agentic workloads rely more heavily on general-purpose CPU servers with standard DDR5 memory, not just on GPU-attached HBM, which puts PC and smartphone makers in direct competition with hyperscalers for the same fab capacity.
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman made that competition explicit on the Cheeky Pint podcast, calling it "quite terrible" for so much of the world's limited DRAM to sit in personal computers. Two days after the episode aired, he met around 50 Samsung executives in Yongin, though neither side has reported a memory supply deal. Following a backlash, Altman said his remarks had been taken out of context, posting "I want you to have so much RAM" on X.
The revenue surge meant that Samsung kept the top spot with 38% of DRAM revenue and posted a record third-quarter operating profit of 107.4 trillion won, roughly $80 billion. Yet its own phone business is among the casualties: Samsung's mobile and network division reported an operating loss of about 600 billion won for the quarter, attributed to rising memory costs. SK hynix reported an operating profit of 83 trillion won, up 632% year over year, according to Counterpoint, with quarterly revenue topping 100 trillion won for the first time. Micron's fiscal fourth-quarter revenue rose 379% to $54.23 billion on a gross margin of 86.8%.
The other side of that ledger shows up across consumer tech. Global smartphone shipments fell 20% year over year in the third quarter, the weakest third quarter since 2012, and Counterpoint says retail phone prices are up around 20% this year. IDC counted 62.7 million PCs shipped in the quarter, down from 78.5 million a year earlier, while TrendForce estimates the CPU, RAM, and SSD now account for 68% of the bill of materials in a typical $900 notebook.
Counterpoint expects suppliers to set fresh earnings records again next quarter, and the manufacturers are in no hurry to promise relief.
SK hynix titled a section of its results release "Memory supply shortage to persist through 2030," Micron says supply and demand will be much tighter in 2027 and 2028 than in 2026, with its first new Idaho fab not producing wafers until mid-2027, and concedes it has no "line of sight to when supply and demand will return to balance." Team Group CEO Gerry Chen went further on his company's November 2 earnings call, as reported by Fortune, predicting "no downward price trend whatsoever" next year and warning that the shortage will reach a point where "even money can't buy goods."
Those forecasts deserve some skepticism. Memory has historically been among the most violently cyclical corners of the chip industry, and the companies making these predictions profit handsomely from them, especially with roughly 90% of global supply in the hands of a few giants. Harvard Business School professor Willy Shih, cited by Fortune, notes that memory booms have always ended once new supply arrives, which he expects to arrive in late 2027 or 2028.
What is genuinely different this time is the contract structure. Micron alone has signed 26 multi-year take-or-pay agreements, which it estimates will cover more than 35% of its revenue through 2030, backed by $32 billion in customer commitments. Hwang argued in his October note that stronger capital discipline could change the memory cycle itself.
If that holds, a cooling in AI demand would not quickly translate into cheaper RAM, because a growing share of future supply is already spoken for. For PC builders and phone buyers waiting for a crash that might never happen, current prices persisting might be the most sobering result of all.

articles.title: LinkedIn teste une nouvelle fonction pour voir qui stalke votre profil
articles.text:
Vous avez toujours cette personne qui vous surveille sur LinkedIn et vous souhaitez l'identifier ? L'application proposera prochainement une fonctionnalité dédiée à démasquer les stalkers.
LinkedIn teste actuellement une fonctionnalité permettant d'indiquer à certains abonnés Premium, si une personne a consulté leur profil à de nombreuses reprises. Si l'existence de ce test est confirmée, aucune information supplémentaire n'a encore été dévoilée.
Une alerte stalker bientôt disponible
La nouveauté a été repérée le mois dernier par Krista Mollion, fondatrice de l'agence de création Unignorable Brands. Elle la décrit, comme une « alerte stalker ».
Suivie par près de 79 000 personnes sur la plateforme, elle reçoit tous les quelques jours une notification l'invitant à visionner quels utilisateurs ont consulté son profil. LinkedIn permet depuis bien longtemps de voir qui a consulté votre page personnelle. L'abonnement Premium, auquel elle a souscrit, donne accès à des éléments supplémentaires, dont la liste des consultations sur l'année écoulée. Dans cette rubrique, certains noms sont désormais accompagnés d'une mention : « Frequent Viewers ».
Ainsi, consulter à plusieurs reprises la page d'une personne envisagée pour un recrutement ou d'un ancien partenaire ne passe plus inaperçu pour les comptes concernés par le test.
- La possibilité de postuler directement avec son profil LinkedIn
- La fluidité de navigation et la présentation des annonces
- Les notifications push pour être alerté des nouvelles annonces similaires à nos recherches précédentes ou enregistrées
Des conversations intéressantes après un contact
Krista Mollion indique exploiter cette donnée en soumettant les noms à Claude pour repérer les profils intéressants. L'outil classe les profils en trois catégories : les proches, les personnes susceptibles de vouloir lui vendre un service, et les contacts liés au développement commercial ou à la prospection.
Elle dit contacter les profils qui ne cherchent pas à lui présenter une offre commerciale, et selon elle, dans neuf cas sur dix, la conversation est intéressante et constructive. Parmi les cas cités figurent une personne chargée d'organiser un sommet en ligne qui recherche des intervenants, et un animateur qui vérifiait si son profil correspondait à son podcast.
« Ce bouton stalker, le Frequent Viewer, est un moyen de repérer ces observateurs invisibles qui vous envisagent pour une opportunité »
Pour un utilisateur ordinaire, ce signal peut servir à prendre contact avec un recruteur en phase de recrutement pour un poste.
Source : Wired

articles.title: Samsung, LG y Amazon responden al rastreo de usuarios en TV: “Ningún audio se envía a la nube sin la palabra de activación”
articles.text:
Después de que LG fuera señalada por presuntas prácticas de vigilancia a través de sus televisores inteligentes, el medio The Verge decidió ampliar la pesquisa y envió un cuestionario de respuesta directa (sí o no) a los principales fabricantes de televisores y plataformas de streaming: Amazon, Apple, Google, Hisense, LG, Panasonic, Roku, Samsung, Sony, TCL y Vizio.
El objetivo era simple: determinar con precisión qué datos recogen estos dispositivos dentro de los hogares, sin que las compañías pudieran escudarse en políticas de privacidad ambiguas.
Las respuestas, recopiladas por el medio estadounidense, revelan un panorama donde la recolección de datos es prácticamente universal, aunque con matices importantes entre una marca y otra.
Qué compañías de televisores usan micrófonos para escuchar en los hogares
La primera pregunta de The Verge apuntó al corazón de la preocupación de los usuarios: si los micrófonos integrados en televisores y controles remotos se activan para captar sonido ambiente. La mayoría de las empresas coincidió en que la escucha solo ocurre tras una activación explícita.
Samsung fue categórica al respecto. “Los televisores Samsung no escuchan ni graban conversaciones privadas”, respondió la compañía, que precisó que el micrófono integrado “solo escucha localmente la palabra de activación específica (como ‘Hola, Bixby’) e ignora todos los demás sonidos”.
Amazon ofreció una explicación similar sobre sus dispositivos Fire TV. La empresa aseguró que “ningún audio se almacena o se envía a la nube a menos que el dispositivo detecte la palabra de activación” y recordó que los controles remotos con micrófono físico “están diseñados para funcionar solo cuando se presiona físicamente el botón del micrófono”.
LG, el fabricante que motivó la investigación, detalló que el reconocimiento de voz “está desactivado por defecto y funciona solo si el usuario ha optado por aceptar el Acuerdo de Información de Voz”. La compañía agregó que, si no se detecta ninguna palabra de activación, “el audio se procesa localmente, se elimina rápidamente y no se almacena, se convierte en texto ni se transmite”.
En este punto conviene una precisión que responde directamente a la inquietud de millones de usuarios: los televisores inteligentes no graban conversaciones completas del hogar de forma constante. Los micrófonos permanecen en espera pasiva y solo se activan ante una palabra clave o la pulsación de un botón, según detallaron la mayoría de los fabricantes consultados.
Es menester señalar que Hisense, Panasonic, Sony y Vizio no respondieron a esta pregunta ni a buena parte del cuestionario.
Cómo el reconocimiento automático de contenido rastrea lo que se mira en pantalla
Otro de los ejes de la investigación fue el reconocimiento automático de contenido, conocido como ACR por sus siglas en inglés, una tecnología que permite a los televisores identificar qué programas, películas o canales están siendo vistos en tiempo real.
Google explicó que “el software de la plataforma Google TV no utiliza el Reconocimiento Automático de Contenido (ACR) para capturar vídeo en pantalla o capturas de pantalla”, aunque aclaró que los fabricantes de hardware de terceros sí pueden instalar software ACR adicional por su cuenta.
LG detalló el mecanismo técnico detrás de esta herramienta: “ACR en los televisores LG no recopila ni almacena capturas de pantalla, imágenes de pantalla, grabaciones de pantalla o grabaciones de vídeo del televisor. En su lugar, utiliza huellas dactilares de audio generadas a partir del contenido de audio”.
Samsung confirmó que esta función, denominada Servicios de Información de Visualización, “está desactivada por defecto” y que los usuarios “deben habilitarlo afirmativamente” para que opere. La compañía también precisó que, una vez desactivado el servicio, “cualquier dato ACR recopilado anteriormente se elimina de nuestros servidores”.
TCL fue más escueta, aunque reconoció que recopila “datos limitados solo para diagnósticos y mejoras de productos de algunos modelos de televisores inteligentes”, y remarcó que utiliza “la seudonimización para evitar el perfil del usuario”.
Roku, por su parte, indicó que su función Smart TV Experience, capaz de identificar contenido en pantalla, “está desactivada por defecto en los EE. UU. y solo está habilitada si el usuario opta por participar”.
Qué datos personales y de ubicación transmiten los televisores a sus servidores
Más allá del audio y el contenido visualizado, el cuestionario indagó sobre información capaz de identificar la ubicación física y la identidad de los usuarios, un punto donde las respuestas mostraron diferencias relevantes entre fabricantes.
Google fue la compañía más transparente al admitir el alcance de esta recolección: “Google TV transmite la dirección IP pública, los datos de escaneo Wi-Fi (SSID/BSSID) y la configuración regional de la cuenta/dispositivo para determinar la ubicación aproximada o precisa del dispositivo”.
Samsung negó explícitamente este tipo de prácticas. “Los televisores Samsung no recopilan ni transmiten coordenadas GPS, SSID Wi-Fi o su dirección física”, sostuvo la empresa, que reconoció únicamente la transmisión de la dirección IP pública “para la comunicación en red y la detección general de la región”.
LG explicó que, cuando ACR está habilitado, “la dirección IP del televisor y la información sobre las redes Wi-Fi cercanas, como las direcciones MAC y la intensidad de la señal, se pueden utilizar para estimar la ubicación aproximada del televisor”.
Sobre los datos personales, Google admitió que, debido a que su plataforma “requiere una cuenta de Google para la funcionalidad inteligente”, se accede y almacena “información del perfil vinculado (nombre, correo electrónico, edad, sexo)”. Samsung, en cambio, afirmó que sus televisores “no recopilan/almacenan ni transmiten nombre, edad, género, orientación o información demográfica”.
TCL aclaró que, si un usuario crea una cuenta en un televisor con Google TV de la marca, “recopila una dirección de correo electrónico y la edad para confirmar que el usuario es un adulto”, aunque remarcó que “la práctica de TCL no es recopilar información de identificación personal de sus televisores”.
Cómo opera el almacenamiento en la nube de los datos recolectados
Varias compañías confirmaron que la información recopilada no permanece únicamente en el dispositivo, sino que se transfiere y almacena en servidores externos, incluso de terceros proveedores.
Amazon reconoció que “la información transmitida a la nube de Amazon está encriptada en tránsito y almacenada de forma segura”. LG fue más específica al detallar que datos como “las direcciones IP, los identificadores a nivel de dispositivo” y la información de cuenta “se almacena en la nube de LG u otros servidores remotos”.
TCL reveló que recurre a infraestructura externa para este fin: “La información limitada descrita anteriormente se almacena con proveedores de servicios en la nube, incluidos Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure y Google Cloud”.
Samsung aseguró que su manejo de datos incluye protecciones técnicas adicionales, al indicar que “la información descrita anteriormente se almacena en forma cifrada o hash dentro de una infraestructura segura en la nube administrada por Samsung”.
Si es posible desactivar la recolección de datos y borrar el historial
Un punto central de la investigación fue determinar si los usuarios tienen control real sobre esta recopilación, y si pueden revertirla una vez otorgado el consentimiento inicial.
Google fue tajante en este aspecto: “Los usuarios no pueden optar por no recibir el 100% de la transmisión de datos mientras están conectados a Internet”, aunque remarcó que esa limitación se circunscribe a “la telemetría esencial del sistema”, necesaria para la operación básica del dispositivo.
LG explicó que existe una vía para interrumpir por completo los servicios inteligentes: “Los usuarios pueden detener la transmisión de datos personales asociados con los servicios de televisión inteligente retirando su aceptación de la Política de Privacidad o los Términos de Uso”, aunque esto implica perder el acceso a esas funciones.
Sobre el derecho al olvido, Apple remitió a un canal centralizado de gestión: “Los usuarios de todo el mundo pueden eliminar los datos asociados a su cuenta en la página de datos y privacidad de Apple en privacy.apple.com”. Google ofreció una respuesta equivalente, al señalar que los usuarios pueden “eliminar permanentemente su historial de actividad, grabaciones de voz y datos de búsqueda personalizados a través del portal Google My Activity”.
Roku indicó que habilitó un canal específico para estas solicitudes: “Los usuarios pueden enviar una solicitud de eliminación en privacy.roku.com, y la procesamos de acuerdo con la ley aplicable”.
Finalmente, sobre si la desconexión a internet detiene por completo el envío de datos, Samsung fue clara: “Un televisor sin acceso a Internet no puede transmitir datos a Samsung”.
TCL coincidió con esa lógica al afirmar que “desconectar un televisor TCL de Internet impide que los datos se envíen a servidores remotos”, aunque varias compañías, entre ellas Amazon y Google, reconocieron que cierta información diagnóstica queda almacenada localmente hasta que la conexión se restablece.

articles.title: Logitech Gives Employees a Paid Day Off to Play Games, Just in Time for GTA 6
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 11th 2026
Logitech Gives Employees a Paid Day Off to Play Games, Just in Time for GTA 6
Logitech employees are getting a day off just to play video games. The company has announced "Logi Game Day," which it calls the first company-wide gaming day in its history, pitched as a way to recognize the cognitive and professional benefits of gaming. Logitech G will host a streaming event at its Americas headquarters in San Jose on November 19, which happens to be the day GTA 6 launches on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. Logitech G general manager Robin Piispanen will host it.
Employees aren't locked into GTA 6, though Piispanen does name-drop it in the press release alongside Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 and Forza. CEO Hanneke Faber framed the whole thing as a push against an old stigma, saying that it's time to retire the stereotype that gaming is a waste of time. Logitech also points to its own Ctrl Tomorrow study (coming from a gaming peripheral maker, of course), where 81% of gamers said gaming builds real-world confidence, reduces anxiety, and helps their day-to-day work performance.Logitech isn't the only company making room for GTA 6. Various reports have pointed to other businesses preparing for the much-anticipated launch. California tuning shop Burger Motorsports is shutting down for the day, and HR software firm BambooHR reportedly saw time-off requests for November 19 jump by 9% to 17% compared to a typical third Thursday in November. GTA 6 is already the most pre-ordered game ever on both the PlayStation Store and the Microsoft Store, and console owners have been able to pre-load it since November 10. PC players, meanwhile, are going to have to wait for a while.

articles.title: I wore the Google Fitbit Edge for a week, and even though its GPS is a little ropey, its wellness and fitness tracking smarts won me over
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
The Google Fitbit Edge is a simple band-based tracker that harkens back to Fitbits of yore — notably the Charge and Luxe series. While I dislike the Google Health app, which has difficulty surfacing historic numbers on its free tier, and is overly reliant on its chatbot for its premium tier, the band is comfortable and unobtrusive. Its tactile button offers just the right amount of interaction to be useful, and not enough to be distracting. GPS and resulting metrics are a little wobbly, but for most people looking for an activity tracker for sports, the gym, and the occasional jog or bike ride, the Edge will do the trick.
Reasons to buy
- + Affordable
- + Clean, simple UI
- + 7-day battery life
- + Accurate fitness, health and automatic activity tracking
Reasons to avoid
- - GPS and pace aren’t 1-1 accurate compared with top trackers
- - Messy Google Health app orientated around premium chatbot service
Why you can trust TechRadar
We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.
Google Fitbit Edge: Two-minute review
The Google Fitbit Edge occupies a middle tier in Google’s new wearables lineup. On the lowest tier you’ve got the Google Fitbit Air, Google's cheapest tracker, and a screenless Whoop competitor, which collects information and displays it all in the Google Health app, with no interaction on-wrist.
At the other end of the spectrum you have the all-singing, all-dancing Google Pixel Watch 5, with its bright domed interactive AMOLED display and full Wear OS functionality. It’s the most interactive a Google wearable can get without you duct-taping one of the new Googlebooks onto your wrist.
In the middle, but leaning more towards the Fitbit Air end of the spectrum, is the Google Fitbit Edge. It’s got a touchscreen like the Pixel Watch 5 (though it's not as bright), GPS (missing on the Air), and a tactile button, enabling interactions such as media control and simple notification viewing, but not nearly as much as the Google Pixel Watch series. You can also swap straps to make it look more jewelry-like or watch-like.
On the other hand, it automatically detects workouts like the Fitbit Air, lasts a week between charges, doesn’t offer watch features like NFC payments or call management, and is very lightweight.
If you've used a Fitbit Charge or a Fitbit Luxe in the past, you’ll be familiar with the Google Fitbit Edge’s shtick. The screen enables you to pick and choose your workout starting point, manually pause or stop it, set timers, start an ECG scan, and offers other key functionalities. It inherently makes it more useful, while not being engaging enough to tempt you to tinker with it, or make it feel like a second phone. Meanwhile, it hums away in the background offering Health Guardian features like Blood Pressure Trends, Irregular Rhythm Notification, and Insulin Resistance estimations.
The Edge has a slightly different sensor array to the Air, which is capable of delivering ECG scans and detecting ambient light, so it can brighten or dim the screen as required. The Edge’s heart-rate sensor is very accurate, consistently recording readings within 5bpm of the Garmin Fenix 9 Pro (which sports Garmin’s Elevate V5 sensor, which we’ve thoroughly tested for accuracy across a multitude of different Garmins) during workouts in my testing. Sleep scores were a little more varied, sometimes matching up to the Garmin very closely, and other times being off by 10 points or so.
While sleep stats diverged a little, the Fitbit Edge’s biggest accuracy letdown during my testing was GPS and resulting information, such as pace. I documented my first test run, in which the Edge overestimated the pace and distance I ran compared to the (tested and accurate) Garmin Fenix 9 Pro, and this happened consistently. On every run, the Fitbit assumed I was running faster and further than the Garmin, usually by around 0.5km.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
However, for every other performance-based metric, the Edge was great, with automatic activity tracking in particular being very accurate. I was initially confused, as I was expecting an activity to show up on the screen, and it didn’t do so. However, once I checked the Google Health app, the activity was there in full.
The Google Health app is my other big sticking point — I covered it in my Fitbit Air review, but I dislike the AI-forward nature of it. It’s clearly built to be used alongside the premium Google Health Coach chatbot, with precious little functionality, and buried metrics, for free users.
I like the Edge. It’s well-priced, it performs well, it's unobtrusive and it's comfortable. Those looking for an old-school Fitbit will feel right at home — until they get to the app.
Google Fitbit Edge: Specifications
| Component | Google Fitbit Edge | 
| Price | $179.99 / £159.99 / AU$269 | 
| Dimension | 11.58 x 39.22 x 25.56mm | 
| Weight | 17.7g without band | 
| Case/bezel | 100% recycled aluminium | 
| Display | 1.3-in always-on AMOLED | 
| Processor | Ambiq AP5 MCU | 
| GPS | GPS, Galileo, GLONASS, BeiDou, QZSS | 
| Battery life | Up to 7 days | 
| Connections | Bluetooth 5.4 | 
| Water resistant | 5ATM | 
Google Fitbit Edge: Price and availability
- $179.99 / £159.99 / AU$269
- Priced higher than the Google Fitbit Air, around the same as the old Charges
- It goes up against the Garmin Cirqa, Forerunner 70, and Apple Watch SE 3
The Google Fitbit Air costs $179.99 / £159.99 / AU$269, which isn’t a bad price for what you're getting. That's similar to what the GPS-equipped Fitbit Charge series used to cost, and considering we’re in a components crisis at the moment, I’m pleased that Google has kept the price fairly low.
However, competition is fierce at this price point, with the Edge going up against the Garmin Cirqa (my pick for this year’s best fitness tracker), the Apple Watch SE 3, the Samsung Galaxy Watch9 and the Garmin Forerunner 70 running watch. All of these devices, I would say, are better performers in some respects than the Fitbit, but not all of them are as sleek or unobtrusive.
Runners should opt for the Forerunner 70, while Apple users will get more out of the SE 3. For those looking for an all-round, simple-to-use fitness tracker, the Google Fitbit Edge might be ideal if you want a screen for media playback control, timers, manual workout settings or simply checking your step count.
Google Fitbit Edge: Scorecard
| Category | Comment | Score | 
| Value | Well priced in the same bracket as its predecessors. | 4/5 | 
| Design | Thoughtful and sleek, with great band options. | 4.5/5 | 
| Features | A bit limited in both hardware and software, but GPS and ECG are good to see. | 3/5 | 
| Performance | Some accuracy issues when it comes to sleep and GPS, but not enough to stop me recommending it to exercisers who are more concerned with general trends than in-depth metrics. | 3.5/5 | 
Google Fitbit Edge: Should I buy?
Buy it if…
You want a ‘set and forget’ tracker
Automatic activity detection is excellent.
Don’t buy it if…
You’re a dedicated runner
The GPS inaccuracy throws off pacing a bit, which means a dedicated running watch is a better choice.
You don’t like the app
The Google Health app is built around Google's premium chatbot service, and limited at the free tier.
Google Fitbit Edge: Also consider
Garmin Cirqa
The best screenless fitness tracker, at a similar price to the Edge.
Read our full Garmin Cirqa review
Google Fitbit Edge: How I tested
I wore the Fitbit Edge for a week on my right wrist, with the Garmin Fenix 9 Pro on my left. Using the Garmin as a benchmark, I compared sleep scores, workout metrics, heart-rate readings, step counts and more. I also drained the battery on the Fitbit Edge to check that performance was as claimed.
First reviewed: November 2026
Matt is TechRadar's expert on all things fitness, wellness and wearable tech.
A former staffer at Men's Health, he holds a Master's Degree in journalism from Cardiff and has written for brands like Runner's World, Women's Health, Men's Fitness, LiveScience and Fit&Well on everything fitness tech, exercise, nutrition and mental wellbeing.
He is the author of the upcoming book The Health Data Heist, set to be published by Bloomsbury in 2027. When he’s not training or writing about health and fitness, he can be found reading doorstop-thick fantasy books with lots of fictional maps in them.

articles.title: Les montres connectées sous WearOS et Apple Watch peuvent désormais utiliser Muse, l'IA de Meta
articles.text:
Votre montre connectée va pouvoir faire office de télécommande pour interagir avec l'assistant Muse de Meta, une fonction attendue par certains utilisateurs, et bien pratique.
L'agent IA Muse de Meta poursuit son déploiement. Après un mode vocal permettant des interactions similaires à Gemini Live, ajouté la semaine dernière, Meta veut porter son agent jusqu'à votre poignet. L'application est d'ores et déjà disponible sur les montres sous Wear OS et Apple Watch.
Trois modes d'entrée disponibles
L'annonce a été faite ce 11 novembre par le compte officiel de Muse sur X, au moyen d'une image montrant la mascotte de l'agent portant des montres connectées. Selon la publication, Meta indique que Muse peut désormais fonctionner « en continu » directement depuis le poignet de l'utilisateur.
D'après les visuels partagés, les utilisateurs disposent de trois modes de saisie sur la montre : texte, dictée et conversation vocale. Selon nos confrères de chez Gadgets and Wearables, les utilisateurs d'Apple Watch bénéficient également d'un raccourci sur le cadran de la montre pour accéder directement à l'application. Cette fonctionnalité n'est pas encore disponible sur Wear OS.
La montre comme télécommande
Une précision est toutefois importante : l'agent ne s'exécute pas sur la montre connectée. L'application joue un simple rôle de poste de commande distant, mais les tâches restent traitées depuis le smartphone. L'utilisateur peut ainsi approuver des tâches ou consulter l'avancement d'une tâche en cours, depuis sa montre.
Pour le reste, la mascotte Muse occupe une majeure partie de l'écran lors des interactions.
Muse est capable d'effectuer des paiements pour le compte de l'utilisateur. Toutefois, Meta n'a pas encore précisé s'il serait possible de valider directement des transactions avec sa montre connectée, ou si une confirmation via un smartphone resterait nécessaire.
Source : AndroidAuthority

articles.title: First Photos of Intel's 256-Core Xeon 7 "Diamond Rapids" Package Surface
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 11th 2026
First Photos of Intel's 256-Core Xeon 7 "Diamond Rapids" Package Surface
Intel's Xeon 7 "Diamond Rapids" seems to have made its first public appearance as actual silicon. Intel had two packages on display at the Tencent Global Digital Ecosystem Conference in Shenzhen on October 29, one showing the heat spreader and the other flipped to show the contact side, though photos of them are only now making the rounds. These chips are meant for the massive LGA 9324 socket on Intel's Oak Stream platform, and the bottom side shows a huge pad area to match.
The specs themselves aren't new, since Intel detailed the package design at HOT CHIPS back in August. The flagship packs up to 256 Panther Cove P-cores without SMT, spread across 16 compute chiplets built on Intel 18A-P, along with 1.28 GB of last-level cache. It also gets 16 memory channels with MRDIMM support up to 12,800 MT/s and 128 PCIe Gen 6 lanes. At the event, Intel pitched Diamond Rapids as a CPU designed for agentic AI infrastructure and reportedly announced joint development with Tencent Cloud for its CVM instances. The new Tencent Cloud instances launched at the same event, however, run on Xeon 6+ "Clearwater Forest" chips.Diamond Rapids is still slated for 2027, and partners are already getting ready, with ASRock Rack showing an early motherboard with 16 DIMM slots at OCP. AMD, meanwhile, made its 6th Gen EPYC "Venice" processors generally available this week, so Intel's 256-core chip will arrive well after its main rival is already shipping. Multithreading only returns to Xeon in 2028 with Coral Rapids.
Sources:

articles.title: Gemini ya funciona en CarPlay: Google permite conversar con su IA en el auto desde el iPhone
articles.text:
Google lanzó la app de Gemini para CarPlay, el sistema que muestra las aplicaciones del iPhone en la pantalla del auto. Desde el 11 de noviembre, los conductores pueden mantener conversaciones por voz con el asistente de inteligencia artificial sin tocar el teléfono, según anunció la empresa.
La compañía informó que el despliegue es mundial y alcanza a todos los usuarios de Gemini en iOS, en todos los idiomas que admite Gemini Live, el modo de conversación por voz del asistente.
Para usarlo hay que actualizar la app de Gemini en el iPhone, activar el permiso del micrófono y haber usado Gemini Live en el teléfono al menos una vez. Después, al conectar el iPhone al auto, basta tocar el ícono de Gemini en la pantalla.
Qué se le puede pedir al asistente en el auto
La interfaz es simple: muestra una onda que indica si el asistente escucha, piensa o responde, con botones para terminar o silenciar, según describió 9to5Google. El conductor puede interrumpir una respuesta para agregar un detalle, cambiar de tema o hacer una pausa.
Google propone usos como pedir el resumen del día, preparar una reunión o practicar una presentación. Como Gemini se conecta con Gmail y Google Calendar, también permite escuchar un resumen de los correos sin leer y redactar una respuesta con la voz.
Google explicó su idea en el anuncio: el trayecto diario al trabajo promedia cerca de una hora al volante, y las asistentes de voz solían servir para tareas rápidas, como reproducir música o pedir indicaciones. La empresa quiere que ese tiempo sirva también para ponerse al día o preparar lo que viene.
MacRumors citó otro ejemplo del anuncio: preguntar por un lugar donde almorzar rápido en el centro de una ciudad. El asistente responde con datos personalizados cuando el usuario lo pide.
Las conversaciones se sincronizan con la app del iPhone. Los resúmenes, notas e ideas quedan en el historial de chats cuando el usuario estaciona, y también puede retomarse un chat reciente desde la pantalla del auto.
Una función que no llega igual a todos
El resumen diario, llamado Daily Brief, debe activarse antes de usarse. Google precisó que algunas funciones de personalización no están disponibles para menores de 18 años ni en el Espacio Económico Europeo ni en Nigeria.
Gemini ya estaba en CarPlay de forma limitada. El 21 de octubre, Google activó un asistente conversacional dentro de Google Maps para la navegación, primero en Estados Unidos, según informaron 9to5Google y The Verge. La app que llegó ahora ofrece la conversación completa, no solo la ayuda para rutas.
CarPlay admite aplicaciones de IA conversacional por voz desde iOS 26.4, según MacRumors. Ese medio señaló que ya habían lanzado su versión ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, Copilot y Perplexity, entre otras. 9to5Mac agregó a Meta AI a esa lista y describió a Gemini como el último gran asistente que faltaba.
El medio alemán heise informó el 23 de octubre que la versión mejorada de Siri todavía no estaba disponible en los autos europeos por razones regulatorias.
Google informó que el despliegue comenzó el 11 de noviembre. 9to5Mac señaló ese mismo día que la actualización de la app aún no aparecía en la tienda, aunque esperaba que llegara en cuestión de horas.

articles.title: Confidential computing and AI agents push KubeVirt VMs forward - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
A decade in, KubeVirt pushes virtual machines into the AI agent era
Confidential computing is drawing fresh interest as enterprises weigh where their most sensitive AI workloads can safely run. That shift is giving virtual machines a new role alongside containers on Kubernetes, rather than a slow retirement.
The timing lines up with a milestone for KubeVirt, the open-source project that runs VMs inside Kubernetes clusters, which graduated from the Cloud Native Computing Foundation this week. Its maintainers are now steering the project toward AI isolation, agent sandboxes and confidential computing, a long-standing technology that is regaining momentum, according to Itamar Holder (pictured, left), principal software engineer and KubeVirt maintainer at Red Hat Inc.
“I think it’s one of the blockers for a lot of companies to join public cloud in general, like companies that really care about super sensitive data,” Holder said. “I think it unblocks them to join.”
Holder and Vladik Romanovsky (right), technical lead and KubeVirt maintainer at Red Hat, spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier and Rebecca Knight at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon NA, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how KubeVirt is evolving from a virtualization tool into an operating layer for AI workloads. (* Disclosure below.)
Confidential computing and the new case for VMs on Kubernetes
KubeVirt’s core idea is running VMs and containers on the same Kubernetes cluster without maintaining two separate stacks. That pairing matters more in the AI era, with Nvidia Corp. developers helping the project integrate dynamic resource allocation for GPU hardware, Holder noted. Romanovsky sees the two forms of compute as partners rather than rivals.
“VMs will do kind of the heavy lifting and larger isolation, and the pods that are running around them would provide a better scaling for cache applications,” Romanovsky said. “In general, it belongs together. VMs and containers can run as one application as well.”
The project is also eyeing a role in AI agent sandboxing, an area where Red Hat is building out infrastructure. The maintainers want KubeVirt to become another isolation backend for the Kubernetes agent sandbox repository, Holder explained.
“I think that we can offer a lot of benefits that other isolation backends don’t have,” Holder said. “We can use live migration and complex hardware configurations with DRA and a lot of other sweet stuff.”

articles.title: SpaceX plans 35-turbine, 748MW power plant for $24B Texas AI center
articles.text:
SpaceX plans massive $24 billion gas-powered Texas data center — application for 35 natural gas turbines and a capacity of 748 megawatts comes despite rising opposition in the state
SpaceX to build a huge AI data center and power plant in Texas
- SpaceX wants 748 megawatts of dedicated power for its Texas computing complex
- 35 gas turbines put SpaceX's Texas power application under environmental scrutiny
- Texas governor-elect promised moratorium could complicate future data center approvals in the state
SpaceX is seeking regulatory approval to build a natural-gas power facility for its planned $24 billion artificial-intelligence computing complex in Texas.
The application covers 35 natural gas turbines with a combined electricity generation capacity of 748 megawatts (MW).
The project will be located in Starbase, where SpaceX operates its rocket launch facilities, and includes plans for the company to develop and operate both facilities.
SpaceX plans dedicated power generation for its Texas computing facility
The proposed development would allow SpaceX to generate electricity independently rather than rely entirely on connections to Texas's main power grid.
This could help the company avoid delays associated with securing sufficient grid capacity for its computing operations.
The Starbase City Commission is scheduled to consider a development agreement and proposed property tax incentives on December 9 2026.
The company is also pursuing natural gas infrastructure in Texas and Florida to transport fuel for its Starship rocket program.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
According to Bloomberg, SpaceX is exploring another gas-fired power plant near Houston to supply electricity to Terafab, an AI semiconductor complex it plans to develop with Tesla.
The 748 MW application adds another major natural gas generation project to SpaceX's expanding infrastructure plans.
However, the company will still need to satisfy applicable environmental and development requirements before proceeding with construction.
Hinojosa's election victory raises uncertainty over future data center approvals
SpaceX's application comes shortly after Democrat Gina Hinojosa defeated three-term Republican Governor Greg Abbott in the recent US midterm election.
Her campaign included proposals to restrict new data center development due to concerns about their effects on household utility costs.
Hinojosa argued large computing facilities were increasing pressure on electricity and water supplies, particularly in rural communities.
"When I become governor, I will prohibit all approvals for data center construction until a law is passed to protect Texans from data centers," she said.
Hinojosa also pledged to "eliminate tax incentives for data center construction and require disclosure of electricity and water consumption."
There are reports that SpaceX is seeking tax incentives and other financial concessions from local authorities, although Hinojosa's proposed restrictions could complicate those efforts once she assumes office.
Hinojosa is expected to assume office in January 2027, potentially introducing a different regulatory approach to technology infrastructure projects.
Opposition to large computing developments is also emerging in other parts of the United States.
According to regulatory intelligence firm RegLayer, at least 47 major data center construction projects encountered permitting delays or organized opposition from residents during 2026.
The disputes involve concerns about electricity costs, water consumption and the local consequences of accommodating facilities with substantial infrastructure requirements.
SpaceX's proposed natural gas installation could address some electricity supply constraints, although its emissions and environmental permitting requirements may attract additional scrutiny.

articles.title: Nintendo DMCA Notice Takes Down 144 Switch Modchip Firmware Repos on GitHub
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 11th 2026
Nintendo DMCA Notice Takes Down 144 Switch Modchip Firmware Repos on GitHub
GitHub has disabled 144 repositories hosting Nintendo Switch modchip firmware following a DMCA notice from Nintendo of America. The notice, dated November 6 and posted to GitHub's public DMCA archive this week, names a single repository called Ansem-SoD/Picofly. Because its fork network had more than 100 repositories and Nintendo claimed that all or most of the forks infringed to the same extent, GitHub took the entire network down. The targeted firmware covers SX Core, SX Lite, Picofly, and HWFLY chips, among others.
Patched consoles like the Switch Lite and Switch OLED need a soldered modchip that glitches the boot process to run custom software. Nintendo says this firmware lets modchips "illegally circumvent Nintendo's TPMs" by bypassing the boot sequence, which makes distributing it trafficking in circumvention technology under the DMCA. The notice also cites the U.S. criminal case against Team-Xecuter, whose member Gary Bowser pleaded guilty in 2021. A guilty plea isn't a ruling that modchips are illegal, of course, but Nintendo doesn't have to prove that for GitHub to act on a DMCA notice. Chips that are already installed keep working, while owners lose an easy source for firmware updates and flashing new chips.This seems to be the first time Nintendo has gone after modchip firmware on GitHub. It also seems to have missed a few spots, as several other repositories with Picofly and HWFLY firmware are reportedly still up. This action comes about six weeks after a court ordered a Reddit moderator to pay Nintendo $4.5 million over piracy, and right after Switch 2 firmware 23.5.0 reportedly patched that console's first software-only jailbreak. The modchip method doesn't work on the Switch 2, so this takedown is aimed squarely at the original Switch.

articles.title: Aerolínea estadounidense prohibió que los asistentes de IA reserven vuelos en nombre de los pasajeros
articles.text:
United Airlines prohibió el 11 de noviembre de 2026 que asistentes de inteligencia artificial de terceros busquen, reserven o compren vuelos en nombre de los pasajeros.
La restricción será aplicada por la aerolínea estadounidense tanto en su sitio web y su aplicación como mediante agencias de viajes y buscadores de tarifas.
La empresa explicó que compartir las credenciales de la cuenta con asistentes externos puede exponer información sensible. Según la compañía, esas herramientas también pueden provocar compras que el cliente no quería, cambios en la cuenta o el uso de millas del programa MileagePlus sin su aprobación.
La aerolínea citó un problema regulatorio. El registro automático en un vuelo exige que una persona confirme que su equipaje no lleva sustancias prohibidas, como explosivos.
Si lo hace un asistente de IA podría violar normas de la Administración Federal de Aviación y del Departamento de Transporte de Estados Unidos.
Las reservas que un asistente hizo antes del 11 de noviembre de 2026 no se cancelarán. La aerolínea recomienda revisarlas y cambiar de inmediato la contraseña de MileagePlus a quien haya entregado esos datos a una herramienta de IA.
Qué sigue permitido y qué queda fuera
Los pasajeros todavía pueden usar IA para investigar o planear un viaje, siempre que la herramienta no entre al sitio web ni a la aplicación.
La empresa aclaró que la tecnología de asistencia para personas con discapacidad no está afectada. Pidió no darle a un chatbot números de confirmación ni claves.
Las agencias y las plataformas de reservas tampoco pueden usar agentes de IA de terceros para buscar, reservar o gestionar viajes de la aerolínea, salvo con permiso de la empresa. Hoy la compañía no trabaja con ninguno. Dice que quiere integraciones estándar, con protecciones de privacidad, seguridad y responsabilidad.
El Wall Street Journal indicó que los agentes aún pueden mostrar vuelos y tarifas, pero no cerrar la compra en el sitio de la aerolínea.
El diario también señaló que la aerolínea ve poca actividad de reservas hechas por agentes y que sus sistemas distinguen si compró una persona, una agencia o un asistente automático.
La empresa indicó que actualizará su centro de confianza digital para explicar las restricciones y que seguirá evaluando cómo interactúan estos asistentes con sus servicios a medida que evolucionen.
Una industria dividida frente a los agentes
Esta es la primera aerolínea de Estados Unidos que dice de forma explícita que bloqueará estos asistentes, según Skift. El mismo medio recuerda que el director ejecutivo, Scott Kirby, afirmó en un evento en Chicago: “No quiero crear otro intermediario”, según el Wall Street Journal. El de Delta, Ed Bastian, se dijo “cauteloso”.
Henry Harteveldt, analista de aviación de Atmosphere Research Group, dijo a CBS News que la compañía no quiere sumar un intermediario “potencialmente aún más poderoso” que Google, los comparadores de precios y las agencias en línea. Agregó que cada búsqueda de vuelos cuesta dinero a las aerolíneas, y que una oleada de búsquedas de robots elevaría ese gasto.
Otras empresas eligieron el camino contrario. Southwest permite que los usuarios de ChatGPT vean sus vuelos disponibles, y Expedia y Booking trabajan con OpenAI, según Reuters. Amazon bloqueó a Muse, el asistente de Meta, mientras que Walmart se asoció con esa herramienta.
Para el pasajero, Harteveldt no prevé cambios en la búsqueda de precios: los vuelos de de esta aerolínea estadounidense seguirán disponibles en Kayak, Hopper y Google Flights, y no será más difícil encontrar buenas tarifas. Tampoco será más fácil hacerlo con asistentes de IA, agregó.
En plataformas como Google Flights, los usuarios pueden seguir utilizando la inteligencia artificial para filtrar costos, pero no permite la compra de boletos.

articles.title: Model fine-tuning on Kubernetes: Google's OpenRL explained - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Google’s GKE Labs turns reinforcement learning into a Kubernetes workload
Model fine-tuning through reinforcement learning is fast becoming one of the most demanding jobs in AI infrastructure. It mixes training, inference and sandboxed agent work in a single loop, often with research code tangled into the systems beneath it.
Google LLC has been tackling that problem from inside its Kubernetes engineering group, and recently donated the result, OpenRL, to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation. The GKE Labs team got there by building an AI agent for Kubernetes tasks, then a benchmark to grade models on that work, according to Sunil Arora (pictured, left), senior software engineer at Google Cloud.
“If you look at reinforcement learning, I think of it as a kind of a super app of AI because it involves training. It involves sampling. It involves agents actually doing things in a sandbox and sometimes kind of evaluating the work,” Arora said. “It’s kind of a very diverse workload and it is, I think, pushing the boundaries of our infrastructure.”
Arora and Justin Santa Barbara (right), developer at Google, spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier and Rebecca Knight at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon NA, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed model fine-tuning and their work in GKE Labs, which puts experimental projects in users’ hands early. (* Disclosure below.)
Model fine-tuning without the infrastructure tangle
OpenRL debuted as a research preview in June 2026, offering a self-hosted training API for a company’s own Kubernetes cluster. It splits the reinforcement learning loop from the compute plumbing, so infrastructure engineers handle scaling while researchers keep control of experiments, Arora explained.
“With OpenRL, one of the things that we are trying to do is kind of abstracting away the infrastructure as kind of core primitives so that researchers and AI engineers can just focus on their RL loop,” Arora said.
Sandboxes are where that loop meets agent infrastructure, since calculating rewards can mean running millions of isolated commands. Google’s Agent Substrate packs more of those sandboxes onto limited compute, according to Arora. For Santa Barbara, the need surfaced one step at a time.
“We built kubectl-ai, and in theory, kubectl-ai could have formatted my hard disk,” Santa Barbara said. “I would quite like a sandbox for this so that if it formats a hard disk, it formats that sandbox and no damage.”

Le TCL C69K Pro est la nouvelle version avec pied central du TCL C69K de 2025. Il mise toujours sur sa dalle Mini-Led 144 Hz, son système son intégré et son rapport qualité-prix.
Avec le C69K Pro (ou C6K Pro selon les revendeurs), TCL renouvelle son téléviseur Mini-Led d'entrée de gamme en 2026, mais sans véritable changement côté technique. Ce nouveau modèle est en effet identique au C69K (C6K) de 2025, qui proposait déjà un rapport qualité-prix intéressant pour ceux qui souhaitent profiter de la technologie Mini-Led sans se ruiner. La seule différence se trouve du côté du design, puisque les deux pieds latéraux en V de l'ancien modèle laissent désormais place à un pied central, plus pratique pour installer le téléviseur sur un meuble relativement étroit.
Pour le reste, on retrouve donc la même dalle LCD HVA Ultra HD 4K avec un rétroéclairage Mini-Led et un taux de rafraîchissement pouvant atteindre 144 Hz. Le téléviseur conserve également sa compatibilité HDR10+ et Dolby Vision, ainsi que Google TV pour accéder aux principaux services de streaming. Le système audio signé Onkyo est lui aussi toujours de la partie, ce qui est plutôt une bonne nouvelle tant il nous avait surpris sur le modèle de 2025.
TCL propose son C69K Pro aux tarifs suivants :
Des prix qui restent accessibles pour des téléviseurs Mini-Led, même si la concurrence est désormais particulièrement rude sur ce segment. Vous trouverez ci-dessous l'essentiel de notre test, repris de celui du C69K.
Le principal changement de cette version Pro concerne le pied. TCL abandonne les deux supports latéraux en V du C69K de 2025 au profit d'un pied central, plus simple à installer sur un meuble étroit. Le reste du design ne change pas, avec des bordures fines et une construction sobre. La connectique comprend quatre prises HDMI, dont deux HDMI 2.1, une sortie audio optique, un port Ethernet, un emplacement CI+, les entrées antenne et satellite, ainsi qu'un unique port USB 3.0. Le wifi et le Bluetooth sont présents, mais on regrette l'absence de prise casque.
L'interface Google TV reste un autre bon point. Fluide et complète, elle donne accès à Netflix, Disney+, Prime Video, myCanal et aux autres grandes plateformes. Chromecast permet de diffuser des contenus depuis un smartphone, tandis que Google Assistant assure la commande vocale. La télécommande, assez longue et non rétroéclairée, reste plus fonctionnelle que séduisante.
Le C69K Pro est plus convaincant pour les joueurs. Sa dalle 144 Hz s'accompagne de quatre ports HDMI, dont deux HDMI 2.1, et de la compatibilité AMD FreeSync Premium Pro. Sur le C69K de 2025, nous avions relevé un input lag de 13,2 ms en 1080p à 60 Hz et de seulement 4,9 ms à 120 Hz. Un excellent résultat qui assure une bonne réactivité, aussi bien sur console que sur PC.
La rémanence de 18 ms est moins flatteuse et pourra provoquer de légères traînées derrière les objets en mouvement. C'est une limite des dalles LCD face aux modèles Oled, nettement plus rapides. La colorimétrie du mode Jeu s'en sort cependant bien. Le delta E SDR atteint 3,4, un peu au-dessus du seuil idéal, mais il descend à 2,3 en HDR. Curieusement, les jeux HDR bénéficient ainsi d'un rendu des couleurs plus fidèle que les films regardés en mode Filmmaker. Dans l'ensemble, le téléviseur dispose des fonctions essentielles pour jouer dans de bonnes conditions, malgré une rémanence perfectible.
Le TCL C69K Pro reprend la dalle LCD HVA Ultra HD du C69K de 2025, avec un rétroéclairage Mini-Led dont nous avions compté 242 zones sur le modèle 65 pouces. Les mesures du précédent modèle restent donc notre référence pour cette version Pro, techniquement identique. En mode Filmmaker, la colorimétrie SDR est excellente, avec un delta E moyen de 1,2, bien sous le seuil à partir duquel les dérives deviennent visibles. La température moyenne des couleurs de 6380 K est également proche des 6500 K recherchés. Le gamma de 2,3 est satisfaisant, même si sa courbe manque de régularité, avec des gris clairs trop lumineux.
La luminosité SDR plafonne à 340 cd/m², une valeur modeste qui peut limiter le confort dans une pièce très éclairée. Le contraste bénéficie du Mini-Led et les noirs sont plus profonds que sur un LCD classique, mais la gestion du rétroéclairage reste assez grossière. On observe ainsi du blooming, ces halos lumineux qui apparaissent autour des objets clairs sur fond sombre. Le clouding est en revanche bien maîtrisé, sans taches lumineuses gênantes sur les aplats uniformes. Les angles de vision ne sont pas non plus son point fort : à 45° de l'axe, la luminosité chute de 75 % et les couleurs se délavent. Il est donc préférable de regarder le téléviseur bien en face.
En HDR, le C69K Pro prend en charge les formats HDR10, HDR10+, HLG et Dolby Vision, mais ses performances sont limitées par un pic lumineux de 580 cd/m² sur une fenêtre de 10 %. Nous sommes loin des 2000 cd/m² du TCL C79K, et plus encore des 3200 cd/m² dépassés par le C89K. Les effets lumineux manquent donc d'intensité et les scènes HDR ne profitent pas de tout le relief attendu. La courbe EOTF reste en dessous de la référence, même si TCL atténue progressivement les hautes lumières pour éviter de perdre les détails les plus clairs.
La précision des couleurs recule aussi en HDR, avec un delta E moyen de 4,1, qui laisse apparaître quelques dérives à l'œil nu. La couverture de 93,7 % du DCI-P3 et de 71,7 % du Rec.2020 reste correcte pour cette gamme de prix, sans rivaliser avec les meilleurs téléviseurs Oled ou QD-Oled. Enfin, le traitement antireflet se montre assez peu efficace : notre mesure de réflectance de 39 % se traduit par des reflets bien visibles dès qu'une fenêtre ou une lampe fait face à l'écran. Pour les films, une pièce peu lumineuse reste donc préférable.
Le système audio signé Onkyo constitue une bonne surprise à ce niveau de prix. Il offre une scène sonore étonnamment large, avec une spatialisation qui donne davantage d'ampleur aux films et aux séries que sur bien des téléviseurs plus chers. Les graves sont présents, mais manquent de précision et deviennent brouillons lorsque l'on pousse le volume. Il ne faut pas non plus attendre de véritables effets de hauteur. Malgré ces limites, cette partie audio est l'un des points forts du C69K Pro. Une barre de son dédiée améliorera encore l'expérience, mais elle n'est pas indispensable pour profiter d'un rendu déjà convaincant au quotidien.
Nos conclusions sur le TCL C69K Pro (ou C6K Pro) sont donc évidemment identiques à celles que nous avions faites sur le C69K premier du nom. C’est un téléviseur Mini-Led intéressant pour les budgets serrés qui profite d'une excellente colorimétrie en SDR, d'une interface Google TV complète, de bonnes performances pour le jeu vidéo et surtout d'un système audio étonnamment convaincant à ce niveau de prix. Il faudra toutefois composer avec quelques limites en matière de qualité d'image. Le pic lumineux HDR reste faible, le blooming est assez marqué et les reflets peuvent rapidement devenir gênants dans une pièce éclairée. Le nouveau pied central apporte un peu de praticité, mais ne change rien aux prestations du téléviseur. Un modèle à considérer pour ceux qui cherchent un Mini-Led abordable, notamment en promotion, mais qui risque de laisser les cinéphiles exigeants sur leur faim.

articles.title: MSI Reportedly Plans RTX 5080 Price Hikes of up to $1,200 in China
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 11th 2026
MSI Reportedly Plans RTX 5080 Price Hikes of up to $1,200 in China
MSI's GeForce RTX 5080 cards could cost up to 8,000 yuan (about $1,200) more in China this month, according to a ChannelGate post shared on X by harukaze5719. The post outlines MSI's November distributor pricing compared to October, with RTX 5080 models going up by 1,300 to 8,000 yuan depending on the card. That's roughly $195 at the low end, while the top figure alone is more than the RTX 5080's entire $999 launch MSRP. Yes, that's apparently a $1,200 increase planned for the RTX 5080 at the top end.
The rest of the RTX 50 stack goes up too. RTX 5070 Ti models rise by 800 to 4,000 yuan (about $120 to $600), and the RTX 5070 by 500 to 1,000 yuan (75 to $150). The RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB picks up 400 yuan, its 8 GB sibling 200 yuan, and the RTX 5060 between 200 and 500 yuan. Even the RTX 3050 gets a 100 yuan bump. These are distributor prices in China, not new MSRPs, and the post doesn't say which RTX 5080 models sit at the top of that range. Colorful and Galax reportedly started sharing similar hikes with their partners earlier this month, so MSI seems to be following the same path. We can certainly expect other AIB partners to follow suit soon.In the U.S., the RTX 5080 already sells for over $2,000 and has since disappeared from NVIDIA's marketplace. A 24 GB RTX 5080 was rumored to arrive early next year, but NVIDIA has reportedly canceled its January 2027 launch over the cost of 3 GB GDDR7 modules. With that card gone and MSI raising prices this much, it's reasonable to expect the 16 GB model to stay expensive for a while.

articles.title: Nvidia's board reportedly preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang after reports of a second affair - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Nvidia’s board reportedly preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang after reports of a second affair
Nvidia Corp.’s board of directors is reportedly preparing to oust its founder and Chief Executive Jensen Huang after reports emerged that he had a second extramarital relationship with an executive at the company, just days after he admitted to an affair with a suspected Chinese spy.
Earlier today, the New York Times said Huang (pictured) was suspected by five people at the company of having an affair with Nvidia Healthcare Vice President Kimberly Powell. Hours later, the Wall Street Journal said Nvidia’s board is preparing to meet on Thursday to discuss Huang’s future at the company, and that all options are on the table, including his possible dismissal.
The Times said Huang and Powell were reportedly captured on camera together being affectionate with one another at a hotel in San Jose, California, in March.
The latest reports come just days after Huang admitted in an email to company employees that he had an extramarital affair with a Chinese woman called Alice Huang, who was formerly the CEO of the Singaporean data center supplier Megaspeed. Alice Huang, of no relation to Nvidia’s CEO, is suspected of working for China’s Ministry of State Security, but it’s not clear if she has passed on any of the company’s secrets.
In response to that report, Nvidia’s board hired the law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to lead an investigation into the affair and try to determine what secrets, if any, were leaked.
Huang reportedly first became involved with the Chinese woman last year, but rumors of an affair between him and Powell have circulated for years. One reason for that is that Powell does not have any background in health or science, despite her high-level role at Nvidia’s Healthcare business.
On Nvidia’s website, Powell’s bio explains that she’s responsible for the company’s healthcare business, “including hardware and software platforms for accelerated computing, AI and visualization that power the ecosystem of medical imaging, life sciences, drug discovery and healthcare analytics.”
The Healthcare business is much smaller than Nvidia’s main data center unit, which accounts for the lion’s share of its multibillion-dollar revenue. It makes chips for medical devices such as MRI machines. The company does not break out sales figures for the unit, instead reporting its revenue within the broader data center business.
Powell appeared at Nvidia’s annual GTC conference in San Jose in March, where she delivered a keynote talking about how the company’s AI technology can help to accelerate drug discovery and enhance clinical efficiency. She has been running the business since 2017.
If Nvidia were to oust Huang, the company that sits at the heart of the artificial intelligence revolution would face an uncertain future. Nvidia is the second most valuable company in the world, controlling around 90% of the global market for computer chips used in AI, becoming a major driving force behind the global economy.
Its brand has become synonymous with Huang, who is involved in all aspects of its business and has appointed family members to key roles in its executive team. Huang is also Nvidia’s largest individual shareholder, holding a 3.56% stake in the company. Should he be ousted, there is no clear successor.
Nvidia’s rise amid the AI boom has made Huang one of the wealthiest and most influential people in the world. He has become a close ally of U.S. President Donald Trump, who was previously told about Huang’s relationship with the suspected Chinese spy but decided to take no action. Trump has come out in defense of Huang, saying that he’s an “honorable man” and that he did not know of the woman’s connections to Chinese intelligence.
Nvidia’s stock fell more than 9% in late trading on Wednesday and is likely to extend its downward trend for a sixth straight week.

articles.title: iFixit dévoile le secret du logo Apple lumineux sur les MacBook Pro OLED
articles.text:
On l'attendait, le démontage des derniers MacBook Pro par iFixit est arrivé. Il révèle le secret du nouveau logo lumineux au dos des ordinateurs portables dernière génération de la marque à la pomme.
Les nouveaux MacBook Pro d'Apple marquent deux premières pour la gamme : l'adoption de la technologie OLED attendue depuis des années, mais aussi, un écran tactile. Ils sont également plus légers que leurs prédécesseurs et voient le retour du logo Apple lumineux au dos des PC portables. Comme à son habitude, iFixit a décortiqué un modèle, afin de voir comment le logo au dos s'allume.
BenQ iScreenBar : la barre lumineuse qui s’accorde avec l’iMac
Des lignes en harmonie avec celles de l’ordinateur d’Apple, une conception rigoureuse, des matériaux sélectionnés, rien n’a été laissé au hasard, tout comme le service qu’elle rend une fois allumée !
Un Mac plus léger, un tout petit peu plus réparable
Le MacBook Pro PROLED à écran tactile pèse 1,82 kg, contre 2,14 kg pour le modèle qu'il remplace. La version 14 pouces affiche quant à elle 1,38 kg sur la balance, à comparer aux 1,60 kg du modèle 14 pouces doté de la puce M5 Pro.
Cette cure de minceur de 203 g au total vient de divers endroits. Le châssis en aluminium perd 92 grammes sur la balance, et l'écran perd 101 grammes, malgré l'intégration du tactile. Le reste étant des économies de poids sur la batterie et le trackpad.
Aussi, l'ouverture de la machine est plus simple qu'auparavant : le capot inférieur ne se fixe plus avec huit vis, mais quatre. Les progrès s'arrêtent là. Vraiment. Selon iFixit, la plupart des composants susceptibles d'être remplacés, à l'image du port USB-C, exigent de retirer la carte mère. D'autres, comme le port HDMI et le SSD, sont soudés à cette dernière et ne peuvent ainsi pas être changés.
OLED vs mini-LED, un vrai changement
L'OLED modifie l'affichage par rapport au mini-LED des autres modèles. Avec une dalle OLEd, chaque pixel génère sa propre lumière. Un écran LCD classique dépend au contraire d'un rétro-éclairage placé sur les bords de la dalle ou derrière les pixels. L'écran mini-LED des MacBook Pro précédents était déjà une vraie évolution, en remplaçant les « ampoules » LED par des « puces » LED afin de renforcer la puissance et la qualité du rétroéclairage. Ce dernier reste toutefois indispensable avec le LCD comme avec le mini-LED, alors que l'OLED s'en passe.
Le résultat est connu : des noirs profonds, un contraste plus élevé et aucun halo autour des objets lumineux affichés sur fond sombre.
Le logo rétroéclairé fait son retour
Sur les anciens MacBook, le logo du capot tirait sa lumière du rétroéclairage de l'écran LCD. Mais avec une dalle OLED, cette solution n'est plus envisageable.
Apple a donc développé un rétroéclairage distinct, dédié au logo : il se compose de quatre LED et de quelques diffuseurs qui répartissent la lumière de manière homogène. L'ensemble se situe derrière l'écran et se révèle, en pratique, impossible à remplacer. La marque à la pomme a encore des progrès à faire côté réparabilité.
Source : GSMArena
