articles.title: Jeff Bezos tiene una teoría sobre por qué la gente odia a los ricos: "El éxito no es sinónimo de maldad"
articles.text:
Probablemente preguntarle a un milmillonario porqué hay tanta gente enfadada con ellos y les ve como a los villanos de la película, sea parte del camino para encontrar una respuesta para un fenómeno que se ha intensificado en los últimos meses.
Esa la pregunta que el entrevistador de la cadena Fox News, Bret Baier le formuló a nada menos que Jeff Bezos en el cuartel general de Blue Origin en Florida. Ver a la segunda mayor fortuna del mundo, con una fortuna estimada de 388.300 millones de dólares, respondiendo porqué los ricos no son los villanos y con cohetes espaciales de fondo es una estampa que no esperábamos ver en una entrevista para la televisión de EEUU.
Un puesto de hamburguesas. Para Bezos, esa percepción es un problema de educación. A algunas personas "se les ha enseñado, creo que incorrectamente" una sociedad basada en esquemas de opresores y oprimidos. Y también que "el éxito es un villano", algo en lo que, como aludido, se mostró diametralmente en contra: "El éxito no es sinónimo de maldad".
Su ejemplo para explicar su opinión fue un negocio de comida rápida: "Puedes ser multimillonario aunque hayas montado un puesto de hamburguesas". Abres un local con diez empleados, luego un segundo, luego un tercero, y acabas con 1.000 restaurantes. Según explicaba el fundador de Amazon, esta "es una historia real con los nuggets de pollo de Raising Cane's", una cadena de comida rápida con mucho éxito en EEUU.
Tal y como recogía de Expansión, Todd Graves fundó la cadena de comida rápida en Luisiana en 1996 y, según datos publicados por Independent, hoy tiene casi 1.000 establecimientos en 44 estados. A su juicio, "no hay nada malo" en hacer un pollo que la gente adora. En la misma charla defendió que toda la riqueza sale de inventar cosas, del arado a la máquina de vapor.
Un malestar con datos. No obstante, el fundador de Amazon y Blue Origin no negó que haya motivos para el enfado ciudadano. "Tenemos problemas reales de asequibilidad. La gente mira el precio de la vivienda y es muy caro", admitió. Habló de los jóvenes que miran el precio de la vivienda y piensan: "Tengo que vivir a dos horas de la ciudad. No puedo vivir cerca de mi trabajo". Bezos aseguraba que no se puede fingir que no hay problemas en la economía que impactan directamente a la población y les genera enfado. "No creo que debamos subestimar los problemas", señalaba Bezos.
En una encuesta de Pew Research, el 33% de los estadounidenses de 18 a 29 años consideraba que era inmoral ser extremadamente rico. Según un informe de Oxfam Internacional, la fortuna conjunta de los milmillonarios se incrementó un 16% hasta los 18,3 billones de dólares en 2025, lo cual supone un récord histórico en cuanto a concentración de riqueza en manos de menos de 3.000 milmillonarios en todo el mundo.
Culpar al casero. Sin embargo, aunque el millonario se muestra comprensivo con el enfado de los ciudadanos, también cree que deben analizarse los motivos y "debemos analizar cuáles son las soluciones reales". "Es muy común que ciertos políticos señalen a los propietarios y digan que esto es culpa de los propietarios avariciosos. Eso no es lo que está pasando", afirmó Bezos. En su opinión, el mercado de la vivienda se basa en la "oferta y demanda. Es economía básica". Si el gobierno subsidia la demanda y limita la oferta, avisó, "vas a tener precios altos".
El millonario puso como ejemplo a la ciudad de Austin: "en los últimos diez años han aplicado muchas políticas para facilitar la construcción de casas". Un análisis de Pew Charitable Trusts lo respalda en parte y destaca que la ciudad construyó 120.000 viviendas entre 2015 y 2024. El alquiler mediano bajó de 1.546 a 1.296 dólares entre diciembre de 2021 y enero de 2026. Eso sí, el estudio mide alquileres, no precios de compra.
La regla de Bezos para votar. "Cuando estés en la cabina de votación y pienses por quién vas a votar, piensa en esto. Si hay un político que elige villanos y selecciona con el dedo, probablemente significa que no tiene una solución", señaló el milmillonario, obviando el posicionamiento que le da formar parte del sector señalado. Bezos aseguró que si uno de sus ejecutivos se dedicara a señalar con el dedo y culpar a otros de los problemas "no estaría aquí mucho tiempo. Le despediríamos muy rápido".
El millonario no nombró a ningún político ni partido, y eso dejó la puerta abierta a muchas lecturas interpretativas. Decenas de espectadores pensaron en Trump, a quien Bezos se ha acercado en su segundo mandato. La excandidata al Senado Amy McGrath escribió en su perfil de X: "No estoy en desacuerdo con la premisa, pero me pregunto si el Sr. Bezos se da cuenta de quién está en la Casa Blanca ahora mismo".

articles.title: Prompt injection attacks drive Red Hat and Nvidia's OpenShell - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Red Hat and Nvidia’s OpenShell puts AI agents on a deny-by-default leash
Prompt injection attacks and silent data exfiltration have turned AI agent security from a theoretical worry into an urgent enterprise concern.
As agents move from developer laptops into data centers, companies need guardrails that don’t strip away what makes agents useful. Red Hat Inc. and Nvidia Corp. have expanded their partnership to tackle that problem through OpenShell, an open-source project that sets limits on what agents can do. The threat model for agents differs sharply from that of traditional software, so the industry has to build a shared standard to secure them, according to Derek Carr (pictured, left), senior distinguished engineer at Red Hat.
“Agents can’t get access to your secrets. They need deny-by-default networking, and you need a rich policy framework for what happened and when for this class of apps,” Carr said. “Nvidia had reached out to us and noted that they were seeing the same problem domain. No one wants to work on this alone. It’s better to work together.”
Carr and Mrunal Patel (right), distinguished engineer at Red Hat, spoke with theCUBE’s John Furrier and Rebecca Knight at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon NA, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how OpenShell helps enterprises run AI agents in production with safeguards against prompt injection and data leaks. (* Disclosure below.)
Prompt injection attacks force a new agent security model
Viral projects such as OpenClaw showed the industry that agents could take real actions on their own. Of course, that power also bred anxiety about agents leaking secrets or spending company money, with concrete warning signs appearing early, Patel noted.
“As soon as we started hearing about the prompt injection attacks and how like folks were seeing the data getting exfiltrated outside, that was scary,” Patel said. “We realized we needed a solution.”
To that end, OpenShell lets operators give agents access to specific endpoints while keeping credentials hidden from the agents and scoped to those endpoints, according to Carr. A policy advisor asks agents to justify blocked actions in plain language, while operators can update policies as workloads change. With OpenShell now under open governance at the Cloud Native Computing Foundation following Nvidia’s contribution, Red Hat aims to make deploying agents on OpenShift as routine as running traditional apps, with prompt injection defenses built into the platform.
“Many companies are struggling to get to one agent in production, let alone thousands or millions,” Carr said. “By having a project like OpenShell in the ecosystem, it provides a blueprint for companies to follow — to get from their first idea of ‘I want to do something with agents’ to a point where they’re safely doing one, 10 or 20 in production.”

articles.title: Black Friday Amazon : 6 accessoires incontournables pour équiper votre bureau à prix réduit
articles.text:
Un poste de travail se renouvelle souvent pièce par pièce, et Amazon a commencé à baisser le prix de ces accessoires avant le Black Friday du 27 novembre. Nous avons retenu 6 offres, de l’écran d’appoint au clavier à switchs magnétiques, en les confrontant aux prix que nous avions déjà relevés.
Télétravail, études ou bureau à la maison : la souris Logitech MX Master 3S et le clavier Logitech MX Keys S sont passés par nos tests, le chargeur Anker et le clavier Keychron K10 HE portent le badge « Offre Pré-Black Friday », et deux écrans bureautique restent sous les 80 €.
Toutes les baisses ne se valent pas. Le chargeur Anker et le Keychron sont sous leur prix le plus bas des 30 derniers jours, quand les deux Logitech sont déjà descendus plus bas cette année : leurs fiches le précisent, avec le prix auquel nous les avions relayés. Les deux écrans sont listés après les quatre fiches détaillées.
Les 4 pièces maîtresses du bureau
Chargeur Anker Zolo 140 W 4 ports à 59,99 € au lieu de 89,99 €
Un seul chargeur pour le portable, le smartphone et les écouteurs : ce modèle GaN de 140 W compte quatre ports et passe à 59,99 €, soit 10 € sous son prix le plus bas des 30 derniers jours. Il est vendu par la boutique officielle d’Anker sur Amazon.
- Jusqu’à quatre appareils : ses deux ports USB-C haute vitesse montent à 140 W, de quoi recharger un MacBook Pro de 0 à 50 % en 30 minutes, selon Anker.
- Un écran de contrôle : il affiche l’état de charge de chaque port et la température du chargeur.
- À savoir : les 89,99 € de référence sont un prix conseillé, et la puissance se partage quand plusieurs appareils sont branchés.
Logitech MX Master 3S à 89,99 € au lieu de 99,99 €
Dans notre test de la Logitech MX Master 3S, nous lui avions attribué 10/10 pour ses clics et molettes presque inaudibles, son capteur précis sur toutes les surfaces et sa construction irréprochable. Elle passe à 89,99 € en coloris graphite, une baisse modeste : nous l’avions relayée à 79,15 € en février.
- Le défilement MagSpeed : la molette électromagnétique parcourt un long document en un geste, et une seconde molette gère le défilement horizontal.
- Plusieurs ordinateurs, une souris : la fonction Flow permet de passer d’un PC à un Mac et d’y transférer texte, images et fichiers.
- À savoir : pas de version pour gauchers et un gabarit peu adapté aux petites mains, relevions-nous dans notre test.
Keychron K10 HE à 119,99 € au lieu de 154,99 €
Un clavier complet à switchs magnétiques, en disposition AZERTY française : le K10 HE passe à 119,99 €, soit 35 € sous son prix le plus bas des 30 derniers jours. Il s’adresse à ceux qui partagent leur bureau entre travail et jeu, et il est vendu par Keychron France.
- Une activation réglable : ses switchs magnétiques Lime se déclenchent entre 0,2 et 3,3 mm, réglables par pas de 0,1 mm, selon Keychron.
- Trois modes de connexion : Bluetooth 5.2 pour trois appareils, sans-fil 2,4 GHz ou filaire en USB-C, sous macOS comme sous Windows.
- À savoir : nous ne l’avons pas testé, et son format complet avec pavé numérique prend de la place sur un petit bureau.
Logitech MX Keys S à 81,99 € au lieu de 119,99 €
Le compagnon de la MX Master 3S passe à 81,99 € en coloris gris. Nous lui avions attribué 9/10 lors de notre test, pour sa frappe fluide, sa double connectivité et son rétroéclairage qui s’allume à l’approche des mains. Nous l’avions relayé à 79,99 € en octobre, dans une version livrée avec un repose-poignets.
- Des touches concaves : une frappe proche de celle d’un portable, rapide et discrète, avec un pavé numérique.
- Trois appareils en Bluetooth : sous Windows, macOS ou Linux, avec une autonomie annoncée de 10 jours rétroéclairage allumé, et jusqu’à 5 mois sans.
- À savoir : notre test relevait une sérigraphie chargée sur certaines touches, et la remise est calculée sur un prix conseillé.
Les 2 autres offres Black Friday pour équiper votre bureau
VPN, logiciels, abonnements : les promos à saisir en ce moment
Souris, clavier ou écran : par quoi commencer ?
Côté souris, la Logitech MX Master 4 est désormais la référence du confort et de la productivité dans notre comparatif des meilleures souris, mis à jour le 11 juin. C’est la remplaçante de la MX Master 3S de cette sélection, que nous avions notée 10/10 lors de son test et qui garde sa molette MagSpeed et sa fonction Flow.
Pour un utilisateur de PC portable, un écran externe offre le gain d’espace le plus immédiat, et les deux modèles de cette liste restent sous les 80 €. Le duo Logitech MX Master 3S et MX Keys S revient à 171,98 € : les deux se règlent dans la même application Logi Options+ et basculent entre trois appareils. Le Keychron K10 HE s’adresse plutôt à ceux qui jouent aussi sur leur poste de travail.
Accessoires de bureau et Black Friday : vos questions
La Logitech MX Master 3S vaut-elle encore le coup face à la MX Master 4 ?
Elle conserve ce qui nous avait convaincus lors de notre test : des clics silencieux, la molette MagSpeed et les fonctions multi-appareils. La MX Master 4, présente dans notre comparatif, lui succède ; à 89,99 €, la 3S reste une option si vous n’avez pas besoin des nouveautés de sa remplaçante.
Qu’est-ce qu’un clavier à switchs magnétiques ?
Ses touches reposent sur des capteurs à effet Hall, qui mesurent la position de la touche plutôt qu’un contact mécanique. La distance d’activation devient alors réglable : de 0,2 à 3,3 mm sur le Keychron K10 HE, selon Keychron.
Peut-on utiliser le MX Keys S et la MX Master 3S sur plusieurs ordinateurs ?
Oui : tous deux se connectent à trois appareils et passent de l’un à l’autre d’une simple touche. La fonction Flow de la souris permet même de déplacer le curseur d’un ordinateur à l’autre et d’y copier texte et fichiers, sous Windows comme sous macOS.
Comment profiter des offres exclusives du Black Friday ?
Durant tout le mois de novembre, Clubic vous propose chaque jour des sélections thématiques regroupant les meilleures offres à saisir en direct.
Retrouvez tous les bons plans du Black Friday 2026 sur la page dédiée à l'événement.
Pour les aficionados de X, n'hésitez pas à suivre notre compte Clubic Bons Plans pour être au courant en direct des meilleures offres.

articles.title: ‘Ridiculous that a multi-trillion-dollar company can’t fix an issue’: Fitbit users fume as their daily metrics go missing from Google Health — and Google admits there’s no fix on the way
articles.text:
Fitbit users say daily health metrics have vanished from their devices, and a recent update could be to blame
Yet more Google Health woe
- Fitbit users’ daily metrics are missing from the Google Health app
- The issue might have been caused by a software update
- Google says a fix is not coming ‘in the immediate future’
Users of the best Fitbit devices are reporting that several key health metrics have gone missing from the Google Health app synced to their wearables, with stats like heart-rate variability, blood oxygen and more nowhere to be found. And it gets worse, as Google has admitted that there might not be a fix for some time to come.
The issue came to light on social media, where multiple threads have sprung up full of users frustrated that, instead of their usual complement of stats, many metrics are simply reading 'No data.' Based on the reports, the problem seems to be affecting breathing rate, blood-oxygen levels, resting heart rate, skin-temperature variation, and more.
For some people, their Fitbit device was still able to record their sleep stats overnight, and previous days’ metrics continue to show up. However, more recent data compiled in the Vitals section is what appears to be affected.
This will no doubt be a frustrating occurrence for Fitbit users wanting to keep up with their latest health metrics. Yet further investigation appears to have revealed a potential culprit.
Google responds
Back on Reddit, Fitbit’s 5.12 update has been suggested as the potential cause of the problem. “After the 5.12 update this particular issue started to arise,” one person noted, before asking: “did you update the app recently?”
For some, uninstalling the Google Health app and then reinstalling it fixed the problem. Unfortunately, one Redditor pointed out that you might have to do that every morning, as the metrics in the Vitals section reset with each day.
Alternatively, signing out of the app and signing back in might be enough to put things right. Another suggestion was to switch each metric’s chart from weekly to monthly and then back to weekly.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Google hasn’t remained entirely silent throughout this situation. A member of the company’s support staff informed one Redditor that Google is aware of the problem and that “We’ll continue to monitor the situation, and keep our team informed of the impact to you and other customers.”
What Google didn’t do, however, was promise a remedy. As the company support rep said of the metrics bug, “We’re aware of it, but may not be able to provide a fix in the immediate future … We understand that this isn’t the resolution you’re hoping for, but rest assured we’re always working to improve our products.”
One frustrated commenter summed up Google’s response this way: “Ridiculous that a multi-trillion-dollar company can’t fix an issue when they have AI that are coded to actually fix things like this and top-of-the-line engineering.”
With no fix on the way any time soon and a wide variety of potential cures mooted on social media, it’s difficult for anyone affected by this issue to know what to do to get their metrics back. For now, perhaps the best you can do is try the solutions mentioned earlier and keep your fingers crossed that Google takes action sooner rather than later.

articles.title: La piel como pantalla: desarrollan una tecnología que permite controlar relojes inteligentes desde el brazo
articles.text:
Los relojes inteligentes podrían cambiar la forma en que los usuarios interactúan con sus pantallas gracias a una tecnología que convierte la piel del antebrazo en un panel táctil. Investigadores de la Universidad Estatal de Carolina del Norte desarrollaron EpiPad, un sistema que permite controlar funciones de estos dispositivos mediante movimientos de los dedos sobre el brazo, sin necesidad de tocar directamente la pantalla.
La propuesta busca resolver una de las principales limitaciones de los smartwatches: su reducido espacio de interacción. Aunque estos equipos incorporan pantallas cada vez más avanzadas, realizar determinadas acciones continúa siendo complicado debido al tamaño de los iconos y los controles. Ampliar una imagen, desplazarse por un menú o seleccionar una opción puede resultar incómodo cuando los dedos ocupan buena parte del panel.
EpiPad plantea una alternativa: utilizar la superficie de la piel como una extensión de la pantalla. De esta manera, el usuario podría deslizar los dedos, hacer zoom o seleccionar elementos directamente sobre el antebrazo, como si estuviera utilizando el panel táctil de una computadora portátil.
EpiPad convierte el antebrazo en un panel táctil
El funcionamiento de esta tecnología se basa en un radar de ondas milimétricas de tamaño reducido, integrado en una pulsera que se coloca alrededor de la muñeca. Este componente detecta los movimientos de los dedos sobre la piel y los interpreta como instrucciones para controlar el reloj inteligente.
A diferencia de otros sistemas que dependen únicamente del reconocimiento de gestos, EpiPad también puede identificar la presión ejercida durante cada movimiento. Para conseguirlo, registra las pequeñas deformaciones que se producen en la superficie de la piel cuando el usuario realiza un toque.
Esta capacidad permite distinguir entre diferentes intensidades de presión y asignarles funciones específicas. Por ejemplo, un contacto suave podría servir para seleccionar una opción, mientras que una presión más fuerte podría activar otra acción.
El sensor también puede reconocer la trayectoria y la posición de varios dedos simultáneamente. Esto abre la posibilidad de realizar movimientos más complejos, como ampliar o reducir imágenes mediante gestos similares a los que se utilizan en las pantallas táctiles convencionales.
La tecnología reconoce los movimientos en menos de cuatro minutos
Para utilizar EpiPad, el sistema necesita realizar una calibración inicial que le permita adaptarse a las características físicas de cada persona. Durante este procedimiento, el usuario sigue una breve secuencia de gestos guiados para que el dispositivo aprenda a interpretar sus movimientos.
Según la información proporcionada sobre el desarrollo, este proceso requiere menos de cuatro minutos. Una vez completado, el sistema puede reconocer las interacciones realizadas sobre el antebrazo.
Aunque el prototipo experimental muestra una placa de circuitos visible, los investigadores trabajan con componentes de dimensiones reducidas. La matriz de sensores encargada de registrar los movimientos y la presión mide apenas 5 por 4 milímetros.
Este tamaño facilitaría su integración en futuras pulseras y relojes inteligentes sin necesidad de incorporar estructuras voluminosas. La miniaturización es uno de los aspectos importantes del proyecto, porque permitiría trasladar la tecnología a dispositivos comerciales sin modificar demasiado su diseño.
Las pruebas muestran menos errores que las pantallas táctiles
Los investigadores evaluaron el funcionamiento de EpiPad con la participación de 20 voluntarios. Las pruebas incluyeron ejercicios de seguimiento de movimientos, reconocimiento de gestos y detección de diferentes niveles de presión.
También compararon el sistema con otros métodos de interacción utilizados en relojes inteligentes, como el control directo sobre la pantalla y los movimientos de inclinación del dispositivo.
De acuerdo con los resultados del estudio, EpiPad consiguió un mejor desempeño en rapidez y precisión, además de reducir los errores al seleccionar elementos. Estos resultados sugieren que utilizar el brazo como superficie de control podría facilitar determinadas tareas que actualmente requieren varios movimientos sobre una pantalla pequeña.
Sin embargo, todavía se trata de una tecnología experimental. Su rendimiento en pruebas controladas no garantiza que funcione de la misma manera en situaciones cotidianas, donde factores como el movimiento del cuerpo, la ropa y las condiciones de uso podrían influir en la detección de los gestos.
EpiPad también podría utilizarse en gafas inteligentes
Las aplicaciones de esta tecnología no se limitarían a los relojes inteligentes. Sus desarrolladores consideran que también podría utilizarse en dispositivos que carecen de pantallas táctiles tradicionales, como las gafas inteligentes con inteligencia artificial.
En estos equipos, controlar funciones mediante movimientos sobre el antebrazo permitiría reducir la dependencia de botones físicos y otros mecanismos de interacción.
Otro aspecto que podría favorecer su desarrollo es el costo de fabricación. Según las estimaciones del proyecto, los componentes del radar son económicos y, con una producción a gran escala, el costo de las piezas podría situarse por debajo de los 10 dólares.
Por ahora, EpiPad no tiene una fecha anunciada de llegada al mercado. Los investigadores buscan establecer alianzas con empresas tecnológicas para avanzar en su desarrollo y evaluar su incorporación a futuros dispositivos. Si consigue superar esa etapa, la tecnología podría ofrecer una alternativa para controlar relojes y otros accesorios inteligentes sin depender exclusivamente de sus pequeñas pantallas.

articles.title: Espanha vai bloquear conteúdos do TikTok após denúncias de abuso infantil • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Espanha vai bloquear conteúdos do TikTok após denúncias de abuso infantil
Investigação identificou 1.183 publicações de abuso infantil na plataforma, que somavam 48 milhões de visualizações.
A Agência Espanhola de Proteção de Dados (AEPD) anunciou o bloqueio de links e conteúdos ilegais identificados no TikTok após uma investigação revelar mais de mil publicações com material de abuso infantil. A medida foi anunciada nesta quarta-feira (11/11), um dia depois de o governo espanhol pedir a suspensão temporária da rede social.
Os conteúdos acumulavam pelo menos 48 milhões de visualizações, enquanto mais de 26 mil perfis participaram de interações com o material. O pedido foi apresentado ontem (10/11) pela ministra da Juventude e Infância, Sira Rego. O governo acionou o Ministério Público e a AEPD para avaliar medidas contra a rede social, segundo a NBC News.
A ministra defendeu a interrupção das atividades do TikTok até a remoção do material denunciado. Entretanto, nenhuma suspensão total foi determinada e a AEPD decidiu, até o momento, apenas pela suspensão dos conteúdos.
O levantamento foi conduzido pela organização espanhola Maldita.es, que analisou o TikTok durante 35 dias, entre setembro e outubro de 2026. Os pesquisadores identificaram 231 perfis responsáveis por 1.183 publicações com imagens e vídeos de abuso sexual infantil.
Segundo a investigação, parte do material permaneceu disponível durante meses, apesar das regras do TikTok que proíbem esse tipo de publicação. A organização também testou os mecanismos de moderação. Dos 50 vídeos denunciados pelos canais oficiais, apenas cinco foram removidos. Outros 13 tiveram o acesso bloqueado somente na Espanha, enquanto os demais receberam respostas consideradas insuficientes pelos pesquisadores.
O TikTok afirmou que precisava receber os dados completos da investigação para localizar e remover o material. A Maldita.es contestou a alegação, argumentando que já havia utilizado os mecanismos oficiais de denúncia da própria plataforma.
Após a divulgação da investigação, o Ministério da Juventude solicitou uma suspensão emergencial do TikTok. O pedido se baseia no Regulamento Geral de Proteção de Dados da União Europeia, que permite medidas provisórias em situações excepcionais, por até três meses.
Nesta quarta-feira, a AEPD anunciou a previsão de bloqueio dos links e conteúdos ilegais identificados. Os dados também serão encaminhados às autoridades irlandesas, responsáveis pela supervisão de dados do TikTok na Europa. Enquanto isso, a plataforma começou a restringir termos de pesquisa associados ao material denunciado.
O caso amplia a pressão regulatória sobre a empresa. No Brasil, a ByteDance, controladora do TikTok, já foi multada pela ANPD por irregularidades no tratamento de dados de menores. Na Europa, a Comissão Europeia também questionou mecanismos do aplicativo considerados prejudiciais, especialmente a crianças e adolescentes.

articles.title: Biostar Introduces BIPTL-IHT Edge AI Motherboard
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 11th 2026
Biostar Introduces BIPTL-IHT Edge AI Motherboard
BIOSTAR, a leading manufacturer of edge AI solutions, industrial computers, motherboards, graphics cards, and storage devices, today announces the BIPTL-IHT, a Thin Mini-ITX industrial motherboard engineered for intelligent edge systems, AIoT deployments, automation platforms, and advanced system integration applications. Powered by Intel Core Ultra series 3 processors based on the Panther Lake-H platform with integrated AI capabilities, the BIPTL-IHT enables businesses to turn data into intelligent action through efficient edge AI computing, extensive connectivity, and flexible expansion within a compact 170 x 170 mm form factor.
Designed for system integrators building modern business infrastructure, the BIPTL-IHT delivers the performance and adaptability required for applications that rely on stable data processing, connected devices, and responsive system control. It is well-suited for deployments such as customer data management systems, industrial automation platforms, AIoT gateways, and smart edge devices, helping streamline system development while maintaining consistent performance across demanding workloads.Leveraging Intel Core Ultra 5, Ultra 7, and Ultra 9 processors, including selected Panther Lake-H SKUs, the platform supports dual DDR5-7200 SO-DIMM memory with capacities up to 128 GB. With integrated NPU resources available directly on the processor, the BIPTL-IHT enables efficient edge AI processing and local inference, reducing the need for external accelerators in many edge AI workloads, simplifying system architecture while improving overall power efficiency.
For visual and display-focused applications, the platform provides broad multi-display support through Intel integrated graphics, enabling up to four simultaneous outputs across HDMI, DisplayPort, and LVDS interfaces. Dual HDMI and dual DisplayPort 1.4 outputs are available on the rear panel, while internal LVDS support allows seamless integration into panel PCs, kiosks, digital signage systems, HMI platforms, and industrial control interfaces. This flexible display configuration supports a wide range of monitoring, interaction, and content delivery use cases.
A versatile expansion design ensures strong adaptability across different deployment needs. The BIPTL-IHT includes dual M.2 Key-M slots supporting PCIe 5.0 x4 and PCIe 4.0 x2 NVMe storage, enabling high-speed local data access and caching. An M.2 Key-B slot with SIM support allows integration of 4G and 5G communication modules, while the M.2 Key-E slot supports WiFi and Bluetooth connectivity. Selected processor configurations also provide a PCIe 5.0 x4 expansion slot, offering additional flexibility for customized system builds.
To meet the requirements of automation and industrial environments, the board offers a comprehensive range of I/O interfaces for machine communication and peripheral integration. Dual 2.5GbE LAN ports based on Intel I226 controllers ensure stable, high-speed networking, with one port supporting vPro for remote management in enterprise deployments. Support for six serial ports, including RS232, RS422, and RS485, ensures compatibility with a wide range of legacy and industrial equipment such as sensors, controllers, and automation systems. Additional features, including 8-bit DIO, SATA connectivity, MIPI-CSI2 headers, TPM 2.0, and extensive onboard headers, further expand its usability across embedded and edge applications.
Engineered for reliable deployment, the BIPTL-IHT supports a wide 9 V to 24 V DC input range and operates within a temperature range of 0°C to 60°C, making it suitable for various edge and semi-industrial environments. Its Thin Mini-ITX form factor allows system builders to create compact, space-efficient solutions without compromising on connectivity or expansion capabilities.
Support for Windows 11 IoT Enterprise 24H2 and Ubuntu 24.04 provides developers with flexibility across embedded, commercial, and industrial platforms. From AI-enabled edge systems and connected business applications to automation controllers and intelligent computing devices, the BIPTL-IHT delivers balanced performance, expansion capabilities, and interface support for evolving edge workloads.
The BIOSTAR BIPTL-IHT reflects BIOSTAR's commitment to delivering practical and forward-looking platforms for AIoT, edge computing, and system integration markets. Combining Intel Core Ultra series 3 processing, integrated AI capabilities, extensive industrial I/O, and a compact design, the BIPTL-IHT provides a reliable foundation for building intelligent systems across a wide range of applications.

articles.title: PC peripheral maker Logitech giving all of its 7,000 employees the day off to play GTA 6 — company announces ‘Game Day’ initiative, dedicated vacation day to play video games
articles.text:
PC peripheral maker Logitech giving all of its 7,000 employees the day off to play GTA 6 — company announces ‘Game Day’ initiative, dedicated vacation day to play video games
"Logi Game Day" is available to everyone from full-time workers to interns, and they can play something else if GTA 6 isn't their style.
As GTA 6, the most anticipated game of the year, perhaps the decade, nears its November 19 release date, one company has offered its employees the chance to take the day off to play it. Amid the expectation that gamers around the globe will call in sick to play the game instead of heading into the office, PC peripheral and hardware outfit Logitech is getting ahead of the game by giving 7,000 employees the chance to take a day off to play it. Or, if they prefer, they can play any other game instead, the company confirmed in a press release detailing the move.
The new initiative is called "Logi Game Day," and it isn't only available to the top brass. Interns and full-time employees alike can take a day off from now until this time next year, at a time when it's been estimated that the GTA 6 launch could see the U.S. economy take a $1 billion hit in terms of productivity. The game, which is a console exclusive ahead of a claimed early 2027 PC release, is already available for preorder, with pre-loading also up and running. It's a good job, too, with a 212GB PS5 download set to be a real downer for eager gamers with slow internet. The ongoing price hikes also mean that upgrading your PS5 storage for GTA 6 won't be a fun time, either.
As for Logitech, the company believes that it's time for people to move away from the belief that playing games is a waste of time, hence its new initiative. It makes sense for a company that makes gaming accessories to say that, of course, but CEO Hanneke Faber argues that the company sees "how engagement in one sphere supports performance in the other.” The hope will be that, by allowing employees to play games, a productivity boost will follow.
Whether that comes to fruition remains to be seen. But there's less doubt about GTA 6's popularity a little more than a week out from its release. If you've yet to get your order in, you can also grab Grand Theft Auto VI for $79.99 now. You'll get a box with a code that you'll need to redeem on your PS5 to be able to download and play the game.
The game's release brings an end to years of rumors and leaks, not to mention legal battles. Take-Two hit Microsoft with a subpoena in relation to a massive leak earlier this year in an attempt to find the perpetrator. Rockstar Games addressed the leaks in a post on the X social network shortly after the subpoena was made public, saying that it "would be an understatement to say that having videos of Grand Theft Auto VI gameplay leak in this way has been heartbreaking for our team."

articles.title: IPO d'Anthropic : chaque fondateur va toucher plusieurs centaines de millions de dollars !
Acabamos de ver cómo un exoplaneta desaparece de la vista de nuestros telescopios. El culpable es su vecino invisible
articles.text:
Durante años, la astronomía ha consistido en mirar al cielo esperando a que las cosas pasen, y gracias a las misiones como Kepler o TESS, nos hemos acostumbrado a detectar exoplanetas observando su tránsito. Pero ante estas observaciones hay una pregunta bastante importante que ronda la cabeza: ¿qué pasa cuando un planeta al que llevas años observando puntualmente decide, de repente, desaparecer sin dejar rastro?
Un ejemplo. Eso es exactamente lo que le ha ocurrido a TOI-2535 b, un exoplaneta del tamaño de Júpiter que ha protagonizado un "truco de magia" que antes no se había visto al desaparecer sin una explicación lógica detrás. Hasta ahora.
Lo que sabíamos. La historia de TOI-2535 b comienza en 2019 cuando el telescopio espacial TESS de la NASA comenzó a observar este planeta orbitando alrededor de una estrella enana K temprana situada en la constelación del Cuervo.
Al principio, todo parecía normal, puesto que en abril de 2019, el planeta cruzaba cerca del centro del disco estelar. Sin embargo, a medida que pasaban los meses, los astrónomos notaron que algo iba mal, ya que los tránsitos empezaron a volverse caóticos y a veces el planeta llegaba hasta seis horas antes de lo previsto, y otras veces se retrasaba seis horas.
Lo raro. Lo más dramático no era su impuntualidad, sino su trayectoria, puesto que el tránsito se fue desplazando hacia el borde de la estrella. Cada vez duraba menos y bloqueaba menos luz, volviéndose rasante, hasta que, entre 2025 y marzo de 2026, desapareció por completo. Esto quiere decir que el planeta ya no cruzaba por delante de su estrella desde nuestra perspectiva en la Tierra.
Y era algo histórico, puesto que es la primera vez en la historia que los astrónomos ven directamente cómo un exoplaneta confirmado alrededor de una estrella única deja de transitar en una escala de tiempo tan corta. De hecho, la distancia entre el centro de la estrella y la trayectoria del planeta cambió a un ritmo de unos 0,16 al año, el más rápido jamás medido en un sistema de este tipo.
El culpable. Los planetas no se esfuman porque sí, y para entender qué estaba pasando, un equipo de investigación recurrió al espectrógrafo NEID, instalado en el telescopio WIYN en el Observatorio Nacional de Kitt Peak en Arizona. Y lo que apuntaban los resultados es que TOI-2535 b tiene un planeta compañero con una masa al menos similar a la de Saturno.
Este vecino invisible está inclinado al menos 5 grados respecto a la órbita de TOI-2535 b y, al estar tan cerca el uno del otro, la gravedad del compañero tira constantemente de TOI-2535 b, haciendo que su órbita se bambolee como una peonza a punto de caer. Este fenómeno se llama precesión nodal.
Se puede entender. El astrónomo Erik Petigura, coautor del estudio, utiliza una analogía con nuestro propio vecindario, puesto que si la órbita de la Luna estuviera perfectamente alineada con la de la Tierra, tendríamos un eclipse solar cada mes. Sin embargo, como la órbita lunar está inclinada, los eclipses son eventos raros y, en el caso de TOI-2535, la interacción entre ambos planetas está cambiando esa inclinación continuamente en periodos de apenas unas décadas.
No es el primero. En el pasado ya vimos el caso de Kepler-413b, que dejó de transitar durante 800 días. Sin embargo, aquel era un planeta circumbinario, y era el tirón de las estrellas lo que alteraba su órbita. También conocemos el caso de TOI-1518b, cuya órbita precesa y podría dejar de transitar en unas décadas, pero allí el culpable no es otro planeta, sino el achatamiento de su propia estrella.
Lo que hace único a TOI-2535 es que la alteración la provoca exclusivamente otro planeta gigante, convirtiendo a este sistema en una rareza cósmica con dos gigantes gaseosos en órbitas de periodo muy corto.

articles.title: Así es la nueva PlayStation Portal: Sony incorpora juego en la nube y más almacenamiento
articles.text:
Sony presentó una nueva versión de PlayStation Portal, su dispositivo portátil para jugar títulos de PS5 a distancia, que incorpora una de las funciones más esperadas por los usuarios: la posibilidad de ejecutar videojuegos directamente desde la nube sin necesitar una consola PlayStation 5 encendida. El equipo también suma almacenamiento interno y estrena un acabado negro, aunque mantiene buena parte de las características técnicas del modelo original.
El anuncio se realizó a través del blog oficial de PlayStation en Japón, donde la compañía confirmó que el dispositivo pasará a llamarse PlayStation Portal Player. El cambio de nombre refleja una modificación importante en su funcionamiento: ya no estará limitado al juego remoto desde una consola, sino que permitirá acceder a una selección de títulos mediante transmisión en la nube.
Por ahora, Sony anunció esta versión únicamente para el mercado japonés y no confirmó cuándo llegará a otros países. La nueva PlayStation Portal podrá reservarse desde el 13 de noviembre y estará disponible a partir del 10 de diciembre, con un precio de 39.980 yenes, equivalente a unos 225 euros al cambio.
PlayStation Portal permitirá jugar sin una PS5
La principal novedad del dispositivo es la incorporación del juego en la nube. Esta función permitirá transmitir videojuegos compatibles del catálogo de PS5 sin tener que conectarse directamente a una consola física.
Para utilizarla será necesario contar con una suscripción a PlayStation Plus Premium y una conexión Wi-Fi. Los usuarios podrán acceder tanto a determinados videojuegos que hayan comprado en formato digital como a los títulos disponibles dentro del servicio de Sony.
De esta manera, PlayStation Portal amplía su utilidad. Hasta ahora, el dispositivo funcionaba principalmente como una pantalla portátil que transmitía la imagen y el sonido de una PS5 mediante una conexión inalámbrica. Esto significaba que los jugadores necesitaban tener la consola para acceder a sus videojuegos.
Con la nueva modalidad, esa dependencia desaparece para los títulos compatibles con la transmisión en la nube. Sin embargo, no significa que PlayStation Portal se convierta en una consola portátil tradicional capaz de ejecutar videojuegos de manera independiente: el contenido seguirá funcionando mediante streaming y necesitará conexión a internet.
Sony también adelantó que el nuevo dispositivo incluirá un mes de suscripción a PlayStation Plus Premium, lo que permitirá probar esta modalidad desde el primer momento.
Más almacenamiento interno y un nuevo diseño negro
Otra de las novedades anunciadas por Sony es la incorporación de almacenamiento interno. La compañía no ha detallado todavía su capacidad ni ha explicado qué funciones permitirá realizar, por lo que no se puede asegurar si servirá para guardar videojuegos, archivos temporales u otros contenidos.
Este apartado genera interés porque el modelo original estaba pensado principalmente para transmitir juegos desde una PS5 y no contaba con una capacidad de almacenamiento destinada a instalar títulos.
En cuanto a su apariencia, la nueva PlayStation Portal dejará atrás el acabado blanco del primer modelo para adoptar el color Midnight Black, una tonalidad negra que también está presente en otros accesorios de la marca.
Por lo demás, el equipo conservará las principales características de la versión anterior. Tendrá una pantalla LCD de ocho pulgadas, resolución Full HD de 1080p y una frecuencia de actualización de hasta 60 fotogramas por segundo.
También mantendrá el sonido 3D, la retroalimentación háptica y los gatillos adaptativos. Estas funciones buscan reproducir algunas de las sensaciones del mando DualSense de PS5, como las vibraciones que cambian según lo que ocurre en el videojuego y la resistencia de los botones durante determinadas acciones.
¿Cuándo llegará la nueva PlayStation Portal a otros países?
Por el momento, el anuncio de Sony está dirigido exclusivamente a Japón. La compañía estableció el 13 de noviembre como fecha de inicio de las reservas y el 10 de diciembre como día de lanzamiento comercial.
El precio anunciado es de 39.980 yenes, unos 225 euros al cambio. No obstante, todavía no existe información sobre cuánto costará en otros mercados ni cuándo podría llegar a América Latina.
Además, quienes adquieran esta versión japonesa deberán contar con una cuenta de PlayStation Network de Japón para utilizar el dispositivo.
La actualización representa un cambio importante en la estrategia de Sony para PlayStation Portal. Al incorporar el juego en la nube, la compañía busca ampliar las posibilidades de un accesorio que inicialmente dependía de una PS5. La llegada a otros mercados y los detalles sobre su almacenamiento interno serán determinantes para conocer el alcance de esta nueva versión.

articles.title: Nvidia board reportedly preparing to oust Jensen Huang after second affair report
articles.text:
A hot potato: On Sunday, Nvidia's board said it still had confidence in Jensen Huang. That confidence lasted all of three days. The board is now reportedly preparing to push him out, with directors set to meet as soon as Wednesday to decide the future of the man who co-founded the chipmaker in 1993 and remains the only CEO it has ever had. The turn came after a second extramarital affair surfaced, this time with an Nvidia executive who reports directly to him.
The Wall Street Journal reported the board's plans on Wednesday, citing people familiar with the matter. A separate source told Reuters that directors were meeting that same evening. Nvidia shares dropped about 8% in after-hours trading.
The board first opened an investigation on Sunday, the same day Huang told his entire staff in writing that he had been unfaithful to his wife. The woman involved is Alice Huang – no relation – who was an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, one of Nvidia's major customers.
The catch: US intelligence officials believe she is a Chinese intelligence asset. Beijing has brushed off the claims, Megaspeed denies wrongdoing, and Nvidia has described its dealings with her as routine.
At the time, the board said it had no reason to believe national security or company secrets had been compromised. But on Wednesday, The New York Times reported a second relationship, with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of healthcare. The paper cited five people who worked at the company. Two of them even said the pair were filmed being affectionate at a San Jose hotel during Nvidia's own developer conference in March.
Unlike the first affair, this one involves someone on Huang's own team. Nvidia's code of conduct tells employees to avoid conflicts, including those created by personal relationships.
Whoever replaces Huang would inherit an unusually flat company. He has roughly 60 people reporting directly to him – most big-company CEOs have a handful – and no obvious second-in-command. Weirdly, he's also said he doesn't believe in succession planning at all. He'd rather leaders just keep passing on what they know as they go.
Bloomberg reports the board is already working with an outside firm to identify candidates and is weighing a temporary chief. Semafor, meanwhile, says some directors favor CFO Colette Kress for the interim role. Interestingly, Apple hardware chief Johny Srouji is reportedly in the running for the top job, too.
Surprisingly, for a founder this powerful, Huang has no super-voting shares to fall back on. He is Nvidia's largest individual shareholder, yet he owns only about 3.6% of the company. Vanguard holds roughly 9% and BlackRock roughly 7%. A simple majority of the board can remove him as CEO, with or without cause.

articles.title: Kubernetes inference takes more than downloading model weights - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
As Kubernetes inference faces launch-day deadlines, CoreWeave deepens its open-source involvement
Cloud providers are scaling Kubernetes inference to serve frontier AI models, and the problems they encounter in production are helping shape the open-source projects they rely on.
CoreWeave Inc. sits near the center of that shift as AI agents reshape enterprise infrastructure. The company describes itself as a cloud built from the ground up for AI rather than retrofitted for it. Much of its growth traces back to the open nature of the container orchestration platform and the ecosystem around it, according to Yoshi Tamura (pictured, left), principal product manager at CoreWeave. CoreWeave has now upgraded to Platinum, the Cloud Native Computing Foundation’s highest corporate membership tier, to help shape how Kubernetes handles the large AI workloads its customers run.
“Without [Kubernetes], I don’t think we would’ve been able to get this kind of explosive growth,” Tamura said. “With this upgrade to Platinum, we indicate that we really mean it. We want to give back to the community. We want to be more involved.”
Tamura and Rita Zhang (right), principal software engineer at CoreWeave, spoke with theCUBE’s John Furrier and Rebecca Knight at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon NA, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed why CoreWeave upgraded to CNCF Platinum membership and what it takes to run Kubernetes inference in production. (* Disclosure below.)
Kubernetes inference and the hard work of running AI in production
Open source can get a model into a cluster, but that doesn’t guarantee it will perform at scale. CoreWeave’s inference team brings together infrastructure specialists and machine learning engineers, working with model labs and open-source inference engines to patch engines and runtimes for newly released models, according to Zhang.
“Running in production is hard,” Zhang said. “We work a lot with the open-source community, not just on the inference stack, but also with the model providers. Just because it’s on Hugging Face and you download the weights doesn’t mean it will work per your requirement. This is where we work very closely with the labs and the open-source community — like vLLM, SGLang — to make sure that for day-zero models we actually are able to patch the engines and provide our own kernels and patch the runtime.”
Kubernetes special interest groups rely on users to bring them production problems, such as finding nodes with the right devices and accounting for cluster topology when scheduling large training and inference jobs, Zhang explained. CoreWeave remains smaller than incumbent cloud providers and relies on open source more than many realize, Tamura added. Its work with leading AI model builders now gives it an early look at where frontier workloads are headed.
“We’re in a very unique position,” Tamura said. “Maybe we can actually find a way to kind of bring it back to the community and sort of lead which direction Kubernetes, a larger community, could go.”

articles.title: Chinese researchers send world-record bidirectional data transmission over 626 miles — 'hollow-core' fiber test hits 64 terabits per second and could transfer 160 4K movies a second by transmitting signal through gas not glass, cutting latency by 30%
articles.text:
Forget broadband buffering — Chinese researchers use 'hollow-core' fiber to send 64 terabits of data per second across 626 miles, enough to download 160 4K movies a second and cutting latency by 30%
Network boosts are coming
- Chinese researchers report major hollow-core fiber upgrades
- Transmission capacities of 64Tbps were reached
- The technology could replace solid-core fiber in infrastructure networks
No matter how fast your broadband (or 5G) connection is, it could always be faster, and 'hollow-core' fiber could help. Researchers in China have now set new records for the technology, demonstrating two-way, high-speed data transmission across a distance of 1,007 kilometers (626 miles).
As reported by CCTV (via Interesting Engineering), a transmission capacity of 64 terabits per second (Tbps) was achieved in each direction, enough to download 160 films in 4K resolution (50GB each) every second — so perfect for movie night. Individual signals took just 3.43 milliseconds to travel the whole length of the link.
The transmission distance is some 50 times greater than previous hollow-core trials of the same type, while latency was reduced by 30%, too. Signal-to-noise ratios and loss margins were also improved, according to the team from the China Telecom Research Institute, Yangtze Optical Fibre and Cable (YOFC), and ZTE Corporation.
It's a technology that companies are already investing in. For example, last year Microsoft signed a deal with Corning and Heraeus to scale up production of hollow-core fiber in order to upgrade its Azure cloud platform. By the end of this year, around 15,000 kilometers (9,321 miles) of hollow-core fiber should be in place supporting Azure.
A core change
As you can guess from the name, hollow-core fiber replaces the glass of solid-core fiber with air that has a glass lattice surrounding it. The glass edges keep optical signals heading in the right direction, but the hollow core means there's less resistance to the light — which results in faster transmission speeds and lower latency.
The technology is better suited to large infrastructure projects than the cabling that connects your broadband network to your home, but you'll still feel the benefit in the coming years: data centers are already making use of the technology, and it's been tipped to support cellular networks too in the future.
Several challenges remain, because hollow-core fiber is more challenging to make and install than solid-core fiber, the current norm. However, as this latest demonstration in China shows, scientists are gradually overcoming some of the problems that remain, making the tech more commercially viable all the time.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
The glass lattice that acts as the container for the data transmissions is particularly important, with recent improvements being made in the design and composition of this glass to reduce lag and increase stability. All of which means, we can expect to hear a lot more about hollow-core fiber going forward.

articles.title: SpaceX develops its own ‘Kessel’ rack-scale system featuring 72 Nvidia Rubin GPUs for data centers in space, report claims — replaces conventional NVLink cable assemblies with a massive 84-layer printed circuit board
articles.text:
SpaceX develops its own ‘Kessel’ rack-scale system featuring 72 Nvidia Rubin GPUs for data centers in space, report claims — replaces conventional NVLink cable assemblies with a massive 84-layer printed circuit board
For terrestrial and orbital deployments.
SpaceX/xAI is developing a custom version of Nvidia's Vera Rubin NVL72 rack-scale AI system that replaces conventional NVLink cable assemblies with a massive 84-layer printed circuit board (PCB), in part for use in orbital data centers, reports SemiAnalysis. The system is codenamed Kessel and retains 36 Vera CPUs, 72 Rubin GPUs, and nine NVLink switch trays, but introduces a different solid-state interconnect architecture. While SpaceX/xAI will continue to buy Nvidia hardware directly from the company, Elon Musk's company will source other components independently, which could give it greater control over its hardware supply chain.
The Kessel system retains the fundamental configuration of Nvidia's Vera Rubin NVL72 platform, which comprises 72 GPU packages distributed across 18 compute trays and nine NVLink switch trays. However, instead of Nvidia's conventional arrangement with internal NVLink cable cartridges, SpaceX plans to position compute and switch trays back-to-back around a passive PCB midplane. The architecture resembles a smaller version of Nvidia's Kyber design with 576 AI GPUs (albeit in 144 packages), which also relies on a PCB-based interconnect rather than conventional cable assemblies, SemiAnalysis notes. Interestingly, the design is aimed at both terrestrial and orbital deployments, according to the analysts.
Arguably the most distinctive feature of Kessel is its 84-layer PCB midplane, which uses ultra-low-loss M10 copper-clad laminates (CCLs). By contrast, Nvidia's Kyber architecture relied on a backplane based on a considerably more complex 156-layer PCB featuring M9 CCLs. The reduction in layer count by nearly half could substantially improve manufacturability and production yields, but the more advanced copper-clad laminate will almost certainly increase material costs. In any case, an 84-layer PCB is a device that is exceptionally hard to build.
The move to a PCB midplane could simplify system assembly by eliminating numerous high-speed cable connections, but it would not necessarily reduce manufacturing costs. An 84-layer PCB that relies on ultra-low-loss M10 laminate is an exceptionally expensive component that requires sophisticated manufacturing processes and precise quality control. To put an 84-layer PCB number into context, modern high-end server motherboards use 15 – 20 layers, whereas server development boards use more than 20 layers to virtually eliminate any electrical issues with the board itself. Furthermore, manufacturing yields of an 84-layer PCB could become a major obstacle, as defects in internal layers may render an entire board unusable. Consequently, the economic viability of Kessel will depend on whether savings from cable elimination and independent component procurement can offset the cost of its complex midplane.
Perhaps more importantly, Kessel represents a departure from Nvidia's conventional system-level procurement model. Instead of purchasing Nvidia's assembled L6 compute boards or even L10 trays that Nvidia plans to sell with its Vera Rubin generation, SpaceX reportedly plans to acquire AI accelerators, CPUs, switches, and networking components directly from Nvidia and procure other components from third-party suppliers (one can wonder how easy it will be for SpaceX/xAI to procure memory amid today's shortages). This would enable SpaceX to select its own PCB manufacturers, component vendors, and manufacturing partners, optimize its hardware for its infrastructure (which will be important for orbital deployments), and perhaps reduce intermediary costs. Meanwhile, the company would assume greater responsibility for system design, validation, manufacturing quality, and supply-chain management, which is something that most hyperscalers have been doing in recent years.
For Nvidia, the implications are less straightforward. Although direct sales of CPU and AI GPU packages could reduce the company's revenue from complete compute-board assemblies, the arrangement could also encourage other large customers to develop their own Nvidia-based systems and eventually deploy more Nvidia-based machines, something that may be important in a world where custom silicon developed by hyperscalers is rapidly gaining traction. However, to make this happen, Kessel must be a smashing success that will offer clear advantages over systems designed by Nvidia.

Galaxy Watch 8 LTE (44 mm) com suporte a atividades na academia e treinador personalizado recebe desconto de 67% no Pix com cupom no Magazine Luiza
O Galaxy Watch 8 LTE de 44 mm está saindo por R$ 1.159 no Pix com cupom NOV100 no Magazine Luiza. O smartwatch da Samsung com Treinador de Corrida Personalizado e funções para academia atinge o menor preço já visto pelo Achados no 11.11, com desconto de 67% sobre o original de R$ 3.499.
Os sensores do Galaxy Watch 8 suportam diversas atividades esportivas, com destaque para o Treinador de Corrida Personalizado que oferece metas e monitora distância e ritmo durante corridas, além de outras atividades como musculação e natação. Na parte da saúde, conta com monitores do sono e da oxigenação do sangue (SpO2).
Sua tela Super AMOLED de 1,47″ possui brilho de até 3.000 nits, que reproduz imagens com cores fiéis e tem visibilidade garantida em qualquer lugar. O vidro Cristal de Safira protege-a contra arranhões e pancadas.

articles.title: Pasos para proyectar la pantalla del iPhone al Smart TV sin descargar aplicaciones y gratis
articles.text:
La pantalla del teléfono puede trasladarse al televisor sin cables ni aplicaciones externas. Los usuarios de iPhone pueden proyectar imágenes, videos, presentaciones y otros contenidos en un Smart TV de forma gratuita mediante AirPlay, la tecnología inalámbrica de Apple.
La función requiere que el iPhone y el televisor sean compatibles, estén encendidos, se encuentren cerca y compartan la misma red WiFi. Con esa configuración, el sistema permite ampliar la visualización del contenido del teléfono en una pantalla más grande desde el Centro de control.
Qué dispositivos permiten usar AirPlay para proyectar la pantalla
La herramienta está disponible en modelos recientes de iPhone, desde el iPhone X, y en iPad con iPadOS 13 o versiones posteriores. Es necesario que el dispositivo tenga acceso al Centro de control, desde donde se activa la transmisión hacia el televisor.
Del lado del receptor, varios modelos recientes de Smart TV de Samsung, LG y Sony incluyen compatibilidad nativa con AirPlay. Antes de iniciar el proceso, hay que revisar las especificaciones del electrodoméstico o sus ajustes de conexión para confirmar que la función esté disponible y habilitada.
Por qué ambos aparatos deben estar conectados a la misma red WiFi
El iPhone y el televisor deben usar la misma red WiFi doméstica para que puedan detectarse entre sí. Esta condición permite que el teléfono identifique los dispositivos compatibles cercanos y establezca una conexión inalámbrica para enviar la imagen y el sonido.
La conexión a una misma red WiFi es el requisito central para iniciar la duplicación de pantalla. Si uno de los aparatos está conectado a una red distinta, el televisor no aparecerá en la lista de opciones del iPhone, aunque ambos dispositivos tengan acceso a internet.
Dónde está la opción de duplicar pantalla en iPhone
El primer paso consiste en abrir el Centro de control del teléfono. En los modelos sin botón de inicio, se accede al deslizar un dedo hacia abajo desde la esquina superior derecha de la pantalla. Allí se agrupan herramientas como el control de brillo, el volumen y las conexiones.
Dentro de ese menú aparece el botón “Duplicar pantalla”. Al pulsarlo, el iPhone busca los televisores, receptores y dispositivos compatibles con AirPlay que estén conectados a la red local. La búsqueda suele durar unos segundos, según la estabilidad de la conexión.
Una vez que el Smart TV figure entre las alternativas disponibles, solo hay que seleccionarlo. El iPhone enviará una solicitud de conexión y, en algunos casos, el televisor mostrará un código de seguridad para evitar que otros aparatos de la red accedan sin autorización.
Ese código debe ingresarse en el teléfono para confirmar el vínculo. Tras validar la clave, la pantalla del iPhone se verá en el televisor y el contenido del dispositivo podrá reproducirse en una pantalla de mayor tamaño. La imagen se mantendrá activa hasta que el usuario decida finalizar la sesión o exista una interrupción en la red.
Qué opciones existen si el televisor no aparece o no tiene AirPlay
Si el televisor no figura en el menú, es clave comprobar que esté encendido, conectado a la misma red WiFi que el iPhone y actualizado. Se debe revisar el menú de configuración del aparato, porque algunos modelos exigen activar AirPlay de forma manual antes de aceptar conexiones.
Cuando el televisor no cuenta con soporte nativo, una opción es conectar un Apple TV mediante HDMI. El dispositivo incorpora la recepción de AirPlay y permite duplicar la pantalla sin instalar aplicaciones adicionales.
Si persisten los problemas, reiniciar el iPhone, el televisor y el router puede ayudar a restablecer la comunicación. Para terminar la transmisión, el usuario debe abrir otra vez el Centro de control, pulsar “Duplicar pantalla” y elegir “Detener duplicación”.

articles.title: Amazon's open-source AWS Emulator lets developers validate their code locally, without the cloud - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Amazon’s open-source AWS Emulator lets developers validate their code locally, without the cloud
Amazon Web Services Inc. is turning its public cloud computing platform on its head with the launch of a new service called AWS Emulator.
It’s a free, locally hosted software suite built by autonomous artificial intelligence agents that can replicate hundreds of the company’s cloud services on developer’s workstations. In a blog post, AWS Senior Principal Engineer Matt Goldberg said that the entire service was designed and written exclusively by AI agents, with not even a single line of its code written or reviewed by a human engineer.
AWS Emulator is designed to help customers overcome a major bottleneck in the application development process that has arisen with the adoption of AI coding agents such as AWS Kiro and Claude Code. Those agents are generating line after line of code faster than human programmers can blink, and the sheer velocity of that production is causing real issues for the teams tasked with verifying it before it can ship in production.
All AI-generated code needs to be validated against real cloud infrastructure, but doing that in the real AWS cloud is becoming all but impossible given latency and cost considerations. Though there are some existing third-party AWS emulators that developers can use, those services cover only a small fraction of AWS’ sprawling catalog of cloud services and quickly drift out of sync as those services evolve. With AWS Emulator, developers now have access to a free-to-use, locally hosted emulator that developers can use to run multiple iterative test loops on their own machines, Goldberg said.
Built by AI agents, for AI agents
The new tool was the brainchild of Goldberg, but he was actually inspired by the creation of AWS’ foundational Paxos-based distributed locking service, called “Alf,” which still underpins core cloud services such as Amazon S3 and DynamoDB.
In a second blog post, Swami Sivasubramanian, AWS’ vice president of agentic AI and emerging technologies, explained that when he and his colleagues first built Alf more than 20 years ago, they could test it only by simulating its entire environment inside a Java virtual machine built manually over several months.
Sivasubramanian explained that his team would have to inject faults and isolate concurrency bugs manually before they could deploy new services in production. But as AWS’ cloud has scaled up, it’s no longer feasible to hand-craft a simulation of its entire platform.
This is the conundrum that inspired Goldberg to see if that task could instead be done by AI agents. After seeing research that showed how AI agents were able to build a C code compiler from scratch, he concluded that they should also be able to replicate any AWS service if given a formal specification and reference implementation.
So he set about doing so, using AWS’ public Smithy API models as the specification and the live AWS platform as the ground truth. He began by prompting AWS Kiro to rebuild the Amazon Simple Queue Service, and it generated a functional replica of that service within just 15 minutes.
Seeing the potential, Goldberg and his team then set about organizing dozens of autonomous agents running on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore into three separate teams. The first is tasked with generating thousands of end-to-end fidelity test suites from API models and verifying them against the live AWS cloud. The second runs the tests against the emulator to try and find any bugs or discrepancies, and if any are identified, those agents will automatically file a GitHub issue.
The third team was tasked with creating and implementing the fixes for those bugs. As a final step before the code enters the GitHub repository, it goes through an automated merge gate that’s supervised by adversarial security agents to check for any vulnerabilities.
Holger Mueller of Constellation Research said AWS is addressing a key challenge that has arisen for software developers in the agentic era, namely how to test that something works in the cloud, without actually running those tests in the cloud, which is prohibitively expensive, not to mention a risk in itself. “AWS’s answer is to effectively build a digital twin of its public cloud to test the capabilities of the AI agents working with it,” the analyst said. “It’s remarkable that AWS built this twin completely with agents. Moreover, the emulator is a smart move, because it enables these test workloads to be offloaded right where the developers are, on their own machines.”
A new role for software engineers
The AWS Emulator is available for anyone to download starting today. It’s built in the Rust programming language and runs as a local HTTP server that can be accessed via a command-line interface on Linux, Windows, macOS or as a Docker container. To get started, developers simply have to redirect their AWS CLI or SDK calls to the localhost to enable rapid, offline validation that’s free.
AWS Emulator has been open-sourced under a Creative Commons CC0 public-domain dedication license, together with its raw commit history and a public backlog of known discrepancies filed under “things-that-do-not-work.”
Sivasubramanian said AWS Emulator illustrates the dramatic evolution of the role of the software engineer. With AI agents now responsible for the grunt work of writing, testing and debugging the actual code, humans are now becoming “systems orchestrators,” tasked with defining the boundaries, architecting the test specifications and designing the guardrails that guide the work of those agents.

articles.title: ‘This is rural. This is country. Leave it as it is’: This planned 600MW data center in London’s green belt has infuriated local residents — and it’s not hard to understand why
articles.text:
‘This is rural. This is country. Leave it as it is’: This planned 600MW data center in London’s green belt has infuriated local residents — and it’s not hard to understand why
The developer's own plans show it won't meet Net Zero
- A data center planned to be built in London's green belt has faced opposition from local residents
- The site will occupy more than 200 acres of green space, with the developers calling the site "a sustainable datacentre campus of the future"
- But the site will not meet Net Zero commitments and is projected to have the highest carbon emissions of any planned or operational UK data center
Residents beside a planned data center on the outskirts of London are not happy about the planned development which will see over 200 acres of greenbelt land ceded to developers to be converted into one of Europe’s largest data centers boasting 400,000 square meters of hardware capacity.
Data center developers in the UK have been having a tough time recently, with plans for the world’s second largest data center in Fife, Scotland, seeing widespread opposition, and a 450MW site in North Wales facing a rather negative reception.
But for some residents of North Ockendon in Havering, the idea of building a data center in green belt designated land is “sacrilege” and the development would damage the look and feel of the local community.
Residents oppose green belt development
According to multiple residents, who spoke with the BBC, the development would detract from the natural setting of North Ockendon and set a precedent for green belt land development.
North Ockendon resident Emma Edmonds said, “Most people absolutely don't want this. It's sacrilege to just build something like that here. It's not the right place at all,” while Danny Leach, whose property sits close to the planned development, said, “There will be the construction for the next eight to 20 years. There will be noise, there's going to be another thousand vehicles a day they're saying.”
“There will be disruption, the mess, and then, obviously, when it's operational, the background noise the data centres make and the amount of electric it uses - we already have two power cuts a month here,” Leach added. “We all need data, but do we need the largest data centre in Europe in this location?”
The North Ockendon Residents Association labelled the project as a “massacre” of green belt land, with a spokesperson adding, “It’s crop-producing farmland, in an age when we are threatened by security, it’s the loss of wildlife habitats, and there’s the pollution cost, which everyone seems to brush under the carpet.”
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
“This is rural. This is country. Leave it as it is,” local resident Graham Ford said.
Developers promise jobs, investment, and a park
In recent months, data center developers have had to become more vocal and involved with communities in the vicinity of a planned development. As the examples in Scotland and Wales have shown, if residents feel they are not getting enough out of a multi-billion pound investment they will do everything they can to make breaking ground as difficult as possible.
To that end, the UK government has announced plans that could force developers to invest in local communities as part of an AI “covenant” aimed at restoring trust between residents and developers and providing a worthwhile benefit to local communities.
The developers of the Havering data center, Digital Reef, have promised a range of benefits for local residents, including 620 full time jobs once the data center is operational, a 113-hectare Ecology Park with a 100%+ net biodiversity gain, and an £11.54 million community payment. The site is also expected to be Net Zero in operation with “zero onsite fossil fuels,” with the site “set to become a leading centre for skills development in the science, technology, sustainability, and data economy sectors.”
But despite claiming to be Net Zero in operation, Digital Reef has said in a planning application that the site “does not align with a science-based 1.5C compatible trajectory and achieving net zero by 2050.”
The site is also projected to have the highest projected carbon emissions of any project in the UK, according to The Guardian analysis of available data. Additional planning documents state that any shortfall of the zero-carbon target “would be provided through a cash in lieu contribution to the borough’s carbon offset fund,” a sum Digital Reef estimates to be about £77.6 million.
Many data centers across the UK, particularly in London, are facing issues with getting hooked up to the electricity grid. Microsoft recently withdrew residency plans from a planned London data center after learning that the site would not be operational until early 2030.
Couple that with a queue of over 140 data centers seeking more than 50GW in grid connections that, if approved, would use more than the UK’s 2026 peak energy demand.
For the planned development, Digital Reef said that at a 50% load the campus would use about 2.65 billion kWh per year of electricity — or the equivalent of more than 1 million UK households.
