articles.title: Un robot construit seul une structure dans l’espace pour la toute première fois : le champ des possibles s’ouvre
articles.text:
Pour la première fois, un robot a assemblé seul une structure en orbite. Une démonstration qui pourrait changer la façon dont on construira les futurs engins spatiaux.
Le secteur spatial est en pleine ébullition. Entre les méga-constellations de satellites, les projets de data centers en orbite et la conquête de la Lune, c’est une toute nouvelle économie qui est en train de naître. Mais cette croissance se frottera forcément à une limite : la capacité d’emport des lanceurs, qui est obligatoirement limitée. Et si ASTRA changeait la donne ?
Une petite antenne d’1,4 mètre
C’est le nom d’un petit robot conçu par des chercheurs de la prestigieuse université Caltech et financé par la DARPA, l’agence de recherche du Pentagone. Il s’inscrit dans le cadre du programme NOM4D, dont l’objectif est de construire de très grandes structures dans l’espace.
Lancé le 30 mars dernier à bord d’une fusée Falcon 9 de SpaceX, il est niché dans un véhicule orbital de la société Momentus, et tient dans un volume d’environ 1 mètre cube. Cela paraît très restreint, certes, mais assez pour renfermer la machinerie et les matériaux nécessaires à la construction. Sa mission : construire une antenne d’1,4 mètre de large.
Ainsi, son bras articulé a attrapé des tubes en fibre composite et des joints en aluminium dans ses réserves, puis les a assemblés comme un jeu de Meccano pour former l’ossature de l’antenne qui compte pour l’instant trois modules. Deux d’entre eux ont été préassemblés : ASTRA s’est chargé de monter le troisième lui-même.
Les usages sont nombreux, les obstacles aussi
Depuis la Terre, les ingénieurs ne peuvent communiquer avec le robot que sept ou huit fois par jour, une quinzaine de minutes à chaque fois. Et les échanges s’avèrent complexes : ils envoient les consignes, regardent les photos transmises par le robot, puis reproduisent le problème sur un double au laboratoire lorsque ça coince. Une fois la solution trouvée, ils la transmettent en orbite.
Résultat, l’antenne, prévue en onze modules, ne sera pas terminée avant la fin de la mission en décembre. Mais ce n’est absolument pas un échec pour les chercheurs, bien au contraire : leur démonstration ouvre de nouvelles possibilités.
Car aujourd’hui, les ingénieurs n’ont que deux options pour envoyer de grands objets dans l’espace, soit plier la structure pour qu’elle se déploie une fois là-haut, ou s’appuyer sur des astronautes pour assembler des pièces lancées séparément. ASTRA ouvre une troisième voie : transporter les matériaux en kit et laisser un robot faire le reste sur place.
Et les applications sont nombreuses. On pourrait, par exemple, bâtir des télescopes dotés de miroirs bien plus grands que ceux d’aujourd’hui, capables de capter davantage de lumière et d’observer des objets plus lointains, mais aussi de gigantesques antennes de communication, ou de vastes panneaux solaires qui récolteraient l’énergie du Soleil pour la renvoyer vers la Terre. Andrew Detor, responsable du programme chez la DARPA, voit très grand et vise des structures de « centaines de mètres, voire de kilomètres », ce qui est impossible aujourd’hui. Mais le chemin pour y parvenir sera encore très long.
Sources : ScienceDaily, Space.com
L’assemblage robotisé en orbite consiste à construire une structure pièce par pièce une fois dans l’espace, à partir d’éléments séparés (tubes, joints, segments). C’est différent d’un mécanisme déployable, où l’objet est lancé déjà formé mais replié, puis s’ouvre grâce à des charnières, des câbles ou des systèmes élastiques. L’assemblage permet en théorie des structures plus grandes et plus modulaires, car on n’est plus limité par la taille de la coiffe du lanceur et par les contraintes mécaniques du repliement. En contrepartie, il exige une robotique plus fine (alignement, verrouillage, tolérances) et une capacité à gérer des imprévus sans intervention humaine directe.
La capacité d’emport désigne ce qu’une fusée peut transporter en masse, mais aussi en volume, notamment à cause de la taille de la coiffe qui enferme la charge utile. Même si un lanceur peut soulever lourd, il ne peut pas embarquer un objet trop encombrant ou fragile sans le plier, le segmenter, ou le renforcer (ce qui ajoute du poids). Les grandes antennes, miroirs de télescopes ou panneaux solaires sont vite pénalisés par ces contraintes géométriques et mécaniques. L’approche “en kit” vise à contourner ce plafond en lançant des pièces standardisées, puis en reconstituant la structure une fois en orbite.
En orbite basse, un véhicule n’est visible depuis une station sol que durant des passages brefs, ce qui limite la durée des liaisons radio à quelques minutes par orbite. La bande passante et la latence peuvent aussi restreindre le télépilotage fin, surtout si l’on dépend d’images et de retours capteurs pour décider des gestes. Cela pousse à travailler en « commandes différées » : on envoie un plan d’action, on récupère des données, puis on corrige au passage suivant. Plus les tâches d’assemblage sont complexes, plus l’autonomie embarquée (détection d’erreurs, ajustements, contrôle de force) devient déterminante pour éviter un cycle lent d’essais/erreurs depuis le sol.

articles.title: Seagate is bringing back the hybrid drive, but you have to supply the SSD
articles.text:
Editor's take: Hybrid drives were all the rage among storage makers a little over a decade ago. Seagate thinks today's chaotic hardware landscape is ripe for further exploitation, which is why the company is now offering an extra-pricey new device designed to resurrect the whole hybrid drive concept.
Seagate has introduced the FireCuda Forge, an external "desktop" HDD designed to approach NVMe-class data rates by embedding a smaller SSD in the same enclosure. Just like classic hybrid drives, FireCuda Forge can store frequently used data on a much faster solid-state cache. Unlike those older designs, however, the SSD isn't included: the user has to supply it.
FireCuda Forge is currently available in 8TB and 20TB capacities, priced at $699 and $899 respectively. The external HDD hosts a "non-populated" slot for a user-provided M.2 SSD, with Seagate capping the usable cache at 1TB, which further increases the expense required to enjoy the improved data rates the device is allegedly designed to achieve.
FireCuda Forge includes Alkemi, a whole new I/O management technology Seagate developed to bring this hybrid drive concept to fruition. The storage giant explained that Alkemi uses an FPGA chip and an embedded Linux OS to manage the solid-state cache. The system constantly monitors file access workloads so that it can decide which data to prioritize and copy onto the faster SSD.
Alkemi is allegedly capable of adapting to each user's needs, employing optimized caching policies to achieve higher cache hit rates. FireCuda Forge is primarily pitched as a gaming storage drive, with Seagate testing several gaming sessions representing 4.3 million I/O requests. Overall, Alkemi reached a cache hit rate of 90%.
The new hybrid drive behaves like a single storage unit, which means the host operating system just "sees" one drive. That makes data management simpler, but it also introduces a potential reliability risk if something goes wrong in either the SSD cache or the HDD portion of the drive.
On paper, a fully populated FireCuda Forge should deliver high-bandwidth throughput for gaming and recording workloads, with speeds up to 2,500MB/s read and 2,000MB/s write over USB4. The external drive is compatible with M.2 2280, PCIe Gen3 or newer SSDs, while official OS support includes Windows 11 and macOS 26.
FireCuda Forge's high price tag will likely hurt the device's popularity, and prices aren't likely to improve anytime soon. Just like the other few surviving HDD manufacturers, Seagate is now enjoying a massive revenue increase thanks to growing demand from AI data centers.

articles.title: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080 24 GB Reportedly Cancelled, 16 GB Model Remains
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 11th 2026
NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080 24 GB Reportedly Cancelled, 16 GB Model Remains
NVIDIA's rumored GeForce RTX 5080 24 GB model has reportedly been put on hold. The company is struggling to secure enough 3 GB GDDR7 memory modules and is instead opting for the less expensive 2 GB modules for the standard 16 GB version. According to a report from Board Channels, NVIDIA has already informed its add-in card (AIC) partners to officially cancel the January 2027 launch plan for the 24 GB model, citing economic challenges. As we are currently experiencing one of the worst supply chain shortages for memory modules, using the more expensive 3 GB GDDR7 modules would result in a significantly higher MSRP and, consequently, a higher price for customers. Therefore, the 2 GB GDDR7 memory modules will continue to be used, and the RTX 5080 16 GB model will remain available.
Readers may recall that NVIDIA did not plan any other changes to the model besides the memory configuration, as the CUDA core count was to remain the same. The new 24 GB model would potentially have slightly higher TDP and clock speeds, but the main improvements would come from increased memory capacity and bandwidth. Since it seems we won't be getting the revised model, and there's no rumor of a "SUPER" overhaul anytime soon, we will have to stick with the standard lineup a bit longer until the next-generation GeForce RTX 60-Series "Rubin" arrives.Earlier rumors suggested that the GeForce RTX 5080 24 GB might launch sooner than expected, with availability projected around January 2027. It was said that NVIDIA was clearing out its RTX 5080 16 GB GPU inventory, with the remaining stock expected to last about two months. However, since AIC partners have not yet received those GPU kits, this timeline was impossible to meet. The cancellation now indicates that the launch is reportedly not happening at all.

articles.title: Softbank loses $3.7 billion on canceled AI data center gas turbine orders days after denying Elon Musk’s claim it was defaulting —company kills reserved 13 gigawatts of power, more than six Hoover Dams’ worth of capacity
articles.text:
Softbank loses $3.7 billion on canceled AI data center gas turbine orders days after denying Elon Musk’s claim it was defaulting — company kills reserved 13 gigawatts of power, more than six Hoover Dams’ worth of capacity
“This is simply not correct at all,” Softbank argued after Elon Musk claimed it had defaulted on a raft of unrequired data center turbines.
By early 2026, Japanese tech investment outfit SoftBank had reserved more power generation capacity than the entire state of Connecticut after cornering a huge portion of the global gas turbine production capacity. Now, the same company has chosen to take a $3.7 billion hit to its earnings after canceling reservations for the highly sought-after power generation hardware. The WSJ reports that SoftBank had reserved more than 13 gigawatts of power-producing turbines, citing unnamed "people familiar with the orders." That's the equivalent of more than six Hoover Dams' worth of capacity, with SoftBank founder and chief executive Masayoshi Son believing that it would be vital to the company's earning potential moving forward. Notably, this development surfaced after SoftBank's CFO fired back at Elon Musk's recent revelation that the company had defaulted on turbine blade contracts, saying, "there is no such default."
The gas turbines were to power AI data centers, and SoftBank is set to build a 9.2-gigawatt power plant in Ohio, with construction scheduled for early 2027. It'll cost $33 billion to build and will provide power to a neighboring eight-gigawatt data center. That data center will be leased to OpenAI, albeit only after Nvidia entered discussions about guaranteeing around $250 billion of financing for the project.
But SoftBank got ahead of itself. After initially planning to use the turbines for future gas-powered plants, the company has now chosen to change direction. Orders for turbines, engines that convert natural gas into the electricity used by data centers, must be placed years in advance of them being required. The company had bet big, placing huge orders with the expectation that demand would greatly outstrip supply. That would leave SoftBank in an enviable position, holding huge orders for the vital components required as part of a data center rollout boosted by AI demand. But those reservations weren't cheap — turbine manufacturers regularly charge customers tens of millions of dollars per gigawatt.
It's now canceled its remaining reservations with GE Vernova, its turbine supplier, while also unwinding contracts for orders that were too far gone. SoftBank told investors on a recent earnings call that the orders had been placed “to secure power generation equipment in anticipation of shortages,” but it now appears it anticipated a little too much.
Crucially, SoftBank is also keen for everyone to know that this move was voluntary and that it did not default on its orders. That's contrary to what xAI CEO Elon Musk claimed in a post on his X social network. SoftBank Chief Financial Officer Yoshimitsu Goto was quick to counter Musk's claims. “This is simply not correct at all,” Goto reportedly said. “There is no such default.”

articles.title: AMD Zen 6 : jusqu’à 32 cœurs par CCD et un IPC qui bondit de 27 % par rapport à Zen 5
articles.text:
Zen 6, ce n'est pas encore pour tout de suite sur les processeurs de nos PC personnels, mais les promesses des modèles EPYC (serveurs) sont chaque jour plus impressionnantes.
Nous le savons depuis déjà plusieurs mois, AMD n'a prévu de lancer de processeurs en architecture Zen 6 pour sa division « client » avant encore plusieurs mois. Intelligence artificielle oblige, la priorité est donnée aux puces à destination des serveurs, les fameux CPU EPYC qui se dévoilent encore un peu plus aujourd'hui.
BenQ iScreenBar : la barre lumineuse qui s’accorde avec l’iMac
Des lignes en harmonie avec celles de l’ordinateur d’Apple, une conception rigoureuse, des matériaux sélectionnés, rien n’a été laissé au hasard, tout comme le service qu’elle rend une fois allumée !
Zen 6 arrive sur EPYC 9006 « Venice »
Souvenez-vous, après un teasing savamment organisé, AMD avait dévoilé le 26 juillet dernier ses premiers processeurs en architecture Zen 6, destinés à remplacer le plus logiquement du monde le Zen 5 actuel.
À l'occasion de cette révélation, AMD avait notamment confirmé que, dans un premier temps, Zen 6 sera réservé aux seuls processeurs pour serveurs, cette catégorie de puces portant le nom d'EPYC. Pas question donc de Ryzen Zen 6, au moins jusqu'en 2027.
Quatre variantes de processeurs EPYC étaient annoncées avec les EPYC 9006 SP7 et SP8 prévus pour les centres de données. Les premiers pourront compter jusqu'à 256 cœurs alors que les seconds seront limités à 128 cœurs, mais dans les deux cas, on parlait d'une fréquence maximale de 5 GHz sur 96 cœurs et d'un TDP de 600 watts.
Des EPYC 9006X et 9006LP sont également prévus afin de toucher des professionnels différents : le 9006X, par exemple, disposera de ce fameux 3D Vertical Cache pour atteindre jusqu'à 1 152 Mo de cache L3, alors que le 9006LP – limité à « seulement » 72 cœurs – aura la particularité d'être associé à de la mémoire vive en LPDDR5X.
Ces informations, AMD les complétait par quelques indications sur ce que l'on peut attendre côté performances… mais sans trop entrer dans les détails non plus. Il fallait se contenter d'estimations : ces puces EPYC Zen 6 (Venice) seraient entre 1,8 et 3,5 fois plus puissantes que les Xeon 6980P d'Intel… bien sûr, selon le protocole mis en place par AMD.
Une moyenne de +27 % d'IPC par rapport à Zen 5
Aujourd'hui, nos confrères de VideoCardz et Wccftech relaient de nouvelles précisions lesquelles, toutefois, sont toujours fournies par AMD. Elles restent intéressantes, mais à prendre avec la prudence habituelle.
Le chiffre le plus important – nous le donnions dès le titre de cette actualité – est ce 27 % d'instructions par cycle (IPC) supplémentaires sur des charges dites serveurs. D'emblée, il faut apporter une information clé à propos de ce +27 %. En effet, AMD indique qu'il est obtenu en comparant 16 cœurs Zen 6c sur un unique CCD avec 16 cœurs Zen 5 partagés sur deux CCD, avec des fréquences de fonctionnement identiques.
AMD ajoute également un +20 % sur les charges de travail cloud et un +31 % sur des charges IA. De fait, le +27 % d'abord avancé par AMD est en réalité une moyenne prise sur plusieurs scénarios et ne constitue pas une comparaison directe des instructions par cycle sur un simple cœur. Cela pourrait avoir son importance au moment de porter Zen 6 sur les processeurs Ryzen.
Les différents documents communiqués par AMD confirment aussi quelques détails à propos de l'organisation des puces. Un CCD Zen 6 standard serait ainsi doté de 12 cœurs – contre 8 sur Zen 5 – impliquant une augmentation du cache L3 partagé de 32 Mo à 48 Mo. Zen 6c va plus loin avec un doublement du nombre de cœurs par CCD (de 16 à 32) et un quadruplement du cache L3 (de 32 Mo à 128 Mo).
De multiples autres précisions techniques ont été communiquées par AMD, qui évoque par exemple une augmentation du reorder buffer de 448 à 640 entrées ou le passage de 240 à 352 entrées du fichier de registre physique entier. Des précisions qui auront plus d'importance quand nous serons davantage fixés sur le passage de Zen 6 aux processeurs Ryzen.
En effet, AMD a également parlé de fréquences maximales de 5,3 GHz, dans des cas bien particuliers, de la prise en charge du PCIe Gen 6 et de la DDR5 MRDIMM jusqu'à 12 800 MT/s, mais la marque s'est surtout gardée d'évoquer de quelque manière que ce soit les Ryzen Zen 6. 2027 ? Vraisemblablement. Premier semestre ? Nous avons de sérieux doutes.
Source : VideoCardz, Wccftech

articles.title: AI infrastructure clouds face a shakeout over software skills - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Neoclouds face a shakeout as cloud-native software skills decide who survives
AI infrastructure clouds have multiplied as GPU capital pours into new data centers, but standing up capacity is proving easier than running it at scale. With Kubernetes now hardened into the operating layer for AI factories, the cloud-native community holds expertise that many of these new providers lack.
KubeCon has been shifting toward an AI infrastructure event, with container orchestration for AI and distributed inference now central to the conversation. The newer AI clouds run on the same computing fundamentals as the hyperscalers before them, yet many specialize narrowly and lack a bridge to the enterprise systems that will ultimately consume their capacity, according to Sarbjeet Johal (pictured), chief executive officer of Stackpane.
“I’m afraid that the neoclouds, if they don’t partner with the ones who are appreciating the brownfield, they will suffer,” Johal said. “They can’t survive on their own because, who is going to take that compute from them? It’s the hyperscalers. The neoclouds are the overflow.”
Johal spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier and Rebecca Knight at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon NA, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed the event’s first-day takeaways, from AI-written code and token economics to the maturing neocloud market and the skills needed to run it. (* Disclosure below.)
Software chops will sort the winners among AI infrastructure clouds
Kubernetes spent more than a decade evolving in fits and starts, and the payoff is now showing up in AI. The Cloud Native Computing Foundation added a dedicated AI inference and agentic track to this year’s KubeCon North America schedule, a sign of where practitioner attention has moved. Kubernetes now runs across about two-thirds of the enterprise, sits inside Nvidia Corp.’s reference architectures and underpins the neoclouds, Furrier noted. Skills honed through years of operating Kubernetes are now being applied directly to the commercial buildout of AI factories, where most of the capital is going.
“Now it’s hardened. So when you have hardened Kubernetes, we’re seeing inference being talked about,” Furrier said. “Who would have thought at this show inference would be discussed? Well, guess what? Distributed inference is the hottest area right now.”
That maturity matters because so much AI capital spending is flowing to new providers. SoftBank Group Corp. unveiled plans to enter the U.S. neocloud business this summer, joining a crowded field. Many existing operators started out building data centers for bitcoin mining or arbitraging spot pricing rather than running large-scale software, according to Furrier, who sees a reckoning ahead. The hard part is less about acquiring GPUs than operating them as a true cloud.
“Half the neoclouds will fail,” Furrier said. “To run a big neocloud, you’ve got to look like CoreWeave. Well, guess what CoreWeave is? The founders know data centers. … People who know large-scale software stacks at scale win.”
The rescue, in Furrier’s view, will come from the cloud-native community. He pointed to CoreWeave Inc., whose engineering is run by former Google Cloud LLC executive Chen Goldberg, as the model for pairing data center know-how with large-scale software skills. He also suggested private equity investors could buy smaller Kubernetes companies to fill the gap. Those companies could command billion-dollar valuations as data center owners with land, power and shell seek help with connectivity, multigeneration Nvidia hardware and workloads that span data centers, he explained. Johal, who watched a similar story play out at Rackspace Technology Inc., agreed that software will decide which providers last.
“We have seen this movie earlier. So if you want to be a good hyperscaler, if you don’t have the software chops, you’re dead,” Johal said of the new AI infrastructure clouds. “We knew how to run data centers at Rackspace, but we didn’t have software chops. … Without software chops, you’re dead in the water.”

articles.title: Legisladores del Congreso de Estados Unidos piden investigar al CEO de Nvidia y un senador reclama su renuncia
articles.text:
El CEO de Nvidia, Jensen Huang, enfrenta pedidos de legisladores de Estados Unidos para que se investiguen sus contactos con una ejecutiva presuntamente vinculada a la inteligencia china. Un senador republicano incluso reclamó su renuncia por posibles riesgos de seguridad nacional.
La controversia se intensificó después de que Huang reconociera una relación extramatrimonial, mientras la compañía abrió una revisión interna para determinar si existieron filtraciones de información o vulnerabilidades en sus sistemas de protección.
Nvidia sostuvo que, por ahora, no tiene indicios de que secretos empresariales o intereses de seguridad nacional hayan sido comprometidos.
Un senador pidió la salida de Huang de Nvidia
El senador republicano por Dakota del Norte, Kevin Cramer, consideró que la situación podría dejar a Huang expuesto a presiones externas. En declaraciones recogidas por Politico, afirmó que el eventual riesgo de extorsión es demasiado alto para el responsable de una empresa central en el desarrollo de chips de inteligencia artificial. Por ese motivo, consideró que debería dimitir.
El legislador, integrante del Comité Bancario del Senado, sostuvo que la continuidad del ejecutivo al frente de Nvidia representa un asunto de seguridad. El presidente Donald Trump indicó esta semana que el Buró Federal de Investigaciones (FBI) analiza el caso, aunque también dijo que Huang le aseguró desconocer los supuestos vínculos de la mujer con organismos de inteligencia extranjeros.
El Congreso quiere conocer los protocolos de seguridad de la empresa
El senador demócrata por Delaware, Chris Coons, anticipó que buscará que el Comité de Relaciones Exteriores del Senado revise si la relación pudo haber afectado la seguridad de Estados Unidos. Según Forbes, Coons considera posible que información sensible haya quedado expuesta.
Además, los presidentes de los comités de Asuntos Exteriores, Inteligencia y Competencia Estratégica con China de la Cámara de Representantes convocaron a Huang a una sesión privada el 18 de noviembre. Los republicanos Brian Mast, John Moolenaar y Rick Crawford solicitaron explicaciones sobre sus vínculos con la ejecutiva, los riesgos de espionaje y los mecanismos internos de protección de Nvidia.
La citación se produjo en medio de un debate legislativo para reforzar las restricciones a las ventas de tecnología avanzada a China. En una declaración conjunta, el senador republicano Jim Banks y la senadora demócrata Elizabeth Warren reclamaron al Departamento de Comercio que cierre vacíos en los controles de exportación y respaldaron la incorporación de la AI Overwatch Act a la ley anual de defensa.
Esa iniciativa ampliaría la supervisión del Congreso sobre las exportaciones de chips avanzados. Los legisladores también evalúan incluir la Chip Security Act, que prevé sistemas para rastrear la ubicación de los procesadores y prevenir su contrabando, y la MATCH Act, orientada a que los países aliados limiten la venta a China de maquinaria para fabricar semiconductores.
La carta enviada a Huang, fechada el 4 de noviembre, fijó este miércoles 11 de noviembre como plazo para responder a la solicitud o proponer otra fecha. Nvidia no hizo comentarios sobre el pedido de comparecencia, aunque indicó que sus clientes de computación en la nube de Asia reciben información comercial habitual y no secretos corporativos ni datos vinculados con la seguridad nacional.
Nvidia abrió una investigación independiente
La empresa informó que su junta directiva creó un comité de directores independientes, con asesoramiento jurídico externo, para examinar los señalamientos. La investigación busca establecer si Huang fue blanco de una operación de inteligencia extranjera y si hubo consecuencias para la compañía o para la seguridad estadounidense.
Nvidia afirmó que no cuenta con pruebas de una filtración de secretos corporativos o información de seguridad nacional, aunque aclaró que la revisión analizará todos los datos disponibles. Huang, quien pidió disculpas a su familia en un mensaje a los empleados, manifestó su disposición a colaborar con el proceso y la compañía indicó que seguirá en su cargo durante la pesquisa.
Alice Huang es señalada por presuntos vínculos con Beijing
La ejecutiva mencionada en los reportes fue identificada como Alice Huang, también conocida como Huang Le. Es una empresaria china que ocupó un cargo directivo en Megaspeed International, una firma de centros de datos con sede en Singapur. No se conoce que tenga algún parentesco con Jensen Huang, pese a que ambos comparten apellido.
Según informó The New York Times, las autoridades estadounidenses concluyeron que la empresaria recopilaba información sobre el CEO de Nvidia para Beijing.
Una investigación posterior reveló que Huang buscó financiación, a comienzos de 2025, para desarrollar un centro de datos en el Sudeste Asiático. El proyecto, valuado en varios cientos de millones de dólares, contemplaba alquilar capacidad de cómputo a empresas chinas y requería acceso a procesadores gráficos de Nvidia. Megaspeed también es objeto de investigaciones en varias jurisdicciones por presunto contrabando de chips.

articles.title: CEO Jensen Huang's job is suddenly on the line at Nvidia
articles.text:
Nvidia’s board is set to decide the future of its founder Jensen Huang after revelations that he had a romantic relationship with a company executive, days after it emerged that he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy.
The board held urgent talks on Wednesday night after news broke of the Nvidia chief executive’s relationship with Kimberly Powell, the chipmaker’s vice-president of healthcare, according to people familiar with the matter.
The relationship with an Nvidia employee deepens an already damaging scandal for the $4.2 trillion semiconductor group. Huang on Sunday admitted to having an affair, two days after the FT reported his romantic links to an executive at an Nvidia client, who US officials believe is a Chinese intelligence asset.
Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Powell, who has worked at Nvidia for more than 18 years and is among its more prominent public figures, could not be reached for comment.
The board, which unusually has no chair in a testament to Huang’s singular role at Nvidia, this week hired a former federal prosecutor to investigate his affair with the suspected spy. But the board has thus far backed Huang to remain as chief executive.
The directors could opt to have Huang step back from his duties as CEO while the investigation proceeds and the board intensifies succession planning. Or they could now push for his immediate departure.
Nvidia’s annual reports and corporate governance paperwork have until now included no specific reference to “succession planning” and set out no details for how it would replace its CEO, even in an emergency.

articles.title: ASRock quietly rolls out new firmware after disastrous previous update killed Radeon RX 7900-series GPUs — company provides no clarity on warranty coverage for dead cards or changelog
articles.text:
ASRock quietly rolls out new firmware after disastrous previous update killed Radeon RX 7900-series GPUs — company provides no clarity on warranty coverage for dead cards or changelog
New firmware might prevent more bricked cards, but ASRock isn't saying for sure
ASRock has rolled out a new firmware update for its Radeon RX 7000-series graphics cards. The latest VBIOS version 1.0.6 appears to be a follow-up to the previous 1.0.5 release. According to community reports, that older version was bricking some of the company's Radeon RX 7900 XT and RX 7900 XTX graphics cards. The new update has now quietly made its way to the ASRock official website, although the company has not published a changelog or provided any details on what the new update addresses.
Last month, AMD released a VBIOS patch for Radeon RX 7000-series graphics cards to address potential security vulnerabilities. While the company did not disclose any technical details about the vulnerabilities, it assured gamers that there had been no reports of them being exploited. According to a statement shared with ComputerBase, the company provided the following rationale for the update:
"AMD is releasing a firmware update as part of our usual approach to address potential security vulnerabilities. These corrections are already made available before the public announcement to give customers time to update their firmware. As a best practice, we recommend that users update the firmware of their graphics cards as soon as they are provided by the respective GPU manufacturer. There are no reports of exploiting these security vulnerabilities in practice."
ASRock subsequently listed the 1.0.5 VBIOS update for 10 graphics card models, spanning its Radeon RX 7600 XT, RX 7700 XT, RX 7800 XT, RX 7900 XT, and RX 7900 XTX families. However, several Radeon RX 7900 XT and RX 7900 XTX owners reported that their systems failed to boot after installing the firmware. Some lucky users were able to use external EEPROM programmers to recover their cards. Although ASRock has since removed the 1.0.5 update from its website, it has yet to provide clarity on what caused the failures or confirm whether the newly released VBIOS addresses the issue.
There are also unanswered questions around how ASRock plans to help customers who have already been affected. According to reports shared with VideoCardz, a user in Japan received a confirmation from ASRock that the failed update would be covered under warranty. However, another owner in Europe was reportedly directed to seek warranty service despite having an out-of-warranty graphics card. This essentially leaves affected owners uncertain of whether they will receive free repairs or replacements.
Additionally, the lack of a changelog or an official statement, along with the new firmware version, makes it difficult for users to determine whether installing the replacement firmware is safe. We can only hope that ASRock provides some clarity around what version 1.06

articles.title: ‘I’m beyond disappointed because ChatGPT means a lot to me’: Users are furious that OpenAI is retiring their favorite voice modes
articles.text:
‘I’m beyond disappointed because ChatGPT means a lot to me’: Users are furious that OpenAI is retiring their favorite voice modes
A small but vocal section of the ChatGPT community really isn’t happy
- OpenAI is retiring two beloved voice modes from ChatGPT — Standard and Advanced
- From December 11, Live mode will be the only voice mode in ChatGPT
- Some vocal ChatGPT users have taken to Reddit and X to complain
OpenAI is retiring the older Standard and Advanced Voice modes for ChatGPT in December across all its subscriptions, leaving only the newer Live Voice mode. Rather than simply diction, ChatGPT’s voice modes are a way of interacting with the chatbot using your voice, so you can have a real-time voice conversation. You talk, and ChatGPT talks back.
While OpenAI says that nearly all ChatGPT users are already using the newer Live Voice mode anyway, there’s a small, but very vocal contingent of the ChatGPT community who are very unhappy to see Standard and Advanced disappear, and they’ve taken to Reddit to express their outrage.
“I'm beyond disappointed because ChatGPT means a lot to me”, said one user, while another follows up by saying that they feel like they’re “paying a monthly subscription to beta-test their questionable decisions”.
The problem derives from a simple matter of preference for the older modes, the way they work, and in particular the sound of the voices they use.
How the three voice modes differ
The big change happens on December 11. Before then, to change between the three voice modes you need to go to Settings, then Voice and choose the mode you want.
Standard mode works by converting your speech to text, then generating a text answer before reading it aloud. Advanced mode works by processing speech directly, but takes turns speaking and listening. That means no interruptions.
The newer Live mode can listen and speak simultaneously with more natural interruptions and responses. Personally, Live mode is my favorite by a long way. To me it feels less robotic and more like a human conversation; however it seems that not everybody is a fan.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
There seem to be a couple of strong reasons why people object to the change. In many cases, they’ve become attached to a particular voice. One Reddit poster describes using the Vale voice for years and finding it comforting, while selecting Vale in GPT-Live doesn’t reproduce exactly the same experience.
Another aspect is that the supposedly more natural conversations of Live actually feel less natural to some people. It does a lot of ‘yeah’ and ‘anyway’ to fill in the gaps while it’s thinking. It interrupts, breaking the user's train of thought, and there are more changes in tone. Many people find this irritating.
Getting some perspective
I think we need to remember that the change doesn’t mean that we’re losing voice in ChatGPT entirely. OpenAI is simply consolidating voice into the Live model so that it can devote more development time to it without having to maintain Standard and Advanced as well.
In a statement on its Help center, OpenAI said: “We recognize that some people are accustomed to Advanced or Standard voice’s style or way of responding, and these model transitions can be challenging. Our Help Center article on navigating model transitions offers guidance to help with the change.”
Of course, it remains to be seen how much the opposition to this change will grow. This isn’t the first time OpenAI has tried to retire Standard Voice mode. In September 2025, it announced that Standard Voice would be retired within 30 days. But on September 9, the company reversed course, acknowledging that users valued the older experience and saying it would remain available while OpenAI addressed feedback.
While this new announcement feels more permanent, it will be interesting to see what happens if resistance to the changes continues to grow.

articles.title: La salida a bolsa de Anthropic se estaba desinflando. Ahora tiene más demanda institucional que SpaceX
articles.text:
Anthropic ha fijado entre 70 y 78 dólares el precio de sus acciones para salir a bolsa. Eso la valora por entre 1,26 y 1,41 billones de dólares Hace unos meses se hablaba de dos billones, y hace una semana, de 1,5.
Sin embargo, un día después, los bancos colocadores ya estudian volver a subirla.
Qué ha ocurrido. Según fuentes citadas por CNBC, los pedidos ya cubren la oferta entera en cualquier punto de la horquilla. La demanda institucional es mayor que la que tenía SpaceX en el mismo momento de su proceso.
Anthropic fijará el precio dentro de una semana, el 18 de noviembre, y empezará a cotizar en Nasdaq el 19 con el ticker $ANT.
El contexto. El recorte se lo han impuesto los grandes fondos después del jueves pasado, cuando el Nasdaq perdió 2,5 billones de dólares en una sesión. Ha sido una semana horrible para la IA.
Los demócratas han arrasado en las legislativas, los votantes están rechazando en masa los centros de datos y NVIDIA ha perdido más de un billón en bolsa en las últimas tres semanas, con el escándalo de Jensen Huang como guinda de la caída.
Entre líneas. Anthropic sale con horquilla y no con un precio fijo, como hizo SpaceX. Si la demanda aguanta, puede subir el precio. Si el mercado se tuerce antes del día 18, puede bajarlo sin que parezca una derrota.
El rastro del dinero. Los 26.000 millones de la colocación privada vienen de AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, NVIDIA y TSMC. Todos le venden chips, fabricación o nube a Anthropic. Solo NVIDIA pone unos 10.000 millones.
Sus cotizaciones dan por hecho que Anthropic va a cumplir 901.000 millones en compromisos de gasto, así que al apoyar la salida a bolsa también se están cubriendo a ellos mismos.
El contraste. Las cuentas de Anthropic están bastante mejor que el ambiente, más propio de un tanatorio:
- 81.000 millones de ingresos anualizados en octubre, 10.000 más que en septiembre.
- 131.800 millones en caja frente a 70.700 millones en compromisos que vencen en el próximo año.
La amenaza. En la oferta oficial, los accionistas actuales apenas venden. Pero los empleados y demás accionistas internos, salvo los fundadores, pueden vender hasta un 10% de sus acciones el primer día. Eso son hasta 25.000 millones de dólares que irán directos al mercado, sin que los bancos decidan quién los compra ni a qué precio.
Y ahora qué. Un 20% de las acciones irá a pequeños inversores, el doble de lo habitual. SpaceX se disparó en su estreno, en pocas semanas cayó por debajo de su precio de salida y hoy apenas lo ha vuelto a superar.
Anthropic tiene demanda para salir de sobra. Lo que está por ver es cuánto aguantará cuando los empleados empiecen a vender.

articles.title: Galaxy Z Fold 8 isola Samsung na liderança dos dobráveis • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Galaxy Z Fold 8 isola Samsung na liderança dos dobráveis
Remessas da Samsung cresceram 13% no trimestre, levando a marca a 69% do mercado global. Z Fold 8 respondeu por quase 55% dos envios da fabricante.
A Samsung alcançou 69% das remessas globais de smartphones dobráveis no terceiro trimestre deste ano, marcando a maior participação da empresa no segmento desde 2023. Grande parte do avanço seguiu o lançamento do Galaxy Z Fold 8, que respondeu sozinho por quase 55% dos aparelhos dobráveis enviados pela fabricante entre julho e setembro.
Segundo os dados da consultoria Smart Analytics Global (SAG), a Samsung ganhou 9 pontos percentuais de participação em um ano e aumentou as remessas em 13%. O resultado, de acordo com o site Android Headlines, contrasta com o encolhimento do mercado de dobráveis em 2% no período, equivalente a pouco mais de 7,5 milhões de unidades.
Quando os aparelhos da sul-coreana são retirados da conta, as remessas combinadas das demais marcas caíram 24% na comparação anual, segundo a SAG. A consultoria atribui a dificuldade de expansão do segmento principalmente aos preços ainda elevados e à falta de recursos exclusivos que tornem os dobráveis mais atraentes para um público mais amplo. A dona da linha Galaxy, vale lembrar, foi uma das precursoras dos dobráveis com o lançamento do Galaxy Fold, em 2020.
Anos depois, a empresa segue trabalhando pela popularização dos modelos com melhorias no painel interno e no mecanismo de dobra, mas também através de projetos como o novo Galaxy Z Fold 8. A proporção, em geral, parece ter chamado a atenção do público.
Segundo a SAG, dobráveis com perfil horizontal mais largo — ou, como costumamos chamar, um formato “passaporte” — representaram cerca de 45% das remessas globais da categoria no trimestre. Apesar de não ser maioria, o número mostra uma adesão crescente ao novo design.
Apesar de ser uma das empresas que mais apostam na tecnologia, com smartphones, tablets e até notebooks com tela dobrável, a Huawei terminou o trimestre com uma participação menor do que há um ano. A fabricante chinesa caiu de 18% para 14% das remessas globais.
Segundo a SAG, o desempenho foi afetado pela desaceleração da demanda por dobráveis na China e também pela chegada do Huawei Pura X View, um celular convencional que aposta em uma tela mais larga. Segundo a consultoria, ele acabou disputando parte do mesmo público interessado nos dobráveis com o mesmo formato.
Já a Lenovo, que também controla a Motorola, seguiu o caminho contrário. A empresa ganhou 2 ponto percentuais de participação e chegou a 8% do mercado global, mantendo a terceira posição. O crescimento parte da expansão internacional da família Motorola Razr 70, que segue o estilo flip. A companhia deve lançar um dobrável no formato passaporte no ano que vem, segundo vazamentos.
Com a estreia do iPhone Duo, a projeção da SAG é que o mercado volte a registrar crescimento de dois dígitos no fechamento do ano com a estreia da marca. A empresa pode, inclusive, ultrapassar a Samsung em volume de remessas, segundo a consultoria.
Somando o novo modelo da Apple ao desempenho do Galaxy Z Fold 8, a SAG estima também que o formato passaporte possa superar 65% das remessas globais de dobráveis até dezembro.
Segundo o SamMobile, porém, problemas na cadeia de suprimentos podem reduzir o número de dispositivos efetivamente enviados pela empresa neste ano. Para 2027, os analistas projetam que as remessas continuem avançando a taxas anuais de dois dígitos.

articles.title: AI-native applications need distributed cloud, not just GPUs - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Enterprises, not a handful of giants, are becoming the GPU buyers that matter
Enterprises building AI-native applications are discovering that raw GPU capacity is only half the equation. As Kubernetes users move from cloud-native to AI-native stacks, the question is shifting from who has the most accelerators to who can run distributed, secure workloads at global scale.
The first wave of so-called neoclouds stood up massive GPU clusters for a handful of the largest buyers, but enterprise developers need far more than data center capacity. The Constant Company LLC, which does business as Vultr, has bet on AMD silicon and open software stacks to win AI infrastructure deals. It is positioning itself as a full-stack cloud built to close that gap, according to Kevin Cochrane (pictured), chief marketing officer of Vultr.
“In the early market … it was all about just standing up large GPU clusters wherever you could get land, power and shell, and then just selling it on through to a hyperscaler,” Cochrane said. “And somehow in that mix, people forgot that you still need cloud, right? You still gotta run this thing.”
Cochrane spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier and Rebecca Knight at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon NA, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed why enterprise AI demands distributed cloud infrastructure, how global networking shapes GPU adoption and Vultr’s new programs for open-source builders. (* Disclosure below.)
Why AI-native applications need a distributed cloud
Every computing supercycle reshapes architecture from the data center up to the application layer, according to Cochrane. In AI, the first iteration was tuned for a narrow group of the biggest GPU buyers, he explained. Enterprises have different requirements, and serving them means returning to computing’s longer trajectory.
“We took a little bit of a step backwards because in that early iteration of the new architecture, when we over-indexed on a limited number of buyers, we went back more to centralized systems,” Cochrane said. “And we have to remember that the long arc of compute is towards decentralized distributed systems driven by open standards and driven by open source.”
Distributed AI also changes how inference gets served. Because many users ask the same question, Vultr aims to maximize token reuse through a global namespace that shares KV cache across nodes, work it is pursuing with partners such as Vast Data Inc., Cochrane noted. Connectivity between data centers matters just as much, since enterprises want private networks isolated from every other tenant on a public cloud.
“In the neocloud moment, I think some of the complexity of what’s required to operate workloads at global scale for enterprises has been forgotten or just assumed it wouldn’t matter,” Cochrane said. “But … it’s the biggest barrier to getting enterprises to actually leverage GPUs from a new cloud because the networking connectivity, it just doesn’t work.”
Vultr is also putting resources behind the open-source community building the AI stack. The company has joined the Cloud Native Computing Foundation as a platinum member, and at KubeCon it highlighted its Open Source Credits Program, which provisions infrastructure for the maintainers behind new CNCF projects.
“All of those projects need compute, right? The maintainers aren’t going to suddenly open up their own personal checkbooks,” Cochrane said. “How can you build the next great CNCF project if you don’t have compute?”

articles.title: Apple is closing its 28-year-old community forum
articles.text:
Apple’s long-time community forum is officially being put to rest.
The company posted a notice on the Apple Community Forum Tuesday night, noting that it will officially close on November 20. All posts are now read-only.
“The Apple Support Community will permanently close on November 20, 2026. Starting today, the site will no longer accept new posts and is available in a read-only state,” the notice said.
“You can continue to find trusted guidance and support on the official Apple Support site.”
As Ars Technica noted, the forum allowed users to get quick tech advice through other members of the forum, with the occasional Apple employee chiming in to help, or provide updates to any fixes. However, as with most community forums, helpfulness and accuracy would vary.
Apple first launched the community forum in 1998, when it launched the Apple Tech Exchange. This forum changed its name to Apple Discussions in 2000, and then to Apple Support Communities in 2011. The name would change one final time to Apple Support Community in 2022.
According to MacRumors, Apple said it decided to retire the forum after a careful evaluation of strategy and customer needs.
Now that the user-to-user support forum is gone, Apple is pushing users to get tech support through the official Apple Support site. However, other peer-to-peer alternatives, like Reddit or the MacRumors forums, can still provide quick answers to problems without going to the company first.
Source: MacRumors, ARSTechnica

articles.title: ValueQuest commits Rs 775 Cr to advance India’s defence, manufacturing push
articles.text:
ValueQuest commits Rs 775 Cr to advance India’s defence, manufacturing push
The Mumbai-based investment manager is backing three businesses operating in the areas of defence tech, precision engineering, and power infrastructure: Sagar Defence Engineering, TASE Global, and Rational Engineers.
ValueQuest Investment Advisors, a Mumbai-based investment manager, has made a total commitment of Rs 775 crore to three Indian businesses in defence technology, precision engineering, and power infrastructure.
The investment firm announced new investments in Sagar Defence Engineering and Rational Engineers and also added to its earlier investment in TASE Global. The Rs 775 crore is a portfolio commitment, not a single company’s fundraise.
Sagar Defence Engineering develops unmanned and autonomous systems for maritime and other defence applications. Rational Engineers makes specialised copper conductors and insulation products for power and distribution transformers. TASE Global operates in India and the United States, manufacturing precision components and assemblies for global original equipment manufacturers and Tier-I suppliers across medical technology, aerospace, defence and industrial markets.
ValueQuest says its private equity platform manages more than Rs 6,000 crore, including co-investments, and is building out SCALE Fund II.
The investment strategy reflects the wider shift in the manufacturing sector. Companies are diversifying supply chains and seeking to reduce dependence on overseas suppliers for strategically important technology and components.
Ravi Dharamshi, Founder and Chief Investment Officer of ValueQuest, said, “The opportunity is not simply for India to manufacture more, but for Indian companies to develop the technology, capabilities and customer relationships to become globally competitive enterprises.”
Defence policy and procurement are helping drive this shift. The government reported that domestic defence production reached a record Rs 1.78 lakh crore in 2025-26, with private firms accounting for 24%. Meanwhile, exports rose to Rs 38,424 crore.
The government is targeting annual production of Rs 3 lakh crore and exports of Rs 50,000 crore by 2029. It has also opened 25% of the defence research and development budget to industry, startups and academia.
Power infrastructure offers another source of demand. The National Electricity Plan envisages peak demand of 388 GW by 2032 and an increase in the transmission network from 5.09 lakh circuit kilometres in June 2026 to 6.48 lakh by 2032. This expansion should support demand for transformers and components, although actual orders will depend on project execution.
Aniket Dharamshi, Co-founder and Managing Partner, ValueQuest, said the firm was not rushing to deploy capital. “Our focus is not on the pace of capital deployment, but on identifying the right businesses,” he said.
Recently, ValueQuest’s Tristar Fund secured over Rs 2,100 crore in commitments within 15 months of its first close, exceeding its original target and greenshoe.

articles.title: Des couleurs pétantes mais une fiche technique vieillotte : ce que cache ce concurrent chinois du MacBook Neo
articles.text:
Le constructeur chinois Infinix dégaine à son tour un PC portable de 14 pouces taillé pour se confronter au MacBook Neo. Avec son châssis coloré de 1,2 kg et son écran Full HD+, le petit XBook 14 Neo ne cache pas ses ambitions mais sa fiche technique recèle quelques cruels sacrifices.
N’est pas MacBook Neo qui veut. Nous avons récemment eu l’occasion de nous en apercevoir avec le Tecno MegaBook T14 Air ou l'Acer Swift Air 14, en dépit de quelques grandes qualités. Si quelques références tirent leur épingle du jeu sur le terrain des ultraportables premiums et abordables (on pense cette fois au nouvel ASUS Zenbook 14 ou au Dell XPS 13 2026, dans une moindre mesure vu son prix français), la majorité se heurtent à des compromis trop sévères pour vraiment valoir le coup. L’Infinix XBook 14 Neo semble faire partie de cette catégorie de produits, malheureusement.
BenQ iScreenBar : la barre lumineuse qui s’accorde avec l’iMac
Des lignes en harmonie avec celles de l’ordinateur d’Apple, une conception rigoureuse, des matériaux sélectionnés, rien n’a été laissé au hasard, tout comme le service qu’elle rend une fois allumée !
De la couleur…
Annoncé sur Instagram, ce qui est rare pour une marque chinoise, ce nouveau XBook 14 Neo est un ultraportable de 14 pouces dont le châssis combine un capot en aluminium et une base en fibre de carbone. Côté dimensions, nous sommes sur un produit léger (1,2 kg), mais tout de même un peu épais (17,4 mm). Infinix nous promet quoi qu’il en soit un bon niveau de solidité puisque ce petit XBook 14 Neo profite d’une certification US MIL-STD-810H, censé attester de sa robustesse face aux mauvais traitements.
Décliné en coloris Twilight Purple, Shadow Blue, Sonic Yellow et Volcano Grey, l’appareil s’annonce assez prometteur jusque-là, mais c’est sans compter sur son écran et les puces qui le motorisent. On se limite en effet à une vieille dalle IPS Full HD+ (1920 par 1200 pixels) et 60 Hz, montant à 300 nits maximum et couvrant seulement à 45 % le gamut NTSC. En d’autres termes, cet écran affiche beaucoup moins de couleurs que la concurrence et s’en tient à une luminosité tout juste suffisante.
… et des vieux « Core »
L’Infinix XBook 14 Neo s’en tient du reste à des puces Raptor Lake-U lancées en début d’année 2023, avec au choix un Intel Core i3-1315U ou un Core i5-1335U, couplées à 8 Go de mémoire vive (DDR4) et 256 ou 512 Go de SSD. Rien de très folichon, donc, même si Microsoft fait des efforts pour rendre Windows 11 utilisable avec 8 Go de RAM. Côté autonomie, Infinix promet jusqu’à 13 heures grâce à une batterie de 55 Wh que l’on rechargera à l’aide d’un bloc secteur USB-C de 65 W.
Ce modèle dispose par contre d’une connectique assez fournie, articulée autour de deux ports USB-C, deux ports USB-A 3.1, un port USB-A 2.0, une sortie HDMI et une prise casque. On y trouve enfin une webcam 720p et un module Wi-Fi 6 / Bluetooth 5.2.
Son prix ? environ 542 dollars (HT) en Malaisie pour la version Core i3 / 8 Go et près de 665 dollars (HT) en version Core i5 / 8 Go. Un placement tarifaire plutôt hardi au regard de ce que propose un Xiaomi RedmiBook 14 (Core 5 220H, 32 Go de RAM, 1 To de SSD et écran 2,8K), par exemple, pour 900 dollars.
Source : NotebookCheck
