articles.title: NASA's secret weapon in the lunar space race may be ... procurement reform?
articles.text:
Senior NASA officials held a lengthy news conference last weekend, laying out a series of lunar contract awards, new contract opportunities, and mission decisions. They followed one after the other: landers, nuclear-powered rovers, scouting drones, power generation, storage, and communication satellites.
It never seemed to end.
“Hopefully, we’re keeping industry on their toes trying to catch up to all the solicitations we’re doing,” said Carlos García-Galán, manager of the Moon Base Program, more than 90 minutes into the news conference. “This is what it takes to do the Moon Base in the timeline we have set forth.”
The rapid-fire announcement of awards tells us a few things about NASA’s efforts to return to the Moon and establish a durable settlement there during the next decade.
First, the agency is serious about this effort—the Artemis Moon Base program represents the most credible effort to establish a permanent outpost on another world in NASA’s history. Second, NASA is reaching out to all corners of the US commercial space industry, casting an extraordinarily wide net to reach companies that have yet to fly any hardware into orbit. Third, NASA is getting creative about how it’s buying these services, and this may matter most of all.
Changing way NASA buys stuff
There was a lot packed into the announcements this weekend, so to make sense of it all, I called Mike Gold, a lawyer and former NASA associate administrator who set up the Artemis Accords, who is now the president of Redwire Space. He was at NASA at the beginning of Artemis and understands what it takes to get the government moving. He said he was blown away. During a period of seven days, Gold said, NASA put out five proposals for lunar contracts.
“The pace that’s occurring, and the nature of the procurements is unprecedented,” Gold said. “You are seeing an all-hands-on-deck approach. Big companies, small companies, new companies, old companies.”

articles.title: The unfolding Jensen Huang scandal: a timeline | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Nvidia co-founder CEO Jensen Huang has never been as flashy or controversy-prone as AI leaders like OpenAI’s Sam Altman or SpaceXAI’s Elon Musk. Now, the 63-year-old industry kingpin has admitted that he cheated on his wife of 40 years in an affair that could have ramifications beyond Huang’s personal life and potentially impact national security.
United States officials believe that Huang’s likely romantic interest, Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, is a Chinese spy who has been feeding information back to Beijing. (Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen, is of no relation to Jensen Huang.)
Megaspeed, a Singapore-based AI infrastructure company, had reportedly purchased $4.8 billion in Nvidia chips over the last two years. The U.S. and Singapore have both previously investigated Megaspeed over suspicions that the firm was illegally sharing chips with China. The Justice Department has since taken over the federal investigation into the company, the Times has reported.
The story took a sudden new turn on Wednesday. Citing five people who worked at Nvidia, the Times reported that Huang also had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, the company’s vice president of health care, who reports directly to him. Nvidia, Huang and Powell have not confirmed the report. Reached by a Times reporter, Huang reportedly said, “I don’t think you should be talking to me directly,” before hanging up.
Separately, the Wall Street Journal reported that Nvidia’s board is preparing to oust Huang, and Nvidia’s shares fell in after-hours trading.
The U.S. and China are embroiled in a fierce technological arms race to build the most advanced AI infrastructure, which could shape each country’s economic future, military prowess, and capacity for innovation. Nvidia is valuable in this competition as one of the world’s largest makers of AI chips, which are essential for accelerating AI development. But as an American company, Nvidia faces government restrictions on the sale of its most powerful chips to Chinese entities.
As the controversy unfolds, we are organizing the most relevant events into a reverse-chronological timeline to keep you up to date.
November 11, 2026: Nvidia’s stock drops as board reportedly preps to oust CEO Jensen Huang
After reports of a second extramarital affair, Nvidia’s board reportedly plans to meet to discuss Huang’s future at the company, per the Wall Street Journal. Stock fell about 8% in after hours trading on Wednesday and is down 11% in the past five days.
Huang famously delegates very little and has about 60 direct reports, he has said. The company has not had an obvious successor or a succession plan.
November 11, 2026: Huang also had an affair with an Nvidia executive who reports to him, NYT says
The New York Times reported that Jensen Huang also had an affair with Nvidia vice president of healthcare Kimberly Powell, who reports directly to the CEO.
According to the report, Huang and Powell were captured on film “being affectionate” at a hotel during a conference earlier this year.
November 11, 2026: Congress plans to subpoena Huang to answer questions about affair
Huang has not responded to a request from three Republican congressman to appear for a closed-door briefing for questioning about his affair with an alleged Chinese spy. House China committee Chairman Moolenaar said Wednesday on Fox Business that if Huang doesn’t agree to the briefing, he’ll likely be subpoenaed.
November 9, 2026: Huang pulls out of various speaking engagements
The Nvidia CEO pulled out of upcoming speaking engagements at the ElevenLabs Summit and Anthropic CEO Forum.
November 9-10, 2026: Details emerge about the business relationships between Nvidia and the alleged spy
Alice Huang and her family reportedly built a network of companies in China and Singapore to acquire Nvidia chips, including founding a Chinese company called Shanghai Century Litong. Founded in 2023, it became an Nvidia-preferred cloud partner, giving it priority access to chips, The Information reported. The Information also reported that Shanghai Century Litong facilitated buying $7.5 billion worth of Nvidia’s chips, including banned chips.
Nvidia’s head lawyer, Tim Teter, intervened in a 2025 U.S. government probe surrounding the suspected smuggling of AI chips by Megaspeed International, Bloomberg reported. Teter contacted Commerce Under Secretary Jeffrey Kessler asking questions about whether the Trump administration played a role in detaining Alice Huang.
In early 2025, Alice Huang and a business partner sought China-based investors for an Asian data center, promising they had no problem in securing GPUs, the Financial Times reported.
November 8, 2026: Trump shows support for Nvidia CEO, calls him a “fine person”
On Sunday night, President Trump weighed in on Huang’s controversy and showed support for the Nvidia CEO.
“I have not spoken to him about it. I just know he’s a fine person, but you never know what’s going on,” Trump said.
When asked if Huang should remain chief of Nvidia, Trump said, “I think so. Oh yeah, sure.”
November 8, 2026: Huang admits to affair in public message to Nvidia employees; Nvidia board of directors begins investigation
Jensen Huang wrote in a letter to Nvidia employees — which was also published as a press release — that he cheated on his wife.
“I owe my family and all of you an apology,” Huang told his company. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.”
Huang did not mention Alice Huang by name in the message, but linked his infidelity to “the national security concerns raised in news reports.”
“Nvidia’s Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation. I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America’s national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American,” Huang wrote.
Nvidia shares slid over 5% the following day.
November 5, 2026: Three Republican committee chairmen ask Huang for closed-door briefing
Three Republican congressmen — Chairman John Moolenaar of the House Select Committee on China, Chairman Brian Mast of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, and Chairman Rick Crawford of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence — sent a request to Huang for a closed-door joint briefing with their three committees.
“Recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the [People’s Republic of China]’s access to sensitive U.S. technology and information,” the chairmen wrote. “The issue of PRC infiltration and access to cutting-edge U.S. technology is core to the investigative work of our three committees this Congress. It is vital that Congress determines the extent to which U.S. national security has been placed at risk.”
October 29, 2026: Jensen Huang publicly revealed to have developed ‘close relationship’ with suspected Chinese spy
U.S. officials had been investigating Alice Huang and Megaspeed for more than a year when the New York Times broke the story in late October that the two executives also had a close relationship.
An Nvidia spokesperson denied that this relationship was something out of the ordinary.
“Jensen’s interactions with Ms. Huang are not unusual or unexpected. Meetings with customers are part of a CEO’s job; Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year,” Nvidia spokesperson John Rizzo said. He added that “if the U.S. government believes that any person is a threat to American industry, it would let us know.”
Spring 2026: A secret memo circulates in the Trump administration about Nvidia CEO’s alleged relationship with Chinese spy
U.S. officials circulated a secret memo among policymakers that warned that Megaspeed’s Alice Huang, who had a relationship with Jensen Huang, was a spy for China’s Ministry of State Security. This memo was not public knowledge until it was later reported by the New York Times.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio supervised the drafting of the memo.
Late 2025: President Trump briefed on U.S. surveillance of Alice Huang and her relationship to Nvidia CEO but does not take action
Around the same time, per the New York Times’ report, U.S. President Donald Trump was briefed about intelligence findings that possible Chinese spy Alice Huang had formed a close relationship with Jensen Huang. Trump did not act on this information.
The Nvidia CEO, an ally of Trump, has repeatedly advocated for the U.S. government to let Nvidia expand its business in China.
October 2025: U.S. and Singapore each investigate Megaspeed over possible Chinese export violations
Megaspeed was confirmed to be under investigation by both the U.S. and Singaporean governments in October 2025. As a customer of Nvidia, Megaspeed was suspected of helping Chinese companies get around American embargoes on chip exports.
Megaspeed, a neocloud that used Nvidia chips, had been renting computing power to Chinese internet giant Alibaba and other Chinese companies, the Times reported. A Commerce Department official who had visited Megaspeed’s data center in Malaysia in 2024 had found a hoard of Nvidia equipment that was still packed in boxes and the concern was that this equipment was being directly shipped somewhere else, like China, rather than installed and sold as a cloud service.
Jensen Huang had been spotted socializing with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang as early as 2024 in Taiwan, where the Nvidia CEO was born.
These investigations into Megaspeed highlighted concerns about the degree to which Nvidia is able to track its chip exports. At the time, an Nvidia spokesperson told press that the company did not have “any reason to believe products had been diverted.”
“NVIDIA visited multiple Megaspeed sites yet again earlier this week and confirmed what we previously observed — Megaspeed is running a small commercial cloud, like many other companies throughout the world, as allowed by U.S. export control rules,” the Nvidia spokesperson said at the time.

articles.title: OmniOps unveils Bunyan Inference Hub to simplify AI deployment in Saudi Arabia
articles.text:
OmniOps unveils Bunyan Inference Hub to simplify AI deployment in Saudi Arabia
Press release:
OmniOps, Saudi Arabia's sovereign AI infrastructure technology company, announced the launch of Bunyan Inference Hub, a platform for governments, enterprises, startups and developers to access open-source AI models and computing resources, with data and workloads hosted in Saudi Arabia.
As organizations move AI applications into production, infrastructure becomes more complex, and the need for different AI models can mean working with separate providers, computing environments, and technical integrations. Organizations that need to follow stricter data residency or security requirements may find that the only way to meet those frameworks is by building and managing their own infrastructure.
Bunyan Inference Hub brings these elements together in one platform. Hosted in Saudi Arabia, it enables organizations to keep their data and AI workloads within the Kingdom, access a catalogue of AI models or bring their own, and use computing resources without managing separate infrastructure for each model or use case. Customers access predefined token bundles across supported models and workloads, with dedicated GPU infrastructure available for organizations that need additional capacity or isolation.
This is enabled by OmniOps’ proprietary inference optimization engine, developed by the company’s R&D team. The engine adapts how AI models run on available hardware to match workload requirements, helping organizations improve GPU utilization, reduce the cost per token, and maintain consistent performance as demand grows, without having to manage the underlying infrastructure.
The platform can run across different GPUs and AI accelerators rather than relying on a single hardware provider. It routes requests to the appropriate model and computing resources, manages infrastructure scaling, and monitors performance and usage. Customers can also set usage limits and track token consumption across teams.
“As entities embrace AI across functions and applications in their operations, ensuring that the consumption of AI models is managed efficiently and with the correct security and cost guardrails has never been more critical,” commented Mohammed Altassan, Founding CEO of OmniOps. “The new hub brings together our proprietary Bunyan Inference technology and experience in sovereign AI deployment in a simplified platform that public and private sector organizations can plug into their operations and use to deploy AI solutions more efficiently.”
The launch comes as demand for AI inference infrastructure grows globally, with more organizations moving AI models into production. Research by ServiceNow shows that Saudi-based entities have increased spending on AI by 124% year-on-year and plan to dedicate 20% of their IT budgets until 2027 to artificial intelligence solutions across their organization. Meanwhile, Gartner forecasts that global spending on AI inference workloads will reach $23.3 billion by the end of 2026.

articles.title: 650 km d’autonomie pour 50 000 € : Volvo s'attaque directement au roi Tesla Model Y avec ce futur SUV
articles.text:
Volvo poursuit le développement de sa gamme électrique pour obtenir le plus rapidement possible un portfolio aussi complet que pertinent. 2027 verra ainsi l’arrivée d’un modèle entièrement inédit qui viendra se glisser entre l’EX40 et l’EX60. Le futur EX50 ira tailler des croupières au Tesla Model Y avec son autonomie XXL et sa recharge ultra rapide. Son prix devrait démarrer aux alentours des 50 000 €. Une future menace en vue ?
Ce n’est en tout cas pas une menace surprise car l’EX50 devait initialement remplacer les vieillissants XC40 et EX40 en un seul et même modèle électrique. Mais ça, c’était à l’époque où Volvo voulait faire une croix sur le thermique. Les choses ont changé depuis, avec une demande toujours incertaine sur les modèles à batterie. Le récent revirement de l’Europe sur l’échéance de 2035 en est une preuve supplémentaire.
4,60 mètres et 50 000 € : le gabarit idéal pour faire plier le Model Y ?
Raison pour laquelle le duo XC40/EX40 survivra pour concurrencer les BMW iX1, Mercedes GLA et Audi Q4 e-tron, plus compacts. L’EX50, lui, jouera le rôle de modèle électrique mondial avec un gabarit idéal. Dans sa récente conférence sur les résultats financiers du troisième trimestre, le constructeur a confirmé à demi-mot l’arrivée de ce véhicule : 2027 verra « un nouveau modèle pour l’Europe et deux modèles spécifiques au marché chinois ».
Plus long que les 4,44 mètres de l’EX40, l’EX50 devrait mesurer 4,60 ou 4,70 mètres, ce qui lui permettra de mieux cibler les 4,79 mètres du Tesla Model Y. L’EX60 s’étendant sur 4,80 mètres est plus proche de l’américain, certes, mais il le surpasse complètement en termes de prix ! C’est bien là que l’EX50 aura sa carte à jouer. Il misera aussi sur une technique avancée, en reposant très probablement sur la plateforme SPA3 utilisée par l’EX60.
Recharge de 10 à 80 % en 16 minutes : la claque technique assénée à la concurrence
L’EX50 se permettra ainsi de reprendre les batteries de son grand frère. On aura alors le choix entre un pack de 80 ou 91 kWh offrant respectivement 600 et 650 km d’autonomie. L’accumulateur de 112 kWh donnant 810 km sur l’EX60 serait prometteur pour abattre la concurrence, mais il pourrait être trop encombrant pour les entrailles du futur EX50. Le rayon d’action maximal restera dans tous les cas supérieur à celui du Model Y.
Côté recharge rapide, le suédois ne chômera pas avec sa plateforme 800 V. La puissance de 400 kW en courant continu DC de l’EX60 sera ainsi de la partie pour un 10 à 80 % de batterie en environ 16 minutes. Le Model Y est là encore loin derrière. Il gardera en revanche la main côté prix. Sauf si Volvo fait un effort ? Probablement produit en Slovaquie, le suédois pourrait être éligible aux aides de l’État, si son tarif passe sous les 47 000 €. Un autre défi…

articles.title: Why CommonFloor’s $200M exit felt like a loss to co-founder Vikas Malpani
articles.text:
Why CommonFloor’s $200M exit felt like a loss to co-founder Vikas Malpani
A decade after Quikr bought the real estate portal, Malpani reflects on leaving the startup he had spent years building and why he chose to start again.
Vikas Malpani thought he would feel like he had won when Quikr bought CommonFloor in 2016. He had spent several years co-building the startup, which began as a tool for apartment communities and grew into a property portal that reached millions of users. The company had been the focus of his working life. After the acquisition, Malpani missed the structure the company had given him. “I expected to feel like I had won. I felt like something had ended,” he wrote in a LinkedIn post.
The deal that brought CommonFloor into Quikr
Malpani founded CommonFloor in 2007 with Sumit Jain and Lalit Mangal. In January 2016, Quikr announced it was merging the portal with QuikrHomes, its real estate business. The companies did not disclose the financial terms. Business Standard reported the deal was worth $200 million, while Malpani put the figure at more than $200 million in his LinkedIn post. All three co-founders left CommonFloor about a year after the acquisition.
The acquisition came as investors were growing wary of startups burning through cash and Indian tech companies were buying smaller rivals to expand their businesses. Quikr struck two deals in 2015 and seven in 2016, according to VCCEdge data. CommonFloor gave it a bigger presence in online property listings, while another purchase that year, Grabhouse, helped it expand into managed rentals. Quikr also bought recruitment portal Hiree and folded it into QuikrJobs.
Starting over after CommonFloor
In an essay on his website, Malpani said he could have stayed in real estate, become a full-time investor or taken an advisory role. He went back to building companies, co-founding Leher, a social platform for live audio and video. The move took him into a business with very different economics from a property portal. Learning how that business worked, he wrote, came more easily than letting go of the identity he had built around CommonFloor. He also had to question whether the instincts he had developed there still applied.
Malpani is now co-founder and CEO of Garvik AI, which builds AI tools for businesses. Its ReBillion.ai platform helps employees find information across their company and lets businesses set up AI assistants. Malpani says the company has deployed those tools in banking, manufacturing, education technology and real estate. That last sector brings him back to a market he knows well, this time selling software to businesses after spending years building a portal for people looking for homes.

articles.title: Elon Musk veut que SpaceX fabrique ses propres machines avec 72 GPU Nvidia Rubin pour ses centres de données dans l'espace, un pari qui pourrait coûter très cher
articles.text:
Elon Musk veut que SpaceX fabrique ses propres machines avec 72 GPU Nvidia Rubin pour ses centres de données dans l'espace, un pari qui pourrait coûter très cher
Avec le projet Kessel, SpaceX ambitionne de concevoir ses propres machines autour de 72 GPU Nvidia Rubin pour ses centres de données dans l'espace. Des puces qui effectuent les calculs IA et sur lesquelles Elon Musk cherche à avoir plus de contrôle. Mais cette stratégie pourrait être coûteuse pour ce projet orbital déjà lourd dans les finances de SpaceX.
Kessel est une version modifiée de la plateforme Vera Rubin NVL72 de Nvidia avec 36 processeurs Vera et 72 GPU Rubin. Elon Musk chercherait à ce que SpaceX achète les puces Nvidia puis choisisse elle-même les autres pièces et fournisseurs. Nvidia s'occuperait donc de fournir les puces pendant que SpaceX garderait le contrôle de la machine tout autour. Une stratégie que la société d'Elon Musk n'a pas confirmée publiquement à ce jour.
SpaceX veut produire ses propres serveurs IA
Kessel remplace une partie des câbles internes par une carte électronique centrale de 84 couches. Des câbles qui sont utilisés pour NVLink, la technologie de Nvidia qui permet aux GPU d'échanger leurs données. SpaceX est donc en quête d'une machine plus compacte pour ses satellites, qui seront équipés de Rubin, la génération de puces Nvidia qui succède à Blackwell.
Mais une telle carte électronique pose un gros problème puisque l'on parle de 84 couches alors qu'une carte mère de serveur haut de gamme tourne autour de 15 à 20 couches. La carte électronique demande donc un matériau plus coûteux avec une fabrication difficile. Au moindre défaut dans une couche interne, c'est toute la pièce qui est inutilisable. La suppression des câbles ne garantit pas qu'une machine soit moins chère.
SpaceX chercherait à reprendre une partie de la stratégie de Nvidia sur ses serveurs complets. L'entreprise d'Elon Musk choisirait ses fabricants de cartes et ses fournisseurs avec les GPU Nvidia, mais un contrôle des pièces autour. Mais une telle liberté demande de gérer les tests et la qualité de fabrication.
En août dernier, Elon Musk a expliqué que les premiers satellites de calcul IA avec des puces Nvidia pourraient arriver au quatrième trimestre 2027. SpaceX espère une montée en puissance en 2028 et a demandé l'autorisation de lancer jusqu'à un million de satellites pour les calculs en orbite. Il s'agit d'une infrastructure d'une ampleur jamais expérimentée pour des centres de données spatiaux.
Un projet spatial aux coûts colossaux
En octobre dernier, SpaceX a conclu un accord de financement d'environ 40 milliards de dollars, soit environ 35,9 milliards d'euros, pour des GPU et des serveurs pour ses centres de données terrestres, qui arriveront au premier semestre 2027. Bret Johnsen, directeur financier de SpaceX, prévoit entre 35 et 40 milliards de dollars, soit environ 31,5 à 35,9 milliards d'euros, d'investissements au quatrième trimestre 2026.
Le coût de l'orbite est l'un des obstacles de ce projet. Amanda Peterson Corio, qui dirige l'énergie des centres de données chez Google, estime que les installations spatiales coûteraient jusqu'à 100 fois plus cher que celles sur Terre. "Explorons d'abord toutes les options terrestres, puis passons à l'extraterrestre", a déclaré Amanda Peterson Corio.
Rappelons qu'il faut payer le lancement, évacuer la chaleur sans air, protéger les puces des rayonnements et gérer l'absence de toute équipe de maintenance. Autant dire un coût faramineux.

articles.title: Cloud engineering teams must protect AI agent data in use - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
AI agents carry memory and storage like people, so their data needs guarding while in use
As AI agents move into production on Kubernetes, cloud engineering teams at financial companies face a security problem that encryption alone can’t solve. Container orchestration has become the default foundation for AI workloads, and the data those agents use is now the main target.
Payment networks feel that pressure more than most because every transaction carries customer data and regulatory exposure. Protecting data while it is being processed, and not just while it is stored or moving, has become central to running agents at scale, according to Krishna Mayuram (pictured), senior principal engineer and vice president of cloud engineering at Mastercard Inc.
“What we call confidential computing is when you are launching these applications in a highly secure, virtualized secure environments or confidential environments or confidential containers, you are able to protect the data in use,” Mayuram said. “We have protected data at rest, data in motion. Now, what is happening to the data in use?”
Mayuram spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier and Rebecca Knight at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon NA, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed cloud engineering, security problems and the challenges of protecting data in use. (* Disclosure below.)
Cloud engineering for agents runs on guardrails
Mastercard runs its platforms on Red Hat Inc.’s OpenShift, a Kubernetes platform that Red Hat is extending to support AI agents. Red Hat has also brought confidential containers to OpenShift on bare metal. Agents act much like microservices and need the same elastic infrastructure, Mayuram explained.
“We need to scale the platform, that’s Kubernetes which gives horizontal scaling, vertical scaling, if you will, and also the agents, just like applications, require all the elastic capabilities of Kubernetes,” Mayuram said.
Scale increases the risk, especially for a company that operates under many countries’ laws. Mastercard recently added trust services for agentic commerce. Internally, the same idea applies, with guardrails at every step from development to deployment, according to Mayuram.
“The business is distributed, the industry is very distributed, and we have different laws of the land. So all these things need to be encompassed with guardrails,” Mayuram said. “Whether agents or regular, the guardrails remain the same. The enterprise security remains same.”

articles.title: iPhone 18 et iPhone Air 2 : des maquettes nous montrent de quoi ils auront l'air
articles.text:
Les prochains smartphones d'Apple se dévoilent un peu plus aujourd'hui. Car plusieurs photos des maquettes des iPhone 18 et iPhone Air 2 viennent de fuiter.
Apple occupe dorénavant beaucoup plus l'actualité, avec plusieurs sorties étalées sur plusieurs mois. Ainsi, après les iPhone 18 Pro de la rentrée, puis la sortie du tout premier iPhone pliable iPhone Duo, ce sera le tour de l'iPhone 18 et de l'iPhone Air 2 d'arriver au grand air, avec un lancement programmé pour le printemps 2027. Mais il ne faudra pas patienter jusque-là pour savoir ce à quoi ils vont ressembler.
L'iPhone Air 2 va bénéficier d'un second capteur photo
Rien de mieux pour rapidement connaître l'allure d'un futur smartphone que de jeter un oeil sur les maquettes de ces appareils. Et c'est ce qu'on peut faire aujourd'hui grâce à cette fuite que l'on doit au leaker chinois, Smart Pikachu.
Ce dernier a ainsi posté plusieurs images des maquettes, que vous pouvez voir dans cet article, sur le réseau social chinois Weibo. Et première information (ou plutôt confirmation de rumeurs précédentes), l'iPhone Air 2 va bien embarquer un second capteur photo à l'arrière, capteur qui devrait probablement être un ultra grand-angle.
Pas vraiment de changement à attendre du côté de l'iPhone 18
L'autre enseignement que l'on a pour l'iPhone Air 2, c'est que son épaisseur devrait être encore revue à la baisse. Les rumeurs évoquent une finesse exceptionnelle, puisque l'épaisseur passerait de 5,6 à 5,2 mm.
Pour ce qui est de l'iPhone 18, on a par contre une confirmation qu'il ne devrait pas y avoir trop de changement par rapport au modèle précédent, l'iPhone 17. Même pour ce qui est du module photo, on retrouve exactement ce qui se faisait l'an dernier. Pas de quoi donc relancer la hype, alors que les ventes d'iPhone 18 Pro ne rencontrent pas un enthousiasme débordant.
Source : GSMArena

articles.title: Reddit "Reviews" will use AI to turn subreddit posts into product recommendations
articles.text:
Connecting the dots: Reddit is traditionally described as the "front page of the internet," a place where almost every netizen goes to look for user recommendations and genuine product experiences. Over the next few weeks, the popular social network will start turning its user-focused communities into a full AI-powered review outlet.
Reddit has announced a significant way in how the company plans to do business on the web. The newly introduced Reddit Reviews service will turn one of the internet's most popular "places" into a review and recommendation hub. Just like everything else related to user-generated data these days, RR makes extensive use of generative AI models to repackage individual opinions and user experiences into a commercial, purchase-oriented platform.
In Reddit's own words, RR leverages the wealth of user opinions already available in some of the site's most popular communities. When a user searches for a product on Reddit, GenAI will provide contextualized summaries and comparisons highlighting the most interesting features of that product.
Reddit Reviews will organize relevant "conversations" taken from the service's communities, turning user interactions into an "easy-to-digest" format.
Each review will include both positive and negative traits of a product, plus additional info related to its specific category. For an espresso machine, RR might provide information about how much counter space the device takes up, how beginner-friendly it is, and more.
Additional RR features include an option to navigate the full category a product belongs to, so users can explore different choices related to their original search. After testing the feature for months, Reddit is now ready to bring the Reviews service to the site's wider community, with a few caveats: RR will initially be available to US visitors.
At launch Reddit Reviews will base its recommendations on around 10,000 products across four categories: Electronics, Health & Beauty, Home & Garden, and Fashion & Apparel. As far as I can tell, the AI-powered reviews can be viewed only in the "new" Reddit site – no option appears to exist to access RR from the "old," still very popular design. Reddit plans to expand Reviews to more product types and visitors outside the US throughout 2027.
The new Reviews section marks another change in the traditional Reddit experience. Reddit CEO Steve Huffman recently announced that the platform will evolve into a "primarily logged-in experience," in part because AI bots are freely extracting data from the site without bringing the company any financial benefit. Reddit has insisted in an Australian court that it isn't a social network, while Reddit Reviews touts the platform's inherent social interactions, where people freely discuss almost every topic you can think of.

articles.title: Congress could issue subpoena to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang if he doesn’t respond by today to request for a ‘joint, closed-door briefing’ — US representatives want to discuss company’s ‘security protocols against foreign adversary espionage’
articles.text:
Congress could issue subpoena to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang if he doesn’t respond by today to request for a ‘joint, closed-door briefing’ — US representatives want to discuss company’s ‘security protocols against foreign adversary espionage’
A former CIA agent says that Jensen Huang had a target on his back, and that other engineers and executives could have also be approached by Chinese spies.
Rep. Brian Mast (R-Fla.), the chairperson of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, has said that he will issue a subpoena to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang if he does not respond to the committee’s request to meet with them on November 18 by Wednesday, November 11, according to ABC News. The House invited him to a “joint, closed-door briefing” with the heads of the House committees on China, Foreign Affairs, and Intelligence, and that they will focus on his company’s “security protocols against foreign adversary espionage.”
Congress first called the embattled CEO on November 7, a few days after rumors started circulating about Huang’s “closeness” to a particular Chinese executive suspected of passing information to Chinese intelligence. The following day, Nvidia released a statement from Jensen admitting to an affair with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, apologizing for his unfaithfulness, while the company’s board of directors confirmed it will launch an independent investigation regarding the allegations that the CEO has been specifically targeted by China’s Ministry of State Security (MSS). Aside from having to face Congress, Jensen Huang is also reportedly being looked into by the FBI.
It remains unclear whether Jensen Huang was targeted by intelligence agencies, but he came into prominence with the AI boom that was arguably fueled by Nvidia’s AI chips. This led to the AI race as we know it today, with the U.S. taking steps to delay China’s advancement for fears that it will use the technology for military purposes. We also don’t know if Huang Le or Alice Huang is actually a Chinese spy or an “innocent” bystander caught in a web of accusations. And, even if she did work with the MSS, the question remains as to whether she specifically targeted the Nvidia CEO or whether Chinese intelligence discovered their indiscretion and used that as a convenient tool for blackmail to extract information from her.
However, former CIA agent Darrel Blocker told ABC News that the authorities should just focus on Jensen. “I think that the biggest concern is that the focus or overfocus on just Jensen Huang and Nvidia risks losing sight of the fact that other people have been targeted by the Chinese. Are they talking to the engineers? Are they talking to other people who might have even more access than even the CEO has? So, this focus should not be singular; it should include everyone in the company, and quite frankly, every tech company out there should be looking at all the contacts that their officers and employees have.”
“It’s definitely not a one-time thing. When you run a trillion-dollar company, you know that you have a bullseye on your back; whether it’s from competition or rather from nation-states, so this is absolutely not a one-off. Jensen Huang is not the only person at Nvidia that has access to the crown jewels, so I would be looking at the other people in terms of the access that they enjoy and their proximity to Chinese nationals.”

articles.title: 'I think we're on the brink of a revolution': Google researcher hails AI agents after they found what looks like an ancient Maya site in Mexico
articles.text:
Google researcher discovers unmapped Maya site in Mexico using 48 AI agents — project takes less than 72 hours after agents scour NASA Lidar data
A speedy result
- AI agents have found what looks like an undiscovered Maya site
- The discovery came from a scan of LiDAR data collected by Mexico
- Experts are now investigating the site that the AI has flagged up
While some of AI's 'talents' — like putting together decent-looking restaurant menus — could legitimately be called into question, there's no doubt that these bots and agents excel at spotting patterns in vast troves of data, and the latest evidence comes from the potential discovery of a hidden Maya archaeological site in Mexico.
Google researcher Pietro Miotti described having a "random thought on vacation" about how AI agents might be used to sift through LiDAR datasets — topographical maps of Earth's terrain, captured from space satellites.
LiDAR (Light Detection and Ranging) lasers can cut through cloud cover and forest canopies, enabling researchers to find shapes in the landscape that aren't visible to the naked eye (or in landscapes that aren't even accessible to archaeologists).
Miotti tasked 48 agents from different AI apps with scouring through a NASA database of LiDAR information collected across Peru, and the AI came back with multiple hits on structures that could be buildings. A second scan by the agents identified one particular site that hasn't yet been mentioned in scientific literature.
'LiDAR the entire planet'
The AI assistance didn't stop there: Miotti's bot helpers told him who he should get in touch with about the discovery (Mexico's National Institute of Anthropology and History or INAH), and then composed an email (in Spanish) to the relevant agency, including details of the find and where on the map it's located.
Representatives from INAH got in touch, and the experts there are investigating further: a real result, in 72 hours. The site's status as an ancient Maya site hasn't been confirmed yet, but it looks like a promising lead, and one that was made possible by AI.
"I think we're on the brink of a revolution across every science, not just coding, physics and math," says Miotti. "And at this point we should LiDAR the entire planet and let agents help us find the rest."

Miotti still wasn't finished there, and got Gemini to generate an image of how the site may have looked in 700 CE — when the Maya people were actually living there. In the modern era, some serious exploring can be done from a computer through a team of AI bots, as well as out in the field.

articles.title: Dos juegos para PC y Xbox que se suman a la suscripción de Xbox Game Pass desde hoy
articles.text:
Dos juegos se incorporan a Xbox Game Pass este miércoles 11 de noviembre de 2026, con propuestas dirigidas a quienes buscan una historia de misterio o partidas de estrategia y defensa. El catálogo suma Hope in the City y Thronefall, disponibles en distintas modalidades para Xbox Series, PC y juego en la nube.
Los estrenos llegan al mismo tiempo que su lanzamiento en Xbox, aunque Thronefall ya contaba con recorrido entre los jugadores de PC. La disponibilidad depende del plan contratado: mientras uno queda reservado para Ultimate y PC Game Pass, el otro se habilita para Premium.
De qué tratan cada juego que se incorpora a Xbox Game Pass
La primera incorporación es Hope in the City, una aventura narrativa de misterio protagonizada por Hope Song, una artista de 17 años. La joven vuelve a su hogar y descubre que sus padres desaparecieron, por lo que debe reconstruir los hechos a partir de objetos, conversaciones y escenas repartidas por la ciudad.
El segundo lanzamiento es Thronefall, un juego de estrategia centrado en la construcción de un reino y la defensa ante ataques enemigos. Su fórmula combina administración de recursos, levantamiento de estructuras y combates en los que el jugador también participa de forma directa.
Qué diferencias hay entre los dos juegos
Las propuestas se alejan entre sí desde su estructura. Hope in the City se apoya en una trama personal, en la exploración de escenarios y en la interpretación de pistas. La experiencia ofrece una alternativa para quienes buscan seguir una historia y resolver un caso a través de conversaciones.
Thronefall, en cambio, se orienta a partidas que pueden repetirse con estrategias distintas. Sus mapas, armas y mejoras permiten modificar el enfoque de cada defensa. El diseño visual minimalista facilita la lectura del terreno y de las amenazas, aunque las decisiones de gestión mantienen el nivel de exigencia.
En qué planes de Xbox está disponible Hope in the City
Hope in the City llega desde el primer día a Xbox Game Pass Ultimate y PC Game Pass. Se puede jugar en Xbox Series, PC y mediante Cloud Gaming, la modalidad de juego en la nube de Xbox para dispositivos compatibles.
Quienes tengan Game Pass Premium deben revisar su catálogo antes de buscarlo, porque el título no figura entre las incorporaciones confirmadas para ese plan. Para acceder, hay que ingresar a la ficha del juego desde la aplicación de Xbox o desde Xbox Store y seleccionar la opción de instalación o juego en la nube.
Qué suscripciones tienen acceso a Thronefall
Está disponible en Xbox Game Pass Ultimate, Premium y PC Game Pass. El lanzamiento incluye Xbox Series, computadoras, Cloud Gaming y dispositivos portátiles compatibles, de acuerdo con las opciones que habilite cada plataforma.
El juego puede reclamarse desde su ficha en Xbox Store o desde la biblioteca de Game Pass. En consola y PC, el usuario puede instalarlo para jugar de forma local; quienes tengan acceso a la nube podrán iniciarlo sin descargarlo, siempre que cuenten con conexión a internet estable.
Cuáles juegos llegarán próximamente a Xbox Game Pass
La programación de Xbox Game Pass continuará el jueves 12 de noviembre con John Carpenter’s Toxic Commando, una propuesta cooperativa de acción contra zombis. Ese estreno apunta a partidas compartidas y a un ritmo distinto del que ofrecen los dos títulos incorporados este miércoles.
Por ahora, Hope in the City y Thronefall ya aparecen en el calendario oficial de Xbox. Los suscriptores pueden encontrarlos desde las fichas de la tienda, comprobar qué modalidad de Game Pass tienen activa y elegir entre una investigación narrativa o la defensa de un reino ante ataques.

articles.title: Koodo launches 36-month device financing with Glow
articles.text:
Telus flanker brand Koodo is finally launching device financing, though the wireless provider is taking a slightly different approach compared to other Canadian carriers.
Instead of offering its own service, Koodo is partnering with U.S.-based telecom financing company Glow to offer device financing to new and existing Koodo customers.
“When you choose Koodo Financing powered by Glow, you enter into a loan agreement with Glow Financial Services for the cost of your eligible device. Glow manages your loan agreement and loan payments while Koodo continues to provide and support your wireless service,” reads a support page about the new service.
Koodo Financing powered by Glow now appears alongside Koodo’s existing Tab system when you select a device on the provider’s website.
Notably, Glow financing is only available online, and simply splits the cost of a device over 36 months with no down payment at an APR as low as 0.99 per cent (depending on the results of a credit check). Customers do still have to pay some costs up front, including a $25 shipping charge and taxes on the full device price.
Update Nov. 11, 2026, at 3:40 p.m. ET: After publication, Koodo confirmed to MobileSyrup that because financing is handled by Glow, not Koodo, “the financing terms can be beyond 24 months.”
The CRTC previously ruled that longer financing terms violate the Wireless Code when other carriers offered 36-month financing terms several years ago. Since then, carriers like Bell have come up with creative loopholes to get around the restriction. Moreover, carriers continue to push the CRTC to lift the 24-month restriction.
Koodo also reiterated that Glow financing is separate from Koodo’s wireless services. However, the carrier did not answer follow-up questions about why customers must get a Koodo wireless plan in order to use the financing, nor did it answer questions about whether customers can keep financing a device if they cancel wireless services.
The carrier’s support page about Glow notes that the payment status of one doesn’t impact the other, so presumably customers could cancel their Koodo wireless service and keep financing a device through Glow.

articles.title: Build autonomous AI agents with Amazon Bedrock and Spring AI | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Build autonomous AI agents with Amazon Bedrock and Spring AI
Java teams have established JVM tooling, continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipelines, and operational patterns, yet taking AI agents from prototype to production is hard: agent frameworks do not solve scalability, governance, security, and operational concerns by default. Amazon Bedrock and Spring AI close those gaps, so Java teams can build autonomous AI agents that plan, call tools and APIs, and maintain context across multi-turn conversations. Agentic AI is moving beyond prompt-response interactions toward autonomous systems that execute complex multi-step tasks.
Java remains one of the widely used programming languages in enterprise software. Teams have existing CI/CD pipelines, operational expertise, and established patterns built around the JVM. Spring AI brings AI capabilities to the JVM through familiar Spring patterns: auto-configuration, dependency injection, and composable advisors. Developers can build AI agents using the same idioms they use for REST APIs, security, and data access.
Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is a platform to build, connect, and optimize agents at scale, with any framework or model. With AgentCore, you can build, deploy, and operate AI agents at scale. It is framework-agnostic and model-agnostic: you bring your preferred agent framework and foundation model (FM). With AgentCore, you can access the production infrastructure you need: managed runtime, memory, browser automation, code execution, and identity management.
In this post, we show you how to build autonomous AI agents in Java using Spring AI and Amazon Bedrock with spring-ai-agentcore. We explore the key implementation patterns for two systems. The first is a single-agent travel assistant that demonstrates tool calling and memory. The second is a multi-agent intelligent document processing (IDP) system that shows how specialist agents, a rules engine, and alerting work together.
Prerequisites
To follow along with this walkthrough, you need the following:
- Java – JDK 21 (required)
- Spring Boot – 4.1 (with Spring AI 2.0 and spring-ai-agentcore 2.0)
- Maven – 3.9+.
- Node.js – 18+ (for the React frontend)
- Terraform – 1.5+.
- Docker – with Buildx for multi-architecture builds.
- AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI) – v2, configured with credentials.
- An AWS account.
What makes a system an agent
A chat completion call can generate text, but it can’t decide what to do next, reach into external systems, or remember what happened yesterday. An agent can, because it unites three capabilities:
- Planning – Given a goal, the model breaks it into steps, prioritizes them, and revises the plan as new information arrives.
- Tool use – Beyond generating text, the model can select and invoke external functions such as APIs, databases, and code interpreters to act in the world.
- Memory – Context carries across turns (short-term) and across sessions (long-term), so each decision builds on what came before.
A Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) application has limited tool use (retrieval) but no planning loop. An agent has all three, operating in a goal-directed loop until the task is complete or it determines it cannot proceed.
The following diagram shows these capabilities in an end-to-end agentic pipeline, from request to grounded answer.
The pipeline has 11 stages. A client submits a document and question. The request passes through a runtime gateway for authentication and rate limiting, then input guardrails screen for harmful content. A router classifies the document and routes it to a specialist agent, which plans its workflow and calls tools, the Amazon Bedrock foundation model, memory, and a rules engine as needed. Low-confidence or flagged results go to a human review queue before the grounded answer returns to the client. Resilience, observability, logging, and least-privilege AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) apply across all stages.
Solution overview
The solution consists of two deployable systems that share common patterns:
- Travel agent – A single autonomous agent with tool calling (weather lookups, itinerary search), streaming responses, conversation memory, and resilience patterns. This is the recommended starting point.
- IDP multi-agent system – A multi-agent intelligent document processing platform with five specialist agents (Lawyer, Mortgage, Insurance, Tax, General), rules and workflow engine, alerting, and observability. This demonstrates production patterns at a scale.
Both systems share the following architecture:
- Spring Boot application with Spring AI ChatClient, Spring AI agentcore and Amazon Bedrock Converse API.
- AgentCore runtime, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, defines the contract (POST /invocations, GET /ping) for managed deployment.
- Conversation memory through AgentCore memory, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, for both short-term and long-term context.
- Tool calling with @Tool annotated methods.
- Structured output mapped to Java records.
- ARM64 container image optimized for AWS Graviton.
- Modular Terraform for infrastructure provisioning.
The travel assistant is the recommended starting point. The following diagram illustrates how a Spring Boot agent interacts with AgentCore runtime, tools, memory, and models available on Amazon Bedrock.
The travel assistant runs a single Spring Boot application with two entry points, the /invocations and /ping contract required by AgentCore runtime. Spring AI orchestrates calls to Amazon Bedrock through the Converse API and resolves tool invocations locally inside the same process. Server-Sent Events stream tokens to the client as they are generated. AgentCore memory supplies both short-term context within a session and long-term context across sessions, so the agent retains conversation history without external state management.
The following diagram shows the architecture for the IDP multi-agent system.
The IDP multi-agent system routes documents through five specialist agents (Lawyer, Mortgage, Insurance, Tax, and General), each built on a shared AbstractDocumentAgent template. A ClassifierAgent reads each document and forwards it to the appropriate specialist. The specialist extracts structured JSON with confidence scores using the multimodal Converse API of Amazon Bedrock. A rules engine evaluates Spring Expression Language (SpEL) expressions from application.yml against the extraction. ALERT or BLOCK severity rules dispatch through the AlertService. Low-confidence documents go to human review. Metrics, audit trail, resilience, and observability apply across all stages.
Agent collaboration patterns
When multiple agents work together, how they coordinate determines system behavior. This solution uses three patterns:
The following diagram compares the three coordination patterns used in this solution.
Three patterns shown side by side. The router dispatches each request to one specialist by document type. The evaluator passes specialist findings through a rules engine that applies to severity levels and dispatches alerts or blocks for human review. The parallel fan-out sends one request to multiple specialists concurrently and aggregates results before the rules engine runs.
Router pattern: A lightweight orchestrator examines the incoming request and routes it to the appropriate specialist. In the IDP multi-agent system, the router inspects document type metadata and forwards it to the Lawyer, Mortgage, Insurance, Tax, or General agent. The router holds no domain logic. It is a dispatch layer only.
Parallel fan-out (optional extension): The base solution implements the router and evaluator patterns. The batch endpoint processes documents sequentially. When a document needs several perspectives at once, you can add a parallel fan-out as a drop-in extension. Dispatch to specialists concurrently and aggregate their results before the rules engine runs. Wall-clock time for the combined analysis is then bounded by the slowest single agent call rather than the sum of all calls.
Evaluator pattern: After specialists return their findings, a rules engine evaluates the combined output against configurable business rules. Rules that trigger ALERT or BLOCK severity dispatch through a pluggable AlertService for human review.
Walkthrough
The following sections walk you through the key implementation patterns, starting with the AgentCore runtime contract and progressing through tool calling, memory, resilience, and multi-agent orchestration.
Fulfilling the AgentCore runtime contract
Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime manages agent lifecycle and scaling. For current rates, see Amazon Bedrock AgentCore pricing and Amazon Bedrock pricing. The runtime routes incoming requests to your agent and monitors its health. Your agent must expose two endpoints:
- POST /invocations – Receives requests and returns responses as JSON or Server-Sent Events (SSE) streaming.
- GET /ping – Reports health status (Healthy or HealthyBusy). Long-running tasks must signal busy status, or the runtime might scale down the agent.
The following diagram shows how the Spring AI developer model maps onto AgentCore runtime, Memory, Browser, Code Interpreter, and Evaluations.
Two layers connected by the spring-ai-agentcore SDK. The application layer uses Spring AI components: @AgentCoreInvocation for endpoint wiring, ChatClient for model interaction, @Tool callbacks, and advisors for memory and guardrails. The infrastructure layer provides AgentCore runtime, AgentCore memory, AgentCore Browser, AgentCore Code Interpreter, and AgentCore Evaluations, all capabilities of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. The SDK bridges both, so developers write standard Spring AI code while AgentCore handles production infrastructure.
With the Spring AI AgentCore SDK, a single annotation handles this contract automatically:
The @AgentCoreInvocation annotation auto-configures the /invocations and /ping endpoints, handles JSON serialization, manages SSE framing for streaming responses, and reports health status. The same project also exposes REST endpoints for the React UI, so the agent serves both AgentCore runtime and a browser from one code base.
A note on streaming: the preceding minimal example returns the model stream directly, which is ideal for a chat UI. When an agent makes multi-argument tool calls, assemble the response with a blocking call() and then chunk the result for streaming, so the tool arguments bind reliably. The travel assistant serves both the AgentCore runtime and the React UI from one service method:
Implementing tool calling
With tool calling, the model can invoke external functions during reasoning. In Spring AI, you annotate a method with @Tool and the model decides when to call it and with what arguments:
You register tools on the ChatClient, and the model decides when to call them:
For structured output, request a Java record type. For multimodal input, attach media to the user message:
Note: We verified this example with Anthropic Claude Sonnet 4.5 on Amazon Bedrock. Spring AI adds the record’s schema to the prompt and parses the reply back into the Java type. Behavior can differ for other model families, so refer to the Spring AI structured output documentation and the Amazon Bedrock documentation for current support. It is best-effort, meaning that models can occasionally return output that does not match the schema. For stricter results, use a provider with native schema enforcement or Spring AI validation and retry.
The model receives the tool definitions as part of its context, reasons about when a tool call would help satisfy the user request, and returns a structured tool call response. Spring AI intercepts this, invokes the annotated method, and feeds the result back to the model for further reasoning.
Adding conversation memory
Real-world agents must remember what users said earlier in a conversation (working memory) and what they have learned over time (persistent memory). The Spring AI AgentCore SDK integrates with AgentCore memory through the advisor pattern: interceptors that enrich prompts with context before they reach the model.
The session ID becomes a conversation ID in actor:session form, so each user’s history stays isolated. For user-facing deployments, derive the actor from a verified OAuth 2.0 (JWT) identity rather than a client-supplied value, so users cannot access one another’s history.
In addition, AgentCore memory offers long-term memory support, employing the following strategies to identify and capture key insights from conversations:
- Semantic – Factual information about users (for example, “User works in finance”)
- User preference – Explicit settings and choices (for example, “Metric units preferred”)
- Summary – Condensed conversation history for continuity across sessions.
- Episodic – Past interactions and lessons learned.
Long-term memory extraction is asynchronous and optional. You choose which strategies to enable when you create the memory, and AgentCore extracts and consolidates records in the background after each conversation, so it never blocks the agent’s response. Choose strategies by workload: use user preference for the travel assistant so it remembers units and seating choices. Use summary when sessions span many turns. Use episodic when the agent should reuse lessons from past tasks. And use semantic to retain durable facts about the user.
Configuring the rules engine
Reading a document is only half the job. Acting on what it finds is the other half. The IDP multi-agent system includes a rules engine so operators can add business checks without touching code. This is an in-process rules evaluator that applies SpEL conditions to extraction results, not a workflow orchestration service such as AWS Step Functions. Rules live in application.yml and each condition is a SpEL expression evaluated against the extraction:
Severity levels control the engine’s behavior. INFO and WARN are logged, while ALERT dispatches through a pluggable AlertService. The default logs and emits a metric, but you can substitute Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS), Slack, or email by providing your own bean. BLOCK holds the document for manual review. Because rules are operator configuration rather than end user input, they provide a safe and auditable extension point. Adding new workflows is a configuration change, not a deployment.
The evaluator pattern is implemented by the rules engine and a pluggable AlertService. The default implementation logs the alert and emits a metric. You provide your own bean to route to Amazon SNS, Slack, or email:
Production readiness patterns
The following patterns address common production requirements that prototypes typically skip.
Resilience
Every model call uses a Resilience4j retry with exponential backoff, a circuit breaker that fails fast when model calls repeatedly fail or time out, and a timeout. Streaming paths emit a fallback message instead of a raw error. When traffic exceeds your account and Region service quotas, AgentCore runtime returns HTTP 429 and the retry handles it. For current limits, see the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore quotas documentation.
Twelve-factor configurations
Every configurable value (Region, model ID, memory ID, timeouts, rate limits, system prompt) is an environment variable bound to a typed @ConfigurationProperties class. The application is stateless, starts fast, drains in-flight turns on scale-down, and ships as one immutable ARM64 image promoted unchanged from development to production.
Security and identity
The Agentcore runtime uses AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) authentication by default. For user-facing agents, add an OAuth 2.0 (JWT) authorizer (such as Amazon Cognito) and derive the memory actor ID (actorId) from the verified identity. The IAM execution role follows least privilege:
- Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) pull.
- Scoped Amazon CloudWatch Logs and AWS X-Ray.
- Amazon Bedrock InvokeModel actions.
- Scoped workload access tokens (GetWorkloadAccessTokenForJWT) for the agent’s workload identity.
- AgentCore memory actions limited to the specific Memory resource ARN.
AgentCore Gateway, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, enforces inbound authentication (acting as an OAuth 2.0 resource server that validates JWT bearer tokens through Cognito, Okta, Auth0, or your own OIDC provider) and supports configurable rate limiting at the gateway layer. Rate limits are fail-open by default, so they should complement your core security controls rather than replace them.
Responsible AI controls
Autonomous agents that take real-world actions need safety controls as a first-class concern. The sample ships with a stand-in demonstration of a lightweight in-process pre-check called GuardrailService. This service screens prompts for disallowed intent and prompt injection, toggled per request with the guardrailsEnabled flag. Production deployments use Amazon Bedrock Guardrails as a standard control applied to every request, not a per-request toggle.
To upgrade the demo service for production, front the agent with Amazon Bedrock Guardrails. Guardrails apply configurable policies outside the model call, covering both input and output:
- Content filtering. Blocks harmful or off-topic content based on configurable thresholds for both prompts and responses.
- Denied topics. Prevents the agent from engaging with topics you define as out-of-scope.
- Sensitive information filters. Detects and redacts PII in both prompts and responses, supporting requirements such as GDPR and HIPAA.
For agents that retrieve external knowledge, enable grounding checks to reduce hallucination risk before the agent acts on tool calls with real-world side effects.
To wire Bedrock Guardrails into Spring AI, implement CallAdvisor and StreamAdvisor functions that call the ApplyGuardrail API and register it with defaultAdvisors on the ChatClient. Because policies live in the guardrail, security teams can update filters independently of the application release cycle.
Observability
The example instruments with the Micrometer Observation API (@Observed), producing timers that become distributed trace spans when you add a tracing bridge (OTLP to AWS X-Ray). The system emits domain metrics:
These metrics are exposed through /actuator/prometheus. The application also emits structured JSON logs to standard output, which Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime captures in Amazon CloudWatch Logs.
Optional extension that’s not implemented in this post: The sample includes the Micrometer OpenTelemetry bridge and OTLP exporter dependencies, but this post’s deployment does not provision an OpenTelemetry collector or enable trace sampling. You can add distributed tracing by setting a nonzero TRACING_SAMPLING value, pointing OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT to an OpenTelemetry or AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry collector, and configuring the collector to forward traces to AWS X-Ray.
Optional extension that’s not implemented in this post: The sample doesn’t implement an automated evaluation or optimization feedback loop. You can add one by persisting application metrics, traces, audit events, and human-review outcomes as an evaluation dataset. AgentCore evaluations or a separate evaluation pipeline can then compare versioned prompts, models, tools, and routing rules against quality, safety, latency, and cost thresholds. Promote changes only after evaluation and human approval.
Deploying the solution
This GitHub repository contains two AI agent applications demonstrating different use cases for autonomous AI. This guide shows you how to deploy them to AWS using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime.
The following diagram shows the deployment architecture: a single Arm64 image promoted through modular Terraform to the AgentCore runtime, with an optional Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) path.
Optional: running on Amazon EKS. Teams already standardized on Kubernetes can run the same Arm64 image on Amazon EKS, using their existing cluster for scaling and health checks against the /ping endpoint, with IAM Roles for Service Accounts (IRSA) for scoped, least-privilege pod-level access to Amazon Bedrock and AgentCore memory. The container is identical, so nothing in the application changes.
Three stages: build and publish, Terraform, and runs on AWS. The CI pipeline packages the application into a linux/arm64 image and pushes it to Amazon ECR with immutable tags. Three Terraform modules provision the ECR repository, a least-privilege IAM execution role, and the AgentCore runtime. The agent runs serverlessly on AgentCore runtime, calling Amazon Bedrock and AgentCore memory. An optional Amazon EKS path reuses the same image with IRSA for scoped pod-level credentials.
Follow these steps to deploy either application.
Step 1: Clone the repository
Open your terminal and run:
Step 2: Navigate to the directory for the agent you want to deploy
- Deploy autonomous agent:
- Deploy IDP multi-agent system:
Step 3: Configure Terraform variables
Before deploying the infrastructure, configure your Terraform variables in the terraform.tfvars file located in the terraform directory.
Basic configuration
The solution uses default values for most settings, but you can customize the following in your terraform.tfvars file:
- AWS Region: The AWS Region where resources are deployed.
- Environment: Environment ID (such as dev or prod) used in resource naming.
- bedrock_model: Amazon Bedrock foundation model (for example: global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0). For model availability by Region, refer to Supported models by AWS Region in Amazon Bedrock.
Step 4: Run the deployment script
For Linux/macOS:
For Windows PowerShell:
The deployment script does the following:
- Create an Amazon ECR repository.
- Build the Java application.
- Create and push a Docker container image.
- Create an IAM execution role.
- Deploy the AgentCore runtime.
Step 5: Run the application
Once the deployment is complete, you can run the application using the following commands.

Cleaning up
AgentCore runtime scales to zero and bills per invocation, so an idle agent costs almost nothing. Your main variable cost is Amazon Bedrock token usage, plus a small amount for Amazon CloudWatch and Amazon ECR storage. For current rates, see Amazon Bedrock AgentCore pricing and Amazon Bedrock pricing. To avoid incurring future charges, tear down the infrastructure when you are finished:
For Linux/macOS:
For Windows PowerShell:
Delete any AgentCore memory resources and Amazon ECR images you no longer need using the AWS CLI.
Conclusion
In this post, you learned how to build autonomous AI agents in Java using Spring AI and Amazon Bedrock. We covered the three capabilities that turn a model into an agent: planning, tool use, and memory. We also showed how Amazon Bedrock AgentCore services carry an agent to production. The Spring AI AgentCore SDK maps these capabilities onto idiomatic Spring through annotations and a familiar ChatClient. Finally, we outlined architecture patterns for multi-agent collaboration. These include the router pattern, the evaluator pattern implemented by the rules engine, and parallel fan-out as an optional extension.
The key takeaway for Java teams: you do not need to leave your environment to build production-quality agents. The patterns you already trust (dependency injection, configuration properties, advisors, Actuator, Micrometer) carry directly into the agentic world. AgentCore supplies the runtime, memory, identity, and governance that production demands.
As next steps, consider the following:
- Connect enterprise systems through AgentCore Gateway and the Model Context Protocol (MCP)
- Add Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases, the fully managed RAG capability, and web search so the agent reasons over your data.
- Implement Amazon Cognito JWT authentication with per-user memory isolation.
- Customize Amazon Bedrock Guardrails policies: add domain-specific denied topics, tighten content-filtering thresholds, and enable grounding checks tuned to your knowledge sources.
- Use AgentCore Evaluations to score production traces and promote prompt or model changes after review.
Each is an incremental addition to the foundation you have built here, not a rewrite.

articles.title: Preload von GTA 6: Datenverkehr steigt teilweise um das Zehnfache an – was das für den Release bedeutet
articles.text:
Preload von GTA 6: Datenverkehr steigt teilweise um das Zehnfache an – was das für den Release bedeutet
Am 19. November 2026 fällt der Startschuss für ein Spiel, auf das viele Zocker:innen schon seit Jahren warten. GTA 6 öffnet die Tore des neonbeleuchteten und chaotischen Vice City. Neu für die Reihe ist, dass das Spiel ausschließlich als Download angeboten wird. Damit im besten Fall niemand am Release-Tag enttäuscht wird, weil die Download-Server in die Knie gehen, lässt Rockstar den Preload von GTA 6 seit dem 10. November zu.
GTA 6 im Preload: Erste Vorzeichen für den Start?
Wie Golem berichtet, vermelden schon jetzt erste Internetanbieter, dass GTA 6 den Datenverkehr beachtlich erhöht. So verzeichnete etwa 1&1 in der Nacht vom 9. auf den 10. November einen Verbrauch, der etwa zehnmal so hoch lag, wie an normalen Tagen. Auch Vodafone berichtet von einem kurzzeitigen Anstieg. Wie uns ein Sprecher des Unternehmens mitteilte, lag der Datendurchsatz am Tag des Preloads etwa 60 Prozent über dem Niveau des Vortags.
Wie Vodafone weiter berichtet, geht der Großteil des Traffics aus Downloads über das Playstation Network zurück. Nach dem ersten Anstieg ging der Datenverkehr aber wieder etwas zurück. Er liegt zwar noch rund 20 Prozent über dem Normalwert, ist aber für das Netz keine besondere Belastung. Vodafone geht davon aus, dass der Preload dazu beiträgt, die Last über mehrere Tage gleichmäßiger verteilen. Marc Hölzer, Bereichsleiter Netzentwicklung bei Vodafone, sagt zum möglichen Anstieg zum Release: „Unser Netz ist auf solche Spitzen vorbereitet und verteilt die zusätzlichen Datenmengen so, dass die Downloads stabil bei den Kunden ankommen. Klar ist aber auch: Das Download-Tempo kann dabei von Nutzer zu Nutzer unterschiedlich sein und zeitweise schwanken.“
Und auch in den USA rüsten sich die Anbieter für den Release von GTA 6. Comcast bietet über seine Untermarke Xfinity etwa erhöhte Download-Raten für alle Kunden und das ohne Aufpreis. So sollen sich die mehr als 200 Gigabyte, die GTA 6 im Download beanspruchen wird, dank Verbindungen mit bis zu zwei Gigabyte pro Sekunde schnell abhandeln lassen.
Gegenüber Gamesindustry berichteten mehrere Branchenexpert:innen, dass der Release von GTA 6 zwar eine Herausforderung für den Datenverkehr sein wird, aber es aktuell keine Anzeichen dafür gäbe, von flächendeckenden Ausfällen auszugehen. Sie gehen davon aus, dass der Preload die Last vom Playstation Network und vom Xbox Store nimmt. Ohne eine neuntägige Vorlaufzeit hätten sonst alle Vorbesteller:innen direkt zum Launch den Download angeworfen und hätten die Server damit überfordert.
Neil McRae, Chief Technology and Innovation Officer beim britischen Internetanbieter Cityfibre, schlägt indes etwas vorsichtigere Töne an: „Es gibt keinen Weg daran vorbei, dass am Launch-Tag extrem viel los sein wird. Das liegt daran, dass viele Leute bis zum Launch mit dem Kauf warten.“ Doch in den vergangenen Jahren sind digitale Events und ausschließlich per Download angebotene Spiele immer mehr zum Standard geworden. Internetanbieter konnten sich laut McRae auf ein solches Großereignis also vorbereiten.
Er sagt dazu: „Egal, ob es der Launch von GTA 6 oder ein großes Update für Fortnite oder Call of Duty ist: Netzwerkspitzen sind mittlerweile ein normales Ereignis statt einer Anomalie. Die Anbieter sind in der Lage, sie zu handhaben.“ Gordon Thornton, der 17 Jahre bei Sony gearbeitet und dort das Playstation Network mit aufgebaut hat, findet ähnlich optimistische Worte für die Server der Playstation: „Sie wissen, wie viele Vorbestellungen es gab und welche Bandbreiten nötig sind, um die Vorbestellungen bereitzustellen […] Es ist der größte Titel und die größte Möglichkeit für die PS5, sie müssen es also hinbekommen.“

articles.title: Taiwan’s chipmaking giant TSMC to invest $1B in Anthropic, OpenAI
articles.text:
Top chip manufacturer TSMC is ready to invest $1 billion in Anthropic and OpenAI. That would give the Taiwanese chipmaker direct stakes in leading AI developers, even as its own contract chipmaking business has profited enormously from the AI data center buildout.
The chipmaker’s board approved plans to invest up to $500 million in OpenAI preferred stock reserved for large investors and another $500 million to purchase Anthropic common shares at the latter’s expected IPO price, according to Reuters. Such an investment may give markets “a shot of confidence as the artificial-intelligence trade shows signs of strain,” The Wall Street Journal reported.
But analysts also warned that such circular financing among investors, suppliers, and customers has made it difficult to evaluate real market demand for AI-related hardware and services, according to the Journal.
TSMC’s chip fabrication plants physically produce the vast majority of Nvidia’s chips designed for AI data center workloads and make most of Apple’s custom chips used in iPhones, Mac laptops and desktops, plus Apple’s planned AI computing server. Most of these fabs are located in Taiwan, but TSMC also operates fabs in Japan and China, and it has an expanding US manufacturing cluster in Arizona. It is also building a new fab in Germany.

articles.title: Nvidia’s stock drops as board reportedly preps to oust CEO Jensen Huang | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Nvidia is reportedly planning to oust its co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang, who has led the company for the last 33 years, the Wall Street Journal reports. Sources told the newspaper that the Nvidia board is meeting as soon as Wednesday to determine Huang’s future at the company.
On Sunday, Huang admitted to having an extramarital affair with a woman purported by U.S. intelligence to be a Chinese spy. On Wednesday evening, the New York Times reported that Huang also had an affair with an executive who reports to him.
Nvidia has become one of the most valuable companies in the world as it designs the chips that power the AI boom, but in the midst of Huang’s ongoing scandal, Nvidia stock fell about 8% in after hours trading on Wednesday. The stock is down about 11% in the past five days.
Huang famously delegates very little and has about 60 direct reports, he has said. The company also has not had an obvious successor or a succession plan. According to Bloomberg, Nvidia is working with an outside firm to identify candidates that could potentially replace Huang as CEO.

articles.title: Jensen Huang devrait se faire limoger par Nvidia
articles.text:
Les jours de Jensen Huang à la tête de Nvidia sont peut-être comptés. Selon le Wall Street Journal, qui a rapporté l’information ce mercredi 11 novembre, le conseil d’administration se prépare à démettre le charismatique patron de ses fonctions. Le dimanche 8 novembre, dans un message aux salariés, il a reconnu avoir été infidèle à sa femme. Il n’a pas nommé Alice Huang, une femme d’affaires chinoise que les services de renseignement américains soupçonnent de travailler pour Pékin. Mais son dossier ne s’arrêterait pas là.
D’après le New York Times, qui cite cinq personnes ayant travaillé chez Nvidia, Jensen Huang aurait aussi trompé sa femme avec Kimberly Powell, vice-présidente responsable du secteur de la santé chez Nvidia et dont il est le supérieur hiérarchique. Une faute grave pour un homme censé montrer l’exemple dans le respect des règles strictes concernant les relations au travail. Le lien hiérarchique accable un peu plus Jensen Huang.
Le conseil d’administration de Nvidia prépare l’éviction de Jensen Huang
Jensen Huang, cofondateur et visage de l’entreprise, pourrait donc être limogé de son poste de CEO par le conseil d’administration de Nvidia. Selon le Wall Street Journal, le conseil d’administration devait se réunir dès ce mercredi 11 novembre pour décider de son sort, sans attendre les conclusions de l’enquête interne. Nvidia a perdu plus de 450 milliards de dollars (environ 390 milliards d’euros) de valorisation boursière depuis l’annonce de l’enquête, et l’action a encore reculé après la clôture de mercredi.
Selon Bloomberg, le conseil d’administration travaille déjà avec un cabinet extérieur pour trouver un successeur, et envisage de nommer un CEO par intérim d’ici là. Jensen Huang, qui a reconnu son infidélité sans nommer Alice Huang, n’a rien confirmé au sujet de Kimberly Powell. Il existerait toutefois des preuves vidéo sur le lien affectueux présumé entre les deux personnes.
Nvidia n’a aucun successeur désigné. Jensen Huang dirige l’entreprise depuis sa création en 1993, et une soixantaine de cadres lui rendent compte directement. Remplacer Jensen Huang serait d’autant plus risqué qu’il incarne le virage réussi de Nvidia vers l’intelligence artificielle. Sous sa direction, Nvidia est passée du statut de fabricant de cartes graphiques à celui de premier fournisseur de puces pour l’IA, et sa capitalisation boursière s’est envolée. Nvidia figure sur le podium des entreprises les mieux valorisées au monde, aux côtés d’Apple et de Microsoft. L’affaire Jensen Huang fragilise sa position.
Le soupçon d’espionnage pèse encore plus lourd pour Nvidia. Alice Huang a dirigé Megaspeed, une société de cloud basée à Singapour, devenue l’un des plus gros clients de Nvidia avec quelque 4,8 milliards de dollars (environ 4,1 milliards d’euros) de matériel acheté. Les autorités américaines la soupçonnent depuis 2024 d’avoir aidé la Chine à contourner les restrictions sur l’exportation des puces, ce que Megaspeed conteste.
