articles.title: Steam Deck now shows average frame rates for thousands of games
articles.text:
Much Data, Very Frame: Valve is trying to ease the pain points of Steam Deck owners by providing a more detailed picture of a game's actual performance. Steam store pages can now show the average frame rate Deck players get in many games, which might help customers make a more informed choice when they're looking to purchase a new title.
Valve announced the addition this week, with the data calculated from previously collected, anonymized figures provided by customers who chose to opt in to frame rate sharing. The average is already available for "thousands" of Steam Deck-tested games, and the same data can be viewed in the Steam Library by users on the Steam Client Beta.
After being tested for Steam Deck compatibility, a game can be classified as Verified, Playable, or Unsupported, and the average frame rate is shown under the "Steam Deck Compatibility" section of each game's store page, no matter how well a title is expected to run on a Steam Deck.
Furthermore, Valve is providing a "framerate histogram" that breaks down the percentage of data samples at each frame rate. This additional view should inform customers about potential hiccups during gameplay, including stuttering issues. All data is anonymized, with Valve confirming that a "majority" of Steam Deck owners have already opted in and shared their frame rate data with the Steam community.
Valve said the average frame rate should improve how Steam Deck users judge compatibility with a specific game, since its ratings rely on standardized testing criteria that "may not match every customer's bar for acceptable gameplay."
An unstable game classified as Unsupported might be considered playable by some users if the frame rate is high enough, while a Verified game might run at a frame rate that's too low for those used to high-refresh displays. The company stated that "by providing average framerate data for each game, customers now have a more complete picture of how the game performs on Steam Deck and can make more informed purchase and play decisions."
The PC gaming giant also describes the feature as a stepping stone toward bringing frame rate data to more devices. Users are already being prompted to share their anonymized frame data on the Steam desktop client's beta, with the full feature expected to reach all Steam customers in the future.
Steam Deck handhelds are not exactly the most powerful gaming devices out there, but they come in a few "standard" hardware configurations that can help with stress-testing the feature before its wider adoption in the wild west of the PC hardware market. Meanwhile, Valve's handheld line is reportedly suffering a steep sales decline, estimated at around 80%, following the latest price hikes imposed by the company, while modders are trying to make their own custom Steam Deck devices with a bit of software tinkering.

articles.title: Wi-Fi : la science a tranché, voici ce que disait vraiment la NASA sur votre cactus
articles.text:
Wi-Fi : la science a tranché, voici ce que disait vraiment la NASA sur votre cactus
Posé à côté d’un écran ou d’une box, le cactus passe parfois pour un bouclier contre les "radiations". Rien n’établit son efficacité pour cet usage. La croyance mêle les propriétés des végétaux, la physique des rayonnements électromagnétiques et des inquiétudes sanitaires.
Le cactus posé à côté du moniteur est d’abord un objet décoratif. Certains lui prêtent un second rôle : absorber les ondes. Une expérience publiée en 2019 a mesuré les champs magnétiques autour d’écrans en présence des cactus testés, et n’a relevé aucune baisse. Elle portait sur les très basses fréquences et sur les seules configurations étudiées ; le reste du spectre électromagnétique n’a pas été examiné.
Une origine floue
Son origine reste difficile à documenter. Les observations anciennes parfois invoquées ne renvoient à aucune publication scientifique identifiable, et rien ne permet de les vérifier.
Les travaux de la NASA sont parfois cités à l’appui. Son rapport de 1989 traitait pourtant d’une autre question : l’élimination de polluants chimiques de l’air, comme le benzène et le formaldéhyde, dans des enceintes expérimentales fermées, sans aborder à aucun moment la protection contre les ondes radio.
Même sur la qualité de l’air, la portée de ces résultats est limitée. Une analyse mise en ligne en 2019, puis publiée dans un volume daté de 2020, a fait le calcul : pour égaler l’élimination des composés organiques volatils qu’assure le renouvellement d’air courant d’un bâtiment, il faudrait de 10 à 1 000 plantes en pot par mètre carré de surface au sol. Quelques plantes ne remplacent pas la ventilation.
Ce que dit la physique
Wi-Fi, Bluetooth et réseaux mobiles fonctionnent avec des ondes radio, à ne pas confondre avec les champs de très basse fréquence produits par les circuits électriques. Ces rayonnements sont non ionisants. Contrairement aux rayons X, leurs photons ne transportent pas assez d’énergie pour ioniser directement les molécules, ce qui ne les empêche pas d’interagir avec les organismes vivants.
Aux fréquences du Wi-Fi et de la téléphonie mobile, les effets sanitaires avérés, ceux sur lesquels l’ICNIRP fonde ses recommandations, tiennent à un échauffement excessif des tissus. Une interaction biologique n’implique pas forcément un effet nocif.
La végétation atténue et diffuse une partie des ondes radio, plus ou moins selon la fréquence, la teneur en eau et la géométrie de l’obstacle. Les ondes contournent aussi les obstacles par diffraction : cacher un écran derrière une plante ne revient pas à le blinder. Un cactus posé sur un bureau n’a rien d’un dispositif de protection.
La distance, en revanche, joue un rôle important dans l’exposition : en champ lointain et en espace libre, à puissance d’émission constante, doubler la distance divise par quatre la densité de puissance. Dans une pièce, les réflexions et les obstacles compliquent cette relation, qui ne donne alors qu’un ordre de grandeur.
Des limites avec des marges
En France, la valeur limite du champ électrique varie avec la fréquence : 61 V/m dans les bandes Wi-Fi, environ 41 V/m à 900 MHz. Ces niveaux de référence encadrent l’exposition aux champs ambiants.
Asus ZenWiFi BT8
Les téléphones relèvent d’un autre indicateur, qui ne se compare pas aux V/m. Le débit d’absorption spécifique (DAS) mesure la puissance absorbée par unité de masse de tissu, avec des limites locales de 2 W/kg pour la tête et le tronc et de 4 W/kg pour les membres. Sur le corps entier, le DAS moyen ne doit pas dépasser 0,08 W/kg pour le public, soit cinquante fois moins que le niveau de 4 W/kg retenu par l’ICNIRP pour établir cette restriction thermique. Ce facteur 50 vaut pour cette seule restriction. Il ne se transpose ni aux valeurs en V/m ni, de façon uniforme, aux limites locales.
Un dossier sanitaire à nuancer
En 2024, une revue commandée et partiellement financée par l’Organisation mondiale de la santé a rassemblé 63 articles parus entre 1994 et 2022. Elle ne relève pas d’augmentation du risque des principales tumeurs étudiées en lien avec l’usage du téléphone mobile, à commencer par les gliomes et les méningiomes. Ses conclusions restent cantonnées aux tumeurs et aux expositions étudiées.Chez l’animal, le tableau est moins net. Une revue publiée en 2025 relève des signaux de cancérogénicité, dont des gliomes et des schwannomes cardiaques chez des rats mâles, des observations qui ne se transposent pas directement aux usages humains courants. Une étude japonaise publiée en 2026 n’a pourtant trouvé aucune augmentation statistiquement significative des tumeurs dans les conditions testées. Pour conclure, il faut donc considérer l’ensemble des travaux.
Le Centre international de recherche sur le cancer (CIRC) a classé les radiofréquences dans le groupe 2B, « peut-être cancérogènes pour l’homme », en 2011. Ce classement signale un danger possible. Il ne chiffre aucun risque pour un usage donné. Un groupe consultatif a placé leur réévaluation parmi les priorités de la période 2025-2029.
Mesurer plutôt que supposer
Pendant un appel, le haut-parleur ou un kit mains libres éloignent le téléphone de la tête. C’est une mesure de prudence, qui réduit l’exposition.
En France, chacun peut aussi faire mesurer gratuitement les champs électromagnétiques dans son logement ou dans un lieu accessible au public. La demande doit être signée par un organisme habilité, après quoi l’ANFR mandate un laboratoire indépendant accrédité. La mesure porte sur les champs ambiants et ne remplace pas les essais de DAS réalisés sur les téléphones.
Le cactus peut donc rester sur le bureau. Comme décoration.

articles.title: CE-Ventures backs UK's Oyster Therapeutics in $60 million Series A round
articles.text:
CE-Ventures backs UK's Oyster Therapeutics in $60 million Series A round
- UK-based biotech company Oyster Therapeutics has raised $60 million in Series A funding, with participation from CE-Ventures, the corporate venture capital arm of UAE-based Crescent Enterprises. CE-Ventures' individual investment amount was not disclosed.
- Previously known as Kesmalea Therapeutics, Oyster is headquartered in London, UK, and develops targeted protein degradation therapies for neurodegenerative diseases, initially focusing on Alzheimer's disease and other conditions associated with abnormal tau protein accumulation.
- CE-Ventures, headquartered in Sharjah, UAE, invests across sectors including biotechnology, deeptech and consumer businesses. Its investment in Oyster expands its life sciences portfolio into neuroscience and targeted protein degradation.
- The funding will support the development of Oyster's lead oral drug candidate targeting tau proteins towards clinical trials, alongside further development of its proprietary SELFTAC technology platform. The company has also entered into a research agreement with Massachusetts General Hospital to advance its understanding of tau biology.
Press release:
CE-Ventures, the corporate venture capital platform of Crescent Enterprises, today announced its investment in Oyster Therapeutics, previously known as Kesmalea Therapeutics, as part of the company’s $60 million Series A financing. Oyster is a pharmaceutical company developing next-generation targeted protein degraders, with an initial focus on tau-driven neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer’s.
The financing will support Oyster’s next stage of development and advance its lead programme, an oral, brain-penetrant degrader targeting the protein tau, towards clinical development. Abnormal tau accumulation is a defining feature of a group of neurodegenerative diseases known as tauopathies, including Alzheimer’s disease.
Oyster’s lead candidate is designed to enter the central nervous system and selectively remove pathological forms of tau while preserving healthy tau. By developing the candidate as an oral therapy, the company aims to create a practical treatment approach suitable for diseases affecting large patient populations.
Rob Johnson, Chief Executive Officer of Oyster Therapeutics, said:
“We are delighted to welcome CE-Ventures as an investor and to have their support as we enter this next phase of growth. This financing enables us to accelerate our lead tau degrader towards the clinic while advancing our broader SELFTAC platform, which we believe has the potential to unlock a new generation of medicines for diseases of the central nervous system. We look forward to working with CE-Ventures and our wider investor syndicate as we build a leading company in targeted protein degradation.”
Oyster’s broader pipeline comprises candidates generated through its proprietary SELFTAC® platform, which is designed to address the size limitations of conventional bifunctional targeted protein degraders. The platform enables smaller components to cross biological membranes before self-assembling into bifunctional degraders, with the aim of improving oral bioavailability and central nervous system penetration while retaining the ability to direct the cell’s natural protein-disposal machinery towards disease-causing proteins.
Tushar Singhvi, Deputy CEO and Head of Investments at Crescent Enterprises, said:
“CE-Ventures continues to expand its life sciences portfolio by backing differentiated technologies with the potential to address areas of significant unmet medical need. Oyster Therapeutics combines a proprietary platform with a clear therapeutic focus in neurodegenerative disease, where new approaches capable of addressing underlying disease biology are urgently needed.”
Oyster has also entered into a sponsored research agreement with Massachusetts General Hospital to access specialist tau biology capabilities, including patient-derived neuronal cell lines and techniques to generate and detect oligomeric tau. The research is being conducted under the supervision of Dr. Catarina Silva, an investigator at the Mass General Brigham Neuroscience Institute, Assistant Professor of Neurology at Harvard Medical School and a leading tau researcher.
Dr. Damir Illich, VP, Life Sciences at CE-Ventures, added:
“Oyster’s SELFTAC® platform addresses a key challenge in targeted protein degradation by aiming to combine the power of bifunctional degraders with properties that support brain penetration and oral delivery. Its lead tau programme gives the company a differentiated approach in neurodegenerative disease, supported by strong scientific expertise and a path towards clinical development.”
CE-Ventures’ life sciences portfolio spans drug discovery, genetic medicine and targeted therapeutics. Oyster Therapeutics adds neuroscience and targeted protein degradation to that mix, further broadening the therapeutic technologies represented across the portfolio.

articles.title: Canadians can't keep up with all the streaming services: survey
articles.text:
Canadians are overwhelmed with choice when it comes to content, with most saying there are too many streaming services to keep track of. Moreover, Canadians are spending 14 minutes on average picking something to watch.
The details come from a new survey about Canadians’ watch habits conducted by Rogers and Angus Reid as part of a promotional push for Rogers’ latest Xfinity upgrade using Comcast’s Entertainment OS tech. The survey took place in August 2026, conducted nationally in English and French with a sample size of 1,015.
The survey found that Canadians take an average of about 14 minutes to choose something to watch, with about 22 per cent of respondents spending 20 minutes or more. Those numbers line up with results from similar studies — for example, Roku shared last month that Canadians spend about 80 hours a year (about 13 minutes per day) deciding what to watch.
Alongside that, 42 per cent of respondents said they chose content purely because it appeared in a “top 10” or trending list, while another 30 per cent said they chose content recommended by a streaming service.
The survey noted that 86 per cent of Canadians think that there are too many streaming services to keep track of, with 82 per cent of respondents saying that they want to find all of the available shows/movies easily in one place, no matter who makes the movies.
In a follow-up question, 88 per cent said that such a universal platform would simplify their entertainment experience, with 86 per cent saying it would help them find content faster.
Xfinity isn’t the only solution
Naturally, Rogers used the results to position its Xfinity TV platform as the universal option that solves these problems, but it’s far from the only one. Truth is, several companies are trying to solve the streaming app conundrum, though few have perfected it so far. Here are some alternatives we’ve tested:
Apple TV: Not to be confused with Apple’s streaming platform, the Apple TV box is a solid universal platform that lets you search across apps and streaming platforms.
Amazon Prime Video: While most think of Prime Video as another streaming service, Amazon lets you add additional subscriptions called channels, meaning you can easily bundle multiple services in one place, making it a surprisingly good universal platform (and it even has sports!).
Google TV: Similar to Apple TV, Google TV offers a platform for all your streaming apps, though I’ve found it struggles with searching for content across apps. If Google, the search company, can ever figure out how to make its TV search work well, it’ll be up there with Apple TV.
Telus Optik TV: This works like Google TV but with a different skin. You can customize the screen based on what apps you use, and it lets you group all your subscriptions under one payment. A decent option for those who already have services with Telus.
Bell Fibe TV: Bell touts Fibe TV as a “no hardware required” TV service, meaning you can stream it with an app and easily take it on the road or watch while commuting. You can also add the basic Netflix and Disney+ add-ons to get many of the top streaming apps under one payment, which is pretty close to the Xfinity experience.
Fubo: While it mainly centres around sports, you can cut a lot of the apps that you have on your streaming box with just a Fubo subscription — which includes DAZN, MLB Network, NFL Network, CHCH, NBATV Canada, and more. I imagine more news/current-events-focused channels like Global or CBC will come down the line to further enhance the experience.
River TV: Gives you access to 25 TV channels (including kids’ networks!) for $16.99/mo, and it’s Canadian.

articles.title: OpenAI Codex on Amazon Bedrock | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
OpenAI Codex on Amazon Bedrock
Developers increasingly use Codex with Amazon Bedrock to explore unfamiliar code, make changes, and handle repetitive engineering work. For platform teams, the challenge is to make those tools available without creating a second model-access, identity, and operations stack.
Codex can use Amazon Bedrock for inference with supported OpenAI models. In this post, we show how to fit that path into the AWS identity, AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM), Regional, and observability practices your organization already uses. Codex still runs on the developer workstation. The main design choice is how its model requests reach Amazon Bedrock and where your organization applies policy and operational controls.
We begin with a small, least-privilege pilot and work through the checks that matter before access expands. The examples use GPT-5.6 Sol. Before starting the pilot, review Supported models by AWS Region in Amazon Bedrock to confirm that Sol, Terra, or Luna is available in the AWS Region and inference path you plan to use.
Recommended default: Start with Native AWS Access for a small, least-privilege pilot. Choose AgentCore Gateway, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, when you want AWS managed gateway infrastructure for routing or Amazon Bedrock Guardrails. Choose an LLM Gateway when a platform team wants to enforce controls in the request path. A custom integration is the advanced version of the LLM Gateway pattern, not a quick start.
The examples come from the open source Guidance for Codex on AWS repository. It includes quick starts for Native AWS Access, AgentCore Gateway, LiteLLM on ECS, Portkey, the AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry (ADOT), and the Amazon CloudWatch setup used later in the post. Choose the quick start that matches your architecture, use it for the pilot, and adapt it to your environment.
Choose your rollout path
Authentication is only one part of an enterprise rollout. Decide who can use the service and which models and Regions are approved. Also define where configuration lives, what telemetry to collect, how usage is allocated, and which skills or Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers are allowed. The following table maps those needs to an access path and an owning team.
Choose the access path that provides the controls you need now. The most straightforward path that meets the requirement usually has the lowest operational overhead.
Decision rules
- Native AWS Access is the usual starting point when AWS identity and IAM controls are enough for the pilot.
- Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is a platform to build, connect, and optimize agents at scale, with any framework or model. Within the platform, AgentCore Gateway fits teams that want AWS managed gateway infrastructure for routing, Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, or related controls.
- A large language model (LLM) Gateway fits organizations that already operate a gateway or want to enforce controls in the request path. Building a custom gateway is the advanced version of this option.
The following diagram compares where identity, routing, policy, telemetry, and operational ownership sit across the three rollout paths.
Native AWS Access
If Native AWS Access fits the pilot, the repository’s Native AWS Access quick start provides the complete procedure and supporting files. The following abbreviated walkthrough focuses on the sequence and the checks that matter most.
Use your workforce identity provider for sign-in
Employees continue to sign in through the identity provider they already use. In this example, Okta handles authentication through Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) and provisions users and groups into IAM Identity Center through System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM). IAM Identity Center then issues the temporary AWS credentials used by Codex. The identity provider is not configured in Codex.
Prerequisites
- Add each pilot user to a dedicated group in the workforce identity system and provision that group to IAM Identity Center. Keep the assignment limited to the pilot.
- Choose an Amazon Bedrock Region and an OpenAI model available to the pilot identity, plus an inference profile if the selected API requires one. Check Sol, Terra, and Luna separately for the chosen account, Region, and inference path.
- Grant only the Amazon Bedrock model inference permissions used by Codex, any direct validation commands, and the selected observability destination.
- Prepare a non-production repository and name a rollback owner.
Configure
The pilot has three checks. First, sign in using the IAM Identity Center profile configured for the AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI) and call Amazon Bedrock Runtime directly. Next, point Codex to the approved model. Finally, run a safe Codex task. The direct call isolates AWS access problems. The final step confirms the Codex configuration.
Step 1: Sign in and validate Amazon Bedrock Runtime access.
This command creates a short-lived AWS session and checks whether the profile can invoke the chosen model in the chosen Region. If it fails, resolve the profile, Region, model or inference-profile access, or IAM permissions before configuring Codex.
Step 2: Configure the Codex provider.
The model value is the Codex model ID. The profile selects the AWS IAM Identity Center session, and region tells Codex which AWS Region to use. Keep these settings in user-level or managed configuration so a repository cannot change the provider.
Verify the pilot and confirm rollback
Before adding users, make sure the pilot reaches the approved model, produces the expected records, and can be disabled cleanly.
- Identity: aws sts get-caller-identity returns the expected IAM Identity Center assumed-role session.
- Model access: The pilot profile invokes the approved model through the API and Region selected for the test.
- Codex access: The user completes a safe, read-only task in a non-production repository, and the expected request-path evidence is available.
- Evidence and rollback: The identity, invocation, audit, and optional telemetry records are present. Remove the configuration or IAM Identity Center assignment, handle any active session according to your procedure or wait for it to expire, and verify that a new invocation is denied.
Watch the Native AWS Access walkthrough
The walkthrough shows the complete pilot sequence: workforce sign-in, direct Amazon Bedrock Runtime validation, Codex provider configuration, and a safe test task.
Figure 2: Native AWS Access walkthrough covering workforce sign-in, Amazon Bedrock Runtime validation, Codex provider configuration, and a safe pilot task
Use the video to verify the order of the checks and the evidence to collect before adding more pilot users.
Run a two-user identity-isolation check
Two users are required to test identity isolation. A single user shows that sign-in works. A second user tests whether attribution remains distinct. Have two pilot users sign in separately and run the same harmless task. Their assumed-role sessions and audit records, and telemetry records if configured, should remain distinct.
The following diagram shows how separate pilot identities should produce separate AWS sessions, request evidence, and optional telemetry while using the same approved Codex and Amazon Bedrock path.
Gateway paths for request-path controls
AgentCore Gateway is an option when you want AWS managed gateway infrastructure for centralized routing or Amazon Bedrock Guardrails. If your organization already runs an LLM Gateway or wants to enforce controls in the request path, use that gateway instead. Validate the selected gateway before exposing it to pilot users.
LLM Gateway: Validate before a pilot
- Check that the gateway accepts the Codex request format.
- Use the sign-in or token flow defined by the gateway team.
- Before inviting pilot users, test model routing, monitoring, failure handling, and rollback.
Custom enterprise integration
A custom enterprise integration is the most involved form of the LLM Gateway pattern. Consider it only when Native AWS Access, AgentCore Gateway, and an existing gateway cannot meet a specific requirement. The result is another service to design, secure, test, support, and operate, so platform engineering and security need to own it from the start.
Observe, govern, and allocate cost
Codex OpenTelemetry, Amazon Bedrock service records, AWS identity records, and billing data answer different questions. Codex OpenTelemetry describes client activity. Amazon Bedrock service metrics and model invocation logs show service-side activity when enabled. AWS identity records and the AWS Cost and Usage Report (CUR) provide identity and billed-usage evidence. Correlate them for the path you deploy, and do not present token volume as a cost report.
Define what code, prompts, files, and tool output Codex might send through the selected model path. Exclude secrets and restricted data unless the organization has approved that data flow. Require developers to review and test generated changes before merge. Telemetry does not establish correctness or safety.
OpenTelemetry metrics from Codex
For observability, this post uses the ADOT collector configuration and CloudWatch dashboard from the repository’s monitoring and operations guidance. Deploy that configuration to each managed pilot device, then run a safe Codex task.
The repository provides the configuration files. Follow its deployment instructions to install the approved ADOT collector and configure its AWS authentication.
Validate the repository path: run a safe Codex task and confirm that the expected operational metrics appear on the managed CloudWatch dashboard.
| Telemetry plane | Examples | Attribution boundary | 
| Codex OpenTelemetry metrics | Token usage, turns, API requests, request duration, tool calls, session source. | Per-user and team dashboard grouping only after the local collector adds validated identity attributes. | 
| Amazon Bedrock service metrics | Invocations, latency, input tokens, output tokens, client errors, server errors. | Use the documented namespace, metric names, and dimensions for the selected Runtime, Mantle, or AgentCore path. | 
| AWS identity evidence, model invocation logs, and CUR | Assumed-role single sign-on (SSO) principal plus billed Bedrock line items. | For Native IAM Identity Center access, CUR 2.0 with caller-identity allocation can expose the SSO principal. Gateway paths require gateway telemetry and spend records for end-user allocation. | 
Amazon CloudWatch dashboard and evidence
The Amazon CloudWatch Coding Agent Insights managed dashboard in the Guidance for Codex on AWS repository shows Codex operational metrics collected through ADOT. Use it to understand client activity, and use AWS identity, audit, and billing records separately when you need attribution or cost evidence.
| Question | Decision | Evidence to keep | 
| Who invoked the model? | Use the AWS identity/audit source for the path you selected. | Pilot identity record and request correlation, where available. | 
| What did it cost? | Use billing data for actual charge and label any inferred allocation clearly. | CUR source, allocation method, and known uncertainty. | 
| Can we stop unsafe or expensive behavior? | Use alarms for detection. Use IAM and managed client controls for their respective access and action boundaries. Use gateway policy when request-path enforcement, such as hard budgets or rate limits, is required. | Control test results and rollback procedure. | 
Watch the Codex OTel and CloudWatch walkthrough
The walkthrough shows how to query Codex OpenTelemetry metrics and confirm that the expected token and request data appears in Amazon CloudWatch.
Figure 4: Codex OpenTelemetry metrics shown in an Amazon CloudWatch dashboard
The example validates the aliased metric result in Amazon CloudWatch Query Studio and shows how the dashboard represents Codex client activity.
Standardize team behavior
After the infrastructure path is working, turn to the developer experience. Repository guidance, managed plugins, hooks, and approved MCP servers can make the rollout consistent without asking each team to assemble its own setup.
Plugins
Organization-owned plugins are a practical way to distribute shared skills, hooks, and approved MCP integrations. Give each plugin an owner and version, review changes before release, and publish it only through approved sources. Test updates with a pilot group and keep a documented removal path.
A plugin might include an MCP server configuration, but that does not make every bundled tool approved. Allow only the servers and tools the organization has reviewed, with user confirmation where it is needed.
Hooks
Hooks can be declared in hooks.json or directly in configuration. Keep the documented event casing, and deploy organization-owned policy commands through approved endpoint tooling.
Use PreToolUse, PostToolUse, or SessionStart where they solve a specific need. Before wider deployment, test allow, deny, timeout, and disconnected-endpoint behavior.
MCP
An MCP server connects Codex to another system, so each server creates a separate trust boundary. Limit access to the users and tools that need it, manage credentials through an approved OAuth or secrets process, and require confirmation for tools that change external systems. Keep MCP credentials out of the model-provider configuration.
Roll out in phases
The following diagram defines the scope and evidence required to advance from preparation through pilot, expansion, and organization-wide standardization.
Administrator launch checklist
- Record the selected path, owning team, Region, and model in the change record.
- Limit the pilot identity to the required permissions, and document how issued credentials or tokens are handled.
- Run a non-production test that covers sign-in, model availability, and one safe Codex task.
- Check telemetry and audit output from the deployed version rather than assuming the example applies unchanged.
- Separate billed amounts from estimates in cost reporting.
- Exercise recovery: remove the configuration or assignment, handle any active session through the approved procedure or wait for it to expire, and verify that a new invocation is denied.
Clean up
When the pilot ends or access must be disabled, remove the rollout resources that are no longer required.
Remove the Codex model-provider and telemetry configuration from managed devices. Remove the IAM Identity Center pilot assignment or gateway access, revoke pilot tokens and secrets, and handle active sessions according to the approved procedure. Uninstall or disable the ADOT collector, and delete the pilot CloudWatch dashboard and alarms if they are not shared with another workload. Verify cleanup by confirming that a new model invocation is denied and that retired telemetry resources receive no new data.
Configuration boundaries
Keep model-provider, credential, and organization telemetry settings in user-level or managed configuration. Project-local .codex/config.toml is repository-scoped configuration: Review it as code, but do not treat it as an enterprise enforcement boundary. AGENTS.md is useful for durable repository guidance, such as test commands and coding conventions, but it is not an enforcement boundary either.
| Setting type | Recommended location | Reason | 
| Model provider, credentials, Region | User-level or managed configuration | These are endpoint and enterprise choices, not repository defaults. | 
| OpenTelemetry exporter | User-level or managed configuration | Telemetry destination and data handling are organization controls. | 
| Repository instructions | AGENTS.md | Carries durable guidance but is not an enforcement boundary. | 
| Permission requirements | Organization-managed requirements.toml | Constrains supported security-sensitive client choices. | 
Conclusions and next steps
Codex can use Amazon Bedrock for inference with supported OpenAI models. Start with the least-complex access path that meets the requirement, prove the identity and model path with a small pilot, and add gateway or client controls only when they solve a specific need.
AgentCore Gateway provides an AWS managed gateway option for routing or Amazon Bedrock Guardrails. Choose an LLM Gateway when a platform team wants to enforce controls in the request path. Build a custom integration only when the available paths cannot meet a documented requirement.
Expand in stages and use evidence from each stage to decide what comes next. The Guidance for Codex on AWS repository contains the maintained configurations and validation procedures used in this post.

articles.title: Kora is a Linux OS that splits AI models across the CPU, GPU, and NPU
articles.text:
New Linux desktop OS splits AI workloads across CPU, GPU, and NPU, and also other machines connected to the same local network — Cyanogen co-founder unveils Kora, details the new AI-first operating system
Intel and AMD NPU support is planned, but founder says neither will be used for language models.
A team led by Cyanogen co-founder Kirt McMaster has unveiled Kora, a new Linux desktop OS with integrated AI models and agents that can split workloads across CPU, GPU, and NPU resources, as well as other machines on the same local network. We reached out to the firm for more info.
Kora, the first product from Kora Systems Inc., previously Playtron, carries the tagline “The Operating System for Intelligence” and has its own Cortex “hybrid inference engine” technology, which is not open source and is optimized for local models. The OS, built “from the kernel to the shell,” runs local models by default and cloud models when needed, and is expected to arrive on PCs in 2027.
The desktop follows the AI-focused motif with “neural workspaces” and a “neural file system,” which refer to sandboxed workspaces and files indexed by semantic meaning. Kora has three operating modes: “Work," "Create," and "Play." That last base is covered by GameFrame, which descends from Playtron’s GameOS. Humain OS, which Kora is developing with Saudi AI company Humain, is the enterprise variant of this OS.
Currently, the only NPU named in the release material is the Hexagon NPU found in the Snapdragon X2 Elite, which Qualcomm pegs at 80 TOPS. On the X2 Elite, Cortex can schedule AI workloads across the CPU, GPU, and NPU, as well as other systems on the local network, which could be a novel capability if it works beyond the Qualcomm hardware.
McMaster told Tom’s Hardware that the Snapdragon X2 Elite NPU runs Google's Gemma 4 26B model at 25 tokens per second for decode. Intel and AMD NPU support is in the works, but according to the developer, neither NPU will be used for LLMs, as GPUs are “just better for LLM workloads on x64.”
Each NPU vendor has its own software stack, or runtime, and prefers that models are compiled in its own format: Qualcomm with QAIRT/QNN, Intel with OpenVINO, and AMD with Ryzen AI software. The press kit doesn't identify support for any Intel or AMD chip, NPU runtime, model format, quantization, or speed figures for those platforms.
Our earlier Windows testing showed the same kind of divide: Snapdragon reached its NPU through the QNN provider under ONNX Runtime, while Intel’s work ran through IPEX, its extension for PyTorch, on the GPU because it was faster than the NPU.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
When asked about cross-vendor support, McMaster reiterated that “only Hexagon on Snapdragon X2 Elite is supported today.” Intel NPU support is planned, with “conversations underway,” though McMaster later clarified that neither Intel’s nor AMD’s NPU will be used for LLMs. On AMD’s Ryzen AI chips, Kora will likely use the NPU for embedding and speech-recognition models through ONNX.
As for what drives the Qualcomm Hexagon NPU, McMaster said Kora uses the “llama.cpp Hexagon backend” and “the upstream FastRPC driver.” That suggests the operating system reaches the NPU through the open-source llama.cpp project, not Qualcomm’s own QAIRT/QNN runtime, by way of the FastRPC driver in the mainline kernel.
| Kora NPU support by vendor, per the company |  |  |  |  | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| NPU | Vendor’s own framework | Status in Kora | Runtime KORA uses | What it runs | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qualcomm Hexagon (Snapdragon X2 Elite) | QAIRT/QNN | Supported today | llama.cpp’s Hexagon backend | Language models; KORA cites Gemma 4 26B at 25 tokens per second | 
| AMD XDNA 2 (Ryzen AI) | Ryzen AI software | Planned for launch | ONNX | Likely embedding and speech-recognition models; not language models | 
| Intel NPUs | OpenVINO | Planned, “conversations underway” | Not stated | Not language models | 
When asked about model formats, McMaster said, “we predominantly support GGUF,” llama.cpp’s model file format, and that Lemma, the inference engine inside Cortex, “can split model layers across processors as needed.” Lemma is built on llama.cpp, whisper.cpp, stable-diffusion.cpp, and ONNX. McMaster says that which runtime is used depends on the model's requirements, and more runtimes will be added down the line.
For today, llama.cpp has a Hexagon backend for Snapdragon and an OpenVINO backend for Intel CPUs, GPUs, and NPUs, although the latter is still marked “In Progress,” and no AMD NPU backend, which would explain why AMD goes through ONNX. AMD NPUs can run LLMs on Linux through the separate Lemonade 10.0 stack with FastFlowLM, as reported by Phoronix in March, though that isn’t the route Kora has chosen.
Beyond NPU stacks, those hoping to run Kora will need to be mindful of their system's available memory. The Gemma 4 26B model Kora uses, which Google lists as Gemma 4 26B A4B, needs about 14.4GB of memory to load its weights at 4-bit (Q4_0) quantization, by Google’s estimate, before any context window, while third-party listings put the download for the Q4_K_M file Kora uses at about 16–17GB. The model only activates about 4 billion of its 26 billion parameters per token but still needs to be fully loaded into memory.
McMaster said that with the model, the X2 Elite reaches “25 TPS decode throughput and 550 TPS prefill throughput,” or tokens per second, running “entirely on the Hexagon NPU with 32K context.” A dense model, rather than a mixture-of-experts, would be far slower. Not given are the RAM configuration or the specific X2 Elite chip.
On memory, McMaster said that “we recommend 64GB because it gives you access to better models,” but that is not a firm requirement. The company projects that “about 70 percent of the model calls it manages will run locally in 2027.”
Kora says its enterprise-focused Humain OS is due first and will be “commercially available in 2027,” on OEM PCs using the Snapdragon X2 Elite. Kora will follow "later in 2027.”
McMaster says that “Kora will be posted on our site and downloadable for anyone to install.” Included will be a list of recommended configurations, “but it should be installable on most modern PCs.” Exact pricing and the overall business model will be shared closer to the date of availability.
Edit: 11/11/2026 9:06am PT: Added further follow-up details provided by the maker. 
Follow Tom’s Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.
Shane Downing is a Contributing Writer for Tom’s Hardware, covering consumer storage, PC hardware, and AI.

articles.title: Le jeu de cartes de League of Legends en promo : la display Riftbound Armes Spirituelles est bradée
articles.text:
Après Arcane, Riot Games a trouvé un autre moyen de faire sortir League of Legends de l’écran. Avec Riftbound, l’éditeur signe un jeu de cartes à collectionner, lancé à l’automne 2025 en anglais. Le rythme est soutenu, avec quatre sets par an : la version anglaise en est déjà au cinquième, et la VF a déjà accueilli Déchaînement, le troisième.
Le deuxième, Armes Spirituelles, est sorti en français le 24 juillet. Philibert propose sa display à 99,96 € au lieu de 124,95 € pendant une vente flash qui court encore quelques jours.
Riftbound Armes Spirituelles, c’est quoi ?
Riftbound transpose les codes du MOBA sur la table. Chaque deck s’organise autour d’une Légende, une carte qui représente un champion de League of Legends. Pour gagner, il faut marquer des points en conquérant ou en tenant des champs de bataille, comme les objectifs qu’on se dispute sur la Faille de l’invocateur. On peut jouer en duel, en 2 contre 2 ou à quatre en chacun pour soi. Riot développe le jeu avec UVS Games et revient ainsi aux cartes après avoir nettement réduit la voilure sur Legends of Runeterra, son jeu de cartes numérique.
Armes Spirituelles est le deuxième set du jeu et sa première extension. Il pioche dans un réservoir de plus de 220 cartes et ajoute douze nouvelles Légendes, dont Ezreal, Fiora, Irelia, Lucian, Jax et Draven, souvent illustrés dans leurs skins Fleur spirituelle. La grande nouveauté, ce sont les équipements : des cartes qui renforcent vos unités au fil de la partie, comme les objets qu’on achète entre deux combats sur League of Legends.
La display contient 24 boosters de 14 cartes. Chaque paquet renferme 7 communes, 3 peu communes, 2 rares foil ou mieux, une foil bonus de n’importe quelle rareté et un jeton. L’éditeur annonce en moyenne plus de six cartes Épiques et au moins deux illustrations alternatives spéciales par boîte.
Est-ce que ça vaut le coup ?
Oui. À 99,96 €, le booster revient à un peu plus de 4 €, contre 5,99 € à l’unité chez Micromania, et ailleurs la display coûte plutôt entre 120 et 145 €. À une période où le TCG a le vent en poupe, c’est une bonne affaire. Le set reste jouable en standard jusqu’à la première rotation, prévue début 2028. Si vous débutez, prévoyez un deck de champion préconstruit (une vingtaine d’euros), car 24 boosters seuls ne suffisent pas pour jouer.

articles.title: Amazon : Ring lance un drone de sécurité pour la maison et un robot de surveillance pour les entreprises
articles.text:
Une alarme se déclenche à l’arrière de votre maison, et un petit drone Ring quitte sa base pour aller filmer la porte concernée, avant de vous montrer la scène sur votre téléphone. Promis depuis 2020, le Ring Drone Cam sera vendu 249,99 dollars aux États-Unis, avec un robot de patrouille à 999,99 dollars destiné aux entreprises.
Ring, la filiale d’Amazon connue pour ses sonnettes vidéo, a créé une division de robotique, Ring Robotics, pour lancer ces deux appareils. Le drone revient de loin. En 2020, la marque annonçait une première version, l’Always Home Cam, vendue elle aussi environ 250 dollars. Ring ne l’a ensuite proposée que sur invitation, à partir de 2021, avant de laisser le projet en sommeil. La marque prévoit les premières livraisons le 27 janvier 2027 aux États-Unis, mais attend encore le feu vert de la FCC, le régulateur américain des télécoms, pour vendre son drone. Et ce nouvel appareil filme l’intérieur de votre logement, alors que Ring essuie depuis des années des critiques sur les vidéos que la police américaine obtient de ses caméras.
Le drone de Ring ne filme qu’en vol
Comme l’explique à CNBC Jamie Siminoff, fondateur et patron de Ring, « les gens aiment les caméras d’intérieur, mais ils n’en veulent pas forcément partout dans leur maison ». Pour installer le drone, il faut lui faire un room tour de la maison à la main dans chaque pièce. Ring dresse alors un plan du logement et propose des points de passage, une porte ou une fenêtre, que vous pouvez modifier. Le drone décolle ensuite à heure fixe, sur demande à la voix ou dès qu’une caméra, un capteur ou une alarme Ring détecte une activité. Personne ne le pilote jamais seul. Sa caméra filme en 2K, avec un angle de 148 degrés, et deux LED s’allument dans l’obscurité. Ring annonce jusqu’à huit minutes de vol, et chaque minute en l’air réclame huit minutes de recharge.
Tant que le drone est posé sur sa base, sa caméra est éteinte, et une LED s’allume pendant l’enregistrement. Ring a aussi rendu l’appareil volontairement bruyant. « C’est bruyant, et pour nous, c’est une fonctionnalité. Cet engin ne va pas vous prendre par surprise », souligne Jamie Siminoff auprès de TechRadar. Pour guider le drone, Ring a conçu AI Pilot, un système de navigation à base de modèles de vision, de capteurs et de calculs sur ses serveurs. Vos vidéos sont chiffrées avec TAKE, le chiffrement par défaut le plus solide de la marque selon Ring, mais l’entreprise n’a pas précisé si vous pourrez les conserver ailleurs que dans son cloud.
Souvenez-vous, en février, on vous a raconté le tollé provoqué par une publicité de Ring diffusée pendant le Super Bowl. Elle vantait Search Party, une fonction d’IA conçue pour retrouver un chien perdu grâce aux images de plusieurs caméras d’un quartier.
Ring transforme le robot Astro en vigile pour les commerces et les bureaux
Le Rover Cam est en précommande, et Ring commencera à le livrer aux États-Unis le 16 décembre. Pour le concevoir, Ring a puisé dans le meilleur d’Astro, le robot domestique d’Amazon. Les deux machines sont presque identiques, avec un écran tactile de 10 pouces en guise de visage et une caméra périscope, dont le mât se déploie jusqu’à 1,2 mètre environ, pour regarder par-dessus un comptoir ou une étagère. La caméra passe à la 4K, contre 1080p sur Astro.
Pour une boutique, un bureau ou un petit entrepôt, Ring a conçu le Rover Cam pour des surfaces de 465 mètres carrés au maximum. Il roule jusqu’à trente minutes par charge et se recharge en une demi-heure environ. Il est possible de lui demander d’enregistrer dès qu’il repère une personne, puis parler à un employé ou à un cambrioleur par son haut-parleur. Son anneau lumineux, bleu pendant les rondes, clignote en rouge lors d’une alerte, et une sirène retentit. Pour programmer ses rondes et revoir ses vidéos, il faudra en revanche un abonnement Ring Protect.
Amazon avait tenté l’expérience avec Astro for Business, vendu 2 349,99 dollars aux petites entreprises fin 2023, puis abandonné après sept mois. Ring retente sa chance à un prix plus de deux fois inférieur. « Ensemble, c’est comme avoir un vigile en patrouille qui ne termine jamais son service », promet la marque. Elle n’a toutefois annoncé de livraisons qu’aux États-Unis, alors qu’elle vend ses sonnettes et ses caméras en France.

articles.title: Mangaluru’s Zupple Labs wins DRDO’s first-ever blockchain defence project
articles.text:
Mangaluru’s Zupple Labs wins DRDO’s first-ever blockchain defence project
Mangaluru-based Zupple Labs is the first blockchain startup selected under DRDO’s Technology Development Fund. Over 30 months, it will build an indigenous security-audit framework for defence applications.
Mangaluru-based Zupple Labs has been selected by the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) under its Technology Development Fund (TDF) programme. Its brief: build India's first indigenous framework for security auditing of blockchain applications in the defence sector.
The selection is rare by any measure. Fewer than 90 projects have made it through the TDF programme in its ten-year history, and this is the first in the blockchain domain.
What DRDO has asked Zupple Labs to build
Over the next 30 months, Zupple Labs will develop a platform that DRDO will use to standardise security audits of upcoming blockchain applications across the defence sector.
As defence agencies explore distributed ledgers for records, logistics and authentication, a common auditing standard matters. It gives every new application the same security bar before deployment, and keeps that capability built and owned in India.
Trust infrastructure for governments
Zupple Labs builds blockchain-powered trust infrastructure for governments and institutions, with a presence across four countries. Its systems secure and authenticate critical citizen records, making them tamper-evident and verifiable.
The records it handles include:
- Land records
- Educational credentials
- Identities
- Permits and work orders
A client list that spans continents
The DRDO mandate builds on an established public-sector track record. Zupple Labs has delivered solutions for:
- The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)
- The United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA)
- The Australian and New Zealand student immigration ecosystems
- The Governments of Chhattisgarh and Maharashtra
- The Government of Kenya
Work with national ministries, a UN agency and foreign governments gives the startup experience in exactly the kind of high-stakes, compliance-heavy environments that defence demands.
From Mangaluru to the national stage
Zupple Labs was a winner of the Karnataka government's Elevate programme in 2019. Seven years on, its DRDO selection is a strong signal for the state's Beyond Bengaluru push to grow startup hubs outside the capital.
Congratulating Zupple Labs on securing a project under DRDO’s TDF programme, Capt Brijesh Chowta, Member of Parliament from Dakshina Kannada, said: “Glad to see Zupple Labs, one of the 10 start-ups in this year’s ‘Bolpu’ cohort, making strides in strengthening the security and resilience of blockchain technology and contributing to India’s growing cybersecurity capabilities.”
The point goes beyond one company. Deep-tech work of national significance is now coming out of Karnataka's tier-2 cities, and Mangaluru is proving it can build for governments, global institutions and the country's defence establishment.

articles.title: Cada vez más gente está viendo el nuevo icono '5G+' en sus móviles. Y es una buena noticia para ellos
articles.text:
Yo me di cuenta hace algo más de un mes, poco después de actualizar a iOS 27: en la parte superior de mi teléfono (un iPhone 14 Pro) apareció de pronto el icono '5G+' junto a las barras que indican la cobertura móvil. Y no soy la única, cada vez más usuarios están viendo ese icono en su smartphone.
Al principio no me llamó la atención, pero pronto caí en la cuenta de lo que significaba eso. Donde antes simplemente ponía '5G', '4G' o, en el peor de los casos, '3G', ahora mi móvil marca '5G+' para avisarme de que está conectado a una red 5G+ o 5G "real".
Eso no quiere decir que antes no disfrutara de esa tecnología, sino que ahora mi teléfono me advierte de ello. Vamos a explicarte qué operadores utilizan el distintivo '5G+', en qué teléfonos puedes encontrarlo y, lo más importante, qué ventajas tiene.
Ahora sabrás si tienes 5G "real". Fue allá por 2023 cuando Orange primero y Movistar después activaron su famoso 5G+, que no es otra cosa que el nombre comercial que se ha dado a la red 5G SA (Stand Alone) o 5G "real" para diferenciarlo del 5G NSA que desplegaron inicialmente los operadores.
Hasta ahora, los usuarios han seguido viendo estos años el icono 5G en la pantalla de sus teléfonos sin poder distinguir si estaban conectados al 5G NSA (con arquitectura de red 100% 5G) o al 5G SA (apoyado parcialmente en infraestructura 4G).
Que ahora veas el nuevo icono del 5G+ no significa que hasta ahora no estuvieras disfrutando de ese 5G SA, sino que los smartphones no diferenciaban visualmente entre las distintas arquitecturas de red porque siempre mostraban el icono '5G'. Ahora, gracias al distintivo '5G+', podemos identificar cuándo se está utilizando específicamente una arquitectura 5G de extremo a extremo.
Sólo tres operadores. Unos meses después del lanzamiento del 5G+ de Movistar, Telefónica sorprendió a todos extendiendo su mejor 5G a O2. Y desde entonces, ningún otro operador ha seguido su ejemplo. Ni siquiera Vodafone (que sólo lo ha activado en algunas regiones) ni otras marcas de Orange España.
Por tanto, a día de hoy, sólo tres operadores ofrecen 5G+ a sus clientes: Movistar, O2 y Orange. El primer requisito para ver el icono, por tanto, es tener una línea móvil con alguno de ellos. Movistar y O2 ya muestran ese indicativo desde hace unas semanas, Orange ha empezado a mostrarlo ahora.
Primero, en iOS; poco a poco, en Android. Además de disponer de un terminal homologado para el 5G+ (que no todos lo están), lo debes tener actualizado a una versión del sistema operativo que muestre el icono del 5G+.
En el caso del iPhone, ese distintivo aparece desde la actualización a iOS 27 que se desplegó en septiembre. También ha empezado a mostrarse en móviles Android con soporte de software actualizado, como algunos modelos recientes de Samsung compatibles con One UI 9.0 y algunos dispositivos de Xiaomi, Motorola, OPPO, OnePlus y Google Pixel. Progresivamente, irá llegando al resto.
¿Es mejor el 5G+? La gran diferencia del 5G SA es que tanto la red de acceso radio como el núcleo central de la red están diseñados específicamente para tecnología 5G, lo que permite habilitar algunas funcionalidades y servicios, como el network slicing, y mejora la experiencia final para el usuario.
Entres otras ventajas, el 5G SA garantiza menores tiempos de respuesta para aplicaciones en tiempo real, una mayor eficiencia en la gestión del tráfico de datos, un mejor comportamiento de la red en entornos de gran concentración de usuarios y capacidad para soportar millones de dispositivos conectados simultáneamente.

articles.title: Asrock releases new Radeon GPU firmware after previous update bricked cards, offers no explanation
articles.text:
Facepalm: If you have an Asrock Radeon 7000-series graphics card, here's some good news: the company is rolling out a replacement firmware update after the previous version reportedly bricked some RX 7900 XT and RX 7900 XTX GPUs. The less welcome news is that the company hasn't said what it plans to do for users whose cards were borked.
As VideoCardz reports, the new RX 7900 XTX download carries the ASRVBFlash 1.0.6 label and a November 6 date. It replaces version 1.0.5, but there's no changelog explaining what's new or confirmation that the problems with the previous release have been fixed. That's not exactly reassuring for anyone considering another attempted update.
The original downloads arrived on October 29, covering ten Asrock models ranging from the RX 7600 XT to the RX 7900 XTX. They followed similar security-related firmware releases from Sapphire and Gigabyte, although Asrock's descriptions offered little beyond the flashing utility's version number.
Some owners soon reported that running the updater left their systems unable to boot. Windows would restart during the process, after which the machine failed to POST with the graphics card installed. Removing the GPU allowed affected systems to start again.
A moderator on Asrock's forum wrote that the failed flashes were due to graphics drivers not being completely removed beforehand. But one owner replied that they had used the uninstaller specified in the instructions and still ended up with a nonworking card.
Some users have recovered their GPUs using external EEPROM programmers. While that's encouraging for those affected, buying specialist equipment to rescue a graphics card after installing its manufacturer's update is hardly something for Asrock brag about.
It's also reported that a Japanese customer received an assurance from Asrock that the failed update would be covered under the company's warranty. Things don't look as positive for one European owner, though. They were directed toward warranty service, even though their card was out of warranty. It remains unclear what support other affected card owners will receive.
Asrock is no stranger to controversy over its firmware. In April 2025, AMD and Asrock pointed to memory compatibility amid multiple reports of Ryzen 9000 failures. The following month, an Asrock executive acknowledged that its BIOS settings were responsible, with current limits set too high for early CPU samples.

articles.title: La Chine réalise l'impossible : elle crée une batterie au lithium innovante capable de maintenir son autonomie, même à −50 °C
articles.text:
La Chine réalise l'impossible : elle crée une batterie au lithium innovante capable de maintenir son autonomie, même à −50 °C
Des chercheurs de l'Université de Nankai ont dévoilé une batterie au lithium qui fonctionne encore par −70 °C et stocke deux fois plus d'énergie que les modèles actuels. Le secret : un électrolyte qui rompt avec un siècle de chimie. La découverte est spectaculaire, mais encore loin de nos voitures.
Cet article a été initialement publié en septembre 2026. Nous le republions aujourd'hui car l'arrivée des températures hivernales ravive les inquiétudes des conducteurs concernant la perte d'autonomie de leur véhicule, et que les solutions technologiques pour y remédier suscitent toujours un grand intérêt au sein de notre communauté.
Tout conducteur de voiture électrique connaît la mauvaise surprise de l'hiver. Un matin de gel, l'autonomie affichée fond de 20, parfois 40 %, et la recharge s'éternise. Ce n'est pas un défaut de fabrication, mais une limite physique que l'on croyait presque indépassable : le froid paralyse la chimie interne des batteries. C'est précisément ce verrou, vieux comme la batterie elle-même, qu'une équipe chinoise affirme avoir fait sauter.
Pourquoi le froid tue les batteries
Pour comprendre l'exploit, il faut regarder ce qui se passe àl'intérieur d'une batterie quand le thermomètre chute. Le cœur du système, c'est l'électrolyte, ce liquide dans lequel voyagent les ions lithium d'un bout à l'autre de la cellule à chaque charge et décharge. Dans toutes les batteries actuelles, ce liquide repose sur des solvants à base d'oxygène, un choix hérité des débuts de la chimie des piles.
Le problème, c'est que ces solvants s'accrochent trop fort à l'ion lithium. Pour circuler, l'ion doit sans cesse se libérer de cette étreinte. Or cette opération demande de l'énergie. Par grand froid, cette énergie manque, l'ion peine à se détacher, le courant ralentit et les performances s'effondrent. C'est la fameuse barrière de désolvatation, le mur invisible contre lequel butent les batteries en hiver. L'équipe de Nankai a eu une idée radicale : remplacer l'oxygène par le fluor.
Le pari du fluor, une rupture de fond
En troquant les solvants oxygénés pour une molécule fluorée, le 1,3-difluoropropane, les chercheurs ont volontairement affaibli le lien entre le solvant et le lithium. L'ion, moins retenu, se libère beaucoup plus facilement, même dans un froid glacial. C'est un renversement de logique : là où la chimie classique cherchait des liaisons solides, cette approche mise sur une accroche délibérément lâche pour fluidifier la circulation.
Les résultats mesurés en laboratoire sont impressionnants. La batterie atteint 707 wattheures par kilo à température ambiante, soit plus du double des meilleures batteries lithium-ion du commerce, qui plafonnent autour de 250 à 300. Surtout, elle conserve environ 400 wattheures par kilo à −50 °C, et continue de fonctionner jusqu'à −70 °C, une température qu'aucune batterie classique ne supporte. À ce niveau de froid, elle restitue encore l'essentiel de son courant avec une efficacité de 98 %. Sur le papier, c'est la fin de la double malédiction des batteries : il fallait jusqu'ici choisir entre densité d'énergie et résistance au froid, ce système promet les deux.
De l'exploit scientifique à la route, un long chemin
Faut-il pour autant s'attendre à faire le plein de kilomètres cet hiver ? Certainement pas, et c'est là qu'il faut raison garder face aux titres enthousiastes. Ces performances ont été obtenues sur de petites cellules de laboratoire, pas dans un véhicule. Or, entre la prouesse en éprouvette et la batterie industrielle, les obstacles sont nombreux et sérieux. Le plus criant : la durée de vie. À ce stade, la batterie ne tient qu'environ 115 cycles de charge, quand l'automobile en exige plusieurs milliers. Elle s'userait donc en quelques mois.
D'autres défis restent entiers. Le solvant fluoré est volatil, il s'évapore dès 48 °C, ce qui pose des problèmes de sécurité et de stabilité par temps chaud, un comble pour une technologie du froid. Les chercheurs planchent déjà sur des molécules plus lourdes pour y remédier. S'ajoutent le risque de dendrites, ces filaments de lithium qui peuvent provoquer un court-circuit sur le long terme, et un coût de fabrication supérieur aux électrolytes classiques. Cette batterie ne roulera donc pas demain dans nos rues. Mais en brisant un dogme chimique vieux de deux siècles, elle ouvre une piste précieuse, d'abord pour l'aérospatiale, les drones de haute altitude ou les missions polaires, là où le froid extrême est la règle et où chaque gramme compte. La révolution n'est pas pour tout de suite, l'avancée scientifique, elle, est bien réelle.

articles.title: ¿Por qué la infidelidad del CEO de Nvidia, Jensen Huang, preocupa tanto a Estados Unidos?
articles.text:
La vida privada de los líderes de Silicon Valley rara vez sacude los despachos de seguridad nacional en Washington, pero el caso de Jensen Huang marcó una excepción sin precedentes. Al frente de Nvidia, la corporación que motoriza el avance de la inteligencia artificial a nivel global, el directivo quedó en el centro de una tormenta geopolítica: el Departamento de Justicia y el FBI abrieron una investigación para determinar si su relación extramatrimonial con una presunta informante de Beijing comprometió secretos estratégicos de Estados Unidos.
El foco del expediente apunta a Alice Huang (Huang Le), exdirectiva de Megaspeed, a quien los servicios de espionaje estadounidenses identificaron como una agente reclutada por el Ministerio de Seguridad del Estado de China (MSS), según reveló una investigación de The New York Times. La trama desató un desplome bursátil que evaporó USD 500.000 millones de valor de mercado de la tecnológica.
Por qué los chips de Nvidia son un activo militar estratégico para Estados Unidos frente a China
Para entender por qué el caso trasciende el ámbito corporativo hay que comprender qué fabrica Nvidia: procesadores gráficos (GPU) capaces de ejecutar millones de operaciones de cálculo en paralelo, la tecnología que entrena los modelos de inteligencia artificial más avanzados del planeta. Según señaló la BBC en su cobertura del caso, estos chips son considerados por las autoridades estadounidenses una cuestión de seguridad nacional debido a sus posibles aplicaciones militares y al peso que tendrán en la carrera por el dominio de la IA.
Por eso Washington prohíbe su exportación directa a China mediante controles comerciales estrictos: quien controle esa tecnología obtendrá una ventaja decisiva en la disputa geopolítica más determinante del siglo, tal como subrayó The Guardian al analizar las implicancias del escándalo. Con entre el 70% y el 95% del mercado mundial de aceleradores de inteligencia artificial, según estimaciones de la firma Mizuho Securities recogidas por medios especializados, Nvidia se ha convertido en un activo estratégico para Estados Unidos de peso geopolítico equivalente al de un arsenal tecnológico-militar de primer orden.
Que su máximo dirigente haya mantenido una relación íntima con una presunta agente del régimen chino coloca a la compañía en el centro de una crisis de seguridad nacional sin precedentes en Silicon Valley, de acuerdo con la cobertura de ABC News.
Cómo Megaspeed habría desviado chips de inteligencia artificial de Nvidia hacia China a través de Alibaba
Las indagatorias de los organismos de seguridad revelaron un esquema corporativo diseñado para burlar los controles aduaneros norteamericanos. Según informó ABC News, los servicios de inteligencia rastrearon los desplazamientos de la ejecutiva en Singapur, Silicon Valley y Taiwán mientras consolidaba compras masivas de hardware avanzado.
De acuerdo con la investigación de The New York Times, la relación entre ambos se consolidó a partir de junio de 2024, cuando fueron fotografiados juntos en Taipéi durante una feria tecnológica, en el mismo período en que Megaspeed concentraba compras masivas de procesadores de Nvidia; una designación que, según el diario, habría sido facilitada por la cercanía entre ambos.
A través de una sociedad instrumental registrada en Singapur, la ejecutiva obtuvo ese estatus y adquirió más de USD 4.000 millones en circuitos integrados avanzados. La compañía construyó centros de datos en Malasia para alquilar potencia computacional al gigante chino Alibaba, lo que abrió una vía indirecta de suministro vedada por la Casa Blanca.
En marzo de 2025, Alice Huang visitó la sede corporativa de Nvidia en Silicon Valley junto con otros ejecutivos; dos meses después fue fotografiada cenando con Jensen Huang en Taipéi, donde los medios taiwaneses la captaron dándole un beso en la mejilla, según documentó The New York Times. Además, la red de financiamiento de la firma registró inversiones vinculadas a filiales de ciberseguridad del China Electronics Technology Group (CETC), contratista clave del Ejército Popular de Liberación en Beijing.
El espionaje chino contra Jensen Huang: el MSS reclutó a Alice Huang para infiltrar Nvidia
La alarma en la administración pública se intensificó tras una prolongada vigilancia electrónica sobre las comunicaciones de la empresaria. Según consignó The Guardian, el secretario de Estado, Marco Rubio, coordinó la elaboración de un memorando clasificado que alertaba que el MSS utilizó a la ejecutiva para recopilar detalles técnicos sobre los chips estadounidenses y presionar a la compañía para que cabildeara a favor de flexibilizar los controles comerciales.
Según reveló The New York Times, el director del MSS, Chen Yixin, aliado histórico de Xi Jinping y oriundo de la provincia de Zhejiang —la misma región conectada a la red empresarial de Alice Huang—, encabeza una agencia que, según estimaciones de analistas de seguridad, supera ampliamente en número de agentes a la CIA y ha incorporado herramientas de inteligencia artificial para seleccionar y perfilar objetivos estratégicos.
La agencia reclutó a la ejecutiva para acceder a Jensen Huang porque, según señaló el exanalista de contrainteligencia de la CIA Peter Mattis en declaraciones recogidas por The New York Times, “está en el punto crucial de una tecnología que moldea el mundo”. Pese a que el presidente Donald Trump fue informado sobre las advertencias de inteligencia en la primavera de 2026, meses antes de que el caso trascendiera públicamente, optó por no interferir para resguardar las operaciones de la tecnológica más valiosa del país, según informó The New York Times.
El mandatario sostuvo que el directivo le aseguró que “no tenía absolutamente ninguna idea de que la persona en cuestión fuera una espía”, versión que respaldó ante la prensa. El gobierno de China rechazó de forma categórica las acusaciones y las calificó de calumnias carentes de sustento.
FBI, Congreso y accionistas presionan a Nvidia por el escándalo de espionaje de Jensen Huang
Para responder al impacto institucional, la junta corporativa contrató al bufete legal Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz para liderar una auditoría independiente sobre la posible exposición de secretos de inteligencia artificial y seguridad nacional, según informó la BBC. La indagatoria quedó a cargo de Joon Kim, exfiscal federal para el Distrito Sur de Nueva York y especialista en fraude financiero y seguridad corporativa.
Aunque el directorio afirmó que “no tiene motivos para creer” que existan filtraciones de secretos industriales o de defensa, el frente judicial se amplió con una demanda colectiva de inversores presentada en California.
Según reveló Bloomberg, el asesor legal de Nvidia, Tim Teter, contactó al subsecretario del Departamento de Comercio, Jeffrey Kessler, para preguntar por la detención temporal de Alice Huang en Singapur. Los investigadores del Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) que recibieron esa comunicación la rechazaron y la elevaron internamente; Kessler les indicó que continuaran manejando el caso estrictamente conforme a las normas oficiales.
Poco después, el expediente fue transferido al Departamento de Justicia ante el temor de que la pesquisa pudiera verse comprometida. Tres presidentes de comités de la Cámara de Representantes citaron además al directivo a una audiencia reservada programada para el 18 de noviembre, bajo apercibimiento de emitir una orden vinculante si el ejecutivo elude la comparecencia, informó ABC News.
Nvidia sin plan de sucesión: por qué la dependencia de Jensen Huang preocupa a Estados Unidos
El conflicto expone la fragilidad de un modelo empresarial que depende en exceso de una sola persona. Jensen Huang comanda la firma sin un plan de sucesión formal, supervisa directamente a más de 60 subordinados y colocó a miembros de su familia en áreas técnicas clave, según señaló The New York Times. A la par, el directivo abogó públicamente por vender procesadores intermedios a Asia, bajo el argumento de que el aislamiento total fomentaría el auge de competidores locales como Huawei.
El desenlace de este expediente judicial determinará si Estados Unidos endurece de forma definitiva las barreras aduaneras sobre la tecnología de inteligencia artificial o si refuerza la tutela estatal sobre las cúpulas corporativas que custodian la infraestructura crítica del mundo occidental.

articles.title: Além de programação: Claude ganha ferramentas para reuniões, planilhas e ideias • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Além de programação: Claude ganha ferramentas para reuniões, planilhas e ideias
As novidades são o Claude Meetings, o Claude Sheets e o Claude Whiteboards, que estão em fase beta.
Normalmente, o nome Claude nos remete a ferramentas de IA voltadas a desenvolvimento de software. Mas a Anthropic quer ir além e, para isso, anunciou três soluções direcionadas a produtividade e escritório: o Claude Meetings (reuniões), o Claude Sheets (planilhas) e o Claude Whiteboards (organização de ideias).
Todas as novidades são baseadas em inteligência artificial, é claro. Mas, como a Anthropic explica, cada uma segue uma estrutura específica. Em resumo: enquanto o contexto do Claude Code está em código-fonte, nas novas ferramentas, o contexto está distribuído entre e-mails, documentos, planilhas, serviços de armazenamento e afins.
Para tanto, a Anthropic acessa essas bases por meio do Model Context Protocol (MCP). Basicamente, trata-se de um padrão aberto, criado pela própria Anthropic, que conecta serviços de IA a aplicativos, serviços e fontes de informação externas.
Esta não é uma solução que concorre diretamente com o Zoom ou o Google Meet, por exemplo. O Claude Meetings, na verdade, permite que o Claude AI participe de reuniões no Google Meet (por enquanto, a única plataforma disponível) para registrar atas, produzir notas, organizar as informações tratadas na reunião, esclarecer dúvidas, entre outras ações.
O Claude Sheets segue o mesmo princípio, isto é, não concorre diretamente com o Excel ou o Google Planilhas, por exemplo. A sua proposta é a de permitir que equipes usem o Claude para criar e organizar planilhas, editar fórmulas, facilitar o trabalho com múltiplas tabelas e assim por diante.
O Claude Whiteboards funciona como uma espécie de quadro branco para organização de ideias, estruturação de projetos e criação de planejamentos. Com a ajuda do Claude AI, os usuários podem transformar informações em diagramas, fluxos e linhas do tempo, por exemplo. É algo que remete a plataformas como Miro e Lucid.
Com exceção do Meetings, as novas ferramentas fazem parte dos chamados Artifacts (Artefatos), isto é, consistem em recursos interativos e complementares do ecossistema do Claude. Todas estão em fase beta, porém. A disponibilidade atual segue este esquema:
Apesar de ainda estarem em fase beta, o trio de ferramentas se junta a Artifacts de escritório já existentes, como Claude Docs, Claude Slides, Claude Design e Claude Motion.
Vale destacar também que, no mesmo anúncio, a Anthropic revelou a liberação do Claude Data (anteriormente, Claude Dashboards) em todos os planos pagos. Esta é uma ferramenta de análise e visualização de dados apoiada em — adivinhe — inteligência artificial.

articles.title: Trump admin loses fight to spy on random journalists’ LinkedIn DMs
articles.text:
The Trump administration’s fight to stop suspected leaks of top-secret military information on LinkedIn can’t sweep in “a vast number of confidential sources” of random journalists “who have no conceivable relationship” to the Department of Justice’s investigation, an appeals court ruled Tuesday.
The order came after the DOJ asked LinkedIn to turn over 18 months of communications from targeted journalists who collectively published more than 1,000 articles on many different topics over that time period. The request was not limited to journalists involved in a controversial report from a news outlet that Trump said exposed confidential military information in a foreign country. (The outlet is not being named to protect national security secrets.) Instead, the DOJ cast a wide net, requesting extensive LinkedIn data on journalists who had any possible link to the journalists around the time the report was drafted.
The majority of journalists have LinkedIn accounts and publish their contact information to encourage sources to connect on the platform, LinkedIn argued. So allowing that government overreach went beyond harming targeted journalists and threatened to undermine a critical platform where journalists frequently connect with confidential sources, judges ruled. Even more concerning, the Trump administration secured a secrecy order barring LinkedIn from telling anyone about the sweeping request for a year. That left journalists unaware for far too long that their First Amendment rights had been compromised, judges ruled.
Judge: Security and free speech can coexist
Penning the unanimous opinion from a three-judge panel, Ronald Reagan-nominated judge J. Harvie Wilkinson III rejected LinkedIn’s request to quash the order entirely and ordered the US district court to substantially narrow the order to avoid posing a grave threat to press freedoms.

articles.title: Jensen Huang accused of having another affair — with an Nvidia exec | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is already under investigation after having admitted to having an affair with a woman accused of being a Chinese spy. Now the New York Times is reporting that Huang is also suspected of having another extramarital affair, with a direct report of his at the company — Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare. Powell, like Huang, is married, the outlet says.
The Times says it was told of the alleged affair by five employees at the company. The sources said that Huang and Powell were captured on video “being affectionate at a San Jose, Calif., hotel” during a conference earlier this year.
Like many companies, Nvidia has rules discouraging superiors from having relationships with employees in subordinate roles, the Times notes. TechCrunch reached out to Nvidia for comment.
The company’s board has initiated an investigation into Huang’s publicly admitted affair. Additionally, two House Republicans said Wednesday that Congress is gearing up to subpoena Huang over the spy allegations if he doesn’t voluntarily respond to their summons to a closed-door briefing. Late Wednesday, after the reports of the second affair were published, the Wall Street Journal reported that the Nvidia board was preparing to oust Huang, who co-founded the company in 1993.

articles.title: Anthropic offre un reset gratuit des limites de Claude à ses abonnés, voici comment en profiter
articles.text:
Anthropic veut se faire pardonner pour les récents « désagréments ». L’entreprise américaine offre ainsi une réinitialisation des limites d’utilisation à ses abonnés payants. Attention, cette opération n’est valable que pendant une durée limitée. Voici comment en profiter.
Un reset pour toutes les limites des abonnements payants
Via son compte X ClaudeDevs, Anthropic a annoncé une réinitialisation complète et gratuite des limites d’utilisation pour les abonnés Pro, Max, Ultra et Team. Ce reset couvre tous les modèles et toutes les limites. À noter que les utilisateurs du forfait gratuit ne peuvent pas bénéficier de cette offre. Pour les abonnés payants, ce reset est activable jusqu’au 10 décembre 2026 à 23 h (heure de Paris).
Anthropic explique avoir décidé d’offrir ce reset des comptes payants pour deux raisons. Premièrement, l’entreprise américaine confie avoir corrigé récemment quelques « petits problèmes qui consommaient plus de limites que prévu », sans préciser lesquels. Deuxièmement, Anthropic reconnaît en quelque sorte que le reset offert le 9 novembre, à l’occasion du lancement de Claude Fable 5.2, n’a pas réellement profité aux abonnés qui avaient déjà atteint leurs limites hebdomadaires. Pour rappel, cette première réinitialisation ne restaurait que le quota hebdomadaire consommé sur les modèles Fable, en plus de recharger le quota de la session de cinq heures. L’entreprise de Dario Amodei veut donc maintenant se faire pardonner, même si ces problèmes n’ont « pas affecté tout le monde ».
Comment activer ce reset de Claude ?
Pour activer la réinitialisation de votre compte Pro, Max, Ultra ou Team, il suffit de vous rendre dans les paramètres, puis de cliquer sur « Utilisation ». Autre possibilité : accéder directement à l’adresse suivante : http://clau.de/reset.
Les personnes concernées peuvent réinitialiser leur compte jusqu’au 10 décembre. Bien entendu, le mieux à faire est de réinitialiser son compte à un moment où les limites d’utilisation sont atteintes. Pour rappel, Claude dispose de deux types de limites d’utilisation : un premier quota renouvelé toutes les cinq heures et un second, hebdomadaire, qui se réinitialise chaque semaine à une date et une heure définies pour chaque compte.
