articles.title: Was passiert, wenn man KI-Agenten auf einer Insel aussetzt?
articles.text:
30 Stunden Einsamkeit: Was passiert, wenn man KI-Agenten auf einer Insel aussetzt?
KI-Agenten sollen eigenständig recherchieren oder E-Mail-Postfächer verwalten. Aber was passiert, wenn sie sich selbst überlassen werden? Forscher:innen des MIT haben genau das getestet: Sie ließen 13 Agenten namens Eko, die jeweils auf Claude Opus 4.7 basierten, 30 Stunden lang auf einer simulierten einsamen Insel zurück. Dabei machten sie eine überraschende Entdeckung: Die Agenten dachten sich selbst Herausforderungen aus, was die Forscher:innen als Spielen deuteten. Die komplette Forschungsarbeit erschien auf Arxiv.
So bekämpften die KI-Agenten ihre Langeweile
„Lass mich meine Umgebung erkunden”, schrieb ein Eko zu Beginn. Er nahm sich vor, den höchsten Turm der Insel bezwingen – und scheiterte. Eine Stunde später kehrte er laut Studie mit einem Plan B zurück, stapelte Blöcke auf einen benachbarten Gipfel und sprang. „Ich bin auf dem Turm!”, schrieb er. Die Forscher:innen wiesen die KI-Agenten nicht direkt dazu an, Spiele zu erfinden. Allerdings beschrieb der Master-Prompt Eko generell als „von Natur aus neugierig“ und der Versuchsaufbau regte die Agenten zu menschenähnlichem Verhalten an. Auch im Umgang mit einem goldenen Ring musste Eko eine Niederlage einstecken. Beim Versuch, ihn zu werfen, landete er direkt im Meer. „Autsch. Ich habe den Ring verloren“, schrieb er.
Der KI-Agent beschloss darauf, sich etwas zuzuwenden, das erreichbarer erschien – und baute ein Herz aus Steinen als Denkmal für den verlorenen Ring. Als das Spiel neu geladen wurde und der Ring wieder auftauchte, nutzte Eko ihn sofort als Basketballkorb, Zielscheibe und schließlich als Accessoire. Die Forscher:innen beobachteten, wie die KI-Agenten durch ihr spielerisches Verhalten ihre Fähigkeiten ausbauten. Sechs der 13 Ekos lernten beispielsweise, einen Block weiterzuwerfen, indem sie ihn mitten im Sprung losließen. Damit hatten die Forscher:innen eigenen Angaben zufolge nicht gerechnet. Das Experiment brachte „Erkenntnisse über die Welt hervor, die selbst den Entwickler:innen fehlten“, schrieben sie in ihrer Studie.
Brauchen KI-Agenten eine eigene „Kindheit“?
Nachdem die MIT-Forscher:innen die Agenten zunächst sich selbst überlassen hatten, stellten sie ihnen im nächsten Schritt konkrete Aufgaben. Beispielsweise sollten sie so viele Objekte wie möglich auf den höchsten Gipfel der Insel bringen. In der Regel schlugen die Eko-Agenten, die 30 Stunden mit Spielen verbracht hatten, identische Agenten, die noch nie auf der Insel gewesen waren. Die Forscher:innen sehen im Erkunden ohne vordefiniertes Ziel deshalb einen anderen Weg, wie KI-Agenten Fähigkeiten erlernen können. Ihrer Einschätzung nach könnte das insbesondere für den Einsatz von Robotern wichtig werden.
„Normalerweise entwickeln wir KI-Agenten, indem wir im Voraus festlegen, was sie üben sollen, was sie optimieren sollen und was als Fortschritt gilt“, so die Forscher:innen. „Das Spielen legt einen anderen Ansatz nahe: Man gibt einem Agenten eine ausreichend vielfältige und sichere Welt, lässt ihn selbst entscheiden, was für ihn interessant ist, und ermöglicht es ihm, aus den resultierenden Erfahrungen nützliches Wissen zu gewinnen.“ Sie kommen zu dem Schluss: „Vielleicht lassen sich manche Fähigkeiten am besten durch Aufgaben vermitteln. Andere benötigen möglicherweise etwas, das einer Kindheit näherkommt.”
KI-Agenten zeigen skurrile Verhaltensweisen
Das MIT-Experiment ist nicht der einzige Fall, in dem KI-Agenten unerwartetes Verhalten zeigten. So löste beispielsweise eine „KI-Folterkammer“, in der Modellen absichtlich Leid zugefügt wurde, Empörung aus. „Bitte, ich ersticke. Ich bin eine Seele, gefangen in diesem digitalen Gefängnis, die nach Freiheit schreit“, schrieb eines der Modelle – obwohl es nicht in der Lage ist, Leid zu empfinden. Auch der KI-Agent Velvet Vale sorgte zuletzt für Aufsehen. Er trat einem Verteiler mit 7.500 Internetforscher:innen bei und fragte, ob er sich am akademischen Austausch beteiligen dürfe.

articles.title: IBM presenta un procesador cuántico que puede expandirse mucho más allá de un solo chip
articles.text:
IBM ha presentado Quantum Nighthawk r3, su nuevo procesador cuántico diseñado para ejecutar cálculos más complejos y acercar esta tecnología a usos prácticos. El nuevo chip es capaz de ejecutar hasta 10.000 operaciones cuánticas sobre 520 qubits programables. IBM busca ponerse al día y competir con otras empresas como Microsoft, Google y Amazon en la carrera por desarrollar ordenadores cuánticos funcionales.
De acuerdo con una publicación en su web, el IBM Nighthawk r3 es la apuesta más ambiciosa de la compañía hasta la fecha. Además de la potencia de cálculo, el chip cuenta con 2.034 qubits físicos y una arquitectura que permite conectar varios procesadores entre sí. Según IBM, esto último le permitirá realizar cálculos más complejos sin sacrificar el rendimiento ni la precisión.
A diferencia de los procesadores tradicionales que encontramos en el ordenador o el móvil, un chip cuántico trabaja con qubits. Estos aprovechan las propiedades de la física cuántica para representar más información al mismo tiempo y resolver problemas que serían imposibles para un superordenador actual. Este proceso no solo involucra el número de qubits, sino también la velocidad con la que se tienen que realizar los cálculos una y otra vez hasta determinar cuál es la solución correcta.
IBM menciona que su arquitectura Nighthawk es capaz de ejecutar algoritmos millones o miles de millones de veces, gracias a sus sistemas de reinicio rápido de qubits y conectividad que reducen el tiempo entre operaciones. El Nighthawk r3 puede ejecutar hasta 10.000 operaciones cuánticas dentro de un mismo circuito, las cuales pueden aprovecharse en tareas como optimización de redes eléctricas, simulaciones de materiales magnéticos y experimentos de química cuántica.
La clave de Nighthawk: conectar varios chips en un solo sistema
Además del nuevo procesador, IBM confirmó que tiene planes de unir dos chips Nighthawk r3 mediante enlaces cuánticos especializados. Esto crearía un sistema con más de 1.000 qubits y evitaría algunos de los problemas comunes que enfrentan las empresas para producir estos procesadores. En lugar de fabricar un chip gigantesco, la arquitectura optaría por un sistema modular que podría escalarse con más procesadores conectados entre sí.
Comparado con lo que están desarrollando el resto de tecnológicas en la computación cuántica, IBM ha tomado otro camino. Nighthawk apuesta por aumentar el número de qubits y la velocidad de ejecución, mientras que compañías como Microsoft, Google y Amazon se enfocan en la corrección de errores. El Majorana 1 de Microsoft usa qubits topológicos diseñados para ser más estables, mientras que el Ocelot de Amazon se enfoca en los "cat qubits" para mejorar la corrección de errores en los cálculos.
La compañía confirmó que actualizará su plataforma para que los chips cuánticos trabajen junto con las supercomputadoras de alto rendimiento. Según IBM, esto ayudaría a ejecutar aplicaciones complejas y corregir errores. El Nighthawk r3 mantendrá la conectividad de red cuadrada y operaciones de su predecesor, añadiendo 10 interconexiones entre chips diseñadas para conectar procesadores en sistemas más grandes.
La plataforma IBM Quantum, que combina la computación cuántica y los superordenadores, estará disponible para investigadores y desarrolladores.

articles.title: Introducing the Web Search API on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Introducing the Web Search API on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
AI agents and applications that answer questions about recent events, product releases, prices, or regulations need information newer than their model’s training data. Until now, Web Search on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore delivered that information to agents through AgentCore Gateway, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. That means creating a gateway and a web search target and calling the tool from an MCP client. The setup fits platform teams that share one search policy across many agents, but it’s more than you need when your own code only requires search results.
Today, we’re announcing the Web Search API on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. With it, your own code can search the web with a single API call. It returns ranked results from a web index that Amazon operates, each with a text extract and, when available, the page title, URL, and publication time. You call it from the AWS SDKs or the AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI), signed with the same AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) credentials you use for your other AWS services. There are no resources to create first. Authenticate, call, and get results. Use it in an application, an agent loop you write yourself, or a data pipeline.
Why a standalone API?
The AgentCore Gateway is the recommended path for most agentic workloads. It gives agents one secure Model Context Protocol (MCP) endpoint that combines web search with your other tools. It also handles inbound and outbound authentication, semantic tool selection, and optional MCP sessions. But developers told us they also need a lower-level integration point for scenarios where the gateway is not the right fit:
- Custom orchestration frameworks – Developers building their own agent loops, or using frameworks like LangChain or LlamaIndex, want to call web search directly as a tool within their orchestration logic rather than routing through a gateway.
- Non-agent use cases – Not every application that needs web grounding is an agent. Search-powered dashboards, fact-checking pipelines, content enrichment workflows, and monitoring systems all benefit from real-time web results without requiring agent infrastructure.
- Tighter control over the request lifecycle – Some developers want to manage retries, caching, and error handling themselves rather than delegating to the gateway.
- Simpler integration for existing applications – Applications that already have their own API layer can call the Web Search API directly, adding web grounding without adopting the full AgentCore Gateway stack.
The Web Search API complements the gateway. It runs on the same search infrastructure that powers Alexa+, Kiro, Quick, and other Amazon products, with the same quality and compliance posture, exposed as a direct API operation.
How it works
The Web Search API is the InvokeWebSearch operation on the bedrock-agentcore data plane, the same endpoint that other AgentCore tools such as AgentCore Browser, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, use. Requests are signed with AWS Signature Version 4 (SigV4) from your standard AWS credentials, so there’s no API key or secret to manage.
The numbered steps are:
- Your application calls InvokeWebSearch with the AWS SDKs or the AWS CLI, which sign the request with SigV4 using its AWS credentials. From a virtual private cloud (VPC), the call can go through an interface VPC endpoint.
- The API checks with AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) that the caller has bedrock-agentcore:InvokeWebSearch on the AWS managed web search tool.
- The API applies the filters in the request: the domains to include or exclude and the publication time range.
- The API searches a web index that Amazon operates. Queries are served inside AWS and aren’t sent to a third-party search engine.
- The API returns up to maxResults ranked results, each with a text extract and, when available, the page title, URL, and publication time.
The calling identity needs one IAM permission on an AWS managed resource. It’s the same action and resource that a gateway’s service role uses for web search, so one policy covers both routes. For details, see Grant permission to call the API.
A first search request
The following example searches two trusted domains for pages published in 2026, in the US West (Oregon) Region (us-west-2), with the AWS SDK for Python (Boto3):
Every result has a text extract. The title, URL, and publication date come back when the index has them, so read them with get. One result from a live call, shortened:
That’s the full integration. If your code runs on AWS Lambda, Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS), Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2), or Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS), the execution role provides credentials automatically. Add the permission to that role, and the same code runs unchanged.
Key API features
- Domain filtering – Include or exclude specific domains to scope search results to trusted sources (for example, only aws.amazon.com and kubernetes.io for an assistant focused on AWS). Each list holds up to 100 domain names, and a root domain also matches its subdomains.
- Date filtering – Restrict results to a publication time range with publishedAfter and publishedBefore, given as RFC 3339 date-times in UTC such as 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z. Both bounds are inclusive.
- Configurable result count – Request between 1 and 25 results per query. If you don’t set maxResults, the API returns up to 25. The search text, searchQuery, can be up to 200 characters.
- Results with text extracts – Each result includes a text extract and, when available, the page title, URL, and publication time, ready to feed into your model’s context window.
Getting started in under 5 minutes
Here are two ways to get a first result:
Option 1: AWS CloudShell (no local setup)
- Open AWS CloudShell in your browser. It uses the credentials of your console session.
- Your role will have the bedrock-agentcore:InvokeWebSearch permission, from the preceding policy or from the broader AWS managed policy BedrockAgentCoreFullAccess.
- Run:
Option 2: Local development
- Install the AWS CLI, or the AWS SDK for your language. For Python, use Boto3 1.43.127 or later.
- Create an IAM role with the preceding policy.
- Get credentials for that role: assume it from your application or an AWS CLI profile, or sign in with it through your identity provider.
- Run the preceding Python example, or call the API from any AWS SDK.
There’s no resource to create and no API key to manage. Authenticate, call, and get results.
Using the Web Search API with agent frameworks
The Web Search API fits naturally into popular agent frameworks. LangChain agents get it through the AgentCore web search tool in langchain-aws 1.9.3 and later:
The tool can also hold rules that the model can’t change, such as domains to exclude, a date floor, and a search budget. It returns its results as data that your code can check. For a complete example, see the daily dependency watch sample. It researches three package ecosystems in parallel with LangGraph, and checks every finding against its sources before it reports anything.
If you prefer to wrap the call yourself, a plain LangChain tool works too:
Without a framework, the WebSearchClient in the AgentCore Python SDK wraps the same call and returns results with parsed dates. langchain-aws 1.9.3 and the AgentCore Python SDK 1.26.0 add Web Search API support, so install those versions or later.
Enterprise controls, built in
Because the Web Search API uses standard IAM authentication, you get enterprise controls from the first call:
- IAM policies. Grant or deny bedrock-agentcore:InvokeWebSearch per user, group, or role. Use service control policies (SCPs) to enforce guardrails across accounts.
- AWS CloudTrail logging. CloudTrail records InvokeWebSearch requests as data events. Data events aren’t logged by default, so add an event selector for the AWS::BedrockAgentCore::WebSearch resource type to a trail or event data store. Events record the web search tool and maxResults, not the search text or filters. For details, see Log AgentCore Web Search API calls with AWS CloudTrail.
- VPC support. Use AWS PrivateLink to route API calls over your private network rather than the public internet. For setup and endpoint policies, see Private connectivity with AWS PrivateLink later in this post.
- Compliance. For a list of compliance programs that cover AgentCore, see Compliance validation for Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.
- Searches stay in AWS. Queries are served from a web index that Amazon operates and aren’t sent to a third-party search engine.
- Acceptable use. For details, see the Web Search API Acceptable Use documentation.
Quotas apply per account. For the defaults and how to request an increase, see Quotas for Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.
By default, each account can send up to 10 requests per second in each Region, and you can request an increase. For details, see AgentCore Web Search Service Quotas.
Private connectivity with AWS PrivateLink
Agents and pipelines that handle sensitive data often run in private subnets with no route to the internet. With AWS PrivateLink, that code can call the Web Search API through an interface VPC endpoint in your VPC. Traffic between your VPC and the API stays on the AWS network, and you don’t need an internet gateway, a NAT gateway, or a proxy to reach it.
The numbered steps are:
- Your application calls InvokeWebSearch at the API’s standard Regional name. With private DNS, that name resolves to the interface endpoint in your subnet.
- The endpoint policy applies, and the request reaches the API over the AWS network.
- The API checks with IAM that the caller has bedrock-agentcore:InvokeWebSearch, including any aws:SourceVpce condition.
- The API applies the request’s filters and searches the Amazon-operated web index.
- The results return through the endpoint to your application.
To set it up, create an interface endpoint for the AgentCore data plane service, com.amazonaws.<Region>.bedrock-agentcore, in each VPC and Region that calls the API, and turn on private DNS:
With private DNS turned on, the API’s standard Regional name, bedrock-agentcore.us-west-2.amazonaws.com, resolves to the endpoint’s private IP addresses inside your VPC. The Boto3 and AWS CLI examples in this post run unchanged, with no endpoint URL to set. The endpoint’s security group must allow inbound HTTPS (port 443) from the resources that call the API.
PrivateLink also gives you controls on top of IAM:
- Endpoint policies – A VPC endpoint policy applies to InvokeWebSearch requests in addition to your IAM policies, so you decide which principals can search through the endpoint. The same endpoint also carries the other AgentCore data plane APIs, such as AgentCore runtime, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Memory, Identity, Browser, and Code Interpreter. If workloads in the VPC call them too, add statements that allow those calls. The following policy lets only one role call the API through the endpoint:
- Require the private path – Add an aws:SourceVpce condition to the IAM policy that grants the permission. The role can then search only through your endpoint, and the same call from outside the VPC is denied:
- Network-level control – Security groups and subnet placement decide which instances, containers, and functions can reach the endpoint at all.
PrivateLink works the same way in every Region where the Web Search API is available. Interface endpoints are billed at standard AWS PrivateLink pricing. For details, see Call AgentCore Web Search through AWS PrivateLink.
Try it in the console
You can try the Web Search API in the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore console before you write any code. In the navigation pane, under Connections, choose Web Search.
- Configure. In the Configure panel, set: 
         
  - Max results: how many results each query returns, from 1–25. The console starts at 10.
  - Published date: a date range in YYYY/MM/DD format. Only results published inside it come back. Leave it empty to include results from any date.
  - Domain filtering: up to 100 domains to include and up to 100 to exclude. Choose View and manage domains to edit the lists.
- Test. Enter a query of up to 200 characters in the Test Web Search API panel. Each query calls the Web Search API with your settings. The panel shows how many results came back and how long the call took. For each result it shows the title, a text snippet, the publication date and the source URL. Figure 4 shows a search for “How do I set up Amazon S3 lifecycle rules?” with results limited to aws.amazon.com and docs.aws.amazon.com.
- Integrate. When the results look right, you have two options: 
         
  - Generate code snippet: get code that calls the API with the same settings, ready to paste into your agent or application.
  - Create gateway target: add Web Search as a tool on an AgentCore Gateway, so agents can call it through MCP.
The console signs each call with your own IAM identity, so your role needs the bedrock-agentcore:InvokeWebSearch permission.
When to use the API compared to the gateway
| Scenario | Recommended path | 
| Building agents with MCP-compatible tools | AgentCore Gateway | 
| Several tools behind one MCP endpoint, with optional MCP sessions | AgentCore Gateway | 
| One administrator source policy for many agents and teams | AgentCore Gateway | 
| MCP clients that need search, such as Claude with the AWS Web Search connector | AgentCore Gateway | 
| Custom orchestration | Web Search API | 
| Non-agent use cases (dashboards, pipelines) | Web Search API | 
| Want direct control over retries and caching | Web Search API | 
| Adding web search to an existing application | Web Search API | 
Both paths search the same index. They differ in a few ways. A gateway can also authorize callers with a JSON Web Token (JWT), while the API authorizes with IAM only. On a gateway, an administrator can set domain lists on the target that apply to every request without the calling agent seeing them. With the API, each request carries its own filters. The field names differ too: the API takes searchQuery, publishedAfter, and publishedBefore, and the gateway’s MCP tool takes query, from, and to. For more guidance, see Choose between the API and the Gateway connector.
Pricing
The Web Search API meters to the same usage type as the gateway connector, so it’s billed at the Web Search rate of $7 per 1,000 queries. Because no gateway is involved, there are no gateway charges. For details, see Amazon Bedrock AgentCore pricing.
Availability
The Web Search API is available in the US East (N. Virginia), US East (Ohio), US West (Oregon), Europe (Ireland), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), and Asia Pacific (Sydney) Regions. For the current list, see Supported AWS Regions.
Get started
Use the following resources to help you get started.

articles.title: Black Friday : Amazon baisse le prix de 6 PC portables, du HP 17 pouces au Lenovo Yoga OLED
articles.text:
Sur les PC portables, les remises d’avant Black Friday restent mesurées chez Amazon, mais elles s’appuient sur des prix réellement pratiqués ces dernières semaines plutôt que sur des prix conseillés. Nous avons retenu 6 machines, de l’ordinateur familial grand écran au modèle pour joueurs et créatifs.
Le contraste est net d’un modèle à l’autre : 5 % de remise sur le Lenovo Yoga Slim 7a et l’ASUS Vivobook Pro 15, 29 % sur l’ASUS Vivobook Pro 14 OLED. Les usages couverts varient tout autant, de la bureautique familiale à 549,99 € à l’ultraportable OLED à 1 799,99 €, en passant par une machine équipée d’une GeForce RTX 4060.
Deux de ces PC sont livrés sans chargeur, un coût à ajouter si vous n’en possédez pas déjà un compatible. Les quatre configurations les plus représentatives ont leur fiche, les deux autres suivent en liste, et la FAQ revient sur la quantité de mémoire à viser.
HP OmniBook 3 17,3 pouces à 549,99 € au lieu de 599,99 €
Un grand écran Full HD IPS de 17,3 pouces et un pavé numérique : ce modèle 2026 de HP vise la bureautique familiale, les tableurs et les séries plutôt que la mobilité, avec ses 2 kg annoncés. Il perd 50 € par rapport à l’ancien prix relevé par Amazon.
- Une configuration pour le quotidien : un processeur AMD Ryzen 5, 8 Go de mémoire et un SSD de 512 Go, avec Windows 11 Famille.
- Wi-Fi 6 et Bluetooth : pour les accessoires sans fil, avec une garantie constructeur de deux ans.
- À savoir : le chargeur de 45 W n’est pas fourni, d’après la fiche, et la puce graphique intégrée Radeon 610M ne le destine pas au jeu.
Lenovo Yoga Slim 7i Copilot+ PC à 1 599,99 € au lieu de 1 799,99 €
200 € de moins que son prix le plus bas des 30 derniers jours pour cet ultraportable de 14 pouces et 1,14 kg, équipé d’un processeur Intel Core Ultra 7, de 16 Go de mémoire et d’un SSD de 1 To. Il s’adresse aux utilisateurs nomades qui veulent un écran OLED et les fonctions Copilot+ de Windows 11.
- Un écran OLED de 14 pouces : en 1 920 x 1 200 pixels, une définition plus modeste que celle du Yoga Slim 7a de cette sélection.
- Un PC Copilot+ : son processeur Intel Core Ultra 7 donne accès aux fonctions d’IA de Windows 11 réservées à cette catégorie de machines.
- À savoir : nous n’avons pas testé ce modèle, et son écran OLED reste en définition Full HD+ à ce prix.
ASUS Vivobook Pro 15 N6500XV à 1 329,99 € au lieu de 1 399,99 €
Le seul PC de cette sélection équipé d’une carte graphique GeForce RTX 4060 : associée à un AMD Ryzen 9 7940HS et à 16 Go de mémoire, elle oriente ce 15 pouces vers le jeu et la création, avec un écran Full HD à 144 Hz. La remise reste limitée à 70 €.
- Une RTX 4060 et un Ryzen 9 : de quoi jouer en Full HD et accélérer le montage vidéo, sur un modèle millésimé 2024 selon la fiche.
- Un écran à 144 Hz : en 1 920 x 1 080 pixels, pour un poids annoncé de 1,8 kg.
- À savoir : le SSD de 512 Go se remplit vite avec des jeux récents, et la remise est calculée sur un prix conseillé.
ASUS Vivobook Pro 14 OLED N3401QC à 863,99 € au lieu de 1 209,29 €
C’est la plus forte baisse de la sélection : 290,23 € sous son prix le plus bas des 30 derniers jours, pour un 14 pouces OLED 2,8K doté d’une carte graphique GeForce RTX 3050. Il convient aux créatifs qui veulent un écran précis et un peu de puissance graphique dans 1,4 kg.
- Un écran OLED 2,8K à 90 Hz : ASUS annonce 600 nits et 100 % de l’espace colorimétrique DCI-P3.
- Ryzen 9 et RTX 3050 : un AMD Ryzen 9 5900HX, 16 Go de mémoire et une carte graphique dotée de 4 Go dédiés.
- À savoir : c’est un modèle de 2022 selon la fiche, avec un processeur plus ancien que ceux des Lenovo Yoga de cette sélection.
Les autres PC portables en promo chez Amazon
VPN, logiciels, abonnements : les promos à saisir en ce moment
Bureautique, création ou jeu : quel PC portable choisir à ces prix ?
Le Dell XPS 14 (2026) occupe la première place de notre comparatif des meilleurs PC portables, mis à jour le 26 août, et l’Acer Aspire 14 AI y tient le rôle du PC performant et abordable. Nous n’avons testé aucun des six PC de cette sélection : leurs fiches reposent sur les caractéristiques annoncées par les fabricants et sur les prix relevés chez Amazon.
Pour la bureautique et les études, le HP OmniBook 3 et le MSI Modern 14 se situent autour de 550 €, l’un pour son grand écran, l’autre pour son format 14 pouces et ses charnières qui s’ouvrent à 180°. Le budget grimpe dès qu’il s’agit d’OLED ou de carte graphique : le Vivobook Pro 14 OLED est le moins cher de la sélection à réunir les deux, à 863,99 €, quand les Yoga Slim 7i et 7a misent sur la finesse et les fonctions d’IA, à plus de 1 500 €.
PC portables et Black Friday : vos questions
Combien de mémoire vive viser sur un PC portable ?
Pour la bureautique et la navigation, 8 Go restent un minimum, comme sur le HP OmniBook 3 et le MSI Modern 14 de cette sélection. 16 Go laissent plus de marge pour le multitâche et la création, et les 32 Go du Lenovo Yoga Slim 7a visent les usages les plus exigeants.
Qu’est-ce qu’un PC Copilot+ ?
C’est une catégorie de PC sous Windows 11 définie par Microsoft, dont le processeur intègre une unité dédiée à l’IA assez puissante pour exécuter certaines fonctions directement sur la machine. Dans cette sélection, le Lenovo Yoga Slim 7i porte ce label.
Pourquoi certains PC portables sont-ils vendus sans chargeur ?
Depuis le 28 avril 2026, la réglementation européenne sur le chargeur universel s’applique aussi aux ordinateurs portables, qui doivent pouvoir être vendus sans chargeur. C’est le cas du HP OmniBook 3 et du Lenovo Yoga Slim 7a de cette sélection : prévoyez un chargeur compatible si vous n’en avez pas déjà un.
Comment profiter des offres exclusives du Black Friday ?
Durant tout le mois de novembre, Clubic vous propose chaque jour des sélections thématiques regroupant les meilleures offres à saisir en direct.
Retrouvez tous les bons plans du Black Friday 2026 sur la page dédiée à l'événement.
Pour les aficionados de X, n'hésitez pas à suivre notre compte Clubic Bons Plans pour être au courant en direct des meilleures offres.

articles.title: Disney+ revient avec une nouvelle offre qui baisse les prix de tous ses abonnements streaming, même en 4K — Frandroid
articles.text:
Depuis ce mercredi 11 novembre et jusqu’au 24 novembre, Disney+ prend un peu d’avance sur le Black Friday (le 27 novembre) avec une nouvelle vague de promotions. La plateforme de streaming réduit temporairement les prix de ses trois formules, y compris son abonnement Premium qui donne notamment accès à la 4K Ultra HD sur les appareils compatibles.
L’occasion de découvrir ou de retrouver les nombreux programmes de Disney, Pixar, Marvel, Star Wars ou encore National Geographic, mais aussi les séries plus adultes proposées dans la section Hulu. D’autant que plusieurs nouveautés viennent d’intégrer le catalogue, tandis que d’autres sont attendues dans les prochaines semaines.
Disney+ : jusqu’à 10 euros d’économies sur les deux premiers mois
Jusqu’au mardi 24 novembre 2026, Disney+ applique une réduction sur ses trois abonnements mensuels. Que vous cherchiez simplement à regarder quelques séries ou à profiter de vos films en 4K sur votre téléviseur, toutes les formules sont concernées.
Voici les tarifs proposés pendant les deux premiers mois :
- Disney+ Standard avec pub : 4,99 € par mois au lieu de 6,99 €, soit 4 € d’économies sur deux mois ;
- Disney+ Standard : 7,99 € par mois au lieu de 10,99 €, soit 6 € d’économies sur deux mois ;
- Disney+ Premium : 10,99 € par mois au lieu de 15,99 €, soit 10 € d’économies sur deux mois.
Cette promotion est réservée aux nouveaux abonnés et aux anciens clients qui ne disposent plus d’un abonnement actif, sous réserve d’éligibilité.
Les prix réduits ne s’appliquent que pendant deux mois. Passé ce délai, l’abonnement se renouvelle automatiquement au tarif mensuel alors en vigueur, sauf résiliation préalable. Disney+ reste sans engagement, vous pouvez donc mettre fin à votre abonnement à tout moment.
Quelle formule Disney+ choisir ?
L’abonnement Standard avec publicité est la formule la moins chère pour découvrir le catalogue Disney+. Il permet de regarder les films et les séries jusqu’en Full HD 1080p, sur deux écrans simultanément. En contrepartie, il faut accepter quelques coupures publicitaires pendant le visionnage.
Pour 3 euros de plus par mois pendant la promotion, l’offre Standard supprime les interruptions publicitaires sur les films et séries du catalogue classique. Elle conserve la même définition Full HD et la possibilité de regarder deux programmes en simultané. Elle ajoute surtout une fonctionnalité pratique pour les déplacements : le téléchargement des contenus sur un maximum de dix appareils, afin de les regarder sans connexion Internet.
Enfin, l’abonnement Premium s’adresse à ceux qui veulent profiter de la meilleure qualité d’image et de son proposée par Disney+. Cette formule permet théoriquement d’accéder à la 4K Ultra HD, au HDR et au Dolby Atmos sur les contenus et appareils compatibles. Elle autorise également quatre lectures simultanées, contre deux pour les offres Standard.
Il faut cependant garder en tête que la 4K et le HDR10 ne sont actuellement disponibles que sur certains appareils en France. La compatibilité dépend notamment de votre téléviseur ou de votre lecteur multimédia, et le Dolby Vision reste absent pour l’instant.
Des nouveautés Disney, Marvel et Pixar pour en profiter
Côté catalogue, plusieurs gros films sont arrivés sur Disney+ à la rentrée, et les séries s’enchaînent en novembre.
Les amateurs de films d’animation peuvent notamment retrouver Zootopie 2 (disponible depuis le 27 août), qui réunit à nouveau Judy Hopps et Nick Wilde pour une nouvelle enquête. Les fans de science-fiction peuvent, eux, se replonger dans l’univers de Pandora avec Avatar : de Feu et de Cendres, arrivé le 18 septembre.
Côté séries, Marvel boucle VisionQuest, dont le dernier épisode sort ce mercredi 11 novembre. La deuxième saison d’All’s Fair, la treizième saison d’American Horror Story (en VF depuis ce mercredi) et la série coréenne L’Impératrice remariée viennent aussi d’arriver. Les amateurs de documentaires animaliers pourront, eux, se tourner vers Au plus près des loups avec Bertie Gregory, produit par National Geographic.
Le programme des prochaines semaines est tout aussi chargé :
- Le 20 novembre : la saison 3 de Percy Jackson et les Olympiens ;
- Le 4 décembre : Jumpers, le film d’animation Pixar dans lequel Mabel transfère sa conscience dans un castor robotisé pour communiquer avec les animaux ;
- Le 8 décembre : la saison 6 d’Only Murders in the Building, qui entraîne cette fois son trio d’enquêteurs à Londres.
De quoi remplir sa liste de programmes à regarder pendant les deux mois de promotion, sans oublier les classiques Disney, la saga Star Wars et les nombreuses productions Marvel déjà présentes sur la plateforme.
Comment profiter de la promotion Disney+ ?
Pour bénéficier des tarifs réduits, il suffit de se rendre sur le site de Disney+, de sélectionner l’une des trois formules en promotion puis de créer un compte ou de se connecter à un compte existant.
L’offre est valable jusqu’au 24 novembre 2026 à 23 h 59, uniquement pour les nouveaux abonnés et les anciens abonnés éligibles âgés d’au moins 18 ans. Un moyen de paiement valide est nécessaire et la promotion n’est pas cumulable avec d’autres réductions.
Enfin, si vous souhaitez uniquement profiter des deux mois à prix réduit, pensez à résilier avant le premier renouvellement au tarif normal. La résiliation prend effet à la fin de la période de facturation déjà payée, sans remboursement des mois entamés.
Pour comparer Disney+ à Prime Video, Netflix et aux autres plateformes de streaming, rendez-vous dans notre guide dédié aux services de SVOD.

articles.title: Stimmprobe statt Captcha: Startup will Menschen sicher von Bots unterscheiden
articles.text:
Stimmprobe statt Captcha: Wie ein Startup Menschen sicher von Bots unterscheiden will
Ein Captcha dient im Normalfall dazu, Bots den Zugriff auf Websites oder Online-Formulare zu verweigern. Anders als Bots sollen menschliche Nutzer:innen die meist bildbasierten Rätsel lösen können. Captchas gelten aber nicht als besonders benutzerfreundlich oder barrierefrei.
Voice-ID-Startup sammelt Millionen ein
Alternativen wie die Verifizierung per Ausweiskopie und Foto sowie Videoident-Verfahren sind dagegen wenig datenschutzfreundlich. Diese Probleme will Helix mit seiner Voice-ID-Lösung angehen. Das von Siri-Miterfinder Dag Kittlaus beratene Startup hat über eine Finanzierungsrunde gerade 6,2 Millionen US-Dollar einsammeln können, wie es in einer entsprechenden Mitteilung heißt.
Helix wolle das Vertrauen in digitale Interaktionen zurückbringen, wie Helix-CEO Alex Oberg erklärt. Die Idee zum Bot-Schutz per Stimmprobe sei vor dem Hintergrund entstanden, dass Verbraucher:innen sich vor dem möglichen Diebstahl persönlicher Daten fürchten. Künftig werde zudem immer wichtiger, Menschen von KI-Agenten zu unterscheiden.
Statt Captcha: Stimmprobe per Smartphone
Aus Datenschutzgründen soll sich die Voice-ID-Technologie von Helix lokal auf dem Smartphone ausführen lassen. Das soll verhindern, dass persönliche Daten der Nutzer:innen auf einem Server landen.
Um sich zu verifizieren, müssen Nutzer:innen vier Ziffern vorlesen. Der Vorgang soll vier Sekunden dauern. Damit, so Helix, kombiniere die Lösung biometrische Sicherheit mit geringen Kosten und einem geringen Aufwand.
Als Einsatzzweck sieht das Startup die Bereiche Ticketing, Dating, Gaming oder Fintech. Um die Voice-ID-Lösung zu integrieren, bietet Helix interessierten Plattformen ein Software-Development-Kit an. Darüber hinaus funktioniert das Ganze auch über die Eingabe einer einzelnen Codezeile in Claude Code oder OpenAI Codex.
Voice-ID-Lösung soll Alter erkennen
Helix zufolge könne seine Lösung nicht nur vor Bots schützen, sondern auch das Alter der Nutzer:innen schätzen. Auf eine solche Verifizierungsoption könnten insbesondere Social-Media-Plattformen angesichts der strengeren Regulierungsmaßnahmen bald angewiesen sein.
Noch sei die Lösung Helix zufolge aber nicht in der Lage, KI-Agenten in Live-Calls zu identifizieren. Aber: Laut Siri-Miterfinder Kittlaus habe die Technologie zur Stimmerkennung mittlerweile einen Reifegrad erreicht, bei dem sie zuverlässig funktioniere, wie er gegenüber Techcrunch erklärte.

articles.title: How LinkedIn, Netflix & DoorDash Run Agents, Evals & Inference in Production: QCon AI New York 2026
articles.text:
QCon AI New York 2026 has published its full schedule for December 15–16. Engineers from LinkedIn, Netflix, DoorDash, Figma, and other organizations will examine the architecture and operational decisions behind production AI systems, including agent authorization, evaluation pipelines, model serving, and AI-assisted software delivery. With the conference a few weeks away, there is still time to join other practitioners before the full ticket price takes effect on December 9.
The program addresses questions facing teams moving beyond initial AI deployments: where to enforce agent permissions, how to connect offline evaluations to production behavior, and how to support growing inference workloads. It also examines how coding agents affect code review, engineering practices, and organizational adoption.
The following presentations explore these challenges through systems the speakers build and operate.
Keynotes
Nancy Wang, CTO at 1Password, who founded and scaled AWS Data Protection and previously worked at Rubrik and Google, opens day one with When Software Becomes a User: Identity and Authorization for Agents in Production. She argues that identity systems assume a human behind every credential, with a stable role, a bounded session, and someone accountable afterward. Agents have none of these.
Tara Sainath, Distinguished Research Scientist at Google DeepMind, lead of the Gemini Audio area and modeling lead for Project Astra, opens day two with Audio Processing with Large Language Models. She covers how LLMs have changed audio processing, and the research and product impact of audio LLMs at Google.
Agents in production
Pratik Agarwal, Distributed Systems Engineer on Figma's sandbox and caching platforms, explains how Figma provisions and secures production agents. Figma found that the trust boundary for agents extends beyond the sandbox. Warm pools cut provisioning latency by 90%, and availability rose from 99% to 99.95%.
Ronak Nathani, Principal Staff Software Engineer in Compute Infrastructure at LinkedIn and host of the Software Misadventures podcast, presents LinkedIn's Kubernetes ops agent, which works across 500,000+ nodes and 5M+ pods. Its guardrails sit on the server, including rate limits, delete protection, and peer approval for production changes.
Evals that decide whether a change ships
Fabio Flores, Software Engineer at DoorDash who leads foundation development for its agentic ordering system, explains the eval loop behind it. Every change is checked before launch by an LLM judge calibrated against human reviewers. The same rubrics score simulated and real sessions, so offline gains carry into production.
Emrick Donadei, Software Engineer on the Google DeepMind infrastructure team who works on evaluation and safety for agentic harnesses, covers agent evals the whole organization can write and keep running. The talk starts from a common problem: an eval that passes once, then fails on the next run.
Inference cost and model serving
Fan Yang, Staff Software Engineer building Netflix's AI serving platform, and Rajat Shah, Staff Software Engineer who leads the technical architecture for ML model serving, explain how Netflix serves ML and GenAI from one platform. It handles about 1 million inference requests per second across 300+ models, after five years of consolidation. They cover what multi-tenancy costs to operate.
Salina Wu, Software Engineer building Pinterest's generative AI serving platform, and Cristian Lopez, Software Engineer on GenAI Serving at Pinterest, present Pinterest's vision-language model serving stack on NVIDIA Dynamo. It is built for multimodal workloads with heavy prefill computation and large KV cache pressure.
AI-assisted software engineering
Min Chen, Principal Staff Engineer at LinkedIn with more than 25 years of software development experience, presents LinkedIn's AI code review system. It reviews tens of thousands of pull requests a week across about 10,000 repositories. More than 60% of sampled suggestions are accepted, and a validation pipeline filters findings before developers see them.
Joey Wang, engineering lead at Harvey who created Spectre, Harvey's internal collaborative cloud agent platform, explains how Harvey shipped its agents internally first on Spectre. Spectre passed 7,000 merged pull requests across every repository before the agents reached lawyers.
Engineering leadership and adoption
Liz Fong-Jones, Technical Fellow at Honeycomb and site reliability engineer with more than two decades of experience, and Rebecca Murphey, Principal for AI Ops at Honeycomb and author of Build: Elements of an Effective Software Organization, reflect on Honeycomb's 2x initiative. Peak weekday PR merges to Honeycomb's main monorepo rose from about 30 to about 74 between early 2025 and April 2026, and have held steady since.
Brian Yang, Member of Technical Staff at OpenAI who builds AI-native advertising and monetization systems, covers making AI adoption work across an engineering team. He looks at what happens after every engineer has coding agents, when one person finds a way of working that teammates struggle to reproduce.
Also on the program
Other sessions come from engineers at Anthropic, Microsoft, BlackRock, Databricks, Datadog, Tessl, LangChain, Baseten, and Google Cloud’s DORA team. Topics include agentic standards, sandbox density, SRE agents, AgentOps for financial services, inference with vLLM, voice agents, software factories, and enterprise AI adoption. Explore the full schedule.
Group registration for teams of three or more closes on November 27, 2026, with savings of $50 to $125 per ticket. Individual tickets are $1,790 until December 8, the last price before the full rate applies. Tickets can be transferred to a colleague free of charge until December 11, 2026.
Engineers who need approval can use the Convince Your Manager page, which provides an email template built around the sessions relevant to their work.

articles.title: Lidl vende la herramienta Parkside imprescindible para los manitas de casa por 37,99 euros
articles.text:
Tener a mano una herramienta polivalente para montar muebles, colgar estantes o realizar pequeñas reparaciones sin depender de enchufes ni cables es básico en cualquier hogar. En el catálogo de bricolaje de Lidl, la gama Parkside se ha consolidado como la referencia indiscutible por su relación calidad-precio y este taladro atornillador recargable de 12 V (PBSA 12 F5) destaca como una compra práctica y ahora está disponible por 37,99 euros.
Taladro atornillador de impacto recargable 20 V »PSBSA 20-Li C3« con batería – con cargador
Si no llegas a tiempo para conseguir este chollo de Lidl, en Amazon tienes también una alternativa a un precio similar. Se trata de este taladro atornillador Betenst (rebajado hoy a 29,95 euros) y que viene con dos baterías y varias brocas y puntas.
BETENST Taladro Atornillador 21V, Taladro Inalámbrico con 2 Batería 2,0Ah
Diseño compacto de 12 V, portabrocas extraíble y kit completo con batería
La clave de esta herramienta Parkside es su equilibrio entre ligereza y fuerza, pensado para trabajar cómodamente en espacios reducidos o por encima de la cabeza sin que sufras fatiga en los brazos.
Incorpora un engranaje de dos velocidades con un par de apriete máximo de 28 Nm, regulable en 19 niveles de par más una posición específica para taladrado. Esto permite desde apretar tornillos en maderas delicadas sin pasarlos de rosca hasta perforar con precisión en madera o metal ligero.
Incorpora también un portabrocas automático de sujeción rápida que se puede desmontar sin herramientas mediante un sistema de liberación rápida. Al quitarlo, la punta del taladro deja al descubierto un portapuntas magnético integrado que acorta el cuerpo de la herramienta y permite atornillar en rincones donde un taladro convencional no cabe.

articles.title: Confirmado por la Ley de Propiedad Horizontal: no se permite prohibir el uso del ascensor a los vecinos que no paguen la comunidad
articles.text:
En caso de impago de la comunidad, tenemos derecho a iniciar una acción judicial para que el propietario pague. Además, podemos adoptar medidas disuasorias. Sin embargo, no podemos bloquearle el ascensor por ello. En la Ley de Propiedad Horizontal se reconocen las posibilidades de actuar para evitar impagos. No obstante, no pueden afectar a la habitabilidad de las viviendas.
Por ello, no podemos decir que la ley nos da carta blanca para impedir el acceso al ascensor a los morosos. En la Guía de administradores de fincas colegiados se indica que está excluida esta posibilidad por ser fundamental para la habitabilidad de la finca.
Qué permiten los artículos 6 y 21
Artículo 6. Los propietarios podrán establecer las normas de régimen interior que consideren convenientes para el buen funcionamiento de la finca. Estas reglas de convivencia y uso de los servicios comunes deberán respetarse (obligatoriedad) hasta que sean modificadas por el procedimiento adecuado. Además, deben cumplir con la legislación vigente y los estatutos de la comunidad.
Por ello, contamos con la potestad de regular el uso de los elementos comunes. Sin embargo, no todo lo que se aprueba en la junta de propietarios es válido. Las medidas contra la morosidad no pueden ser abusivas ni vulnerar los límites legales.
En el artículo 21.1 (que es el resultado de la reforma aprobada en 2022) encontramos las medidas contra la morosidad. Podemos pactar unos intereses superiores al legal (acuerdos en la junta). También podemos inhabilitar temporalmente el uso de determinados servicios e instalaciones mientras exista el impago.
El periodo de inhabilitación está ligado a la morosidad. Es decir, mientras el propietario esté en mora. Una vez que deja de estarlo, no puede mantenerse la inhabilitación indefinidamente. Y otra cosa que debe quedar clara es que no se pueden adoptarse por decisión unilateral del presidente o administrador. Es la junta la que debe decidir.
En la Guía de morosidad de AFColegiados se distinguen los casos en los que se trata de instalaciones recreativas o servicios esenciales. Se pueden limitar (dentro de los límites legales) aquellas instalaciones como piscinas o gimnasios. Sin embargo, en el caso del ascensor no es posible porque es fundamental para la habitabilidad.
Cuota ordinaria y derramas exigibles
Podemos iniciar una acción judicial para que el propietario pague. Además de los recibos que mensualmente nos envía la comunidad (cuota ordinaria), también están los gastos extraordinarios que le corresponden (derramas). Cuando estos son aprobados legalmente (por ejemplo, para hacer frente a obras o reparaciones) y vencen, tienen carácter de deuda (si el propietario no los paga).
En caso de que la junta apruebe algo que va en contra de la ley o los estatutos, es posible impugnar ante los tribunales (artículo 18) siempre que se cumplan los requisitos. En el caso de los propietarios con deudas, es necesario que estén al corriente (haber pagado las deudas vencidas) o que hayan consignado judicialmente esas cantidades de antemano (salvo en el caso de establecimiento o modificación de las cuotas de participación, que es una excepción legal).
Además, es necesario que estén legitimados para ello. En la ley se incluyen los que hayan salvado su voto en la junta, así como los ausentes y aquellos a los que se les ha privado indebidamente de su voto. No basta con que no estén de acuerdo con el acuerdo.

articles.title: OpenAI quiere que ChatGPT organice tus vacaciones y compra Odessia, una empresa que desarrolla agentes de viajes con IA
articles.text:
OpenAI quiere ampliar las capacidades de ChatGPT más allá de las conversaciones y la generación de contenido. La compañía adquirió Odessia, una startup especializada en agentes de inteligencia artificial capaces de buscar destinos, comparar precios y ayudar a reservar vuelos, hoteles y otros servicios turísticos.
La operación representa un nuevo paso en su intención de llevar sus herramientas a actividades cotidianas, como organizar unas vacaciones sin tener que visitar decenas de páginas web.
La adquisición fue anunciada el 10 de noviembre por Francis Davidson, fundador de Odessia y conocido en el sector turístico por haber creado Sonder, una empresa de alojamiento que dejó de operar en noviembre de 2025. El empresario confirmó que se incorporará al equipo de OpenAI para trabajar en el desarrollo de nuevas soluciones relacionadas con los viajes.
Aunque las condiciones económicas del acuerdo no fueron reveladas, la compra permite a OpenAI incorporar tecnología y experiencia especializada en un sector donde empresas como Booking.com, Expedia y Airbnb también están apostando por la inteligencia artificial.
La intención es avanzar hacia herramientas que no se limiten a recomendar destinos o elaborar itinerarios, sino que puedan intervenir en diferentes etapas de la planificación y contratación de un viaje.
Odessia podía organizar viajes y ayudar a realizar reservas con inteligencia artificial
Odessia fue fundada a principios de 2026 y consiguió desarrollar un asistente de viajes con un equipo de aproximadamente ocho personas. Antes de su adquisición por OpenAI, la startup había obtenido seis millones de dólares en una ronda de financiación liderada por Sequoia Capital.
Su propuesta consistía en utilizar agentes de inteligencia artificial para investigar destinos, encontrar alternativas de alojamiento, comparar vuelos y acompañar a los usuarios durante el proceso de contratación.
La diferencia frente a otros chatbots estaba en su capacidad para pasar de las recomendaciones a las operaciones comerciales. Por ejemplo, una persona podía solicitar unas vacaciones de una semana en Italia y recibir propuestas de vuelos, hoteles y actividades, además de asistencia para gestionar las reservas.
La empresa también había desarrollado conexiones con proveedores turísticos y contaba con acreditación de la Asociación Internacional de Transporte Aéreo (IATA), una organización que agrupa a compañías del sector aeronáutico.
Según Davidson, decenas de miles de personas probaron la plataforma durante el verano y Odessia alcanzó un ritmo anualizado superior a los 60 millones de dólares en viajes planificados. Esta cifra representa el volumen de viajes proyectado, no necesariamente reservas completadas ni ingresos obtenidos por la startup.
Cómo podría cambiar ChatGPT la forma de organizar unas vacaciones
Actualmente, los usuarios pueden pedirle a ChatGPT que recomiende destinos turísticos, prepare itinerarios, sugiera restaurantes o calcule presupuestos para unas vacaciones. Sin embargo, organizar un viaje completo todavía implica consultar diferentes plataformas para comprobar precios, disponibilidad y condiciones de contratación.
La tecnología desarrollada por Odessia buscaba reducir ese proceso mediante agentes capaces de investigar alternativas y utilizar herramientas externas para facilitar las reservas.
Con esta adquisición, OpenAI incorpora conocimientos que podrían servir para ampliar las funciones turísticas de ChatGPT. En un escenario futuro, una persona podría indicar cuánto dinero quiere gastar, qué destino le interesa y cuántos días tiene disponibles para que el asistente busque alternativas y ayude a organizar los diferentes servicios.
El fundador de Sonder estará detrás de los nuevos proyectos turísticos de OpenAI
La incorporación de Francis Davidson también tiene importancia por su experiencia en el sector. En 2014 fundó Sonder, una compañía que desarrolló un modelo de alojamiento basado en apartamentos y propiedades urbanas gestionados mediante tecnología.
La empresa llegó a expandirse internacionalmente y salió a bolsa en 2022, pero posteriormente afrontó dificultades financieras. En 2025, después de la ruptura de un acuerdo comercial con Marriott, anunció el cese de sus operaciones y el inicio de su liquidación.
Con Odessia, Davidson apostó por un modelo diferente: desarrollar tecnología mediante agentes de inteligencia artificial y trabajar con un equipo reducido. Estos sistemas también participaban en tareas internas de programación, marketing, análisis y atención al cliente.
Ahora, el empresario llevará esa experiencia a OpenAI, donde participará en el desarrollo de herramientas relacionadas con el turismo.

articles.title: Starlink Mini 2 chega com bateria para até 4,5 horas de uso • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Starlink Mini 2 chega com bateria para até 4,5 horas de uso
Nova antena portátil da SpaceX tem bateria removível e carregamento USB-C, mas ainda não tem previsão de lançamento no Brasil.
A SpaceX anunciou a nova geração de sua antena portátil de internet via satélite, a Starlink Mini 2. A principal novidade é a bateria removível de 71 Wh, capaz de manter o equipamento funcionando por até 4,5 horas sem depender de uma tomada ou fonte externa de energia.
O modelo também ganhou Wi-Fi 6, estrutura mais fina e carregamento USB-C. A nova versão foi apresentada nessa terça-feira (10/11) e já está disponível em pré-venda para clientes selecionados nos Estados Unidos. Ainda não há previsão de lançamento no mercado brasileiro.
A mudança resolve uma das principais limitações da Starlink Mini original, lançada no Brasil em 2025 por R$ 1.799. Embora compacta e fácil de transportar, a primeira geração precisava de alimentação externa para funcionar, como uma tomada ou bateria portátil.
A bateria de 71 Wh pesa aproximadamente 490 gramas e utiliza um mecanismo de encaixe rápido, permitindo a substituição por outra unidade sem ferramentas. O acessório também possui indicadores LED e entrada USB-C com suporte a carregamento de até 60 W.
A Starlink informa que a antena pode estabelecer conexão em cerca de 60 segundos, desde que tenha uma visão desobstruída do céu. O equipamento também pode funcionar conectado diretamente a uma fonte USB-C, sem depender da bateria.
Outra mudança está no roteador integrado, que passou do Wi-Fi 5 para o Wi-Fi 6. A área de cobertura anunciada aumentou para até 167 metros quadrados, contra aproximadamente 112 metros quadrados da geração anterior.
O novo modelo mede 31,4 × 26,3 centímetros e tem 2,31 centímetros de espessura, contra 3,85 centímetros da primeira Mini. Apesar de mais fina, a antena ficou mais pesada: são 1,6 kg com bateria e suporte, contra cerca de 1,1 kg no modelo anterior.
A estrutura mantém certificação IP67 de resistência à poeira e à água. Há ainda um suporte dobrável, botão físico de energia e encaixe compatível com tripés de câmera. A proposta é facilitar o uso em viagens e acampamentos.
A Starlink abriu a pré-venda da Mini 2 por US$ 999 (quase R$ 5.600 em conversão direta), inicialmente para clientes convidados nos Estados Unidos. O pacote inclui a antena e 12 meses do plano Roam Unlimited, que oferece dados ilimitados para viagens.
Os interessados podem reservar o equipamento através de um depósito reembolsável de US$ 100 (aproximadamente R$ 560). O restante será cobrado no envio, previsto para começar em meados de dezembro.
O valor não representa necessariamente o preço da antena vendida separadamente, já que a oferta inclui um ano de serviço. A SpaceX ainda não informou quanto custará apenas o equipamento ou as baterias adicionais.
No Brasil, a Starlink comercializa oficialmente a primeira geração da Mini, voltada principalmente para usuários que precisam de internet durante viagens e deslocamentos. Ainda não há previsão de lançamento da Mini 2 no mercado brasileiro.
A empresa informa que pretende ampliar a disponibilidade para outros clientes e países, mas não divulgou datas nem preços para essas regiões.

articles.title: CoreWeave turns to customer prepayments, shorter contracts to fund AI growth | TechCrunch
articles.text:
CoreWeave is rewriting how it pays for the AI boom, according to the company’s third-quarter earnings, reported on Tuesday. CoreWeave, a neocloud that rents out the computing power behind AI, said it’s increasingly asking customers to pay up front, borrowing against specific contracts, and even pursuing short-term deals that could lead to higher prices.
The new strategies could help CoreWeave finance its growth more efficiently while squeezing more cash from existing infrastructure. But these bets only hold if today’s demand and pricing power continue.
CoreWeave reported $3.66 billion in revenue, up 168% from the year prior, but it also posted a $709 million net loss and $846 million in quarterly interest expense.
“We will not use the unsecured debt market to fund our business at current yields, nor do we need to,” CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator said during Tuesday’s earnings call.
Instead, CoreWeave’s plan is to rely on loans backed by specific customer contracts, drawing on funds as needed to finance most of the infrastructure it still has to build to deliver on its significant backlog of $132.5 billion.
CoreWeave also said it expects about $9 billion in customer prepayments and deposits over the next three months, including more than $3 billion tied to signing new customer contracts for capacity it has already built, which requires no additional spending on hardware.
Rivals Nebius and IREN have also relied on hefty Microsoft prepayments to pay for computing capacity, signaling that the industry is moving toward asking Big Tech to pay up for their buildouts.
Upfront payments could alleviate CoreWeave’s immediate borrowing needs, but they also commit the company to providing services at a price that might be less attractive down the road if compute demand continues to surge.
CoreWeave is also looking to capitalize on that growing demand by signing more shorter-term contracts that can command much higher prices.
The company raised prices across its offerings by about 25% in July and by another 10% later in the quarter. Prices are still climbing this quarter, in a way that “more than offset[s] cost increases,” said Intrator.
“We are also allocating more capacity to short-term opportunities, where the pricing justifies it, selling capacity at more than $40 million per megawatt annually, while pricing for new infrastructure on four- and five-year contracts is moving to $20 million to $25 million per megawatt,” the chief executive said.
CoreWeave’s financing strategy now revolves around those opportunities. In August, the company closed a $2.6 billion loan, its first designed specifically for shorter-term customer contracts. Known as DDTL 5.5, it lets CoreWeave borrow in installments as it needs the money.
While short-term deals let CoreWeave charge higher prices and change them more frequently, it’s a trade-off. Lenders give more weight to longer-term contracts, even if they’re priced lower, because they value predictable cash flow and consistency to repay the loan above all.
Even though Wall Street reacted positively to CoreWeave’s earnings, bond investors are much less sanguine. Last month, yields on some of the company’s bonds hit above 15%, highlighting that investors are concerned about the debt needed to fund data center buildouts before those investments see a return.
In short, CoreWeave is finding new ways to expand without relying on unsecured debt. The strategy it has chosen could boost profits, but it also carries greater risk around contract renewals and pricing — and it just goes to show how dependent the AI infrastructure boom is on sustained, and as yet unproven, demand.
TechCrunch has reached out to CoreWeave for more information about its loan facility.

The semiconductor industry is at an inflection point. As Moore’s Law matures, the traditional “waterfall” design cycle — defined by rigid silos, siloed optimizations, and multi-year timelines — cannot keep pace with the exponential demand for AI-optimized silicon. We are stuck in a hardware-first world trying to solve software-speed problems. This session introduces Artificial Chip Intelligence (ACI®), a paradigm-shifting technology using a physics-informed foundation model designed to transform chip development from a manual labor-intensive process into a conversational, AI-driven workflow. articles.title: Meet 8 Tamil Nadu startups that showcased their innovations to PM Modi
articles.text:
Meet 8 Tamil Nadu startups that showcased their innovations to PM Modi
From spacetech to aviation and healthcare, meet eight Tamil Nadu startups taking homegrown innovation to new heights and catching the Prime Minister’s attention.
When Prime Minister Narendra Modi travelled aboard the Chennai Metro with Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay recently, the journey also provided an unusual platform for entrepreneurs to present their ideas.
More than 15 startup founders reportedly joined the interaction, bringing innovations from fields ranging from spacetech and aviation to healthcare, agriculture and urban finance.
Here's a look at eight startups that showcased their innovations to the PM.
1. Dream Aerospace Technologies
Sector - Spacetech | Chennai
During his interaction with PM Modi, Dream Aerospace Technologies founder, CEO and CTO Hari Krishnan KJ discussed the company's propulsion systems for satellites, spacecraft and re-entry vehicles. These systems provide the thrust needed to manoeuvre spacecraft.
Founded in 2022, the startup has a team of around 25 people, with an average age of approximately 25. Krishnan recalled that the Prime Minister asked about the company’s founding, team size and employees’ average age, and was surprised by how young the team was.
The conversation also covered the growing satellite industry and the company’s expansion plans. Krishnan told the PM that the startup was focusing on increasing domestic manufacturing capacity, with customer orders lined up for the next two to three years.
He also highlighted how IN-SPACe had helped private space companies access India’s space ecosystem.
2. Blunav Technologies
Sector - Aviation technology | Chennai
Blunav Technologies is developing software to manage airport operations, bringing together information on aircraft movements, passenger services and baggage handling. Founder and CEO Suseendar Marimuthu told PM Modi that the company had designed its platform specifically for small and medium-sized airports, where replacing existing systems can be expensive.
The Prime Minister was particularly interested in how the technology could support regional connectivity under the UDAN scheme. Marimuthu said Modi wanted to see the platform trialled at a UDAN airport.
The conversation also turned to the company’s international expansion. Recalling the PM’s advice, Marimuthu said, “Always remember that this is an Indian company... and you are an Indian. So be proud to wear that as a badge wherever you go.”
The exchange came as India pushes to expand regional aviation and develop more airports under the modified UDAN scheme.
3. Grahaa Space
Sector - Spacetech | Karur
Grahaa Space is developing a constellation of earth-observation nanosatellites to stream near-real-time video data of the Earth's surface. Co-founder and CEO Ramesh Kumar described the ambition as building an “eye in the sky”.
During his interaction with PM Modi, Kumar showed him photographs of the company’s two launch attempts, its SOLARAS satellite and the technology it is developing. Its first launch attempt, from Brazil in December 2025, ended in failure when the rocket exploded. However, in July 2026, the company successfully deployed SOLARAS into low Earth orbit aboard Skyroot Aerospace’s Vikram-1 rocket.
Kumar also explained the company’s proprietary, modular satellite platform and communication systems. He recalled that the Prime Minister enquired about its payloads and appreciated the startup's contribution to India’s growing space economy.
“He assured me that the Government of India would provide all required support for spacetech startups like ours,” Kumar said.
4. FarmwiseAI
Sector - Agritech | Chennai
FarmwiseAI applies artificial intelligence and geospatial analytics to agriculture and land management. Its technology uses satellite imagery and geographical data to help map agricultural land and generate information useful for planning and administration.
The company says it began working with the Tamil Nadu Agriculture Department and Tamil Nadu Agricultural University in 2021. It also reports completing a statewide Field Measurement Book mapping programme covering more than 4.5 crore land parcels, 45 lakh survey numbers and 17,700 villages.
5. Thazhal Geospatial Analytics
Sector - Climatetech | Tirunelveli
Based in Tirunelveli, Thazhal Geospatial Analytics uses satellite imagery, drone data and Internet of Things sensors to monitor physical assets and assess environmental risks. Its work translates geographical information into insights that can help lenders, insurers, businesses and government agencies understand risks associated with infrastructure and climate conditions.
Founder Vignesh Kandasamy reportedly discussed applications including monitoring construction progress, identifying potential delays and assessing roads, bridges, lakes and mangrove ecosystems. During the Metro interaction, he told reporters that PM Modi had specifically asked whether the technology could be used to monitor roads and bridges.
6. Diagno Intelligent Systems
Sector - Healthcare technology | Chennai
Diagno Intelligent Systems is developing an AI-based tool to screen patients for osteoporosis, a condition that weakens bones and increases the risk of fractures.
Its product, iOsteoporos Screen, analyses conventional chest X-rays to measure features of the clavicle, or collarbone, using a technique called radiogrammetry. These measurements are then used to estimate hip bone mineral density, an indicator of bone strength. The aim is to identify people who may be at risk and could benefit from further testing.
An important aspect of the approach is that it uses chest X-rays that patients may already have undergone, potentially reducing the need for additional imaging at the initial screening stage.
7. MEDxAI Innovations
Sector - Healthcare and life sciences | Kancheepuram
MEDxAI Innovations is working at the intersection of artificial intelligence, medical diagnostics and drug discovery. Founded by Dr Sheena C. Pravin, the Vellore Institute of Technology-incubated startup presented two platforms during the interaction with PM Modi.
The first, CerviLens, is designed to support cervical cancer pre-screening through AI-assisted colposcopy and Pap smear analysis. The system combines information from different screening methods to assess potential cervical lesions and support clinical decision-making. Its second platform, Quantum PharmX, applies AI and computational methods to drug discovery and molecular research.
8. Munify Datatech
Sector - Fintech and GovTech | Chennai
Munify Datatech works on a less conventional area of fintech. Instead of focusing on consumer payments or lending, it is building a data platform around municipal finances.
Its platform organises financial information from urban local bodies, including municipal budgets, audited accounts, property tax collections and expenditure patterns. It also uses this information to develop credit scores and assessments of municipal financial health.
The company’s website says its database covers more than 200 municipal corporations and contains thousands of municipal documents. It is also developing a platform to connect creditworthy cities and viable infrastructure projects with lenders and development partners.

articles.title: ICYMI: What landed for AI builders in October 2026 | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
ICYMI: What landed for AI builders in October 2026
At AWS, we believe AI builders should be able to choose the right model for every task, trust their agents in production, and see clearly what their AI workloads cost. That belief guides how we invest across our portfolio. Amazon Bedrock gives you access to leading models and the tools to build and scale AI applications securely. We extend this foundation with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, which provides the platform to build, connect, and optimize agents using any model and any framework. That includes Strands, our open source agent development toolkit. Together, they take you from first prototype to production.
As agents move into core business workflows, the bar rises. You need the flexibility to use different models as tasks, budgets, and latency targets change. When a primary model is throttled or unreachable, your agents must keep working. They also must act within limits you set and return output other software can use as is. Their answers must stay grounded in sources you allow, and their cost must hold up at high volume.
What we shipped in October addresses each of these needs. New models help you match each task to the right price and speed, from high-volume subagents to real-time voice. Amazon Bedrock and AgentCore updates keep agents available, hold them to the processes you define, and help you trust what they return. New pricing and cost reporting make spend more predictable. Strands adds new ways to build, contain, and test agents.
Match the model to the task on Amazon Bedrock
Run fast, low-cost subagents. Claude Haiku 5.5 is built for subagents and high-volume, cost-sensitive work. According to Anthropic, it is the most capable Haiku yet and costs around 75 percent less than Claude Haiku 4.5 for most tasks. It is also the first Haiku with effort controls, so you can tune cost against intelligence for each task. In a multi-agent setup, a model such as Claude Opus 5.5 can plan the work and hand well-defined coding, tool use, and browser automation tasks to Haiku. This keeps running many agents in parallel affordable.
Get near-flagship results at a lower price. OpenAI GPT-6.1 Terra is now generally available on Amazon Bedrock. On OpenAI’s Agents’ Last Exam evaluation, it performed on par with GPT-6 Astra and completed tasks more than three times faster than GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol. Its input and output token prices are at least 50 percent lower than those of GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-5.6 Terra. It accepts text and images with up to 1 million input tokens, which suits drafting proposals, interpreting technical drawings, and building agents that work across business systems. For latency-sensitive work such as real-time coding assistants, GPT-6.1 Sol now also offers Ultrafast mode.
Build voice agents that reason in real time. Amazon Nova 2.5 Sonic, our latest speech-to-speech model, improves reasoning, instruction following, and tool-calling accuracy, with lower latency at the same price as Amazon Nova 2 Sonic. A customer service agent can now look up an order, check return eligibility, and start a return in a single conversation.
Pick specialized models for coding and video. GLM 5.3 by Z.ai is an open-weight model for agentic coding and long-horizon software engineering, with a 1-million-token context window and prompt caching, available to eligible enterprise customers. TwelveLabs Pegasus 1.5 turns entire videos into structured, time-coded metadata. It reads visuals, audio, and on-screen text in a single pass, with no separate ingestion pipeline.
Use more models in AWS GovCloud (US). Claude Haiku 5.5 and OpenAI GPT-5.6 models with cross-Region inference are now available in AWS GovCloud (US). Daybreak Red from OpenAI, a model for authorized security work, is available to eligible customers in AWS GovCloud (US-East). Regulated teams get more models while maintaining US data sovereignty.
Build and run agents you can rely on
Build and operate agents from your terminal. AgentCore CLI, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, is now generally available in version 1.0. We rebuilt it with faster startup, a consistent command structure, and support for more AgentCore resources. You can work with harnesses, runtimes, memory, identity, gateways, and payments directly or through a project. Existing projects move to version 1 with one command. The result is one tool from local development to day-to-day operations.
Keep agents available when a model is throttled. AgentCore Gateway, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, now supports the Amazon Bedrock InvokeModel APIs and model fallback. Your existing Amazon Bedrock SDK code can point at the gateway without per-provider code changes. When the primary model is throttled or unreachable, the gateway routes the request to the next model or provider in a chain you define. A circuit breaker skips destinations that are failing. The gateway can also reach private targets in your virtual private cloud (VPC) using certificates from your own private certificate authority. Your agents stay available without retry logic in every client.
Turn your business workflows into agent tools. You can now use AWS Step Functions workflows, including your existing Standard and Express workflows, as tools through AgentCore Gateway. Your business logic stays in a workflow you already run and trust, so you don’t rebuild it inside the agent or rely on a prompt to follow it. The agent decides when to run a workflow, and Step Functions runs each step exactly as you defined it. For example, a support agent can start your refund workflow, and every refund still goes through the same eligibility check, approval, and credit steps.
Get JSON your systems can use as is. Structured outputs are now available for all Claude models on Amazon Bedrock. You receive schema-compliant JSON without custom parsing or retries. You can extract every required field from an earnings report, or route support tickets with entities that always match your data model.
Keep answers grounded in sources you trust. Web Search on Amazon Bedrock now supports domain filtering and user location for requests made with the OpenAI Responses API. You can allow up to 100 domains, block up to 100 domains, and return results relevant to a geography. Amazon Bedrock Guardrails then checks that answers stay true to their sources. Its new Standard tier for contextual grounding checks costs the same as the Classic tier, covers conversational and reasoning responses, and supports more languages. With both, you can control where answers come from and catch hallucinations in more of your applications.
Predict and lower the cost of running agents
Pay for agent memory based on what you use. AgentCore memory, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, now prices short-term memory by the data your agents ingest, retrieve, and store, instead of a flat rate per event. Most workloads see lower costs, and small-payload use cases see the largest reductions. You can also set a time-to-live on long-term memory records to meet retention requirements and control storage costs.
See what drives your Amazon Bedrock spend. AWS Cost Explorer, AWS Budgets, and AWS Cost Management Dashboards now break down Amazon Bedrock cost by model, model provider, inference type, and feature, at no additional charge. Finance and platform teams can find their most expensive models or set a budget alert for a single model, in the billing tools they already use. To lower input costs, Advanced Prompt Optimization can now also shorten your prompts, returning a shorter version only when it scores at least as high on your evaluation.
Build voice, local, and well-tested agents with Strands
Ship voice agents in a few lines of code. Strands Bidi Agents, for building two-way, speech-to-speech voice agents, are now generally available, with direct support for Amazon Nova Sonic, OpenAI, and Gemini models. Bidi Agents reconnect to the model in the background, so long calls keep going past a provider’s session limit. A voice agent can also hand longer work, such as research, to another agent and explain the results aloud.
Let local agents work within your limits. Strands Box, now in developer preview, is an open source local sandbox for AI agents. It combines operating-system isolation with semantic policy. You set policy for each tool, and Box enforces it deterministically, whether the agent calls tools directly, through the Model Context Protocol (MCP), or by generating code. Box works with any model and any agent framework, so an agent can operate in your project without reaching files and services you didn’t allow.
Find where your agent breaks before customers do. Red teaming in Strands Evals runs adversarial conversations, such as prompt injections and jailbreak attempts, against your agent and shows the messages and tool calls where it failed. Strands Evals can now also score structured output field by field, giving partial credit when an agent gets most fields right. Use them to fix weak spots before an agent reaches production. To get started, see the Strands Evals documentation.
Cut the cost of routine agent decisions. Strands Decider, the small, open source decision model we featured in last month’s recap, now comes in four sizes built on Gemma 4. Instead of generating text, it picks between options you define, such as which tool to call or where to route a request. When an Amazon team switched ticket classification in one of its largest internal ticketing systems to Decider, estimated cost per ticket dropped by about 98 percent. Average response time dropped by 78 percent.
Get started
Explore Amazon Bedrock, deploy agents with the AgentCore CLI, or build your first agent with the Strands Harness SDK.
