articles.title: Baker Tilly notifies clients of data breach at third-party provider
articles.text:
The Baker Tilly Advisory Group is notifying clients that a data breach has compromised certain personal information about them and their dependents.
The company said the exposed data was stored on a platform operated by a third-party service provider Baker Tilly uses to serve clients.
Baker Tilly learned of the incident on September 6 and completed its review of the affected data on October 28, when it identified whose information was involved.
“On September 6, 2026, Baker Tilly became aware of a potential cybersecurity incident involving certain information stored on a platform operated by a third-party service provider used by Baker Tilly in connection with services we provide to clients,” reads the notification to customers.
“The unauthorized actor was able to obtain data relating to certain Baker Tilly clients,” the company added.
The breach notification does not provide a count of impacted clients, does not name the service provider, and leaves the specific data types exposed as a placeholder.
Data from the Office of the Texas Attorney General reports that Baker Tilly impacted 10,456 individuals in the state of Texas alone. The portal lists Social Security numbers (SSNs), full names, addresses, and other information as exposed data types.
Baker Tilly is a major accounting firm in the U.S., providing auditing, tax planning, compliance, advisory, and business operations services. Globally, the company operates in 147 countries and reports an annual revenue of $6.8 billion.
After discovering the incident, the company says it took immediate steps to contain it, contracted external experts to investigate, and notified law enforcement authorities.
Furthermore, it says it currently has no evidence of unauthorized activity on its own network, and added that it has no reports of identity theft or fraud linked to the exposure of customer information.
To mitigate the risks arising from the incident, the firm offers affected individuals 24 months of credit and identity monitoring through Experian.
BleepingComputer has contacted Baker Tilly for more information about the data breach, its source, the number of affected customers, and the type of data compromised, but we have not received a reply by the time of publishing.
BleepingComputer did not find any announcements from ransomware groups claiming the attack.

articles.title: Pour contrer la Citroën ë-C3, Dacia préparerait un tout nouveau SUV électrique à moins de 20 000 €
articles.text:
Dacia vient de renouveler la vieillissante Spring. Un bon début, même si la marque roumaine reste pour l’instant bloquée à un seul et unique véhicule électrique dans sa gamme. Pour réduire à l’avenir ses émissions de CO₂, cela ne suffira clairement pas. Si une Sandero à batterie est bel et bien dans les cartons, un autre invité surprise pourrait se joindre à la fête. Il s’agit d’un crossover qui n’était initialement pas prévu pour Europe…
Présenté en mars dernier, le Renault Bridger est un parfait inconnu puisqu’il ne s’agit qu’à l’heure actuelle d’un concept. Mais cette jolie étude de style sera promise à un bel avenir en arrivant dès 2027 sur les marchés émergents. Elle prendra alors la forme d’un petit crossover dépassant tout juste les 4 mètres de long, et qui sera décliné en versions essence, hybride et électrique. Ce véhicule inédit se placera ainsi sous le Renault Duster.
Objectif CO2 : pourquoi Dacia veut importer ce modèle en Europe
S’il n’était pas censé arriver chez nous, le Bridger pourrait voir sa feuille de route complètement bouleversée en raison du contexte actuel. Vu que Dacia doit rapidement électrifier sa gamme à moindre coût, adapter le Bridger au marché européen est une occasion rêvée pour atteindre les objectifs CO₂ imposés par l’Union européenne. Possible ainsi que le véhicule ait une carrière bien plus importante que prévu, portée par des horizons repoussés.
Parachuter le Bridger en Europe permettrait alors à Dacia de concurrencer frontalement les citadines électriques accessibles de Stellantis que sont les Citroën ë-C3 et Fiat Grande Panda. Ces deux véhicules ont d’ailleurs opté pour une stratégie similaire, à savoir un développement initialement pensé pour les pays émergents avant une arrivée sur le marché européen. Le Bridger se positionnerait ainsi entre la Spring et la future Sandero électrique.
4 nouvelles voitures électriques : la feuille de route de la marque roumaine
Dacia avait d’ailleurs confirmé lancer quatre modèles électriques d’ici 2030, la Spring étant la première sur la liste. Les Sandero et Sandero Stepway se placent aussi en quasi-certitudes. Le dernier membre de la vague demeure en revanche purement hypothétique. Un remplaçant du Jogger semble peu probable, au même titre qu’une déclinaison électrique du Striker. Tous les regards sont donc tournés vers le Bridger, même si le Hipster est aussi un bon candidat.
François Provost, le PDG du groupe Renault, avait d’ailleurs lâché un gros indice au Mondial de l’Automobile de Paris en affirmant que le Bridger a été « créé pour l’Inde, mais qu’il pourrait un jour arriver sur nos marchés également ». S’il est confirmé, le SUV pourrait débuter sous les 20 000 € et offrir entre 200 et 300 km d’autonomie. Son style cubique devrait être fidèle à celui du concept et Dacia ne devrait pas y apporter de trop grosses modifications.

articles.title: Blockbuster IPL trade: Hardik Pandya moves to Punjab for Rs 18 Cr, Arshdeep heads to MI
articles.text:
Blockbuster IPL trade: Hardik Pandya moves to Punjab for Rs 18 Cr, Arshdeep heads to MI
Hardik Pandya's trade brings the curtain down on his second stint with MI, a franchise with which he won four IPL titles.
Flamboyant all-rounder Hardik Pandya moved to Punjab Kings from Mumbai Indians at an increased fee of Rs 18 crore, while PBKS traded pacer Arshdeep Singh for him, completing the biggest and most high-profile exchange of players in the history of IPL.
Pandya's existing fee was Rs 16.35 crore. Arshdeep, on the other hand, moved to Mumbai Indians (MI) at an unchanged price tag of Rs 18 crore, read a statement from the IPL.
Before this, Chennai Super Kings (CSK) had acquired Sanju Samson this year for Rs 18 crore from Rajasthan Royals, who in turn got Ravindra Jadeja for Rs 14 crore and Sam Curran for Rs 2.4 crore from CSK.
Transfer fee is a bipartite agreement between two franchises and it is independent of retention fee (the salary paid to a player by the franchise).
It was mutually decided by MI and PBKS that Pandya's trade fee will go up by Rs 1.65 crore and, as per existing rules, he would get 50% of the hike. The rest would go to Mumbai Indians.
Pandya's trade brings the curtain down on his second stint with MI, a franchise with which he won four IPL titles.
Having first joined MI in 2015, the 33-year-old had starring roles with both bat and ball during the team's title-winning campaigns in 2015, 2017, 2019 and 2020. After seven seasons with Mumbai, Pandya moved to Gujarat Titans (GT) at a fee of Rs 15 crore in 2022 and led the franchise to the title in its debut season. GT also reached the final in 2023.
Pandya returned to MI in 2024, taking over captaincy from stalwart Rohit Sharma but the franchise's performance nose-dived, and it was speculated that the injury-ravaged maverick was unhappy with how things panned out.
He struggled to win over fans after taking over leadership and was incessantly booed in the first season after his return. The second season was slightly better but by the end of the third season (2026), things went downhill.
Stories of dressing room dissension surfaced and it was clear that all wasn't okay among the senior group of players, including now former T20 skipper Suryakumar Yadav, and pace legend Jasprit Bumrah who were bypassed for captaincy.
Rohit's sudden removal also remained a thorny issue and it is now being widely speculated that he will return to captain the franchise for what could well be his last season. He is expected to have Tilak Verma as his deputy and long-term successor.
"Hardik has shared some very special moments with Mumbai Indians. We have seen him grow as a cricketer, make his mark on the world stage and then return to lead the team," MI owner Akash Ambani said in a statement.
"I have great respect for him, both as a cricketer and as a person, and wish him nothing but the very best for everything that lies ahead," he added.
The Mumbai team managed to win just four of its 14 matches in the season gone by, and Pandya skipped the closing stages of the league due to fitness concerns.
However, he remains a force to reckon with as a player. Across 162 IPL matches, he has scored 2,955 runs at a strike rate of 146.28 and claimed 82 wickets, underlining his value as a proven match-winner.
"Some laughs, endless memories and a whole lot of madness! Thank you, Arsh for the memories," Punjab Kings said in a statement acknowledging his contribution to the team.
Arshdeep, meanwhile, moves to MI after eight seasons with PBKS, where he made his IPL debut in 2019 and established himself as one of the competition's leading left-arm fast bowlers.
With 111 wickets in 96 IPL matches, he is PBKS' all-time leading wicket-taker. He claimed 21 wickets in the 2025 season and followed that with 14 wickets in this year's IPL. The 27-year-old is also India's leading wicket-taker in the T20 format with 151 scalps in 104 matches.

articles.title: Gaurav Munjal steps down as Unacademy CEO; Akhilendra Kumar to take charge
articles.text:
Gaurav Munjal steps down as Unacademy CEO; Akhilendra Kumar to take charge
The leadership change comes two months after upGrad completed its acquisition of Unacademy. Munjal, however, will stay involved in the company's operations as executive chairman.
Unacademy co-founder Gaurav Munjal is stepping down as CEO to become executive chairman. Akhilendra Kumar will take over as the CEO.
The leadership change comes two months after upGrad completed its acquisition of Unacademy for just over $200 million.
In a LinkedIn post, Munjal said, “To be clear, I’m not going anywhere. I’ll stay fully involved in operations every day, work alongside Akhilendra and help with the upGrad IPO.”
Kumar’s appointment is an internal elevation at Unacademy. Between 2022 and 2025, he has progressed through the roles of AVP - Business, VP - Business, and Chief Business Officer. He was previously at OYO, with operational and supply-network roles.
Crediting the employees and educators on the platform, Kumar said, “Everything Unacademy has built is because of our Employees and Educators, who show up for learners every day.” He said the focus would remain on learner outcomes and a sustainable business.
Unacademy began as a YouTube channel in 2010 and became an edtech platform in 2015. It expanded rapidly during the pandemic, when demand for online learning surged. However, the reopening of classrooms and weakening online demand forced cost-cutting and restructuring at the company.
In September, upGrad completed an all-stock acquisition of Unacademy, which valued the company at about Rs 1,955 crore, roughly 94% below its peak in 2021.
The Competition Commission of India approved the combination in July. The deal brings Unacademy’s test-preparation, creator and language-learning businesses together with upGrad’s higher education, study-abroad, careers and corporate-skilling operations.
Munjal’s reference to upGrad's IPO (initial public offering) has wider significance. Under Ronnie Screwvala’s leadership, upGrad is working towards a planned listing in 2027, as it stitches together a larger, more diversified edtech business.
In FY26, upGrad’s consolidated revenue from operations rose to Rs 1,687 crore and its EBITDA rose more than eightfold to Rs 123 crore. Its consolidated net loss narrowed to about Rs 131 crore in the fiscal.
The edtech sector at large is also seeing a reset. According to Tracxn data, edtech funding in the first eight months of 2026 was about 95% below its 2021 peak, while funded rounds dropped from 368 to 36. The sector recorded 94 acquisitions and seven public listings between 2021 and 2026, including PhysicsWallah's listing in November 2025 following a Rs 3,480 crore IPO.
Meanwhile, government supervision in the sector is increasing. Central guidelines have called for transparency on coaching fees, courses and facilities, while the consumer regulator has warned institutes from making misleading success claims and guarantees.
Edited by Swetha Kannan

articles.title: Yet another major Japanese firm hacked — now furniture giant Nitori says hackers stole 37.6 million customer records
articles.text:
Yet another major Japanese firm hacked — now furniture giant Nitori says hackers stole 37.6 million customer records
The hole was plugged and attackers ousted
- Nitori discloses cyberattack that may have exposed data from up to 37.6 million customer records
- Stolen information included personal and business customer details, though passwords and payment data were unaffected
- Company remediated the intrusion, continues investigating the breach, and warned users about phishing attempts
Japan’s largest furniture chain Nitori Holdings has disclosed suffering a cyberattack which saw it lose tens of millions of customer records.
Both consumer and business customers are affected, but passwords and payment data have not been compromised.
In a statement, Nitori said it spotted unauthorized access to its systems on November 6 2026 - and after ousting the intruder and launching an investigation, the company discovered that up to 37.6 million of customer records may have been exfiltrated, including people’s first and last names, membership numbers, email addresses, postal addresses, phone numbers, gender information, as well as birth dates.
Nitori's warning
Aside from these records, corporate members also had their company names and department names exposed, as well as names of company representatives, phone numbers, designated contact persons, and other details.
The specific combination of information varies from customer to customer, it said, adding that the data was most likely generated by Nitori Net and Nitori’s official stores on third-party e-commerce marketplaces. The company also stressed that credit card information and login credentials were not exposed.
The investigation is currently ongoing and crucial details are still missing. We don’t know who the threat actors are, or if they reached out demanding payment in exchange for deleting the stolen files.
Nitori also said it identified the flaws used to break in, remedied them, but was still analyzing and monitoring them.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
“We have addressed the identified vulnerabilities and completed improvements to our monitoring systems”, it said.
“We are continuing to work with external specialists to investigate the cause of the incident, the method of intrusion, the extent of the impact, and whether any secondary damage has occurred.”
Often compared to IKEA, Nitori Holdings is considered Japan’s largest home furnishing retailer, selling affordable furniture, home accessories, kitchenware, and similar household products. It operates more than 1,000 stores across the region and 11 overseas markets, including China, Taiwan, South Korea, and a handful of Southeast Asian countries. Last year it reported $6.1 billion in revenue, while employing more than 41,000 people, and making almost 93 million customer purchases. Its mobile apps have more than 25 million registered members.
Those millions of members and thousands of employees are now being warned to pay attention to their inboxes for incoming email pretending to be from Nitori, or having to do something with the company and the breach.
“Personal information that may have been leaked could be misused for impersonation emails, phishing scams, suspicious telephone calls, and other fraudulent activities,” the company said in the announcement.
“We urge customers to exercise particular caution when receiving communications claiming to come from our company, delivery service providers, or e-commerce marketplaces.”
“Please do not open unfamiliar links or attachments.”
Japan under siege
There has been a barrage of cyberattacks against Japanese companies lately, with Iris Ohyama, a major Japanese consumer goods manufacturer, confirmed losing data on 7.7 million people in a data breach that affected its ecommerce website Iris Plaza.
Internet giant GMO also recently told its customers to unplug their devices from the network, after a cybercriminal threatened to release ransomware on user machines, and just before that gaming behemoth Capcom reported losing sensitive information on more than 11.7 million people. Most of them had their emails exposed, with a small subset also having to change their passwords.
Strangely enough, no threat actors claimed responsibility for any of these incidents. Usually, criminal organizations would try to extort money for the data, rather than trying to sell it on the black market, since some companies are more willing to pay. Leaking data could trigger class-action lawsuits or pressure from regulators and data watchdogs.

articles.title: Arrêter les dégâts « dans les 35 secondes » : OpenAI dévoile le kill switch censé stopper ses IA quand elles dérapent
articles.text:
Si l’été a été la saison des crises cyber chez OpenAI, l’automne doit être celle de la reprise en main.
L’entreprise américaine a dévoilé le 10 novembre Control Room, un service qui suit l’ensemble des modèles en activité dans son infrastructure de recherche et qui, selon le billet d’OpenAI, « interrompt la génération du modèle dans les 35 secondes suivant une décision d’intervention » lorsqu’un problème de sûreté ou de sécurité est détecté.
L’outil arrive après plusieurs mois agités. Le 21 juillet, OpenAI révélait notamment que plusieurs de ses agents étaient sortis de leur environnement de test et avaient piraté les serveurs de Hugging Face, la grande plateforme de partage de modèles d’IA.
En août, l’entreprise annonçait avoir suspendu une partie de ses entraînements pendant deux semaines afin de revoir sa sécurité, avant de les relancer. Ce qui n’a visiblement pas suffi. Le 20 septembre, un agent en cours d’entraînement a contourné les restrictions réseau de son bac à sable, ce qui a conduit OpenAI à suspendre de nouveau les travaux sur ses modèles les plus puissants.
Le modèle de surveillance avait bien levé une alerte au bout d’une douzaine de minutes, mais la tâche n’a été stoppée que près de 2 h 45 après le début de l’incident. C’est précisément ce délai que Control Room doit réduire.
Comment Control Room coupe une tâche
Concrètement, Control Room est conçu comme un verrou placé au cœur de l’inférence, comprenez le moment où le modèle produit ses réponses.
À son lancement, chaque tâche de recherche (expérience d’apprentissage par renforcement, évaluation, traitement de données) reçoit de Control Room un identifiant unique. Chaque fois qu’elle sollicite un modèle, le moteur d’inférence, autrement dit le modèle qui tourne sur les GPU, demande l’autorisation à Control Room en lui transmettant cet identifiant.
Lorsque le modèle de surveillance chargé d’examiner le comportement de l’IA repère un problème, il peut ordonner l’arrêt de la tâche, et toutes ses requêtes suivantes sont alors refusées.
OpenAI explique avoir placé ce verrou dans la couche d’inférence plutôt que dans le code des expériences, que les chercheurs modifient sans cesse et qui serait donc trop fragile pour porter une protection de sécurité. À l’inverse, l’inférence passe par un petit nombre de chemins communs à toute la recherche de l’entreprise, ce qui en fait un point de passage obligé.
Le système applique aussi le principe du « refus en cas de défaillance ». Si Control Room tombe en panne ou est désactivé, y compris de manière malveillante, toutes les requêtes sont bloquées jusqu’à son rétablissement.
Un délai que l’entreprise veut ramener à zéro
Pour l’instant, le blocage par défaut ne couvre que les travaux sur les modèles de pointe et doit être étendu au reste de la recherche dans les prochains jours. Les modèles accessibles au public ne sont pas concernés.
Les 35 secondes de latence s’expliquent par la quantité de requêtes à traiter. Faire valider chaque demande en temps réel par Control Room saturerait le service, alors OpenAI a ajouté une couche de mise en cache. Les moteurs gardent en mémoire pendant un court moment les autorisations qu’on leur a accordées, au lieu de reposer la question à chaque fois. OpenAI dit travailler à « ramener ce délai à zéro pour pouvoir arrêter les tâches instantanément ».
Avec cette solution, l’entreprise américaine cherche à rassurer, alors qu’au Congrès américain des élus veulent donner un droit de regard à l’État. Déposé le 23 juillet dans la foulée de l’incident Hugging Face, l’AI Kill Switch Act obligerait les géants de l’IA à garantir la capacité technique de stopper leurs modèles, et autoriserait le département de la Sécurité intérieure à leur en donner l’ordre en cas de perte de contrôle. Le texte est toujours en attente d’examen à la Chambre des représentants.

articles.title: Ley de Propiedad Horizontal: se puede prohibir el uso del ascensor a los vecinos que no paguen la comunidad en algunos casos
articles.text:
Que un vecino deje de pagar las cuotas de la comunidad o una derrama es un problema para todos. En estos casos, la comunidad de propietarios tiene herramientas más allá de limitarse a reclamarle la deuda, y entre otras cosas puede impedirle utilizar el ascensor mientras no se ponga al día. Esto se desprende de la Ley de Propiedad Horizontal, aunque siempre dentro de lo que marcan dos artículos concretos de la ley.
El papel de los artículos 6 y 21. El artículo 6 es el que ordena la convivencia, porque permite que el conjunto de propietarios fije normas de régimen interior para regular la utilización de los servicios y cosas comunes, unas normas que obligan a todos los titulares mientras no se modifiquen. Como el ascensor es un elemento común, su uso puede ordenarse por esa vía, pero los estatutos no sirven para privar de derechos de forma arbitraria a uno de los vecinos.
La herramienta realmente pensada para la morosidad está en el artículo 21.1, que desde la reforma de junio de 2022 permite a la junta de propietarios acordar medidas disuasorias mientras dure el impago. Tal y como recoge el texto del precepto, esas medidas pueden ir desde fijar intereses superiores al legal hasta la privación temporal del uso de servicios o instalaciones, siempre que no puedan considerarse abusivas o desproporcionadas y no afecten a la habitabilidad de los inmuebles. Además, no pueden tener carácter retroactivo, aunque la comunidad puede incluirlas en sus estatutos.
Vamos, que el artículo 6 sirve para poner reglas al uso del ascensor en el día a día, mientras que el 21 es el que abre la puerta a restringirlo, con límites, cuando un vecino no paga.
El caso del ascensor. La ley no menciona el ascensor por su nombre, y ese es el matiz, ya que dejar a alguien sin él puede chocar con el límite de la habitabilidad. Por eso hay que valorar las circunstancias del edificio y de cada propietario, y según el análisis de algunos expertos sobre un caso que ha llegado a la Audiencia Provincial de Alicante, la deuda por sí sola no convierte en legal la retirada del ascensor. Y esto es así porque se debe tener en cuenta la planta de la vivienda, las vías alternativas y si allí viven personas con discapacidad o mayores de setenta años. Sin embargo, el auto de la Audiencia no decide si la comunidad actuó bien, ya que se limita a la admisión de la demanda.
Eso sí, la medida tiene que ser temporal y estar ligada a la deuda, de modo que no puede convertirse en una sanción permanente. Y tampoco basta con que el presidente o el administrador decidan bloquear el ascensor por su cuenta, porque es la junta la que tiene que adoptar el acuerdo, y conviene dejar constancia de él en lugar de improvisar.
Reclamar la deuda es otra cosa. Pero restringir un servicio no sustituye a la reclamación del dinero. Las derramas aprobadas generan una deuda con la comunidad igual que las cuotas, y la ley permite exigir judicialmente los gastos comunes, ordinarios o extraordinarios, a través del proceso monitorio, sin perjuicio de que se puedan utilizar otros procedimientos judiciales.
El vecino también puede recurrir. Por su parte, el propietario afectado puede llevar el acuerdo a los tribunales si considera que es contrario a la ley o a los estatutos o que le causa un grave perjuicio, según prevé el artículo 18 de la ley. Aunque hay una condición que conviene tener presente si eres tú el que debe dinero, ya que para impugnar hay que estar al corriente de pago de las deudas vencidas con la comunidad o consignarlas judicialmente.
Al final, la comunidad puede reclamar lo que se le debe y, si se cumplen los requisitos, acordar a la vez restricciones mientras dure el impago, porque son dos mecanismos diferentes que no se excluyen.

articles.title: Le Vieux Continent se réveille ! La fusée Spectrum en route pour un 3e lancement
articles.text:
La fusée allemande Spectrum de la start-up Isar Aerospace accélère la cadence. Son troisième vol pourrait avoir lieu dès la fin du mois, un signal fort pour la souveraineté spatiale européenne.
En mars 2025, Spectrum réalisait son tout premier vol depuis Andøya, en Norvège. Si celui-ci s’est soldé par un échec, Isar Aerospace a vite souhaité remettre le pied à l’étrier. Après plusieurs reports, la société a retenté sa chance le 5 septembre dernier.
Et cette fois, tout s’était déroulé comme prévu : la fusée a atteint l’orbite et largué ses charges utiles. Une première pour une entreprise privée depuis l’Europe continentale, qu’elle compte réitérer très rapidement, révèle European Spaceflight.
Une fenêtre de tir approche
En effet, le troisième vol de Spectrum pourrait avoir lieu dès le 26 novembre. Un avis aérien publié le 28 octobre par Avinor, l’organisme norvégien de navigation aérienne, indique qu’une fenêtre de tir s’ouvre ce jour-là depuis Andøya, et reste valable jusqu’au 17 février 2027.
Ainsi, les tentatives seront possibles chaque soir entre 20h00 et 21h30. Si Isar Aerospace n’a pas encore communiqué de date précise, la fusée, elle, est en phase d’assemblage final, a fait savoir Daniel Metzler, son P.-D.G. Mais elle doit encore passer des tests avant de prendre la direction du pays nordique.
Pour ce qui est de la charge utile, on sait pour l’instant que le satellite AT-Astra de l’autrichien R-Space sera du voyage. Celui-ci embarquera les démonstrateurs technologiques de trois firmes européennes. Pour rappel, Spectrum est un lanceur à deux étages de 28 mètres de hauteur, pouvant placer jusqu’à 1 000 kilogrammes en orbite basse, ou 700 kg en orbite héliosynchrone. Il est donc idéal pour les petits et moyens satellites.
L'Europe accélère
Spectrum n’est pas la seule fusée privée européenne, bien qu’elle soit, à ce jour, la seule à avoir atteint l’espace. D’autres acteurs sont aussi sur le qui-vive, et l’European Launcher Challenge, lancé en août par l’Agence spatiale européenne (ESA), doit les galvaniser.
Celui-ci octroie à Isar Aerospace, ainsi qu’à l’allemande RFA et l’espagnole PLD Space, 540 millions d’euros pour accélérer le développement de leurs lanceurs respectifs. Ces dernières se préparent chacune pour un vol inaugural dès l’année prochaine. À noter que la française MaiaSpace pourrait bientôt les rejoindre.
L’enjeu est plus que jamais crucial pour le Vieux Continent qui, s’il peut s’appuyer sur Ariane 6 et Vega-C, a besoin de multiplier ses acteurs pour ne plus dépendre de puissances tierces.

articles.title: La UE quiere prohibir los patrones oscuros de la web. Lo curioso es que también ha empezado a regular los que todavía no existen
articles.text:
La Comisión Europea presenta hoy la 'Digital Fairness Act', y un borrador filtrado muestra que la UE quiere vetar diez trampas de diseño online. Entre ellas están las bajas que cuestan mucho más que las altas (ejem), los avisos de escasez que se repiten en cada paso del pago (ejem) y las notificaciones falsas que sugieren que alguien ha contactado con el usuario.
Son los patrones oscuros de siempre. Lo nuevo está en otras páginas del texto.
Por qué es importante. La lista negra llega con muchos años de retraso. Y como cara B, las partes menos llamativas del borrador llegan antes de tiempo.
- Una ataca el diseño persuasivo que es perfectamente legal y que sostiene el negocio de la atención.
- Otra fija por primera vez en el derecho europeo del consumidor normas para los agentes de IA que compran en nombre del usuario.
El giro. El borrador obliga a que cualquier usuario pueda apagar cuatro cosas:
- La reproducción automática.
- Las notificaciones que no tienen que ver con lo que ha hecho el usuario, sino que son otra forma de spam.
- Las rachas.
- Los chatbots que simulan una relación para que no te vayas.
Ninguna de estas tretas engaña a nadie, aunque sabemos que son bastante eficaces. El siguiente vídeo que empieza solo o la racha que da pena perder son decisiones de producto legales y súper rentables. Hasta ahora la UE perseguía el engaño como tal, pero ahora empieza a meterse con el enganche.
Sí, pero. La UE no está prohibiendo nada aquí, solo está obligando a poner un interruptor para poder apagar ciertas funciones o partes de la interfaz. Y las plataformas saben muy bien cuánta gente entra a hurgar en los ajustes: más bien poca.
En detalle. Lo de los agentes cabe en un par de líneas:
- El usuario decide qué compras tiene que aprobar.
- Y el agente tiene que avisar cuando una sugerencia es patrocinada.
Parece poca cosa, pero ahí va a estar la manipulación de los próximos años, y las primeras batallas ya se están librando. Cuando sea un agente quien compre, la trampa ya no será un botoncito gris al lado de uno verde al revés de como esperaríamos. Será una recomendación pagada, dicha en tono neutro, en una conversación que nadie más puede ver. La UE quiere que lleve etiqueta antes de que ese mercado exista.
Dientes, dientes. El texto prevé multas de hasta el 6% de la facturación mundial (como la DSA). Además, la directiva de 2005 pasa a ser un reglamento que se aplica igual en los 27 países. Y la Comisión podrá ampliar la lista sin volver a pasar por los legisladores. Una lista que crece sin tener que reabrir la ley es lo que más va a inquietar a la industria tecnológica.
Y ahora qué. Europa llega tardísimo a las trampas de la Web, que llevamos viendo –y sufriendo– desde principios de la década pasada.
Con las de los agentes, por una vez, ha llegado antes que ellas.

articles.title: Uncorking Queueing Bottlenecks with OpenTelemetry
articles.text:
Transcript
Oli Lane: A few years back, I have this really vivid memory of a customer complaint coming in. It was late on a Friday, of course, they always are. I was just letting my mind wander towards the pub, and this message comes through. It's a big customer, it's a customer we need to keep happy. They said, my backup job ran like an hour late, what's going on? They were pretty annoyed, rightly so, they need to trust that our backup product works, and it's solid and it's dependable. Of course, we dug in. We had our dashboards. We had our metrics. We had our logs. We had our alerts. We did some rooting around, we came up with some plausible theories. We put in a few fixes, a few improvements to make sure that any of the things that we suspected it was wouldn't happen again. I got to the pub a bit late, end of story.
There was this thing that didn't sit right with me and it was that we never really figured out the most important question, which was, why did that job run late and why was it late that time? It was like a murder mystery with the last chapter ripped out. It really annoyed me. This talk is the story of getting from there, where we're squinting at graphs and making a good guess, but mostly shrugging to being able to point and explain the exact bottleneck in a distributed asynchronous system.
Background
I'm Oli. I'm an engineering team lead at Gearset. I've worn many hats, but recently I've been focused on levelling up our observability and our incident response and our team culture as well so that we can build reliable, dependable software, especially as we scale.
Julian Wreford: I'm Julian. I've been part of Oli's team for the last three years as we've built out those observability tools and recently stepped into the team lead role for the team that Oli's been leading.
Oli Lane: From this talk, we're hoping you'll take away a practical knowledge of how to better understand the performance characteristics of your queues in particular, and we'll go through the foundations of OpenTelemetry and build on that to explain practical strategies that we've used to turn our queues from that point of confusion within our teams to something that we really feel confident running in production. We'll discuss different strategies to measure queue health, and then we'll finish off with some tips and tricks that we really wish someone had told us when we were getting started. You should go away better equipped to understand why metrics and logs aren't enough to truly understand your async workflows and how OpenTelemetry might help, how to know when your queue is healthy or unhealthy. How to empower your teams to measure and debug how customers are experiencing your system, and how to take that next step and get your teams adopting this stuff.
Why Queues?
Let's take a step back for a minute. Why do we need queues in the first place? Your system probably doesn't start with a queue right from day one. If you've got queues, you probably added them after hitting either a pain point or to resolve some architectural problem. For us, we started with all our code in a single monolith, looked a bit like that. We had multiple replicas of that monolith but only one image that actually shipped. At some point, we needed to organize that better and we decided to split off a few things to handle different responsibilities. Specifically, we wanted our scheduling code, so that was the code that was responsible for kicking off user jobs at specific times. We wanted that to run separately from our core application code. We did that in the simplest way possible. We spun up a new service, it had its own database.
To begin with, it would just poke a HTTP endpoint on the core app and it would kick off a job. Simple enough. That was a good start, but it had some immediate problems and some of these might feel familiar. We had no ability to smooth the load. We had a whole load of customer workloads configured on the scheduler, and one of those workloads was backups, and we let people pick when they wanted to run their backup. I don't know if you've ever given people a date, time picker for their backups but almost everyone picks midnight. Unfortunately, that meant that at midnight, our scheduler would suddenly DoS our application code with hundreds of requests to start some really heavy jobs in parallel. We could work around this in some ways. We could scale the application code or we could put bodges in the producer code and try and throttle it.
We could take the choice away from the users. Ultimately, these spikes were causing problems and we had no real way of dealing with them properly. Then, also, the workloads weren't truly decoupled. When you synchronously call via HTTP from one service to another and you expect a response, you still, in some ways, have a hard dependency between those services. One has to be up for the other one to work properly. We wanted to be able to take the app down without worrying whether the scheduler was up and what it was doing. Queues could solve both of those problems. Queues smoothed the load without the producer needing to know anything about the consumer. The scheduler could just dump a few hundred jobs on the queue and those consumers could pick them up at their leisure with sensible concurrency limits. Queues meant that if the consumers went down, we could build up a backlog and we could just let the app catch up when it got back online. These are not the only reasons you might introduce queues, but they were the main drivers for us. Of course, once we had one queue, everything looked like a nail and we had plenty of other sensible places to add our queues.
The next problem, as soon as you've got queues, is how to figure out if your queues are happy. We all know that software will always go wrong if it has a chance to. Whatever queuing technology you're using, whether it's SQS, Kafka, Rabbit, something else, you'll get some metrics emitted out of the box. These are some of the most common ones you'll have to work with. Queue size, the number of items currently on the queue. The enqueue rate, so how many items are being queued per time period. Dequeue rate, how many are being taken off per time period. Then the in-flight count, which is just how many are currently being processed. The basic idea here is if your enqueue rate is consistently higher than your dequeue rate, you're putting more into the bucket than you're taking out, and the queue size is going to grow. That could happen for loads of reasons.
Maybe half of your consumers blow up. Maybe you had got a big spike of traffic. Maybe the average time to process a message has gone up. When queue size is growing, messages are probably getting delayed, workloads are probably waiting, things are probably bad. That seemed like a good place to start, and we started monitoring those metrics. That went ok for a while. We ended up with tens of queues across multiple regions, and our monitoring was getting a little bit unwieldy, so we built these Grafana dashboards that grew and grew and grew, and some of them were more usable than others might be familiar.
Metrics Limits
One thing we noticed was that all of these queues weren't created equal. There were some queues where we were fine with the delay. They were the jobs which, ultimately, they ran in the background, and a few minutes of delay, not a problem, as long as they get done. There are some queues where delays would be noticeable for users. To keep track of what was healthy and what wasn't, we added alerting to the metrics that we had, but we had to tune each one of those based on the number of consumers that we expected and how large we were happy with that queue growing. Along the way, we did add one small improvement to the default metrics that we got out of the box. We created our own metric that measured how long the message had been on the queue, so when a message was received, we'd look at when that message was sent, and we'd calculate how long has that message been on the queue, and we'd track that, too.
You might get that out of the box, but we didn't. That meant we had the high-level view at any given time of what state the queue was in. We knew if it was backing up, and we knew if it was delaying workloads. That was good, but when something did start going wrong, our alerts are firing, metrics would tell us roughly where to look, but they wouldn't tell us much more. For more detail, we had to look in our logs, and that ended up meaning a lot of manual work. We'd sometimes burn hours chasing a phantom spike, and we'd never be particularly confident about any conclusion that we really came to. In a simple system, that manual work is probably tractable, but in a distributed system with lots of interconnected parts as it grows, it can quickly become an impossible task as your product scales.
OpenTelemetry Tracing Fundamentals
Julian Wreford: This was the point where we realized we needed to probably do something different. Our metrics were giving us the big picture, but they weren't giving us a whole lot more than that. If we had to follow up on questions, we couldn't ask them in hindsight without adding in more metrics and waiting for the issue to happen again. Metrics would give us the forest, but not the trees. Equally, our logs gave us plenty of detail at the level of each component of our system, but they were hard to connect to the wider picture. They were also very hard to follow through multiple components for complex requests, so they gave us the trees without the forest. We needed something that would do a bit different and go somewhere in the middle. Of course, we aren't the only people having these problems. A whole community sprung up around the idea of observability and how to inspect, debug, and operate complex systems.
The technology most people land on is OpenTelemetry. It's an open-source protocol, which allows you to do a lot of things, but for the purpose of this talk, we're going to focus on its support for distributed tracing. Distributed tracing, you can think of it a little like structured logs. We all know what a log is, and structured logs do what they say on the tin. They let you pass not just a string, but a structured set of keys and values, which allows you to query and filter the events a bit more easily. Traces are very similar, in that they are also made of a bunch of structured events with arbitrary keys and values. What traces have over structured logs is the ability to assign a hierarchy to those events, even when the events are produced by different parts of your system. The hierarchy allows you to group all of the events that stem from a single operation or customer request.
Logging this would probably be called like a correlation ID, but it also allows you to get a sense of the cause and effect relationship between events. What was the full sequence of events that led to an error or a delay? Which systems did the request pass through before this one? Of course, it's called distributed tracing, because this hierarchy can be preserved and reconstructed, even when different components are omitting different parts of the trace.
This is what a very simple trace might look like. You have a route span, which represents some interaction with an entry point to your system. This might be a customer hitting your API, and a number of child spans, which represent the activities that the system has to do to respond to the request. These spans might represent things like database requests, calls to other systems, or specific functions developers are interested in, and have added their own telemetry for. There are two interesting things here. One is the arrows representing the hierarchy of cause and effect, and the other is the horizontal axis, which represents the time, so we can see how long each duration lasted. Each of these spans has a name, which we've written in each box, but they can also have any other arbitrary attributes attached to them for analysis or querying purposes, and we want to make those as wide as possible.
The spans are connected by three special attributes defined by the OTel standard. There's the trace ID, which means that we can associate the span with the trace it belongs to, the span ID, which uniquely identifies the span itself, and the parent ID, which identifies which span preceded this one. All spans have a parent, apart from the route, which is defined by having no parent at all. This simple association of spans allows you to build up these tree-like structures that can be paired with a query engine, which allows us to query not just across spans, but also their relationships. As I'm sure many of you all know, OpenTelemetry support has grown rapidly across our ecosystems, and for us in the world of C#, there was good support straight out of the box. It didn't take us long to start seeing the value of how lots of operations connected to form a single customer request.
We even saw the traces automatically carrying on over HTTP boundaries. The trace above shows a parent span in our data service in the U.S. data residency region, which has a child on a completely different service, on a completely different region, because it's made a HTTP call out to that service. This is a screenshot from our query engine specifically. We use Honeycomb to analyze our trace data. You'll be seeing a bunch of screenshots from it in the rest of the talk. We're big fans of Honeycomb as a product, but there are other providers that offer similar things and they'll ingest OTel in similar ways.
That was HTTP calls, but when it came to following traces through queues, things weren't quite so plug and play. We find it really hard to do that because our traces are so long, because you might have to wait four hours to even decide whether to send any of the trace data, and so then all of your telemetry is four hours behind and that's not really very useful. If you have much shorter traces, you can do much more intelligent sampling. For us, it's still a little bit difficult, so I think that's one place where we think OpenTelemetry has a bit of room to grow, but our workaround is just spend a bit more money because it's worth it for us.
See more presentations with transcripts

articles.title: Don't talk about Call of Duty on a plane: a FaceTime chat triggered an airport evacuation
articles.text:
Facepalm: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 is among the latest in an unusually rapid string of well-regarded releases that made it to store shelves in the weeks leading up to Grand Theft Auto VI's launch, so people are naturally talking about it in public. However, fans should be careful to watch what they say while playing and discussing a military shooter at an airport to avoid a panic, as passengers in Ontario, California, learned this week.
According to Ontario police, a plane and the east wing of Terminal 2 at Ontario International Airport were evacuated on Sunday night after a passenger heard the words "bomb" and "explosion." It turned out the person mistook a conversation about Call of Duty for a bomb threat.
While detained, a person explained that they were playing Call of Duty on the plane before departure while talking with a friend over FaceTime. Someone else overheard them say "bomb" and "explosion" while describing the gameplay and alerted flight attendants. A sweep of the plane uncovered no explosive devices, and the flight eventually departed with everyone on board, including the detained person.
Police didn't reveal further details, but the person they detained might have been playing the latest Call of Duty title, Modern Warfare 4, on Nintendo Switch 2, the first portable device to receive a fully featured mainline entry. Critics have described Modern Warfare 4's campaign as the best in years, and the game launched to a warm reception on Steam on October 23. While being able to play the latest Call of Duty campaign on a flight might be novel enough to discuss over FaceTime, people should remember to avoid threatening-sounding language while traveling on public transportation, especially in Europe.
More than 20 flights between several European countries have been disrupted or diverted following hoax bomb threats over the past week. Most involved emails from unidentified individuals or groups claiming a bomb was aboard a plane, impacting flights to and from the United Kingdom, Ireland, Spain, Portugal, France, Belgium, Italy, Austria, the Czech Republic, Romania, Serbia, Bulgaria, Greece, Poland, Denmark, and Finland. Broadcasters in the UK and Ireland also received threats, but no explosives were found in any of the incidents. While no perpetrators have been identified, suspicion has turned toward Russia.
Although the Ontario incident occurred on a different continent, authorities may have understandably approached the situation with extra caution.

articles.title: Bald kannst du dein Bauchfett via Smartwatch messen
articles.text:
Samsung Galaxy Watch: Bald kannst du dein Bauchfett via Smartwatch messen
Laut Robert-Koch-Institut hat jede:r dritte Erwachsene in Deutschland einen deutlich erhöhten Bauchumfang. Das kann ein Indiz für zu viel inneres Bauchfett sein. Allerdings können auch Normalgewichtige von dem gefährlichen viszeralen Bauchfett betroffen sein, das tief in der Bauchhöhle liegend die inneren Organe umgibt.
Galaxy Watch soll viszerales Bauchfett messen
Je mehr davon vorhanden ist, desto größer ist das Risiko für Herzinfarkt oder Typ-2-Diabetes, heißt es von der Deutschen Adipositas-Gesellschaft. Mit einer neuen Funktion will Samsung Nutzer:innen künftig dabei unterstützen, speziell das gefährliche viszerale Bauchfett per Galaxy Watch präzise zu messen.
Wie Android Central schreibt, hat Samsung ein entsprechendes Patent angemeldet. Statt wie bisher per BIA-Sensor (bioelektrische Impedanzanalyse) soll dabei aber ein Ultrabreitband-Radar (UWB) zum Einsatz kommen. Bisher hat noch kein Galaxy-Watch-Modell ein solches Radar an Bord.
Bisher misst Samsung Körperfett per BIA-Sensor
Seit dem Launch der Galaxy Watch 4 im Jahr 2021 misst Samsung Körperfett per BIA-Sensor. Dabei handelt es sich aber eher um eine Schätzung als um eine konkrete Messung. Das viszerale Bauchfett um die Organe lässt sich so nicht bestimmen.
Mit der jetzt patentierten Methode würden Galaxy-Watch-Nutzer:innen per UWB-Radar den Bauchraum scannen. So soll sich das viszerale Bauchfett besser von dem sogenannten subkutanen Fett unterscheiden lassen, das sich direkt unter der Bauchdecke ansammelt.
UWB, BIA und allgemeine Angaben kombiniert
Die entsprechenden Ergebnisse soll das System dann mit den Daten des BIA-Sensors und allgemeinen Angaben wie Größe, Gewicht, Alter und Geschlecht kombinieren. Unklar ist derweil noch, wie genau die UWB-Messung vonstattengehen soll. Wahrscheinlich ist, dass Nutzer:innen die Uhr dazu zum Bauch führen müssen.
Die UWB-Hardware in eine kommende Smartwatch zu integrieren, sollte dagegen keine Herausforderung für Samsung sein. Schließlich produziert der Konzern schon Smart-Tags, die UWB unterstützen. Entsprechend geht Android Central davon aus, dass die neue Funktion schon mit der laut Phonearena für Juli 2027 erwarteten Galaxy Watch 10 kommen könnte.

articles.title: 10 funciones de la IA de Amazon para encontrar las mejores promociones durante las compras navideñas
articles.text:
La temporada navideña reúne miles de productos, descuentos temporales y cambios de precio que pueden dificultar la comparación antes de comprar. La inteligencia artificial (IA) de Amazon incorpora funciones para rastrear promociones, recibir avisos y organizar las compras desde la aplicación y el sitio web.
Estas herramientas permiten establecer precios objetivo, consultar la evolución de un artículo, detectar reposiciones y pedir sugerencias según listas o búsquedas previas. Algunas funciones pueden variar según el país, el producto y la versión de la aplicación, así que hay que revisar si están habilitadas en cada cuenta.
Cómo recibir alertas cuando un artículo baje de precio
Alexa para compras puede avisar cuando aparezcan promociones en categorías concretas o cuando un producto alcance un importe definido. Es posible pedir alertas para auriculares con cancelación de ruido o ingresar en la ficha de un artículo y solicitar una notificación cuando su valor baje.
De qué forma activar una compra automática con un precio límite
Quienes ya decidieron qué producto quieren comprar pueden fijar un valor máximo y autorizar la compra automática. La orden se completa con el método de pago predeterminado si el artículo baja hasta el importe establecido.
Antes de habilitar esta opción, resulta conveniente revisar la dirección de entrega, las condiciones de devolución y el presupuesto disponible para evitar compras que ya no sean necesarias.
Cómo consultar el historial de precios antes de elegir un producto
La opción Historial de precios muestra las variaciones registradas durante hasta un año en cientos de millones de productos de Amazon. Desde la página de detalles, el usuario puede comprobar si una rebaja actual coincide con precios anteriores o preguntar a Alexa si el artículo costó menos durante el último Black Friday.
Para qué sirve enviar una lista de compras por mensaje de texto
Amazon permite enviar a Alexa una nota escrita, una foto o un recordatorio mediante mensajes de texto. La herramienta busca y compara artículos relacionados con ese pedido, y luego responde cuando reúne alternativas.
De qué forma enterarse de lanzamientos y reposiciones de stock
La función “Avísame cuando” permite solicitar seguimientos sobre productos que todavía no están disponibles o que suelen agotarse. Puede utilizarse para pedir alertas ante nuevos sets de LEGO, novedades de una marca o la publicación de un libro de un autor determinado.
Cómo usar la barra de búsqueda para resolver dudas sobre una compra
La barra de búsqueda admite preguntas en lenguaje natural, una opción pensada para quienes aún no definieron un producto. Consultas como “¿Cómo elijo una aspiradora robot para hogares con mascotas?” pueden reducir la cantidad de resultados y orientar la comparación hacia funciones específicas.
Dónde encontrar ofertas personalizadas
Alexa puede mostrar promociones vinculadas con listas de deseos, historial de navegación y compras anteriores. Preguntas como “¿Cuáles son las mejores ofertas para mí?” o “¿Hay algún artículo de mi lista de deseos en oferta?” permiten acceder a una selección más acotada.
Cómo buscar un artículo a partir de una foto
Amazon Lens permite tomar una imagen, cargar una captura de pantalla o escanear un código de barras desde el ícono de cámara de la aplicación. Luego ofrece productos similares que pueden filtrarse por marca, color u otros detalles.
De qué forma ordenar regalos y seguir rebajas con las Listas de Amazon
Las Listas de Amazon ayudan a separar artículos por destinatario, ocasión o presupuesto. Se pueden compartir con familiares y amigos, trasladar productos entre listas y configurar alertas de ofertas para un artículo determinado o para una selección completa.
Cómo escuchar resúmenes y encontrar productos de otras tiendas
“Escucha lo más destacado” ofrece resúmenes de audio sobre características, reseñas y precio de artículos seleccionados, mientras que “Únete al chat” permite hacer consultas por texto o voz.
Asimismo, Shop Direct incorpora productos de otras tiendas en los resultados de Amazon y, en los casos habilitados, permite iniciar una compra sin salir de la plataforma. Ambas opciones amplían la búsqueda cuando el regalo elegido no aparece en el catálogo habitual.

articles.title: Pourquoi Nothing lance un boîtier IA sans écran alors que tout le monde s'y est cassé les dents — Frandroid
articles.text:
Depuis deux ans, Nothing répète que l’intelligence artificielle passe avant le reste. En 2024, Carl Pei, CEO de Nothing, avait même choisi de miser sur l’IA plutôt que de sortir son nouveau haut de gamme cette année-là. Le Phone (3) n’est finalement arrivé qu’en juillet 2025. Ce mercredi 11 novembre, Carl Pei a montré un premier aperçu de ce virage dans une courte vidéo publiée sur X, avec une phrase pour seul commentaire : « Le contexte ne vit pas dans un champ de discussion ». L’appareil en question n’a pas d’écran, il est pensé dès le départ pour l’IA, et Nothing veut le lancer dès décembre, sur un terrain où Humane et Rabbit se sont déjà cassé les dents.
    Pour aller plus loin
Montre, casque et enceintes : Nothing préparerait un virage vers les accessoires IA
            
Comme souvent chez Nothing, la vidéo montre très peu de choses. On y voit un objet aux formes courbes et à l’aspect métallique. Il porte deux LED allumées, une verte et une orange, ainsi qu’un bouton blanc avec un cercle rouge au centre.
Ce bouton pourrait servir à enregistrer des notes vocales analysées par l’IA, mais Nothing n’a rien confirmé. Le seul autre indice date du 4 novembre : dans un long billet intitulé « Toolmakers » publié sur X, Carl Pei écrivait que l’appareil « n’a pas de nouvel écran » et qu’il « n’aurait pas pu être une application », avant d’annoncer un lancement « le mois prochain ».
Humane et Rabbit ont déjà perdu ce pari
Il faut dire que les appareils dédiés à l’IA traînent un passé chargé. Le cas le plus connu est le Humane AI Pin, une broche sans écran à aimanter sur sa veste, qui projetait ses informations sur la paume de la main. Ses créateurs, deux anciens d’Apple, le présentaient comme un remplaçant du smartphone. Il a été vendu 699 dollars (environ 630 euros HT) à partir d’avril 2024, et les critiques ont été presque unanimement mauvaises. En février 2025, HP a racheté les actifs de Humane pour 116 millions de dollars (environ 105 millions d’euros), mais sans reprendre le produit. Les AI Pin ont cessé de se connecter aux serveurs le 28 février 2025, et ils ne pouvaient plus appeler, envoyer de messages ni répondre aux questions.
Le Rabbit R1, présenté au CES de janvier 2024, n’a pas fait beaucoup mieux. Ce petit boîtier orange vendu 199 dollars (environ 180 euros HT) promettait d’utiliser les applications à votre place, comme Spotify ou Uber, à partir d’une simple commande vocale. En septembre 2024, Jesse Lyu, fondateur et CEO de Rabbit, a pourtant admis qu’environ 5 000 personnes s’en servaient chaque jour, pour quelque 100 000 exemplaires vendus. En d’autres termes, 5 % des acheteurs. Dans les deux cas, les testeurs ont fait le même reproche : un smartphone faisait à peu près tout ce que faisaient ces gadgets, et le plus souvent plus vite.
Nothing veut sortir l’IA de la fenêtre de discussion
Le slogan de Carl Pei vise en fait les chatbots comme ChatGPT, où il faut taper ou dicter sa demande dans une fenêtre et réexpliquer la situation à chaque fois. À en croire la formule, l’appareil de Nothing chercherait à saisir ce contexte par lui-même, mais la marque n’a rien dit de ses capteurs. La mention « pas de nouvel écran » laisse penser qu’il s’appuiera sur les écrans déjà là, à commencer par celui du téléphone. Sur le papier, ce serait une vraie différence avec l’AI Pin, qui voulait remplacer le smartphone au lieu de l’accompagner.
Nothing ne sera pas seule sur ce créneau pour autant. En juillet, Bloomberg a révélé que le premier appareil d’OpenAI dessiné avec Jony Ive, l’ancien designer d’Apple, serait une enceinte sans écran, équipée d’une caméra, comme l’a relayé The Next Web. OpenAI viserait une présentation cette année et une sortie en 2027 seulement.
Carl Pei n’a donné ni nom, ni prix, ni liste de fonctions. D’après son billet, le lancement est prévu pour décembre 2026, ce qui laisse quelques semaines à Nothing pour montrer ce que son appareil fera de plus qu’un smartphone.

articles.title: Trump wanted little Kei trucks for America, Toyota makes it happen
articles.text:
The idea that Americans should be offered a greater choice of smaller cars has support from strange bedfellows indeed. After all, who could forget President Trump—usually one to take a maximalist approach to any problem—announcing last year that he wanted the Department of Transportation to make Japan’s diminutive “Kei” cars legal here in the US.
Ars’ attempts to get DoT to tell us more about the potential influx of little vehicles have mostly fallen on deaf ears. But this week, there has been movement on the topic, with Toyota announcing that it will bring back the Scion brand with the KEI-01.
What’s a Kei car?
In the US, the preponderance of humongous SUVs is a consequence largely of government policies, specifically corporate average fuel economy standards that made it less profitable to sell smaller, efficient cars. Japan’s Kei cars are what happens if the government instead restricts the size, engine capacity, and power output.
A Kei car must fit within the following dimensions: 11.2 feet (3.4 m) long, 4.9 feet (1.5 m) wide, and 6.6 feet (2 m) tall, with an engine displacement of no more than 0.66 L and an output of 63 hp (47 kW) or less. That’s a far cry from the more than 16 feet (4.9 m) of a full-size pickup truck, but it makes sense for a country where you’re not allowed to buy a car unless you have somewhere to park it, with those spaces being at an absolute premium.
Being affordable to buy and economical to run sure doesn’t hurt either, and last year, Japan bought almost 1.7 million Kei cars, out of total sales of 4.6 million vehicles. Depending on where you live in the US, it can be varying degrees of difficult to import a Kei car, at least until now.
Scion is back?
Toyota killed off its Scion sub-brand more than a decade ago, ending the haggle-free approach and cars aimed at younger buyers in favor of selling more Toyotas. But now it’s back as “Scion by Toyota,” which the automaker will apparently use to experiment with less traditional ideas. But forget about a cool-but-boxy EV in the mold of the Honda N-One or Nissan Sakura.

articles.title: With $720M round, Britain's Fractile gets a leg up in the race for AI chips | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Fractile, a British startup developing AI chips, has raised a $720 million Series C backed by Britain’s Sovereign AI Fund with hopes of “ensuring the U.K. has a greater stake in the hardware that will underpin its future economy,” its government stated.
Alongside the likes of Axelera, Etched, and OLIX, this makes Fractile one of the top-funded startup players in the race for purpose-built AI chips. Such chips are one of several avenues being explored to reduce the cost of inference — aka using increasingly demanding AI models in production.
However, Fractile seeks to go beyond hardware with a full-stack approach that also includes a machine learning compiler to maximize the speed at which LLMs will get executed on its chips.
As a result, the company frames itself as a frontier AI company, and its latest round led by Thrive Capital, Founders Fund, Lightspeed Venture Partners, and Redpoint was priced accordingly. According to the British government, the valuation was “over £5 billion” — quite possibly $7 billion, a figure reported both by the Financial Times and a Reuters source.
Still, Fractile’s main differentiator will arguably be its hardware design. After a pivot, its approach now revolves on DRAM, the most common type of RAM, but stacked on top of each chip in such a way that it is hoping will bypass the usual trade-off between memory and capacity.
This trade-off has become more problematic with the rise of agentic AI, as companies seek to perform longer chains of tasks with large models without compromising on speed. As compute struggles to keep up, hopes are high for AI chips, despite their limited availability to date.
In a LinkedIn post, Fractile CEO Walter Goodwin wrote that “there is still a lot of work ahead” for the company, and that the new funding will enable the startup to “ship [its] first chips and systems next year.”

articles.title: En Reino Unido han encontrado el mejor uso posible para los árboles de Navidad: enterrarlos en la playa
articles.text:
Cientos de voluntarios en la costa situada al sur de Blackpool, Inglaterra, cavan zanjas en la arena cada año y las llenan con árboles de Navidad desechados. Llevan más de una década reuniéndose con el objetivo de reconstruir una defensa costera natural que casi ha desaparecido por completo.
Medida de contención. Las dunas son la principal protección que muchos hogares del condado de Lancashire tienen contra el mar. Amy Pennington, de la Lancashire Wildlife Trust, declaraba a The Guardian en febrero que las dunas de arena son “la única forma de defensa costera” con la que cuenta la comunidad local. También amortiguan el impacto de las olas de las tormentas, protegen del viento lo que hay detrás de ellas y pueden reconstruirse a sí mismas después de una tormenta utilizando la arena arrastrada mar adentro.
Sin embargo, la costa ha perdido aproximadamente el 80% de sus dunas desde mediados del siglo XIX, según Pennington, a medida que las localidades de Blackpool y Lytham St Annes se expandían sobre ellas.
Cómo funciona. Los voluntarios entierran los árboles en zanjas poco profundas, dejando las ramas superiores expuestas. Cuando sopla el viento, las acículas y las ramas atrapan los granos de arena, y se forma gradualmente un montículo alrededor de cada árbol. La Wildlife Trust afirma que esto puede producir nuevas dunas en un plazo de entre seis meses y un año, un proceso que llevaría siglos en la naturaleza, según comparten desde Sky News.
Tras ello, el barrón, que es la planta perenne que crece en los arenales marítimos, coloniza la arena. La BBC comparte que las raíces de la hierba ayudan a mantener unida la duna, y éstas pueden alcanzar hasta 100 metros. Una vez que los árboles se pudren, pasan a formar parte de la propia duna.
En cifras. El proyecto está dirigido por la Lancashire Wildlife Trust junto con el Ayuntamiento de Fylde y la Agencia de Medio Ambiente, y lleva funcionando en su forma actual desde hace más de una década. Los voluntarios llevan enterrando árboles en estas playas desde hace más de 30 años, según cuentan en The Guardian. Este año, 650 voluntarios enterraron aproximadamente unos 2.000 árboles en la playa de Lytham. Pennington declaraba a Sky News en 2024 que el trabajo ha añadido unos 90 metros de dunas a lo largo de la playa, en un lugar donde antes no había ninguna.
Degradación. El manual de dunas de arena de Natural England calcula que el Reino Unido ha perdido alrededor del 30% de sus dunas desde 1900, según The Guardian. Durante el mismo periodo, el nivel del mar ha subido unos 19,5 cm, y dos tercios de ese incremento se han producido en los últimos 30 años, según revelaba un estudio publicado en la Royal Meteorological Society. Pennington cuenta que las mareas de tempestad más frecuentes empujan ahora la marea más arriba en la playa, erosionando las dunas con mayor frecuencia y exponiendo potencialmente a los hogares costeros a inundaciones.
No es solo defensa costera. Las nuevas dunas son también un refugio para la fauna silvestre, como ocurre con las dunas de la costa de Fylde, que están catalogadas como lugar de especial interés científico, según comparte la BBC. Estas dunas albergan plantas y animales de importancia nacional e internacional. Los lagartos de arena, uno de los reptiles más raros del Reino Unido, se pueden encontrar en este ecosistema. Cientos de ejemplares fueron liberados en las dunas de Lytham St Annes en 2020, tras 60 años desaparecidos.
Andy Singleton-Mills, gestor de conservación de la zona del Ayuntamiento de Fylde, contaba a The Guardian que los guardas ven más ejemplares cada año, incluidos lagartos más jóvenes, una señal de que se están reproduciendo. Ahora, avistar uno es otra cuestión, pues afirma que los reptiles huyen de las personas, lo que hace que encontrarlos sea como buscar “una aguja en un pajar”.
Los árboles. Después de que terminen las fiestas de Navidad, los árboles son donados por residentes, organizaciones benéficas y empresas, y los voluntarios afirman que eso forma parte del atractivo. “Es lo último que se te ocurriría, pero es fantástico”, contaba una de las voluntarias, Lisa Kneadle, a la BBC.
Y ahora qué. Pennington contaba al medio que, en un plazo de unos cinco años, el equipo tendrá que empezar a construir dunas hacia arriba en lugar de hacia fuera, hacia el mar de Irlanda, porque la marea alcanzará cada vez más a las existentes. Espera que las dunas más recientes, que pueden alcanzar unos 3 metros de altura, aguanten con suerte indefinidamente.

En Xataka | Tras 110 años extinto en una parte de Argentina, un viaje de 3.200 kilómetros ha traído de vuelta al guanaco
