articles.title: Plurai wants to help AI agents work better using the same approach that helped get self-driving cars to roads | TechCrunch
articles.text:
AI agents are all the rage, but they’re not quite as capable as their purveyors would have you believe.
Efforts to benchmark agents doing complex tasks show that they aren’t typically reliable enough to function without close supervision. LiveBench 2.0 shows Claude Fable 5.2 and ChatGPT-6 Astra succeeding on 82.9 and 75.6 out of 100 tasks, respectively, and an effort by the AI infrastructure company EON to test agents in a simulated corporate environment found the most successful model tested, Claude Opus 4.8, performed tasks at 76.8% accuracy.
Now, a startup known as Plurai wants to boost those numbers with the same techniques that put self-driving cars on the street: Simulations using synthetic data based on a company’s own digital systems, meant to prepare models to tackle difficult edge cases.
Co-founders Ilan Kadar and Elad Levi previously worked for Nexar, which develops autonomous driving technology. Kadar worked with Waymo to simulate and evaluate its end-to-end deep learning driving software.
“The moment that we saw the wave of AI agents, we saw the same pattern: That it is very easy to build a demo, but [hard] to get something that will be reliable and cost effective,” Kadar told TechCrunch. “Since we saw the same pattern, the same pitch was that we want to build this simulation layer.”
On Wednesday, the startup said it had raised $13 million in seed funding to make that happen. The round was led by Team8, with participation from U&I, Velocity, and Mercer.
Like the end-to-end models trained to drive cars, AI agents are probabilistic systems operating in unpredictable environments. When pressed by customers, agents tasked with booking travel can ignore spending policies. Or, when tasked with querying one database, agents can reliably provide an answer, but combining information from multiple datasets tends to gum up the works. A long conversation with a customer service bot can overwhelm an agent with too much context and lead to wrong turns.
To fix that, Plurai creates a digital twin of the company’s electronic systems, including the knowledge base and tools that an agent will have access to in production. It then maps all the possible flows of the agents and uses that graph to prepare the model with evaluations and fixes for possible edge cases. The platform works alongside existing agentic tools like Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, and Cursor.
However, Kadar says the company’s real promise is using the data it gathers to post-train small, open-weight models tailored to individual customer needs. Tests performed in cooperation with Nvidia and Nebius showed the company’s models outperforming midtier frontier models at lower costs.
“We can take a large language model, we can take the task, decompose it into a smaller task using the simulation, train [an open-weight] model, and using the simulation, verify that the quality is higher or comparable to the frontier model, and an order or two orders of magnitude cost reduction,” he said.
Reah Miyara, a Google DeepMind researcher who backed Plurai as an angel investor, said the company’s edge comes from understanding failure modes in production, and generating synthetic data to tune models. As businesses try to optimize their AI expense, Plurai’s approach could prove a real advantage, since IT leaders are seeing that “frontier-capable models are out of distribution with my specific data, and the cost of these things isn’t sustainable in the long term,” Miyara said.
Plurai hopes analogies between AI agents in physical and digital environments can prove predictive: While powerful general AI models are imbuing robots with fascinating capabilities, they aren’t yet reliable enough to be deployed widely. Meanwhile, robots powered by AI models built for specific tasks are in the field right now, working for customers and gathering valuable real-world data.
“My view is that no matter how smart OpenAI and Anthropic model will be — and they will be much smarter — they will not know your business and your policy,” Kadar said.

articles.title: Nvidia contrata empresa para encontrar substituto de Jensen Huang, diz agência
articles.text:
O conselho de administração da Nvidia contratou uma empresa externa para identificar possíveis substitutos para Jensen Huang, fundador e CEO da companhia. A iniciativa ocorre em meio à crise provocada por revelações sobre relacionamentos extraconjugais do executivo, incluindo um caso com uma empresária suspeita de atuar para a inteligência chinesa.
A informação foi divulgada pela Bloomberg, com base no relato de uma pessoa familiarizada com o assunto. Segundo a reportagem, os conselheiros também avaliam a possibilidade de nomear um CEO interino enquanto procuram um substituto definitivo.
Integrantes do conselho se reuniram nesta quarta-feira (11) para discutir o futuro de Huang.
A possibilidade de uma mudança no comando ganhou força depois que o The Wall Street Journal publicou que o conselho estaria se preparando para afastar o executivo. A nova informação indica que a companhia já começou a considerar alternativas para eventual saída do fundador.
Crise envolve dois relacionamentos extraconjugais
- A crise começou quando Huang admitiu ter mantido um relacionamento extraconjugal com Alice Huang, executiva da Megaspeed International, empresa de Singapura que está entre os grandes clientes da Nvidia no Sudeste Asiático;
- A empresária é suspeita de atuar como agente do governo chinês, segundo informações atribuídas a autoridades de inteligência dos Estados Unidos;
- A Megaspeed também está sob investigação americana por possível participação no contrabando de chips. Tanto a Nvidia quanto a empresa negaram irregularidades, enquanto Pequim rejeitou as acusações de espionagem;
- A situação se agravou depois que o The New York Times publicou que Huang também teria mantido um relacionamento com Kimberly Powell, vice-presidente de saúde da Nvidia, que responderia diretamente ao CEO. A reportagem citou pessoas que trabalharam na companhia;
- Os relatos colocaram o conselho diante de uma decisão delicada. Afastar Huang significaria substituir o único CEO que a Nvidia teve desde sua fundação, em 1993. Por outro lado, mantê-lo no cargo pode prolongar a pressão de parlamentares, investidores, clientes e funcionários sobre os relacionamentos do executivo e os possíveis riscos para informações confidenciais da companhia.
Leia mais:
- Nvidia: quem é Lori Huang, esposa de Jensen Huang que ficou no centro de escândalo
- Investidor de 31 anos investigou Nvidia meses antes de escândalo envolvendo CEO
- Congresso dos EUA pode intimar CEO da Nvidia por caso envolvendo suposta espiã chinesa
Nvidia não tem plano de sucessão definido
A crise também expôs a falta de plano de sucessão para Huang. Aos 63 anos, o executivo é considerado uma figura central para a identidade e o desempenho da Nvidia, que se tornou a principal fornecedora de chips para o desenvolvimento de inteligência artificial (IA).
Além de comandar a empresa, Huang atua diretamente em negociações e investimentos na cadeia de fornecimento de IA e em startups do setor. Também é um dos principais porta-vozes da indústria, defendendo os benefícios da IA e minimizando preocupações sobre seus riscos.
A influência do fundador ajuda a explicar a dificuldade de encontrar um substituto. Sua eventual saída poderia ter consequências que ultrapassam as operações da Nvidia e atingem o mercado de tecnologia como um todo.
Após a divulgação das reportagens sobre os relacionamentos de Huang, as ações da Nvidia caíram 8% nas negociações estendidas de quarta, segundo a Bloomberg.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: Three People Arrested for AI-Enhanced Impersonation Fraud - Schneier on Security
articles.text:
Three People Arrested for AI-Enhanced Impersonation Fraud
It’s hard to believe how lucrative this crime can be:
According to a press release from the United States attorney’s office for the southern district of New York, three men  Jacob Soall, Sharon Hazan, and Guy Sheetrit  were arrested for using AI to alter and impersonate the voices and images of executives and attorneys at various companies in order to convince employees to send over large payments. Soall and Hazan were arrested in Spain over the summer, while Sheetrit was arrested in the United Kingdom in September. The alleged fraud took place between 2024 and 2026.
With the help of AI, the men allegedly acted as a corporate executive, targeting employees of various companies and telling them they needed their help with sensitive financial transactions. They would then instruct the employees to get in touch with lawyers at a large international law firm. The men would then impersonate a lawyer at these firms and have the employees wire a large amount of money.
The men ultimately stole more than $129m from companies all over the world including in the US, according to the DoJ.
Always remember that there are three parts of AI security: security of AI, security with AI, and security from AI. This is the third.
Clive Robinson • November 11, 2026 7:36 AM
@ Bruce, ALL,
Most new technologies bring a new looking form of fraud with them.
Eventually either people get used to it and the fraud success rate drops, or the technology goes out of fashion / use.
I used to know an accountant who was indirectly at the heart of the first major fraud by Fax Machine.
The details are dull you just need to know that a previous technology called Telex had a legal status and people assumed it carried forward with faxes (it did not).
There are still remnants of Telex hanging around, but faxes appear to have been consigned to the under the desk basket of history.
Thus the question,
“How long before Current AI and ML systems suffer those or similar fates and which will be first?”
Take YouTube, a friend was looking at some cooking videos, they asked me if using sweet potatoes to make cakes was possible as they had seen one or two vids that had them in “healthy cake making”.
I pointed out that you can substitute cold mashed potatoes for sone flour in breads and some cakes as I’d done it (similar with rice flour) but I’d not tried sweet potatoes as I did not think it would work well.
So we looked through a few vids and it quickly became clear they were all copies of each other with different faces and stuff in the background moving from shot to shot. And importantly there was a US flag in each and every one of then…
It then became clear as they all promoted certain types of sham products, but importantly asked you to contact them through the comments.
For those that do not know there are fairly strict rules and regulations about pushing things, but… If you interact first through the comments then they mostly don’t apply in the US.
So these scammers know how to get things to work, and in many cases will get away with it even if the money they make is “small potatoes”.
Hence why some scammers have in effect “followed the money” with these “scamming corporates” doing it via social engineering of the employees…
Ask yourself,
“Who is really to blame, the ‘running scared or overworked’ employee or their corporate bosses…

articles.title: Toyota’s Scion is back, starting with an American-made, 25-mph kei truck
articles.text:
Toyota is dusting off the Scion badge for a radically different mission. Rather than targeting youth-market hatchbacks, “Scion by Toyota” is being positioned as an experimental mobility incubator — and its first vehicle is an authentic Japanese-style kei truck built in Indiana.
Toyota’s Scion is back, starting with an American-made, 25-mph kei truck
Toyota is reviving the Scion badge as an experimental mobility incubator—starting with an Indiana-built, 25-mph kei truck engineered for American fleets.
Kei vehicles, which are built to satisfy Japan’s light vehicle regulations, are enjoying surging popularity around the world, including here in the US. More than 30,000 used kei trucks have been imported into the US since 2020, with roughly 7,500 units entering the country each year. Even President Trump is a fan, telling reporters last year that he authorized the Department of Transportation to approve their production.
Toyota looks to be the first to test the American market’s appetite for the tiny trucks. The choice to use the Scion brand, which was discontinued in 2016, would seem to indicate that the automaker is hoping to appeal to younger car buyers. But more than that, Toyota says it sees Scion as a testing ground for utility, outdoor adventure, and customization that wouldn’t typically fit in any of its other models.
When it lands in the second half of 2027, Scion’s KEI-01 sports a 660cc three-cylinder gas engine paired with a continuously variable transmission. It won’t win any drag races, but it should delivery enough power for stop-and-go driving while using a minimum amount of fuel.
It’s true super power comes from its diminutive dimensions. At roughly 11 feet long and under 5 feet wide, the KEI-01 is about half the footprint of a full-size pickup. It can easily thread through cramped alleys, narrow barn aisles, garden gates, or busy campus pathways where standard trucks can’t fit.
The truck features an on-demand 4WD system with a push-button locking mode. If you’re cutting across muddy farm turf, gravel work paths, or wet slush, power splits to all four wheels to keep the truck from spinning out or getting stuck.
Inside, the vehicle looks pretty cheap, with lots of black plastic and a noticeable absence of any premium materials. That will hopefully help keep the price nice and low — though Toyota hasn’t disclosed any trim options yet. Japanese imports typically range from $6,000 to $12,000.
Because it is certified under federal Low-Speed Vehicle (LSV) rules — also used for golf carts and golf cart-adjacent vehicles — its top speed is strictly capped at 25 mph. The truck bed features three sides that fold completely flat, removing the need to lean over high-metal sides to drop in cargo. The KEI-01 can hold up to 600 pounds of soil, tools, or gear, and can easily tow small utility trailers or mowers.
Unlike an open utility cart or ATV, this tiny truck has a fully sealed cabin equipped with both heating and air conditioning. The extended roofline gives drivers extra headroom, reclining seats, and interior storage behind the seats to keep tools dry and secure. True to classic Japanese utility imports, the steering wheel is on the right side of the cab. Beyond the cool factor, curbside delivery and stepping directly onto sidewalks or worksite shoulders is quicker and safer.
To make the KEI-01 to conform to the rules and regs of auto manufacturing in the US, Toyota is investing $34 million into its Princeton, Indiana manufacturing plant to stand up local assembly and add roughly 50 jobs. Production kicks off in the second half of 2027, but everyday drivers won’t be able to buy one off the lot immediately.
Scion by Toyota is launching the mini-truck strictly as a fleet-focused pilot program targeting corporate campuses, farms, municipalities, and local delivery operators, distributed through a specialized group of existing Toyota dealerships. While Toyota notes it may consider opening up sales to consumer retail down the road if demand justifies it, the initial rollout is very much treated as an experiment to evaluate real-world US utility.
The KEI-01 was joined by two adventure-themed concepts that show Scion’s new focus extends far beyond budget hatchbacks. The SxS Concept packs a 300-plus-horsepower hybrid turbo setup for high-speed off-roading, while the modular BKE Concept explores compact personal mobility. Together, they signal that Scion’s second act is aimed squarely at niche utility and experimental recreation.
Images by Toyota

articles.title: Jack Newton’s tips for a $1 billion acquisition
articles.text:
It’s been just over one year since legaltech firm Clio acquired AI research platform vLex for $1 billion USD, and Jack Newton, Clio’s founder and CEO, is marking the occasion by sharing some lessons he learned from the historic deal.
The news: Newton posted to LinkedIn on Tuesday some thoughts on how his team successfully executed what he called “the most consequential change in our company trajectory,” two years after the company raised what was, at the time, the largest software funding round in both Canadian tech and legal tech history.
From the source: Newton wrote that the top focus post-purchase was on how the two teams could closely integrate their work. “A strategic thesis only matters if the company can execute against it,” Newton wrote, adding that they were able to bring in 400 new employees and launch a new product (Clio Work) in just three months by following that strategy.
The context: While Clio’s post-acquisition path hasn’t been without speed bumps, the deal has broadly been a significant success for the company, and one of just a few of its size in Canadian tech. It’s not the first time that Newton has pulled back the curtain; in September, he spoke out about the need for Canadian VCs to pay more to give domestic companies a “home-field advantage.”

Nvidia’s governance problem
For better or worse, Jensen Huang is Nvidia. Now that he’s admitted to having an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, what’s next for the chipmaker at the centre of the global AI boom? There’s a lot we still don’t know about the situation, but the board has launched an investigation into its chief executive, even though it has no clear succession plan.
Huang’s ability to carry the company on his shoulders and manage more than 50 direct reports was once lauded; now, Nvidia is learning that a flat leadership structure is not without risk.
Mark your calendars
Anthropic updated its IPO filing this week, setting itself up to become a publicly traded company potentially worth $1.4 trillion next Thursday, Nov. 19. The IPO is already reported to be multiple times oversubscribed, with an estimated price between $70 and $78 per share. Each of its seven co-founders is set to cash out about $250 million.
Emerge’s fund fiasco
The Ontario Capital Markets Tribunal has found that former fund manager Emerge Canada, which sold Toronto-listed versions of Cathie Wood’s ARK ETFs, diverted about $6 million from its suite of ETFs over three years to prop up its businesses. The tribunal will determine the mismanagement penalties at a later hearing. Wood and ARK weren’t involved in the improper behaviour.
The “reverse engineering” fun is over
After months of people using AI tools to hack gated electronics, install new operating systems on their smart TVs, and unbrick abandoned internet-of-things devices, 404 Media reports that users trying to “Reverse Engineer Anything” are now being blocked by guardrails inside Anthropic or OpenAI’s models. This “suggests that the future of the practice lies in open-weight, local, and uncensored models, making it less accessible to the masses and the people who could probably benefit from it most.”
No changes expected to C-22
Canada’s Minister of Public Safety Gary Anandasangaree told the National Post that he doesn’t anticipate any changes to the Lawful Access Act. The minister’s statement runs counter to strong pushback from tech companies, civil liberties groups, Canada’s privacy watchdog, and even some senators, who argue the bill will need further amendments to better protect the privacy of Canadians. It’s still before the Senate, so the debate isn’t over yet.

articles.title: Estos son los tres portátiles que elegiría en este Black Friday
articles.text:
Es una de las compras más importantes que realizamos: un portátil con el que poder trabajar, estudiar desde casa o simplemente ver series y películas. Todos tenemos uno en casa y cuando toca cambiar, quizá es inevitable sentirse abrumado por todas las ofertas y equipos diferentes que hay. Por eso, aprovechando que viene el Black Friday, hemos seleccionado tres portátiles que representan una compra muy inteligente, por todo lo que ofrece y con un precio de lo más ajustado.
La clave en primer lugar está en acudir a una tienda que genere seguridad y facilidad de compra. Que si nos surge cualquier contratiempo, nos puedan ayudar de manera personalizada. Es ahí donde PcComponentes destaca por encima del resto: precios bajos, una oferta enorme y todas las garantías de compra necesarias.
Lenovo IdeaPad
Son los portátiles de Windows más populares en los últimos diez años. Lenovo se ha especializado en lanzar portátiles para todo tipo de usuarios, desde los que necesitan un uso más básico a uno más completo. La gama IdeaPad es la más equilibrada, con precios no muy altos pero con características muy interesantes.
En PcComponentes hemos encontrado dos modelos que están muy bien. Por un lado, el Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3, con pantalla de 15,3 pulgadas y procesador Intel Core 5. Lo completa una configuración de 16GB de RAM y 1TB de almacenamiento SSD. Podrás guardar de manera local todo lo que necesites porque esta capacidad es una pasada. Es un equipo muy bien construido, fino pero con sensación de resistencia. Tiene un precio habitual de 799 euros pero ahora mismo lo tienes por 649 euros. Es uno de los portátiles más vendidos, y por algo será.
El segundo modelo es muy similar, misma familia IdeaPad Slim 3 pero cambian algunas cosas. Por ejemplo, el tamaño de la pantalla que crece hasta los 15,6 pulgadas. El procesador también cambia, desde Intel a AMD, en concreto el AMD Ryzen 5. El almacenamiento también disminuye y se queda en 512GB. Estas pequeñas diferencias hacen que su precio también se reduzca, llegando a los 529 euros. Si tienes un presupuesto más ajustado, este modelo no te defraudará.
MacBook Neo
Es el portátil del año, el que más ha llamado la atención por su diseño pero sobre todo por su rendimiento teniendo en cuenta el precio que tiene. El llamado "MacBook barato" es perfecto para el 99 por ciento de la población. SU chip A18 es capaz de ejecutar prácticamente cualquier aplicación. Está disponible en varios colores y, ahora, con un descuento de 40 euros.
Estos han sido sólo tres portátiles en oferta pero hay muchos más, déjate caer por la web de PcComponentes y encontrarás muchos más.

articles.title: Variable-Length Prompts on Chimera GPNPU
articles.text:
Home >

                                                                Variable-Length Prompts on Chimera GPNPU                                                    
Low Power-High Performance
                        WHITEPAPERS
		
How a flexible binary can serve every length up to the capacity you set.
								November 11th, 2026 - 
								By: Quadric.io
								
							
If you are sizing a language model for an edge product, the prompts it will see span a wide range. A spoken command is a dozen tokens, a pasted document is several thousand, and the same device serves both. Somewhere in the software stack, a decision is made about the gap between the longest prompt you provisioned for and the prompt that actually arrives. That decision sets how many binaries you build and qualify. It also sets how much of every inference is spent computing padding.
Most compiled inference stacks do not make that decision at all. A graph compiled for 1024 tokens processes 1024 positions every time it runs. If you send it 50 tokens, it computes the other 974 as padding. To serve short prompts efficiently as well as long ones, you have to build a separate binary for each length range and qualify all of them. Quadric Chimera GPNPU does not work this way. It gives you one guarantee and one optimization.
Read more here.

At electronica 2026 in Munich, EE Times talks with Lars Reger, CTO of NXP Semiconductors, about the physical AI era and how it reaches far beyond humanoid robots.
Lars introduces NXP’s new NavQ95 platform, built on the i.MX 95. It comes with reference designs, complete drone kits, and robotics SDKs, so startups and newcomers can go from unboxing to a working robot or drone in about 30 minutes. He explains why most of the 50 billion smart connected devices expected by 2040 will be purpose-built machines rather than humanoids. Or, as he puts it, he won’t buy a humanoid to push his lawnmower.
The conversation also covers:
Why trust, security, and functional safety matter in autonomous devices, from neonatal baby monitors to drones that can’t simply stop and reboot mid-flight.
Lars’s long-running “fridge hacking” warning, and why it’s now coming true.
How geopolitics is shaping NXP’s strategy: local-for-local security certifications, sourcing from two fabs on two continents, and RISC-V as an alternative architecture.
Why AI at the edge will arrive gradually as people replace old appliances, not as the step change Wall Street expects.
Nitin Dahad is executive editor of EE Times. An electronic engineering graduate from City University, he’s been an engineer, journalist and entrepreneur. He was part of ARC International’s startup team and took it public, and he co-founded a publication called The Chilli in the early 2000s. Nitin has also worked with National Semiconductor, GEC Plessey Semiconductors, Dialog Semiconductor, Marconi Instruments, Coresonic, Center for Integrated Photonics, IDENT Technology and Jennic. Nitin also held a role with government promoting U.K. technology globally in the U.S., Brazil, Middle East and Africa, and India.

articles.title: Ce NAS à moins de 200 € peut remplacer votre cloud, héberger Plex et même vos projets IA — Frandroid
articles.text:
On pense souvent aux NAS comme à de simples boîtiers destinés à sauvegarder des fichiers. Pourtant, ces petits ordinateurs connectés au réseau peuvent faire bien davantage. Stocker les photos de toute la famille, diffuser sa bibliothèque de films sur une télévision, héberger des applications ou conserver ses projets de développement accessibles à distance : les possibilités sont nombreuses.
Avec son processeur Intel x86 et ses 4 Go de RAM et son système d’exploitation TerraMaster TOS, le TerraMaster F2-425 constitue une porte d’entrée intéressante vers l’auto-hébergement. D’autant qu’AliExpress permet actuellement de faire descendre son prix sous la barre des 200 euros, sous certaines conditions.
Les points forts du TerraMaster F2-425
- Un processeur Intel x86 quadricœur, 4 Go de RAM et une connexion Ethernet 2,5 Gb/s
- Deux baies SATA pour installer jusqu’à 60 To de stockage brut
- La prise en charge de Plex, Jellyfin, Docker et des outils de cloud personnel
Affiché à 257,69 euros sur AliExpress, le TerraMaster F2-425 profite de deux réductions potentielles pendant l’opération du 11.11. Le code FRD1140 permet d’économiser 40 euros dès 229 euros d’achat sur les produits éligibles, faisant passer le NAS à 217,69 euros.
Une réduction supplémentaire de 20 euros peut s’appliquer en payant par PayPal sur les commandes d’au moins 199 euros. Si les deux avantages sont disponibles et cumulables lors de votre commande, le prix final descend alors à 197,69 euros. Ces promotions sont annoncées jusqu’au 18 novembre 2026, dans la limite des quotas disponibles. Pensez à vérifier les remises et les éventuels frais au moment du paiement.
Votre propre Google Photos ou iCloud, mais hébergé chez vous
Le premier intérêt du TerraMaster F2-425, c’est de reprendre le contrôle de ses données. Au lieu de confier toutes vos photos, vidéos et documents à Google Drive ou iCloud, vous pouvez les conserver sur des disques installés directement dans le NAS, chez vous. Le tout sans abonnement mensuel de stockage cloud, même s’il faut évidemment acheter les disques et prendre en compte la consommation électrique.
Le boîtier possède deux baies compatibles avec les disques durs SATA de 3,5 pouces, mais aussi les SSD SATA de 2,5 pouces. Il accepte jusqu’à 60 To de capacité brute au total, de quoi accueillir plusieurs années de photos, de vidéos et de sauvegardes. Pour sécuriser davantage ses fichiers face à la panne d’un disque, il est possible de configurer les deux unités en RAID 1. Attention, cette configuration réduit la capacité utilisable et ne remplace pas une véritable sauvegarde indépendante.
Avec l’application TNAS Mobile, il est possible de sauvegarder automatiquement les photos de son smartphone et de retrouver ses fichiers à distance. L’application Photos de TerraMaster propose également des fonctions de classement et de recherche. Les utilisateurs plus aventureux peuvent installer des solutions comme Immich ou Nextcloud, via des conteneurs, pour se constituer un véritable cloud personnel. Attention toutefois : Immich demande officiellement au moins 6 Go de RAM pour fonctionner normalement. Avec les 4 Go du NAS, il faut désactiver ses fonctions de machine learning, ou augmenter la mémoire.
Un serveur Plex ou Jellyfin pour profiter de tous vos films
Mais le F2-425 ne sert pas uniquement à conserver des fichiers. Il peut aussi devenir le centre multimédia de votre logement. En installant Plex ou Jellyfin, vous pouvez organiser votre bibliothèque de films, séries et vidéos personnelles, puis la retrouver sur une télévision connectée, une tablette, un ordinateur ou un smartphone compatible.
Son processeur Intel quadricœur embarque une partie graphique capable d’accélérer matériellement le traitement de vidéos H.264 et H.265, notamment en 4K. C’est un avantage lorsque le serveur doit adapter une vidéo à l’appareil utilisé pour la regarder. Le nombre de flux simultanés dépendra néanmoins des fichiers et des paramètres, et le transcodage matériel nécessite Plex Pass avec Plex. Pour les vidéos AV1, il ne faut pas compter sur une accélération matérielle équivalente avec le processeur N5095 indiqué dans la fiche technique.
Autre bon point : le port Ethernet 2,5 Gb/s offre une connexion réseau plus rapide que le Gigabit classique, à condition de disposer d’équipements compatibles. De quoi faciliter le transfert de gros fichiers, les sauvegardes d’ordinateurs ou la diffusion de contenus sur plusieurs appareils. Et grâce à son format compact, le NAS peut rester branché en permanence, près de votre box ou dans un bureau.
Un mini-serveur personnel à piloter avec Claude Code ou Codex
C’est peut-être l’usage le plus intéressant pour les bidouilleurs. Grâce à son architecture x86 et à la prise en charge de Docker, le TerraMaster F2-425 peut également servir de petit serveur domestique. Vous pouvez y déployer un site web, héberger des services personnels, installer des outils de développement ou automatiser certaines tâches. Le tout depuis une machine qui reste disponible sans avoir à laisser son ordinateur principal allumé.
Avec une configuration adaptée, ce type d’installation peut même être associé à des agents de programmation comme Claude Code ou OpenAI Codex. L’idée ? Conserver ses projets sur le NAS, accéder à un environnement de développement distant et demander à l’agent de modifier du code, préparer un service ou gérer certains déploiements. Depuis un smartphone, une connexion sécurisée et un terminal distant ou une interface web adaptée peuvent permettre de retrouver cet environnement, même en déplacement.
Ce fonctionnement ne signifie pas que le NAS est capable de faire tourner localement les grands modèles de langage de Claude ou d’OpenAI. Les agents utilisent généralement des modèles accessibles à distance, et les tâches lourdes resteront limitées par les performances du boîtier. Avec 4 Go de mémoire vive, mieux vaut privilégier quelques services légers ou envisager une extension de RAM pour multiplier les applications.
Le système d’exploitation TOS 7, désormais disponible pour ce modèle, facilite justement la gestion des fichiers, des utilisateurs et des applications. Avec Docker Compose et Portainer, il devient possible d’administrer plusieurs services sans repartir de zéro à chaque installation. Les utilisateurs expérimentés peuvent ainsi se construire une petite infrastructure personnelle, avec leurs données et leurs projets au même endroit.
À moins de 200 euros avec les deux réductions, le TerraMaster F2-425 est donc une alternative intéressante à l’achat d’un mini-PC dédié aux services domestiques, avec l’avantage d’intégrer directement deux baies de stockage. Il ne remplace évidemment pas un Mac mini pour les tâches de calcul intensif ou l’exécution locale de gros modèles IA, mais pour héberger un cloud personnel, Plex, Jellyfin et quelques projets, il a de solides arguments. Reste à prévoir le budget des disques, puisque ce NAS est vendu sans stockage.

articles.title: Anthropic lance Claude Meetings, l’IA qui transforme les réunions en plans d’action et tâches
articles.text:
Au milieu d’une visioconférence sur Google Meet, vous demandez à Claude de dessiner le planning du projet dont vous discutez avec vos collègues, et l’assistant d’Anthropic le construit sous vos yeux avant la fin de l’appel.
Anthropic a présenté Claude Meetings. Avec cette fonction, son IA entre dans vos réunions vidéo en tant que participant visible. Claude suit la conversation et commence à travailler sur les tâches évoquées en même temps que vous parlez. Le service ouvre en bêta pour les abonnements Team et Enterprise, et uniquement sur Google Meet, car Microsoft Teams et Zoom ne sont pas compatibles au lancement. Claude débarque ainsi dans l’outil de visioconférence de Google, où Gemini prend vos notes en français pendant vos appels.
Claude rédige vos plans d’action pendant l’appel
Impossible de faire entrer l’assistant en douce. « Claude se signale en tant que participant et publie un avis dans le chat de la réunion », précise Anthropic. Et si vous recevez des invités extérieurs à votre entreprise, Claude ne rejoint l’appel qu’avec l’accord d’un administrateur.
Une fois dans la réunion, Claude prend des notes et répond dans le chat aux questions des participants. Il va aussi chercher des chiffres dans les applications connectées à votre compte, rédige des plans et établit des échéances. Quand la discussion porte sur l’organisation d’un projet, vous pouvez lui confier un tableau blanc partagé, Claude Whiteboards, disponible en bêta pour tous les abonnements payants. Claude le remplit au fil de la conversation, et il suffit de lui demander à voix haute de regrouper les idées par thème ou de signaler les étapes oubliées.
Après l’appel, vous retrouvez sur claude.ai les notes et les documents produits par l’assistant. Chez Anthropic, Claude assiste à presque toutes les réunions internes depuis environ deux mois, selon Nicholas Lin, responsable produit chargé du travail de bureau.
- Excellente compréhension des consignes complexes
- Très bon niveau en rédaction
- Analyse de longs documents efficace
Anthropic concurrence Copilot et Gemini jusque dans Google Meet
Les assistants de réunion ne manquent pas. Dans Teams, Microsoft réserve aux abonnés de Microsoft 365 Copilot son agent Facilitator. Il prend les notes de toute l’équipe et répond dans le chat aux questions restées en suspens. Chez Google, Gemini vous envoie le compte rendu de vos réunions Meet et prévient chaque participant dès qu’il commence à écrire. Anthropic promet d’aller plus loin, en faisant passer votre équipe de la discussion à l’exécution sans attendre que la réunion se termine.
Pour garder vos documents dans Claude, Anthropic a sorti en même temps Claude Sheets, en bêta pour tous les abonnements payants. Avec ce tableur, Claude met en place vos budgets et vos tableaux de suivi, que votre équipe peut ensuite modifier à plusieurs et exporter vers Excel. Nicholas Lin reconnaît une version assez basique, peu adaptée aux modèles financiers complexes. Anthropic a enfin ouvert à tous Claude Data, l’ancien Claude Dashboards, qui récupère les données de vos logiciels de gestion de la relation client pour les transformer en tableaux de bord.
Anthropic ne prétend pas pour autant chasser Excel ou Google Sheets de votre entreprise. « Je pense que les produits de Microsoft et de Google gardent leur utilité, selon les moments et les besoins », souligne Nicholas Lin.

articles.title: N-able releases security hotfixes for zero-day vulnerabilities
articles.text:
N-able released hotfixes to address zero-day bugs affecting its N-central remote monitoring and management (RMM) platform, which were publicly disclosed over the weekend and forced it to take vulnerable hosted environments offline.
This follows N-able's decision to take all hosted N-central environments offline across the Americas, Europe, and Asia-Pacific regions until it could patch them against potential attacks targeting the zero-day flaws in the wild.
"N-able is actively responding to non-responsible communication of critical vulnerabilities in N-central late Sunday night, November 8, found by an independent researcher," N-able told BleepingComputer on Monday. "As a precautionary measure, we took our Hosted N-central environment offline today, November 9, and provided guidance to customers operating on-premises N-central servers to temporarily take their servers offline until further notice."
N-central lets IT departments and managed service providers (MSPs) monitor, manage, and maintain client networks and devices from a centralized web-based console.
N-able has now released N-central 2026.4 HF2 with security patches and technology updates for some of the leaked zero-days, including "the most critical" vulnerabilities:
- CVE-2026-125883 - Multiple XXE Vulnerabilities
- CVE-2026-125878 - Multiple OGNL Injection vulnerabilities
- CVE-2026-125879 - Local privilege escalation to root via nable-writable syslog-ng config
- CVE-2026-125880 - Stored XSS via MMS3 patch metadata (admin context)
- CVE-2026-125881 - Schema-hint SSRF via service import schema validation
- CVE-2026-125882 - RCE via file repository upload path traversal (Credit Nate Fair, Sprocket Security)
- CVE-2026-91000 - Insecure IPC Channels lead to local privilege escalation
In a Tuesday update, N-able said that all hosted N-central servers (NCODs) across all regions have now been successfully upgraded and advised and "strongly" recommended that all N-central On-Premises customers upgrade their installations to the newly released version "as soon as possible."
"Customers should follow the published upgrade guidance carefully before restoring normal access to their N-central environment. Earlier incident guidance advised On-Premises customers to keep their N-central servers offline while remediation was being developed," it said.
While N-able has yet to flag these flaws as exploited in the wild, threat intelligence company Defused said on Tuesday that attackers have already started scanning the Internet for vulnerable systems and warned admins to take N-central servers offline immediately.
"During the past 24 hours, we have observed probing of N-able N-central for the 0-days that were dropped publicly yesterday," Defused said. "We have seen opening of anonymous agent sessions, pulling appliance config and hitting the remote control endpoint without auth. These pathways are part of the 0-day exploit surface."
Internet security nonprofit Shadowserver reports that just over 148 N-central servers are currently exposed online, a sharp decrease from the 1,338 it detected on Monday.
Disclosed after previous reports were allegedly ignored
Security researcher Sean Bales disclosed the vulnerabilities late Sunday, November 8, and published a GitHub repository called Able2Shell containing proof-of-concept exploits for the flaws.
Bales said the zero-day bugs affect N-central Appliance 2026.4.0.31, a pre-release version of the software, and believes that most (if not all) of the flaws also affect earlier versions.
The disclosed vulnerabilities include remote code execution (RCE), authentication bypasses, credential disclosure, arbitrary file writes, directory traversal, XML external entity (XXE) injection, and cross-site scripting (XSS) flaws.
The security researcher also demoed a critical unauthenticated XXE-to-RCE exploit chain that abuses N-central's service-import functionality to steal a trusted local session, reset the targeted account's password, and execute commands on the server as the nable user.
Attackers could also use this exploit to create a Default Administrator account with attacker-controlled credentials, which provides them rogue admin access to the N-central management interface, as shown in the video demo embedded below.
Bales told BleepingComputer that he released the N-central zero-days without notifying N-able because the company allegedly failed to patch vulnerabilities (including two unrelated remote code execution bugs and a privilege-escalation flaw) he reported in a different N-able product about five to six months ago.
When asked about Bales' allegations regarding the previously disclosed security issues, N-able did not address the questions and instead responded with a statement about the N-central security incident and precautionary shutdown.
N-able provides cloud-based remote monitoring, cybersecurity, and data protection tools for Managed Service Providers (MSPs) and enterprise IT departments at more than 500,000 organizations in over 140 countries.

articles.title: Inside the economics of OPay and Moniepoint’s business
articles.text:
A Bolt driver in Nigeria will likely ask you to pay via OPay at the end of a trip, while a local store is more likely to have a Moniepoint terminal at its checkout. Both fintechs, which hold microfinance banking licences, have become synonymous with scale in Nigeria’s payments market, carving out niches in consumer payments and merchant processing.
In 2025, Nigeria processed more than ₦1.2 quadrillion ($880.51 billion) worth of electronic transactions. Moniepoint and OPay accounted for a significant share of this activity, processing a combined $644.85 billion.
Moniepoint said it processed 14 billion transactions worth ₦412 trillion ($286.85 billion at ₦1,436.31/$ as of December 31, 2025) in 2025. OPay processed 62.3 billion transactions worth $358 billion. OPay processed 4.45 times as many transactions as Moniepoint, but Moniepoint’s average transaction value was $20.49, approximately 3.56 times OPay’s $5.75.
Moniepoint said it serves more than 20 million businesses and individuals, while OPay reported 50.1 million monthly active users.
These numbers offer a window into the operating economics of both companies: who moves more money, who makes more money from moving it, and who keeps more of what they make?
It is important to note that Moniepoint operates largely in Nigeria, with a recent expansion into Kenya. OPay operates in Indonesia, Egypt, and Pakistan, but derives most of its scale from Nigeria. It generated 88.1% of its revenue from the country in 2025.
What the average numbers show
Moniepoint’s average transaction value of $20.49 is approximately 3.56 times OPay’s $5.75.
This difference could reflect Moniepoint’s greater concentration of merchant payments, business transactions, or other relatively large payments. OPay’s lower average could reflect more frequent, lower-value consumer transactions.
These are hypotheses rather than confirmed explanations. The companies’ transaction disclosures do not provide enough detail to establish exactly what drives the difference.
There are other indicators of how frequently their customers use their platforms. OPay says its digital wallets were used an average of 209 times per user per month. Moniepoint said its cards were used 1.7 million times daily.
However, the total value passing through a payment platform is not the same as the revenue it earns. Their revenue depends on fees, commissions, lending, merchant services, and other income sources.
OPay disclosed $536.25 million in revenue in 2025. Moniepoint does not publicly disclose revenue figures.
One way to illustrate Moniepoint’s revenue potential is to examine OPay’s revenue relative to the value it processed. Its $536.25 million in revenue represented about 0.15% of its $358 billion in transaction value.
If Moniepoint generated revenue at the same rate, its $286.85 billion in transaction value would translate to approximately $430.28 million in revenue.
This is an illustrative scenario, not an estimate of Moniepoint’s actual revenue. The two companies have different transaction mixes, fee structures, and revenue sources.
Loans are becoming another revenue engine
Both OPay and Moniepoint increased their lending activity in 2025, using the financial activity passing through their platforms to extend credit.
OPay originated $938.3 million in new loans in Nigeria, up 284.71% in one year.
Moniepoint, meanwhile, said it disbursed more than ₦1 trillion ($696.23 million) in loans to small businesses in 2025. In 2023, it disbursed $71 million in working capital loans.
Moniepoint uses its merchant relationships to extend business credit. Its terminals give it visibility into how much a business processes, how frequently it receives payments, and how its transaction activity changes over time.
This provides an alternative source of information for assessing a business that may not have conventional financial statements or sufficient collateral.
The company’s lending portfolio targets merchants, including provision stores, supermarkets, restaurants, and wholesale distributors. It says businesses that received its loans recorded an average 36% increase in transaction value after accessing credit.
OPay’s lending operation has a broader consumer-facing distribution advantage. Its wallet gives it access to millions of users who already transact frequently on the platform. In 2025, its quarterly unique borrowers in Nigeria reached 4.6 million, more than twice the 2.1 million recorded a year earlier.
While OPay has built much of its credit product around consumers, it is also looking to expand merchant lending, which it recently introduced. The company says merchant loans typically feature higher limits, lower rates, and longer tenors aligned with business cash flow cycles.
Both companies are effectively turning payment histories into credit intelligence, but they are applying that information to different customer segments.
For OPay, lending is already a significant contributor to revenue. In 2025, it generated $260.3 million in loan financing revenue, up from $71.5 million in 2024. This represented growth of approximately 264.1% and accounted for 48.5% of its total revenue.
But lending also carries risks. OPay’s provision for expected credit losses increased from $24.8 million in 2024 to $121.3 million in 2025, nearly five times the previous year’s figure.
The provision was approximately 46.6% of its loan-financing revenue. This is not the same as realised loan losses, but it shows the growing credit risk exposure accompanying the expansion of its lending business.
Moniepoint’s lending economics are not public, making it difficult to establish how much revenue its credit business generates or how much it spends managing defaults. The company claims that its non-performing loans (NPLs), loans for which principal or interest payments are overdue by 90 days or more, are small.
According to the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), NPLs rose to 7% in 2025.
Profits
Processing billions of transactions and generating hundreds of millions of dollars in revenue is one thing. Turning that activity into profit is another.
For payment companies, scale comes with considerable costs: technology infrastructure, transaction processing, customer acquisition, regulatory compliance, fraud management, staff costs, and, increasingly, the cost of extending credit.
OPay generated $536.25 million in revenue in 2025 and ultimately made $110.79 million in income before taxes. That translates to a net profit margin of approximately 20.66%. In other words, it retained about 21 cents in profit per dollar of revenue.
Moniepoint does not disclose its revenue or profit figures. However, applying OPay’s revenue-to-transaction-value ratio and net profit margin to Moniepoint’s transaction value produces an estimated profit of $88.89 million. This is an indicative estimate, not a reported financial result, and assumes both companies have comparable revenue yields and cost structures.
The numbers show how OPay has built a high-frequency payments business and is increasingly extracting revenue from lending. Nearly half of its 2025 revenue came from loan financing, although rising complaints about high interest rates to cover credit-loss provisions indicate that this growth carries additional risk.
Moniepoint, on the other hand, has built a merchant-focused payments network that gives it access to business transaction data and opportunities to extend working capital. Its higher average transaction value and growing lending portfolio point to a different monetisation strategy: building deeper financial relationships with merchants rather than relying primarily on the frequency of everyday consumer payments.
The ₦1,000 Journey
Explore the hidden infrastructure, relationships, and data behind an everyday digital payment.
OPay: Consumer & Merchant
Moniepoint: Merchant & Consumer
Both companies have built considerable scale in Nigeria. But sustaining that position will increasingly depend on how they navigate a changing regulatory environment.
In June 2026, the CBN introduced new market-structure requirements that could constrain financial institutions seeking to dominate both consumer payments and merchant acquiring.
In a circular, the regulator stated that any licensed financial institution controlling more than 25% of the consumer-issuing market would be restricted to a maximum of 15% market share in merchant-acquiring activities.
For OPay and Moniepoint, this introduces another variable into an already competitive market. Their ability to grow will depend not only on how many transactions they process or how much revenue they generate, but also on how they position themselves across the layers of Nigeria’s payments infrastructure.

articles.title: Fin des voitures thermiques : l’Europe prête à laisser la porte ouverte après 2035 ?
articles.text:
L’Union européenne aurait-elle voulu aller trop vite sur la fin de commercialisation des voitures thermiques ? Le cap est fixé à 2035 : passé cette date, les constructeurs ne pourront plus vendre de voitures neuves embarquant un moteur à explosion, qu’elles soient thermiques ou hybrides. Toutefois, la réglementation semble évoluer en faveur d’une conservation limitée des moteurs thermiques.
Des objectifs qui s’assouplissent
Lors de l’adoption du règlement (UE) 2023/851, le cap était clair : une réduction de 100 % des émissions de CO2 des véhicules neufs en 2035 par rapport à 2021. Ce qui veut dire que les voitures neuves utilisant un moteur thermique devront disparaître des catalogues européens des constructeurs.
Toutefois, l’Union européenne semble revenir sur cette décision forte. En ce début novembre, un vote de la commission de l’Environnement a pour but de remodeler cette règle. Le cap de 2035 serait conservé, mais la réduction des émissions de CO2 devrait atteindre 87,5 % par rapport à 2021. Ce qui laisse quelque peu d’espoir aux moteurs thermiques de continuer à exister sous le capot de certains véhicules.
Des mécanismes de compensation sont aussi prévus par le projet de texte du règlement. Il est notamment prévu l’achat de crédits liés à l’utilisation d’acier « vert » produit en Europe, permettant de produire des véhicules plus polluants que la cible de l’Union européenne si d’importants efforts sont faits sur la décarbonation de la production du véhicule.
Une ouverture pour quelques voitures avec des moteurs thermiques
En réduisant son objectif de 100 % à 87,5 % de décarbonation, l’Union européenne ne sauve pas les voitures thermiques pour autant. En effet, il y aura un espoir pour que des voitures hybrides performantes utilisent toujours un moteur thermique, mais celles-ci vont devoir faire des efforts considérables sur les émissions d’échappement.
L’ONG Transport & Environment estime que cette modification pourrait permettre à jusqu’à 39 % des voitures vendues après 2035 de conserver un moteur thermique. Toutefois, il ne s’agirait pas de moteurs performants et émouvants. Il y a de fortes chances que ces moteurs soient fortement dépollués, bridés et silencieux. On pourrait voir des hybrides à la manière des Super-Hybride DM-i de BYD se développer, avec l’usage du moteur thermique principalement pour générer de l’énergie vers les batteries et, occasionnellement, entraîner les roues.
Un espoir pour les moteurs thermiques et la pression franco-allemande
Les moteurs thermiques pourront toutefois continuer d’exister s’ils fonctionnent uniquement avec du carburant synthétique e-fuel. Ces véhicules seront alors considérés comme totalement décarbonés. Toutefois, il n’est pas certain que cette solution sauve le moteur thermique pour toutes les bourses. Les e-fuels seront très certainement très coûteux, avec des tarifs dépassant largement ceux de l’essence actuellement. Les véhicules e-fuels seront réservés à une certaine élite, Porsche étant un acteur majeur sur le sujet des e-fuels.
Cet assouplissement probable des règles de l’Union européenne résulte d’une alarme déclenchée par les constructeurs européens, notamment Renault, qui met en évidence les ralentissements de la demande de voitures électriques. Les voitures électriques grignotent encore des parts de marché, mais pourraient ne pas obtenir 100 % de parts de marché avant 2035, surtout sur des segments spécifiques comme celui des utilitaires. Une coalition franco-allemande œuvre même pour un objectif de 80 % de décarbonation en 2035 par rapport à 2021.
Le vote de la commission de l’Environnement ne garantit pas l’adoption de ce nouvel objectif. Le texte doit être adopté en séance plénière au Parlement européen en décembre.

articles.title: Developers have been hacking around MCP’s file-upload problem for two years. A fix is taking shape.
articles.text:
Developers have been hacking around MCP’s file-upload problem for two years. A fix is taking shape.
The Model Context Protocol (MCP) has played an instrumental part in connecting AI assistants to external tools and data since Anthropic launched the project some two years ago. Want to have a coding agent check the status of a bug? Give it access to your issue tracker through an MCP server. Or ask an assistant how many orders your company shipped last week? Connect it to a tool that can query your database.
Part of the Agentic AI Foundation since last December, MCP has a roadmap that reflects the demands of running the protocol in production. For instance, maintainers have been working to make servers easier to deploy without keeping track of individual client sessions, and to let companies manage access through their existing identity systems.
But a perennial problem developers have faced is how to pass a file from an AI app to an MCP tool. For example, say you attach a PDF to a chat and ask the assistant to save it to cloud storage — the assistant can call a tool to save the file, but developers still have to work out how to get the PDF from the chat app to the tool. That can mean issuing a temporary upload link, or perhaps sending the user to a separate upload page.
To address this gap, the folks at the MCP project have outlined a draft extension that gives clients and tools a common way to handle uploads and downloads.
Why MCP needs a way to move files
In a blog post published on Tuesday, Den Delimarsky, lead maintainer of MCP and member of technical staff at Anthropic, and Google software engineer Wil St. Charles, lay out the rationale for the new extension, noting that developers’ needs have changed as they’ve started asking agents to do more with the tools MCP connects them to.
“Many of those MCP server projects now need to work with files — often driven by increasing agent capabilities and autonomy.”
“Over the past two years, the things people build with the protocol have become more ambitious. Much more ambitious,” they write. “Many of those MCP server projects now need to work with files — often driven by increasing agent capabilities and autonomy.”
This demand has shown up in the community more or less since MCP’s inception. In December 2024, a developer building a tool to process files asked on GitHub how to get a file from the client to the server. An Anthropic team member acknowledged the difficulty and said they were exploring how a tool could send a file back to an AI app. Other community members subsequently chipped in with advice, with one noting that they had built their own way to send files from the AI app to the MCP server. Their MCP client uploaded the file directly to the server before calling the tool, with the upload itself happening outside the protocol.
Developers have been looking for ways to hack around the gap ever since. In one Reddit thread a few months back, one user said a temporary S3 upload link worked in Claude once outbound access was enabled, but they couldn’t get the same approach working in ChatGPT, so they built a separate web app and upload page. Another developer said they had built a drag-and-drop interface to an MCP App, which let users submit files themselves but still left the agent without a way to initiate the upload on its own.
There are packaged options, too. FastMCP offers a drag-and-drop upload component for developers building MCP Apps, while Box recently launched secure file upload and download support for PDFs and Office documents through its own MCP server.
The folks at the MCP project, for their part, have been slowly working toward a common standard. Delimarsky opened an exploratory upload proposal in August 2025, and a File Uploads Working Group, initially made up of members from Anthropic and OpenAI, followed in April. In October, the group added file downloads to its remit.
Now, a draft specification sets out how transfers in both directions could work.
“While we have the shape outlined, we’re not sure yet that what we started with is what we’ll end up with.”
“While we have the shape outlined, we’re not sure yet that what we started with is what we’ll end up with,” the authors write. “The best way to find out is, you guessed it — contact with reality.”
How MCP would move files
The experimental file-transfer extension builds on the framework for extensions MCP introduced in July to let clients and servers opt into new features without changing the core protocol. The experimental stage gives developers a place to prototype and refine an idea before, or alongside, a formal Specification Enhancement Proposal (SEP).
Either way, the file itself bypasses the model.
Under the extension, if you ask an assistant to save an attached PDF to cloud storage, for example, the model calls the tool and the MCP client handles the upload. The client can send a small file within the tool request, and for a larger file, the client uploads it separately and calls the tool again to finish the job. Either way, the file itself bypasses the model.
For downloads, a tool that exports a CSV, for example, can include a download URL once it’s finished producing the file. The client can then fetch the CSV directly, and the model gets a message telling it what the tool produced.
One of the big security implications centres around how much control the host should have over where files go. As things stand, the proposed extension limits when a client can send its MCP credentials to an upload destination. The host asks the user to approve the upload before the MCP server supplies that destination, so the user may not know where the file will go when they approve it.
“These safeguards control where the client’s MCP credential is sent, but they don’t by themselves control where the file goes,” the authors write.
So a user who thinks they’re saving a confidential PDF to company storage could end up sending it to an endpoint controlled by a malicious server operator. The authors recommend limiting external uploads to approved destinations, and are asking whether hosts should be required to enforce that restriction.
It’s worth noting that developers can prototype against the draft today by implementing the proposed transfer on a test client and server. However, there’s no formal reference implementation yet.
“That’s because we expect that a lot of the inner workings will, in fact, be quite different once we start integrating our experiment with third-party file services, such as cloud storage, database import/export, and many others that require file input and output,” the authors add.
The MCP maintainers say they are targeting a stable release by year-end, and support will remain optional — developers who choose to skip the extension won’t need to change their existing MCP clients or servers.

articles.title: Mais de 84 milhões de brasileiros não usaram o Gov.br em 2025, aponta TCU
articles.text:
Mais de 84 milhões de brasileiros não utilizaram a plataforma Gov.br em 2025. O número revela desafio para a digitalização dos serviços públicos no país: apesar da expansão do sistema, milhões de pessoas ainda não conseguem ou não precisam acessar a ferramenta, enquanto parte dos serviços federais não oferece alternativa presencial.
Os dados fazem parte de auditoria apresentada pelo Tribunal de Contas da União (TCU) nesta quarta-feira (11). Segundo o levantamento, 84,6 milhões de pessoas ficaram sem utilizar a plataforma ao longo do ano passado. Desse total, 39,6 milhões não tinham conta Gov.br, enquanto outros 45 milhões estavam cadastrados, mas não acessaram o sistema.
O tribunal também identificou 6,7 milhões de pessoas que tentaram utilizar suas contas, mas não conseguiram concluir nenhum acesso. É importante destacar que não usar a plataforma não significa necessariamente ter sido impedido de acessar serviços públicos: parte dos brasileiros pode simplesmente não ter precisado dela.
Maioria dos serviços federais não oferece alternativa presencial
- Um dos principais problemas identificados pelo TCU está na falta de opções para quem enfrenta dificuldades com os canais digitais. Dos 5.616 serviços federais analisados, 4.056 não ofereciam atendimento presencial em nenhuma etapa do procedimento;
- Na avaliação geral do tribunal, 72% dos serviços públicos federais examinados só podiam ser acessados pela internet. Apenas 2% permitiam que o cidadão escolhesse entre realizar todo o procedimento on-line ou presencialmente;
- A fiscalização também identificou dificuldades para criar, recuperar e desbloquear contas. No Distrito Federal, usuários chegaram a pagar R$ 40 a estabelecimentos, como lan houses, para conseguir realizar esses procedimentos. Em outras localidades, problemas de conectividade e energia dificultavam o acesso;
- Os obstáculos são maiores entre pessoas idosas, cidadãos com baixa escolaridade, moradores de áreas rurais e da Região Norte, além de pessoas com deficiência.

- Quem está por trás do Gov.br? Conheça a ‘guardiã’ dos dados dos brasileiros
- Gov.br: atualização facilita recuperação de contas para celulares perdidos; veja como fazer
Balcões presenciais ainda têm alcance limitado
Para atender quem precisa de ajuda com a plataforma, o governo mantém os Balcões Gov.br, unidades presenciais que auxiliam na criação, recuperação e desbloqueio de contas.
Em agosto de 2026, a rede contava com 277 unidades distribuídas por 212 municípios. A cobertura estimada, porém, era de apenas 25% da população brasileira.
A meta do Ministério da Gestão e da Inovação em Serviços Públicos era chegar a 950 pontos de atendimento até dezembro de 2026.
O TCU recomendou ao ministério a ampliação do atendimento presencial, a adoção de medidas para facilitar o acesso às contas, a criação de iniciativas de inclusão digital e o estabelecimento de metas para reduzir o tempo de resposta às solicitações dos usuários.
Gov.br chegou a quase 180 milhões de contas
Os dados da auditoria contrastam com a expansão da plataforma. Segundo indicadores divulgados pelo Ministério da Gestão, o Gov.br chegou a aproximadamente 179,5 milhões de contas cadastradas em outubro de 2026.
Em março, a pasta informou que o sistema havia ultrapassado 80 milhões de usuários únicos em um único mês, com 1,7 bilhão de acessos no primeiro trimestre do ano.
Os números mostram o alcance crescente da ferramenta, mas não significam que todos os cadastrados consigam utilizar os serviços sem dificuldades. A auditoria do TCU aponta justamente a necessidade de garantir alternativas e suporte para quem encontra barreiras no ambiente digital.
O levantamento sobre cidadania digital fez parte de conjunto de cinco auditorias apresentadas pelo tribunal. Os temas foram escolhidos a partir de consulta pública realizada entre novembro de 2025 e fevereiro de 2026, dentro da iniciativa “Você escolhe, o TCU fiscaliza!”.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: Summit Lithium Technologies exploring M&A deal, possibly to foreign buyer
articles.text:
Calgary-based lithium extraction company Summit Lithium Technologies is evaluating strategic options that could result in a sale to a foreign buyer.
Summit Lithium CEO Amanda Hall revealed that her company was courting buyers in an online policy briefing hosted by the National Angel Capital Organization (NACO) on Tuesday. The event featured a conversation between Hall and Dominion Dynamics CEO Eliot Pence that was part of a broader discussion on how the 2026 federal budget will affect entrepreneurs.
“We want a good fit to see our developments and capabilities get accelerated into commercial lithium projects.”
Joe Arencibia
Summit Lithium Technologies
When NACO CEO and moderator Claudio Rojas asked where Hall’s business was heading in the next five years, she said Summit Lithium is looking at mergers and acquisitions (M&A) and that it’s “completing the journey.”
“As we’re in M&A, all of the buyers are international, but they like that we have a Canadian presence and they want to keep us here just under a new banner,” Hall said, adding that she thinks it’s exciting to continue to grow a business under a different banner in Canada from Calgary.
When reached for more information, Summit Lithium president and COO Joe Arencibia told BetaKit in an email that Hall was speaking in shorthand about a broader process and that the company is looking at several options, including strategic partnership opportunities, grants, or M&A.
“Summit has gotten to the point of having well-developed technology that’s ready to move to commercial scale, and traditionally the best way to do this is with strategic/industrial partners versus more venture capital,” Arencibia wrote. “So, Summit is looking at several options, including M&A.”
Arencibia did not provide specifics, other than to say that Summit Lithium is talking to established industry partners to collaborate on large-scale, revenue-generating commercialization projects, as well as government agencies in Canada and the United States for specific funding programs that support critical metals and energy transition.
On the sale side, Arencibia confirmed the interested parties are outside of Canada but that Summit Lithium intends to keep its footprint in the country. He added that the company is looking “beyond dollars” as it searches for a partner.
RELATED: How Summit Lithium’s Amanda Hall emerged from the investment “valley of death”
“We want a good fit to see our developments and capabilities get accelerated into commercial lithium projects,” Arencibia said. He also noted Summit Lithium is making “great progress” on the process, and while the response has been enthusiastic, “these things take time.”
Founded in 2018, Summit Lithium (formerly known as Summit Nanotech) designed a patented system to isolate and extract lithium, a high-demand metal used in rechargeable batteries, more sustainably and efficiently with nanotechnology. In 2025, the company made the Global Cleantech 100 list, which showcases private cleantech companies poised to make a substantial impact on the market in the next five to 10 years, and was recognized in this year’s issue of BetaKit Most Ambitious.
The company has raised more than $100 million CAD in its lifetime, most recently a $25.5-million USD ($36.3-million CAD) round in March 2025 to help it transition from demonstration to commercialization plants. In the NACO briefing, Hall noted her company “won’t be raising another round” and that, as she’s “closing the circle,” Summit Lithium’s angel investors are coming back to reinvest in the company.
“The parties who started my company with me, that were linking arms with me at the beginning and supporting me, and teaching me how to run a business, and how to grow and scale a company; they’re the ones standing with me at the finish line,” Hall said. “That’s really amazing.”
Arencibia clarified that, while it’s too soon to say, Hall “has no plans to go anywhere.”
Feature image courtesy Summit Lithium Technologies.

articles.title: Google’s Tabletop AI experiment lets you build custom collaboration apps
articles.text:
Google has cooked up a new experimental AI tool called Tabletop that generates customized collaborative hubs to help you coordinate with family, and friends. The Tabletop platform shares some visual similarities with workplace management apps like Asana and Monday, but with a built-in AI feature that allows you to vibecode personalized interactive tools by describing them, such as savings trackers, chore charts, event plans, and more.
Google’s Tabletop AI experiment lets you build custom collaboration apps
Tabletop provides customizable, collaborative spaces for all your personal planning needs.
“Just add in your links, files and ideas, then prompt @tabletop — or pick a starter template — to generate custom interactive trip itineraries, dinner polls, expense splitters and tournament brackets,” Google Labs design and engineering lead Roman Nurik said in the blog post. “Once your space is ready, drop the invite link in your group chat to let everyone jump in and use it at the same time like a Google Doc.”
Access to the Tabletop beta is rolling out via a waitlist, and currently limited to people over the age of 18 in the US. Some of the example use cases that Nurik provides in his video above would clearly require giving kids or teens access to Tabletop, however, and using this for personal family planning looks like a compelling alternative to stuffy workplace software, so that age requirement might only be in place while Tabletop is in public testing.

articles.title: El calendario completo de ‘Los Anillos de Poder’, explicado: número de episodios y fechas de estreno
articles.text:
La temporada 3 de Los Anillos de Poder ya se ha estrenado en Amazon Prime Video. La plataforma ha regresado una vez más a su serie de la Tierra Media, esta vez con la firme intención de convencer a los fans con una entrega más oscura y bélica. Y es que este proyecto sobre El Señor de los Anillos, para bien o para mal, se ha convertido en una de las series más destacadas del último lustro.
En esta nueva entrega, que tiene lugar 5 años después de la anterior, la Tierra Media está en guerra. Los ejércitos de Sauron han avanzado por todo el continente, conquistando cuanto encuentran a su paso. Solo unos pocos bastiones aislados se interponen entre el Señor Oscuro y la victoria total: Khazad-dûm, donde los enanos permanecen ahora recluidos en las profundidades de sus salones bajo la montaña, y los reinos élficos de Lindon y Rivendel, protegidos por sus Tres Anillos. Ahora, todos los pueblos libres de la Tierra Media deberán encontrar la forma de unirse e impedir que Sauron alcance su objetivo: someter toda forma de vida bajo su dominio absoluto.
Los primeros capítulos de la temporada 3 de Los Anillos de Poder ya han llegado a Amazon Prime Video en lo que sin lugar a dudas era uno de los estrenos más importantes de la plataforma en este final de año. A partir de ahora, la compañía seguirá con la serie una estrategia de estreno semanal muy particular. Y es que el servicio de streaming lanzará sus nuevos capítulos durante las próximas semanas cada miércoles, aunque en menor cantidad que en esta primera fecha. Así se llegará al octavo y último de ellos, que será el final de temporada.
Calendario de estreno de Los Anillos de Poder temporada 3
Con esta estrategia de estreno cada semana, el calendario completo de Los Anillos de Poder temporada 3 es el siguiente.
- Episodio 1: miércoles 11 de noviembre.
- Episodio 2: miércoles 11 de noviembre.
- Episodio 3: miércoles 11 de noviembre.
- Episodio 4: miércoles 11 de noviembre.
- Episodio 5: miércoles 18 de noviembre.
- Episodio 6: miércoles 18 de noviembre.
- Episodio 7: miércoles 25 de noviembre.
- Episodio 8: miércoles 25 de noviembre.
Prueba Amazon Prime Video totalmente gratis durante 30 días y disfruta del catálogo completo de la plataforma sin límites. Solo con darte de alta tendrás acceso instantáneo a las mejores películas y series, además de envíos gratis en Amazon y otras ventajas.
De esta forma, Los Anillos de Poder contará con un sorprendente calendario de estreno que mantendrá a su temporada 3 en emisión durante menos de un mes. Es una estrategia distinta a la de otros años con la que la plataforma confía en generar mucha conversación en un periodo corto de tiempo. A partir de su final, tendremos que esperar novedades sobre una hipotética, aunque previsible, temporada 4.

articles.title: Download für GTA 6 optimieren: Diese Optionen haben Fritzbox-Nutzer
articles.text:
Download für GTA 6 optimieren: Diese Optionen haben Fritzbox-Nutzer
GTA 6 ist für Gamer:innen mittlerweile zum Greifen nahe. Denn schon jetzt kann das langersehnte Rockstar-Game auf PS5 und Xbox Series X heruntergeladen werden. Aufgrund der Installationsgröße von über 200 Gigabyte müssen Zocker:innen für GTA 6 nicht nur den freien Speicher ihrer Konsole optimieren. Je nach Internetgeschwindigkeit musst du auch rechtzeitig mit dem Download beginnen, um zum Release direkt loszocken zu können.
Download von GTA 6: Diese Fritzbox-Einstellungen helfen
Wenn dein Internetvertrag nicht gerade eine Gigabit-Leitung beinhaltet, kann der Download von GTA 6 etwas länger dauern. Solltest du eine Fritzbox als Router nutzen, gibt es Optionen, um das Herunterladen etwas zu beschleunigen. Denn Fritzboxen erlauben, den Datenverkehr bestimmter Geräte und Anwendungen im eigenen Netzwerk zu priorisieren.
Dadurch stellst du sicher, dass die volle Downloadgeschwindigkeit für deine Playstation 5 oder Xbox-Konsole samt GTA 6 statt für andere Geräte im Haushalt genutzt wird. Bevor du die Änderungen vornimmst, solltest du dir allerdings im Klaren sein, dass die Funktionen anderer internetfähiger Geräte dadurch eingeschränkt werden könnten. Zudem könntest du den Ärger deiner Mitmenschen im selben Haushalt auf dich ziehen, wenn du unangekündigt die gesamte Downloadrate für GTA 6 hortest.
Internetnutzung von PS5 und Xbox optimieren
Willst du die Priorität von Geräten in der Fritzbox ändern, rufe dazu die Benutzeroberfläche des Routers über einen Browser auf. Das geht entweder über die Adresse „fritz.box“ oder die ab Werk eingestellte IP-Adresse „192.168.178.1“. Die Zugangsdaten findest du auf deiner Fritzbox. Nachdem du eingeloggt bist, klicke in der linken Seitenleiste auf „Heimnetz“ und anschließend „Netzwerk“.
Dort findest du eine Liste mit allen verbundenen Geräten. Suche in der Liste nach „PS5“ oder „Xbox“, um das richtige Gerät zu finden. Hat deine Konsole keine eindeutige Bezeichnung in der Liste der Fritzbox-Geräte, musst du den Umweg über die PS5 oder Xbox selbst nehmen. Rufe in der Konsole die Netzwerkeinstellungen auf und notiere dir die MAC-Adresse. Diese ist eindeutig und kann mit der Liste der Fritzbox abgeglichen werden, um das korrekte Gerät zu identifizieren.
Hast du die Konsole gefunden, klicke daneben auf das Stiftsymbol. Wähle bei „Internetnutzung“ den Punkt „priorisiert“ aus. Das bedeutet, dass bei voller Internetauslastung immer die Konsole priorisiert wird. Sollten in der Zwischenzeit andere Geräte einen Download starten, wird ihnen erst nach dem Abschluss des GTA-6-Downloads wieder Bandbreite zugewiesen.
Dem GTA-6-Download Priorität geben
Im Anschluss kannst du in der linken Seitenleiste auf „Internet“ und „Filter“ klicken. Öffne dann in der Übersicht den Reiter „Priorisierung“. Hier kannst du weitere Einstellungen zur Verteilung der Geschwindigkeit in deinem Heimnetz vornehmen. Für GTA 6 und den Download auf PS5 und Xbox sind dabei „Priorisierte Anwendungen“ im unteren Bereich relevant.
Füge in dem Bereich eine neue Regel hinzu und wähle erneut die Konsole aus der Liste der Geräte aus. Lege dann im zweiten Dropdown-Menü fest, dass die Regelung für alle Netzwerkanwendungen gelten soll. Dadurch legst du ebenfalls fest, dass die Konsolen bei hohen Anforderungen an das Netzwerk priorisiert behandelt werden sollen.
PS5 und Xbox Series X: Was hilft beim Laden von GTA 6?
Bei den Konsolen, für die GTA 6 erscheint, lassen sich leider kaum relevante Einstellungen treffen, um den Download signifikant zu beschleunigen. Dafür gibt es aber auch kein Feature, dass die Downloadrate versehentlich begrenzen könnte. Die einzige Option, das Herunterladen von GTA 6 auf PS5 und Xbox Series X zu beschleunigen, ist die korrekte Verbindung mit dem Internet.
So einfach eine WLAN-Verbindung zwischen Konsole und Router hergestellt ist: Bei der eigentlichen Downloadgeschwindigkeit gibt es immer Einbußen. Je weiter der Abstand zum Router oder zu einem Repeater ist, desto weniger Bandbreite kommt letztlich für den GTA-6-Download an. Da hilft es nur, die Konsole zumindest für den Download mit einem LAN-Kabel direkt mit der Fritzbox zu verbinden. So stellst du sicher, dass die Konsole die volle Internetgeschwindigkeit ausnutzen kann. Ist der Download abgeschlossen, kannst du die Konsole wieder zu ihrem angestammten Platz und damit ins WLAN zurückbringen – und GTA 6 pünktlich zum Release starten.

                                                                UCIe Connectivity for 2.5D and 3D Multi-Die Designs                                                    
Low Power-High Performance
                        WHITEPAPERS
		
The differences and engineering considerations behind choosing and implementing UCIe connectivity for advanced multi-die designs.
								November 11th, 2026 - 
								By: Synopsys
								
							
UCIe provides a common standard for die-to-die connectivity, but connecting dies in a 2.5D package is fundamentally different from connecting them in a 3D design.
In 2.5D designs, UCIe links traverse package channels where insertion loss, crosstalk, and increasing data rates influence PHY and package design. In 3D designs, shorter vertical connections and fine-pitch bonding allow bandwidth to scale through connection density, reducing the need for high-speed serialization, equalization, and channel training.
This white paper examines those differences and the engineering considerations behind choosing and implementing UCIe connectivity for advanced multi-die designs.
What you’ll learn:
- How UCIe connectivity differs across 2.5D and 3D designs
- How F2B and F2F topologies affect interface design
- How 3D integration changes implementation, test, and reliability requirements
- How to align UCIe IP, package topology, and implementation strategy
